cards.pattern: People assume there's a much more [X] than there is.
cards.quote: I think people assume that there's a much more detailed semantic understanding of everybody's interests and preferences in the algorithm than there is.
cards.zh: 我覺得大家會以為演算法對每個人的興趣和偏好，有一套比實際上細膩得多的語意理解。
cards.why: 用「people assume... than there is」直接指出集體誤解，但主詞是 people 不是 you，不會讓聽的人覺得被打臉。台灣人常直接說「That's wrong」，這句是資深的替代寫法。
swaps: There's a common misconception that...
People tend to overestimate how much...
cards.pmNote: 破除利害關係人對系統能力的想像，是 PM 對齊期望的第一步。
cards.episode: Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity

cards.pattern: In a world where [前提], it's more important to [主張].
cards.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
cards.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。
cards.why: 「In a world where X, it's more important to Y」把主張架在一個對方已經同意的前提上，聽起來像推論而不是意見。這是矽谷提案最常見的開場結構。
swaps: Now that X is cheap, the bottleneck shifts to Y
As X gets easier, Y becomes the real constraint
cards.pmNote: 「做得出來」不再是瓶頸時，機會判斷 (opportunity assessment) 才是 PM 的核心價值。
cards.episode: Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity

cards.pattern: What's clearly happening is [現象], and [誰] is wrestling with what that means.
cards.quote: What's clearly happening is all of the functions are starting to bleed into each other, and the whole industry's wrestling with what that means.
cards.zh: 很明顯正在發生的是，各個職能開始互相滲透，而整個產業還在摸索這代表什麼。
cards.why: 把「事實」和「解讀」切開講：現象很確定（clearly happening），意義還沒定論（wrestling with）。這讓你既顯得有觀點，又不會把話說死。
swaps: The trend is clear; what it means is still an open question
We can see X happening. What we don't know yet is Y
cards.pmNote: 定義問題時分開「觀察」與「詮釋」，能避免團隊在還沒對齊事實前就吵解法。
cards.episode: Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity

cards.pattern: We try to [做法] a bit, but then end up with [結果].
cards.quote: So we try to build a team based on the needs of the work a bit, but then end up with a much smaller core.
cards.zh: 所以我們會盡量照工作本身的需求去組團隊，最後就會收斂成一個小很多的核心。
cards.why: 句尾那個 a bit 是母語者的減壓閥——把「我們照需求組隊」這種可能被質疑的說法先自己打個折，反而更可信。台灣人寫英文常常忘了加這種緩衝詞。
swaps: to some extent
more or less
roughly speaking
cards.pmNote: 團隊編制跟著工作型態走，而不是先定編制再塞工作。
cards.episode: Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity

cards.pattern: That is a function of [原因].
cards.quote: And that is a function of you want to have, for anybody who's running code, someone who can review their code and who's familiar with that code base.
cards.zh: 而那是因為：只要有人在寫程式，你就會希望有另一個熟悉那個 codebase 的人能 review 他的程式。
cards.why: 「That's a function of X」比「That's because X」更冷靜、更像在做結構分析。用在解釋現狀成因時，會讓你聽起來像在拆系統而不是找藉口。
swaps: That comes down to...
That's driven by...
That falls out of...
cards.pmNote: 組織設計的限制往往來自協作成本，而非人力預算。
cards.episode: Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity

cards.pattern: I don't think we should [X]. I think we should [Y]. That's hard, by the way.
cards.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
cards.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。
cards.why: 先給明確立場，再補一句 That's hard, by the way 承認執行難度。這種「立場堅定＋誠實承認困難」的組合，比只講立場更有說服力，也預先擋掉了「你講得太簡單」的質疑。
swaps: ...which is easier said than done
...and I'll be the first to say we haven't solved that
cards.pmNote: 主張與可行性分開陳述，是資深 PM 建立信任的方式。
cards.episode: Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity

cards.pattern: The risk you take if you [不做 X] is that [後果]
cards.quote: So the risk you take if you're not telling stories is that you will be forgotten. 100%. You will be forgotten.
cards.zh: 所以你不講故事的風險就是：你會被忘記。百分之百，你一定會被忘記。
cards.why: 把「你應該做 X」翻譯成「不做 X 的風險是什麼」，責任從說話者轉到聽者身上。後面把同一句短短重複一次，是英文口語裡加重語氣的固定手法，中文直譯會覺得囉唆，英文聽起來卻很有份量。
swaps: The downside of not doing this is...
What you're risking here is...
If we don't, what happens is...
cards.pmNote: 提案時講「不做的代價」通常比講「做的好處」更能推動決策——這就是 loss aversion 的實務用法。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

cards.pattern: If [對象] isn't [X], they're no longer [Y].
cards.quote: If your audience isn't wondering what you're about to say, they're no longer listening to you.
cards.zh: 如果台下的人沒有在好奇你下一句要講什麼，他們其實已經沒在聽你講話了。
cards.why: 用 if...they're no longer... 把「注意力」這種抽象東西變成一個可以當場檢查的條件。no longer 比 don't 多了時間感——他們本來在聽，是你把他們弄丟的，語氣更狠但不指責。
swaps: The moment they stop wondering, you've lost them.
If they're not asking themselves X, they've checked out.
cards.pmNote: 簡報設計的檢查點：每一頁都該讓聽眾產生下一個問題，而不是結束一個問題。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

cards.pattern: I assume, 100% of the time, that [對自己最不利的前提].
cards.quote: I assume all the time, 100% of the time, that no one wants to hear anything I have to say.
cards.zh: 我永遠都假設——百分之百的場合都假設——沒有人想聽我講任何話。
cards.why: 先自己承認最不利的前提，後面講的方法就不像自我感覺良好，而像是有備而來的專業判斷。這種「先把自己放到最低」的開場，在英文簡報裡是資深講者的標記。
swaps: My default assumption is that nobody's paying attention.
I start from the assumption that I have to earn their attention.
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

cards.pattern: The good news is [X]. The bad news is [同一件事的代價].
cards.quote: The good news is, you're just like everybody else. The bad news is, you're mediocre just like everybody else.
cards.zh: 好消息是，你跟大家一樣；壞消息是，你跟大家一樣平庸。
cards.why: good news / bad news 拿同一件事翻兩面，是英文簡報裡最順手的轉折。厲害的地方在於 bad news 重複了同一組字（just like everybody else），聽眾以為在聽安慰，結果被刺了一下。
swaps: The upside is X. The catch is X.
That's the comfortable part. Here's the uncomfortable part.
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

cards.pattern: To her credit, [她做了 X]（即使那不是我建議的）
cards.quote: And to her credit, she didn't put it in, and it still worked brilliantly.
cards.zh: 而且說句公道話，她確實沒放進去，結果一樣做得很漂亮。
cards.why: to her credit 是在講「她沒照我說的做」之前，先把功勞給對方的緩衝墊。英文商業對話裡要說別人做了不同選擇時，幾乎都會先墊這一句，台灣人多半直接跳到結果。
swaps: To be fair to her,...
In fairness,...
Credit where credit's due,...
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

cards.pattern: It's not because [直覺的解釋]. It's because [真正的原因].
cards.quote: It's not because my life is more interesting. It's because I have a better lens and I understand what to look for.
cards.zh: 不是因為我的生活變得比較精彩，是因為我的鏡頭變好了，我知道該找什麼。
cards.why: 先否定聽眾腦中最順的那個解釋，再給真正原因。這比直接講真因難反駁——因為你已經替對方把反例講過一次了。data review 上解釋數字變化時特別好用。
swaps: That's not down to X. That's down to Y.
The difference isn't X — it's Y.
cards.pmNote: 指標變好時，先排除「大環境變好」這種懶惰歸因，才是可信的成效敘述。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

cards.pattern: People say [常識], and it doesn't. What happens is [真實機制].
cards.quote: People say that time flies and it doesn't. What happens is it goes by unaccounted.
cards.zh: 大家都說時間過得很快，其實不是。真正發生的是：那些日子根本沒被記下來。
cards.why: What happens is... 是把「我不同意」包裝成「我來說明實際上發生什麼」的萬用開關，聽起來像在描述事實，不像在吵架。挑戰團隊共識時，這句比 I disagree 安全太多。
swaps: The usual explanation is X, but what's actually happening is Y.
That's the story we tell ourselves. The mechanism is actually...
cards.pmNote: 拆穿一個團隊共識時，重點不是否定它，而是給出更精確的機制描述。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

cards.pattern: …, which means we're not going to [X]. Instead, we're going to [Y].
cards.quote: speaking with adjacency, which means we're not going to match content to content. Instead, we're going to match theme, meaning or message.
cards.zh: 我把它叫做「鄰近敘事」，意思是我們不去對內容，而是去對主題、意義或訊息。
cards.why: 自創一個名詞後，馬上用 which means 拆解，再用 not... instead... 給出對照。這三步是把一個新概念塞進別人腦袋的標準流程，少任何一步都會被問「所以你到底在說什麼」。
swaps: ...— by which I mean we stop doing X and start doing Y.
The shift here is from X to Y.
cards.pmNote: 新框架要能被團隊複述，必須「命名 → 定義 → 對照舊做法」一次講完。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

cards.pattern: I'm going to disagree with [某人] a little bit.
cards.quote: So I'm going to disagree with Sedaris a little bit.
cards.zh: 這點我要跟 Sedaris 有一點不一樣的看法。
cards.why: 先宣告「我要小小反對一下」，a little bit 把力道預先調小，聽者有心理準備、對方面子也保住。台灣人不同意時常整段沉默或直接跳結論，缺的就是這句預告。
swaps: I'd push back on that slightly.
I see it a bit differently.
I'm going to take the other side on this one.
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

cards.pattern: What you're essentially saying is [把對方立場翻譯成更難辯護的版本].
cards.quote: If you don't say yes, what you're essentially saying is, I am so presumptuous that I understand what's on the other side of that door already.
cards.zh: 你如果不答應，你其實等於在說：我狂妄到已經知道那扇門後面是什麼了。
cards.why: 把對方的行為翻譯成一句他自己不會承認的話，是英文辯論裡最有力也最危險的一招。用 essentially 讓它聽起來像整理不像扣帽子——不加這個字就會變成人身攻擊。
swaps: The implicit assumption there is...
What that position commits us to is...
cards.pmNote: 把反對意見還原成它隱含的假設，比逐點反駁更能推進討論。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

cards.pattern: They don't want to [X]. They want to have [X 的完成式].
cards.quote: But that's really not actually what they want. They want to have been funny, because being funny means you must take a risk.
cards.zh: 但那其實不是他們真正想要的。他們想要的是「已經很好笑」這個結果，因為要好笑就得冒險。
cards.why: 用完成式 to have been 把「想要結果」和「願意付代價」切開——一個時態就完成整個洞察，中文得繞好幾句才講得清楚。這是英文裡罕見、但一學就能用的高階招式。
swaps: They want the outcome, not the process.
What they want is to have already done it.
cards.pmNote: 利害關係人說「我要創新」時，往往要的是創新的成果，不是創新的失敗率。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

cards.pattern: People don't [大範圍的問題]. They [精準的小問題].
cards.quote: Most people don't forget their talk. They forget the transitions in their talk.
cards.zh: 大部分人不是忘記整場講稿，是忘記段落之間怎麼接。
cards.why: 用「不是 A，是 A 裡面的某一小塊」把問題縮小到可以動手解決的尺寸，這是 PM 定義問題最常用的收斂句型。而且否定句在前，聽眾會先放下自己的誤判再接收新資訊。
swaps: It's not X that breaks — it's the seam between X and Y.
The failure isn't in A, it's at the handoff.
cards.pmNote: 問題定義得越窄越好解；「使用者流失」不是問題，「第三步驗證後流失」才是。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

cards.pattern: That's fine, but [代價].
cards.quote: That's fine, but you're going to need me the next time too. You're going to keep needing me because you're not really becoming a storyteller.
cards.zh: 這樣也行，但下次你還是得找我。你會一直需要我，因為你並沒有真的變成一個會說故事的人。
cards.why: That's fine 先接受對方的選擇，再講出後果——不否定人，只點出代價，讓對方自己重新決定。比 that's wrong 好用一百倍，是英文職場最實用的一句軟釘子。
swaps: That works, but it does mean...
Totally your call — just know that...
cards.pmNote: 擋需求時，把「不行」換成「可以，但代價是」，決策權還給對方，責任也一起還回去。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

cards.pattern: I often say [對現況的一句意象式評語].
cards.quote: I often say most communication in business is round white and flavorless, intentionally so, because a lot of people are afraid to stand out.
cards.zh: 我常說，商業場合的溝通大多是圓的、白的、沒有味道的——而且是故意的，因為大家都怕突出。
cards.why: 用三個感官形容詞（圓的、白的、沒味道）取代 boring，把抽象的批評變成畫面。I often say 則把這句包裝成他的招牌說法，聽眾會直接記住並轉述。
swaps: Most of it is beige.
It's all the same shade of safe.
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

cards.pattern: …is what I call the [自創的名字].
cards.quote: The way I learned how to pitch in business school, and I think the way most people did, is what I call the arrogant doctor.
cards.zh: 我在商學院學到的提案方式——我想大部分人學的也是——就是我說的「傲慢醫生」那一套。
cards.why: 用 what I call 幫一個現象命名，等於把討論的主導權拿到手上：之後大家只能用你的詞來討論這件事。中間插一句 and I think the way most people did，把個人經驗擴大成普遍現象。
swaps: I've started calling this the...
There's a pattern here I label...
cards.pmNote: 替一個反面模式命名，是策略敘事的第一步——Andy 整套方法都建立在「先命名舊遊戲」上。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

cards.pattern: Not to say [對方可能的反駁], but just [你的重點].
cards.quote: Not to say it's not better, but just this is the structure of it, and it kind of sets you up for bragging.
cards.zh: 我不是說它不好，我只是在講它的結構——這個結構會把你逼到一直自誇。
cards.why: 在對方開口反駁之前，先自己把反駁講一次，再把話題拉回自己的重點。這是英文口語裡最常見的 pre-empt，也是台灣人最常漏掉的一步（漏掉就會被打斷）。
swaps: I'm not saying X isn't true — my point is just that...
That's not a knock on X. The issue is the structure.
cards.pmNote: 預先處理反對（pre-mortem）不只在文件裡做，講話時也要一句一句做。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

cards.pattern: You'd think after [經驗] I'd have [答案] — and I don't.
cards.quote: You'd think, I've been doing this for 10 years, I'd have a very snappy definition of it there, and I don't.
cards.zh: 你會以為我做了十年，應該早就有一句俐落的定義——結果我沒有。
cards.why: 先講出聽眾心裡的期待（You'd think...），再自己承認落差。承認不知道反而顯得誠實又資深，因為你證明了你知道「好答案應該長什麼樣」。
swaps: I still don't have a clean answer for that, and I've been at it a while.
I wish I had a crisper way to put it.
cards.pmNote: 知識誠實：能說出「這題我還沒有好答案」的人，其他答案才可信。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

cards.pattern: In making it [A], you're losing [B].
cards.quote: And it's hard because in making it compact you're losing completeness.
cards.zh: 這很難，因為你把它壓得越精簡，就越不完整。
cards.why: 把取捨壓成一句 in doing X you're losing Y，不用先鋪陳一大段就能把 trade-off 講清楚。開頭那句 it's hard because 也很關鍵：先承認難，對方才不會以為你沒想過另一面。
swaps: Every bit of X we gain costs us Y.
The price of making it sharper is that it's less accurate.
cards.pmNote: 命名一定會犧牲精確度；策略敘事寧可被說「講得太滿」也不要模糊。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

cards.pattern: I would soften it a little bit — I wouldn't say [對方替你下的定論].
cards.quote: I would soften it a little bit... I wouldn't say I'm not a fan of creating category.
cards.zh: 我會講得軟一點——我不會說我不喜歡做品類（category）這件事。
cards.why: 主持人替他把立場講死了，他沒有否認也沒有接受，而是說「我會講得軟一點」再重講一次自己的版本。要修正別人替你下的定論，這是最不傷和氣的做法。
swaps: I'd put it less strongly than that.
That's close, but I'd phrase it differently.
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

cards.quote: Lenny, are you trying to get me in trouble?
cards.zh: Lenny，你是想害我惹麻煩喔？
cards.why: 被問到會得罪人的問題時，用一句玩笑先把問題的殺傷力拆掉，同時替自己爭取幾秒鐘思考，之後再認真回答。英文會議裡處理尖銳提問的第一動作，通常是幽默而不是防衛。
swaps: You're going to get me in trouble here.
Am I allowed to answer that honestly?
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

cards.quote: I mean, I almost see them as orthogonal.
cards.zh: 我幾乎覺得這兩件事是正交的（彼此不衝突、也不互相決定）。
cards.why: orthogonal 一個字就擋掉「所以你是反對 X 嗎」這種二選一的逼問——不是對立，只是不同軸。前面加 I almost 讓語氣不那麼絕對，是理工背景的人在英文會議裡很吃得開的用法。
swaps: Those are two different axes.
They're not in tension — they're just separate questions.
cards.pmNote: 討論策略時分清「互斥」與「正交」，能省掉大量無效爭論。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

cards.pattern: I'm really hesitant to [做對方要求的事]. What I'd say is these are [X], not [Y].
cards.quote: I am really hesitant to recommend any template. And what I'd say is these are principles for building it, not any prescribed formula.
cards.zh: 我真的很不願意推薦任何範本。我會說，這些是建構的原則，不是一套規定好的公式。
cards.why: hesitant 把拒絕包裝成「我個人的保留意見」，不是「你的要求不合理」。後半用 X not Y 提供替代品——拒絕時一定要留東西在對方手上，不然對方只會再問一次。
swaps: I'd rather not give you a template — here's the principle instead.
I'm wary of turning this into a checklist.
cards.pmNote: 擋需求的標準結構：拒絕 + 說明為什麼 + 給一個對方拿得走的東西。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

cards.pattern: Having [不完美的 X] is a million times more valuable than having [完美的 Y].
cards.quote: So having a shit draft is a million times more valuable than having all these great ideas. But it's also really painful.
cards.zh: 有一份爛草稿，比手上一堆很棒的點子有價值一百萬倍。但那個過程真的很痛。
cards.why: a million times more valuable 這種誇張比較在英文口語是常態、不是失禮；台灣人習慣保守講 is better，力道差很多。後面補一句 but it's also really painful，先認了痛，主張才不像空話。
swaps: A rough draft beats a great idea every time.
One bad version on paper is worth ten good ideas in the room.
cards.pmNote: 先做出可以被批評的東西，團隊才有東西可以收斂；空討論只會累積意見。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

cards.quote: I always ask, "What worked? What didn't work?"
cards.zh: 我每次都會問：哪裡有用？哪裡沒用？
cards.why: 固定兩問比 any feedback? 有效太多——問題越窄，回答越具體。而且拆成正反兩題，對方講完好話後幾乎一定會補上壞話，你就拿到真正想要的那一半。
swaps: What landed and what didn't?
What would you keep, what would you cut?
cards.pmNote: 回顧會議（retro）最小可用版本就是這兩題。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

cards.pattern: So put another way, [用白話重講一次].
cards.quote: So put another way, it defines what are the alternatives to what you do? How are you different?
cards.zh: 換個講法：它定義的是——你的替代方案有哪些？你跟它們差在哪？
cards.why: 講完一句比較抽象的定義，馬上 put another way 換白話重講，是英文簡報裡「怕你沒聽懂、但不讓你尷尬」的標準補位動作。比 do you understand? 高明太多。
swaps: In other words,...
Said differently,...
The practical version of that is...
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

cards.pattern: This is my long-winded way of [X], but this is the only way I know how to [Y].
cards.quote: This is my long-winded way of doing it, but this is the only way I know how to get positioning done.
cards.zh: 這是我比較囉唆的做法，但這是我唯一知道能把定位做出來的方法。
cards.why: 先自嘲講太長（long-winded），再用 the only way I know 把自嘲翻回權威。謙虛和自信各放一半，是英文裡講自己方法論時最好的比例。
swaps: That was the long version, but it's the version that works.
Sorry, that's a mouthful — but I don't know a shorter route.
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

cards.pattern: We can't just [某部門] cook up [X] and then heave it over the wall to everybody else.
cards.quote: We can't just have the marketing department sit down and cook up new positioning and then heave it over the wall to everybody else. It's a team sport.
cards.zh: 不能讓行銷部門自己關起門想一套新定位，然後往牆外一丟就沒事了。這是團隊運動。
cards.why: heave it over the wall（丟過牆）是英文職場批評跨部門甩鍋的固定意象，比 didn't communicate well 精準，又因為講的是行為不是人，不會變成點名。收尾 It's a team sport 給出正面替代。
swaps: throw it over the fence
hand it off and walk away
cards.pmNote: 定位／策略要能落地，marketing、product、sales、CS 必須在同一個房間裡產出，不是收文件。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

cards.pattern: I need to put a stake in the ground and say [暫定結論].
cards.quote: So I need to be able to put a stake in the ground and say, "I got to beat all that in order to win a deal."
cards.zh: 所以我得先釘一根樁，說：我必須打贏這些，才拿得到這筆生意。
cards.why: put a stake in the ground＝先立一個暫定結論好往下走，隱含「之後可以再改」。討論卡住時用它推進，比 let's decide 少壓力、比 let's discuss more 有進展。
swaps: Let's take a position on this for now.
I'll commit to an answer so we can move.
cards.pmNote: 定位第一步不是講自己多好，是先定義「我們要打敗誰」——包含 status quo（客戶什麼都不換）。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

cards.pattern: So it works like this. I start with [第一步]…
cards.quote: Yeah. So it works like this. I start with competitive alternatives.
cards.zh: 對，運作方式是這樣：我從「競爭替代方案」開始。
cards.why: So it works like this. 是講框架前的一句路標，聽眾一聽就知道接下來是有順序的清單，注意力會自動排隊。沒有這句，同樣的內容會被聽成一團。
swaps: Here's how it goes.
The sequence is this:
Let me walk you through it in order.
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

cards.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
cards.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。
cards.why: 先預告「我要講有爭議的話」，聽眾會坐正；後半又補「但我不覺得該有爭議」，等於同時立了場、也留了退路。這種一句話兩層的操作，是英文裡拋出強觀點的高階做法。
swaps: This might be an unpopular opinion, but I'd defend it.
Hot take, though I don't think it should be.
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

cards.quote: Yes and no. It depends on how you define that really.
cards.zh: 算是，也不算。要看你怎麼定義。
cards.why: 對方用一句話把你歸類時，Yes and no 既不吵架也不照單全收，接著把球丟回去要求先定義用詞，主導權就回來了。短、好背、幾乎萬用。
swaps: Sort of — depends what you mean by that.
Both, actually. Define X first.
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

cards.pattern: I think it is an utter waste of time to [X].
cards.quote: So I think it is an utter waste of time for marketing to build these stupid little one pager persona things.
cards.zh: 所以我覺得行銷花時間做那些一頁式的 persona 小卡，根本是浪費時間。
cards.why: utter waste of time 是重砲，但前面加 I think 就還在「意見」的範圍內。英文允許用很強的形容詞表達立場，中文直譯會顯得太衝——關鍵是那個 I think 的免責前綴。
swaps: I think that's effort we're throwing away.
Honestly, I'd cut that entirely.
cards.pmNote: B2B 真正要吃透的只有 champion 那一個 persona，其他人的卡片多半是自我安慰。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

cards.quote: I can then translate those capabilities into value, the so what for the customer.
cards.zh: 然後我把這些能力翻譯成價值，也就是對客戶來說的「所以呢」。
cards.why: the so what 被當名詞用（那個「所以呢」），一個詞就代表「這件事對客戶到底有什麼意義」。商業英語裡高頻，但台灣人幾乎不會主動講，聽到也常聽不出是名詞。
swaps: What's the so-what here?
the payoff for the customer
why they'd care
cards.pmNote: 功能 → 價值的轉換：每個 feature 後面都要問一次 so what，問不出來就別寫進簡報。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

cards.pattern: Better how? You've got to be able to articulate [模糊的字].
cards.quote: But better how? You got to be able to articulate better.
cards.zh: 但「比較好」是好在哪？你得有辦法把「比較好」講清楚。
cards.why: 兩個字的反問 Better how? 就逼對方把模糊形容詞拆開，比 Could you elaborate? 有力得多，而且完全不失禮。articulate 這個動詞（把某個感覺講成可說明的東西）也很值得學。
swaps: Faster how?
Better in what way, exactly?
Can you make that concrete?
cards.pmNote: 會議上遇到「更好／更快／更彈性」這類形容詞，先問 how，再談要不要做。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

cards.pattern: What matters is [真正的判準].
cards.quote: What matters is, does it resonate for your buyers?
cards.zh: 真正重要的是：它能不能打中你的買家？
cards.why: What matters is... 一句話把離題的討論拉回判準；後面直接接一個問句，等於順手給了對方檢查方式。開會發散時最省力的收斂工具。
swaps: The only question that matters here is...
What we should be judging this on is...
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

cards.pattern: The true test of whether [X] is working is [具體場景]. That's the real test.
cards.quote: The true test of whether the positioning's working is, if I'm sitting across from a qualified prospect and I tell the story, does the prospect get excited and want to buy something?
cards.zh: 定位有沒有效，真正的檢驗是：我坐在一個合格的潛在客戶對面把故事講完，他會不會眼睛一亮、想買東西？
cards.why: The true test of X is... 用來否定一堆假指標、只立一個真指標，是資深者在會議上收斂爭論的招牌句。而且他給的是一個場景不是一個數字——當沒有好指標時，這是誠實又有力的替代。
swaps: The real test is whether...
If you want one signal, it's this one:
cards.pmNote: 沒有好量測時，用一個可重現的場景當判準，好過硬湊一個假指標。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

cards.quote: And so here's where I think we go off the rails in marketing.
cards.zh: 而我覺得行銷就是在這一步脫軌的。
cards.why: go off the rails（脫軌）加上 here's where，精準指出是「哪一步」出錯，不是整件事全盤否定。批評一旦有座標，就不像人身攻擊；而且用 we 不用 you，責任共同承擔。
swaps: This is the step where it breaks down.
Here's where I think we lose the plot.
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

cards.pattern: At that stage, what you've got is a [X] thesis.
cards.quote: At that stage, what I think you've got is a positioning thesis... But it's just a thesis.
cards.zh: 在那個階段，你手上有的其實是一個「定位假設」……但它就只是個假設。
cards.why: 把還沒驗證的判斷叫 a thesis 而不是 a decision，一個字就標示了不確定的程度，之後改變主意也不算打臉。這是英文裡管理期望最省力的做法：先幫自己的結論標好熟度。
swaps: Treat that as a working hypothesis.
That's our current best guess, not a decision.
cards.pmNote: 早期定位刻意留鬆，讓市場把你拉向你沒想到的客群（April 的漁網比喻）。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

cards.pattern: A lot of [某群人] get tripped up because they're taking [不適用的建議].
cards.quote: A lot of early stage founders get tripped up as they're taking late stage sales advice.
cards.zh: 很多早期創辦人會踩坑，是因為他們套用了後期階段的銷售建議。
cards.why: get tripped up 把「做錯」講成「被絆倒」，責任落在建議來源、不落在人身上。要指出別人做錯又不想傷人時，這個被動意象非常好用。
swaps: That's where people usually come unstuck.
A lot of teams trip over this.
cards.pmNote: 引用最佳實務前先問：這是哪個階段、哪種規模的公司驗證出來的？
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.pattern: I try and stay away from [某個字], because it's hard to define.
cards.quote: I really try and stay away from better, because that's really hard to define, and better means something different to everyone.
cards.zh: 我盡量不用「比較好」這個字，因為它很難定義，而且每個人心中的「比較好」都不一樣。
cards.why: 把異議指向「用詞」而不是「人」，是會議上要擋掉含糊字眼時最安全的做法。I try and stay away from 又是個人習慣的講法，聽起來像分享而不是糾正。
swaps: I'd avoid the word X here.
I've stopped using that word because it doesn't survive follow-up questions.
cards.pmNote: 定位不要說「更好」，要說「不一樣」——better 會被要求定義、被要求量測，然後被拖一年。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.quote: The only thing that's different is the insight that the founder has on the market, which is a hard pill to swallow. And I know that's hard to hear too.
cards.zh: 唯一的差別是創辦人對市場的洞察——這顆藥很難吞。我也知道這話很難聽。
cards.why: 講完刺耳的結論，立刻承認「這很難接受」，等於先把對方的防衛心說出來。比 sorry to say this 高一階：它不是道歉，是同理，結論一點都沒有收回。
swaps: I know that's not what anyone wants to hear.
That one stings, and I don't have a nicer version of it.
cards.pmNote: 轉換率低通常不是通路問題，是「你講的事情不夠有趣」——這是最難承認的診斷。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.pattern: There's this thing in my head, I haven't fully validated it, but I'm going to share it with you.
cards.quote: There's this thing in my head and I haven't fully validated it but I'm going to share it with you.
cards.zh: 我腦中有個想法，還沒完全驗證過，但我還是講給你聽。
cards.why: 先幫想法標好成熟度（還沒驗證），就能大膽拋半成品又不用負全責。矽谷會議的常態，台灣人多半覺得「沒想清楚不要講」而錯過整個討論。
swaps: This is half-baked, but bear with me.
I don't have data on this yet — just a pattern I keep seeing.
I don't know, it's just a thought.
cards.pmNote: 把未驗證的觀察講出來，團隊才有機會幫你驗證；憋著就只是你一個人的直覺。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.pattern: Probably going to get slapped for saying this, by the way.
cards.quote: Probably going to get slapped for saying all this stuff, by the way.
cards.zh: 順帶一提，我講這些大概會被電。
cards.why: 講完不主流的建議補一句「我大概會被打」，先自嘲就把可能的攻擊接住了，聽起來也更敢講。by the way 放句尾，讓這句像隨口一提而不是討拍。
swaps: I'll probably get hate for this one.
This is going to be unpopular, I know.
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.quote: Yes, such a great point, Lenny. You absolutely need to time box this.
cards.zh: 對，這點問得很好。這件事你一定要設一個時間框。
cards.why: time box 當動詞用（把它框在一段時間內）是英文職場高頻詞。前面先給對方一句 such a great point——即使是同意，也要先把功勞遞出去，這是英文會議的潤滑劑。
swaps: Cap it at 90 days.
Put a hard end date on it.
cards.pmNote: 接服務型合約要以 90 天為單位切，到期重新 scope，才不會被綁死。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.pattern: If you [先讓步] just to [達成目標], you're negotiating with yourself.
cards.quote: So discounting just to get the deal over the line, you're negotiating with yourself.
cards.zh: 為了把案子推過線就先給折扣，那你是在跟自己談判。
cards.why: negotiating with yourself（跟自己談判）＝對方還沒開口你就先讓步。一句話就替一個常見錯誤命名，之後團隊會直接拿這個詞互相提醒——這就是好命名的價值。
swaps: Don't bid against yourself.
You're conceding before they've even asked.
cards.pmNote: 折扣要換東西（設計夥伴、兩年推薦背書），不能只換簽約。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.pattern: It's never a [對方以為的] problem. It's a [真正的] problem.
cards.quote: Everyone that I know says they have a bottom of funnel problem. It's never a bottom of funnel problem. It's a top of funnel problem.
cards.zh: 我認識的每個人都說自己是漏斗底部有問題。從來都不是漏斗底部的問題，是漏斗頂端的問題。
cards.why: 用 never/always 這種絕對句先推翻對方的自我診斷，再給新診斷。重複同一組名詞（bottom / top of funnel）讓對比極好記——換掉名詞就能套用到任何「大家都以為是 X 其實是 Y」。
swaps: It's rarely X. It's almost always Y.
People call it a X problem. It's a Y problem.
cards.pmNote: 轉換率的病灶通常在 qualification（找錯人講錯話），不在成交技巧。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.pattern: So which [選項] do you want to play? Let's just start there.
cards.quote: So which game do you want to play? Let's just start there.
cards.zh: 所以你想玩哪一種賽局？我們就從這裡開始。
cards.why: 不給答案，先丟一個二選一的框，再用 Let's just start there 把問題縮到只剩一步。帶人、帶會議都能用——對方一旦選了框，後面所有討論就有邊界。
swaps: Which of the two are we optimising for? Start there.
Pick a lane first, then we'll work the details.
cards.pmNote: 企業銷售與中小企業銷售是兩種 go-to-market，不能同時打——這是策略即取捨的典型。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.quote: Hopefully I'm not making this sound too daunting. I'm just really trying to lay out all the mistakes I've made.
cards.zh: 希望我沒有把這件事講得太嚇人。我只是想把我自己踩過的坑全部攤出來。
cards.why: 講完一長串壞消息，先照顧對方情緒（怕嚇到你），再把自己的失敗當成資訊來源。用「我犯的錯」而不是「你會犯的錯」，可信度最高、防衛心最低。
swaps: I don't want this to sound discouraging —
None of this is theory; it's a list of things I got wrong.
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.quote: It's so hard to give a founder hard feedback. Who wants to be the bearer of bad news?
cards.zh: 要給創辦人難聽的回饋真的很難。誰想當那個報壞消息的人？
cards.why: 用反問 Who wants to...? 把「沒人願意講真話」講成普遍人性，既替不肯給你壞消息的人開脫，也順便解釋了你為什麼收不到真實回饋。bearer of bad news 是固定說法，直接背起來。
swaps: Nobody wants to be the one to say it.
It's an awkward message to be the messenger for.
cards.pmNote: 客戶「很客氣」通常不是好訊號；要看行為（有沒有拉人進下一場會）而不是措辭。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.quote: In most cases, you can ask them, is that a hard line? Or how negotiable is that?
cards.zh: 大多數情況你都可以直接問：這是硬性規定嗎？還是有多少討論空間？
cards.why: 遇到「制度就是這樣」不要爭辯，先問這條線有多硬。how negotiable is that 把對抗改成資訊詢問，對方回答時就自己把彈性講出來了——這是談判裡最划算的一句話。
swaps: Is that fixed, or is there room?
How much flexibility do you have on that?
cards.pmNote: 面對採購／法務的規則，先確認硬度再決定要不要投入時間繞路。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.pattern: I fundamentally do not believe in [X], which is [為什麼重要的比喻].
cards.quote: I fundamentally do not believe in outsourcing the heartbeat of the organization, which is sales.
cards.zh: 我從根本上不相信可以把一家公司的心跳外包出去——而銷售就是心跳。
cards.why: I fundamentally do not believe in... 講的是原則不是偏好，語氣很重但不針對任何人。後面接一個比喻（the heartbeat of the organization）當理由，讓強硬立場有畫面可以站。
swaps: I don't think you can delegate that away.
That's not something a company should hand off.
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.pattern: I always assume [對方] knows way more than I do.
cards.quote: I always assume that the buyer I'm speaking to is highly educated and knows way more than I do.
cards.zh: 我永遠假設坐在對面的買家很懂，而且懂的比我多很多。
cards.why: 先把對方設定成比自己懂，是英文商業對話裡低姿態高效率的開場。knows way more than I do 的那個 way（加強語氣的「多很多」）讓語氣自然、不做作，這個小字台灣人很少用。
swaps: I assume they've already done the homework.
I go in assuming they're ahead of me on this.
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.pattern: We have a lot to learn. Can we gain your insight into how this problem is manifesting on your side?
cards.quote: Hey, I'm an early stage startup. We have a lot to learn. Can we kind of gain your insight into how this problem is manifesting on your side?
cards.zh: 嗨，我們是很早期的新創，還有很多要學。能不能請教你，這個問題在你們那邊是怎麼呈現的？
cards.why: 先自曝短處再請教，對方就從「被推銷」變成「被請教」，回饋才會誠實。how this problem is manifesting on your side 又把問題講得很中性——不是預設你有病，是問症狀長什麼樣。
swaps: We're still figuring this out — how does it show up for you?
I'd love your read on how this plays out on your side.
cards.pmNote: 早期銷售不是為了成交，是為了拿到 insight，先取得賣的資格（earn the right to sell）。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.pattern: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this [N] step framework.
cards.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
cards.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。
cards.why: Let me just try to 三個字把「我要總結」變成「我試試看」，就算整理錯了對方也只會補充不會糾正你。英文會議想確認自己有沒有聽懂，這是最安全的入口。
swaps: Let me play that back to you.
So if I've got this right, it's...
Let me see if I can summarise that.
cards.pmNote: 會議收斂的第一步是複述，複述能同時檢查理解與逼出隱含分歧。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

cards.quote: I'm taking us off track, but I want to go a little deeper with this.
cards.zh: 我知道這樣會離題，但我想在這裡多挖一點。
cards.why: 自己先承認「我要岔題了」，聽起來就不像失控而像刻意選擇，別人也不會急著把你拉回去。這是英文會議裡爭取時間的合法手續。
swaps: Slight detour, but —
Can I take us sideways for a second?
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

cards.pattern: Let me take us back on track and let's talk about [主軸].
cards.quote: So let me take us back on track and let's talk about just the high level framework here.
cards.zh: 我們把話題拉回來，來談一下這個框架的高層次架構。
cards.why: take us back on track 用 us 不用 you，收線的同時把責任分攤掉，不會像在指責誰講太多。這是主持會議最常需要、台灣人卻最不敢做的動作。
swaps: Let's bring it back to...
Coming back to the main thread —
Parking that, let's return to...
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

cards.pattern: So to quickly recap a few of the key things I've written down as we're talking.
cards.quote: So to quickly recap a few of the key things that I've written down as we're talking.
cards.zh: 我快速把剛剛邊聽邊記下來的幾個重點整理一下。
cards.why: 加上 that I've written down as we're talking，等於證明你全程有在聽、而且只挑重點——比乾巴巴的 to recap 多了可信度與參與感。
swaps: Quick recap of what I've got so far:
Let me read back the key points.
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.pattern: Backing up a little bit — we jumped right in. I'm curious how you'd even describe [基本概念].
cards.quote: Backing up a little bit, we jumped right in. I'm curious how you even describe positioning, what the heck is positioning?
cards.zh: 稍微倒回去一下——我們一開始就直接跳進來了。我很好奇你會怎麼定義「定位」這件事？
cards.why: 問一個很基本的問題之前，先說 we jumped right in（是我們跳太快，不是我沒跟上），把「不懂」的責任轉成流程問題。要在英文會議裡問笨問題，這是最漂亮的包裝。
swaps: Can we rewind a step?
Before we go further, can we define terms?
cards.pmNote: 對齊（alignment）常常敗在沒人敢問「我們講的是同一個東西嗎」。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

cards.pattern: I want to talk about [新主題], but just to close the loop on that…
cards.quote: I want to talk about public speaking skills, but just to close the loop on that.
cards.zh: 我想聊聊公開演講的技巧，不過在那之前先把剛剛那題收尾。
cards.why: close the loop（把迴圈關起來）是英文職場最常用的收尾動詞片語。先預告下一個主題再回頭補完上一題，聽者知道你沒忘、也知道還要多久。
swaps: Before we move on, let me close this out.
One last thing on that, then we'll move on.
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

cards.pattern: Just to calibrate — what [規模／範圍] are we talking about here?
cards.quote: Just for folks that are listening, just to calibrate what size of company you're talking about selling to here.
cards.zh: 為了讓聽的人有個基準——你剛剛講的是賣給多大規模的公司？
cards.why: calibrate（校準）把「你講的到底適用在哪」問得很專業，而且不是質疑對方，是幫大家對準刻度。加一句 for folks that are listening，等於替全場問，自己不用承認沒聽懂。
swaps: Just so we're calibrated on scale —
What size are we talking about, roughly?
cards.pmNote: 任何建議都該附上適用條件（階段、規模、市場），否則就是無法執行的口號。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

cards.quote: What else can people do to become better storytellers in business? I know this is a big question, but let's see where it goes.
cards.zh: 在商業場合還可以怎麼把故事講得更好？我知道這題很大，但我們就看看會聊到哪。
cards.why: 先承認問題太大，等於免除對方「必須給完整答案」的壓力，對方反而會放鬆講出好東西。let's see where it goes 把一個模糊的問題變成一場共同探索。
swaps: That's a huge question — take it wherever you want.
Big one, but I'll throw it out anyway.
cards.pmNote: 1:1 帶人時，開放式大問題要先鬆綁期待，對方才敢想。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

cards.quote: I'd maybe put it a little bit differently.
cards.zh: 我可能會換一個講法。
cards.why: 整句沒有一個否定詞，卻已經把對方的說法擋掉了。maybe + a little bit 是雙重緩衝，讓「我不同意」聽起來像「我來補一個角度」，是英文會議裡最安全的反對開場。
swaps: I'd frame it slightly differently
Let me put that another way
cards.pmNote: 接住別人的總結再微調，比直接推翻更容易保住後續的合作關係。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

cards.quote: Yeah, it's definitely a huge part of it. There's a couple of things that I noticed get in the way.
cards.zh: 對，那絕對是很大一塊。不過我有注意到幾件事會卡住。
cards.why: 先給一個「不是敷衍」的實質認可（definitely a huge part），再用 get in the way 把異議說成「有東西擋路」而不是「你錯了」。台灣人習慣的 but 在這裡被換成一個新句子，火藥味整個降下來。
swaps: That's a big piece of it. What I'd add is...
Agreed on that. A couple of things complicate it though
cards.pmNote: 先確認共識再談分歧，是跨部門對齊時省下最多來回的順序。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

cards.pattern: The other thing that's a little bit different about what you said is [差異].
cards.quote: The other thing that's a little bit different about what you said is that emotions do need to be felt.
cards.zh: 還有一點跟你剛剛講的稍微不一樣，就是情緒是真的需要被感受到的。
cards.why: 把「你錯了」重寫成「這裡有個 different」，差異變成一個中性的名詞，不指向任何人的對錯。a little bit 再把差距縮小，聽起來像微調而不是推翻。
swaps: Where I'd diverge slightly is...
One nuance I'd add to that is...
cards.pmNote: 把分歧描述成「差異」而非「錯誤」，是評審別人方案時最不傷關係的說法。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

cards.pattern: Clearly, [反證], so I'm not buying it.
cards.quote: Clearly, you're not so scared that you can't do anything, so I'm not buying it. I don't do it quite like that, I do it with a lot more love than that.
cards.zh: 很明顯你沒有害怕到什麼都做不了，所以這個說法我不買單。我實際上不會講得這麼硬，我會帶更多善意。
cards.why: I'm not buying it 是用「消費者拒買」的比喻拒絕一個說法，比 that's not true 輕，因為否定的是「說詞」不是「人」。後半句是母語者自我標註語氣的習慣——先講重話，再說明真實情境下我會更溫和。
swaps: I'm not sure I buy that
That doesn't quite square with what I'm seeing
cards.pmNote: 用對方自己的行為當反證，比用你的判斷當反證更難反駁。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

cards.quote: I'm like, "Oh, cool. Tell me what I'm missing."
cards.zh: 我會說：「好啊，跟我說我漏掉了什麼。」
cards.why: 被罵之後的標準反應句。Tell me what I'm missing 假設「錯的是我的視野不是我的能力」，一句話把對抗轉成資訊交換，而且逼對方講具體的東西而不是情緒。
swaps: Walk me through what you're seeing
What am I not seeing here?
cards.pmNote: 接住批評的第一句話決定對方後面願不願意講真話。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

cards.quote: Give me a day and I'll come back to you.
cards.zh: 給我一天，我再回來找你談。
cards.why: 不是拒絕、也不是硬撐，而是把「我現在接不住」轉成一個有期限的承諾。come back to you 隱含「這件事我認領了」，是英文職場最常見的緩衝兼認領句。
swaps: Let me sit with that and get back to you tomorrow
Can I take a day on this?
cards.pmNote: 當場答不出來時給出時間點，比硬給一個爛答案更能保住信任。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

cards.pattern: You keep using the word [X], and I just want to [反轉].
cards.quote: You keep using the word advice, and I just want to, so for anybody who's listening, do not take my advice.
cards.zh: 你一直在用「建議」這個詞，我想借這個機會講一句：不要照我的建議做。
cards.why: 把攻擊點放在「用詞」而不是「人」，是英文裡最安全的挑戰法。You keep using the word X 同時做了兩件事：指出對方的預設，以及取得重新定義的發言權。
swaps: We keep saying 'growth' — can we define what we mean?
I notice we keep calling this a bug
cards.pmNote: 團隊反覆使用的詞，往往藏著沒對齊的假設；拆詞就是拆假設。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

cards.pattern: I definitely would not [對方的說法]. What I would say that's a close cousin to that is [你的說法].
cards.quote: I definitely would not want anyone to feel joy. What I would say that's a close cousin to that is that enjoyment is such an important tool for productivity.
cards.zh: 我絕對不會要求任何人去感受喜悅。跟那個很接近、但我會這樣說的是：享受是生產力非常重要的工具。
cards.why: a close cousin to that 是把自己的立場「掛」在對方的問題旁邊，既不接受錯誤前提、也不讓對方覺得問題被打槍。台灣人碰到被誤解時常只會 no, that's not what I meant，這句是專業版。
swaps: That's not quite it, but here's the neighboring idea
The version of that I'd actually defend is...
cards.pmNote: 被問到一個前提錯誤的問題時，重新定義問題比硬答更有價值。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

cards.pattern: Love him or hate him, [引用有爭議的人].
cards.quote: Another one, love him or hate him, one of the things that Elon Musk has said that I found it very valuable in my time.
cards.zh: 還有一個，不管你喜不喜歡他啦——馬斯克講過一句話，我覺得對我很受用。
cards.why: love him or hate him 是預先處理反對（pre-empt）：在對方跳出來說「引用這個人？」之前，先承認爭議，把焦點鎖回內容。一句四個字省掉一整段離題。
swaps: Whatever you think of the company, they got this right
Setting aside the controversy for a second
cards.pmNote: 引用有爭議的來源時先承認爭議，能避免討論被身分之爭綁架。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

cards.pattern: What I'm hearing is [你的理解].
cards.quote: What I'm hearing is the core issues, we're not able to feel our emotion.
cards.zh: 我聽到的重點是：核心問題在於我們沒辦法真的感受到自己的情緒。
cards.why: What I'm hearing is 把「我沒聽懂」變成「我來覆述確認」，聽起來像在整理不像在求救——對英文非母語者是保命句。而且覆述錯了對方會直接更正，資訊反而更完整。
swaps: So if I'm following you correctly...
Let me play that back to you
cards.pmNote: 把聽到的內容覆述一次，是會議上成本最低的對齊動作。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

cards.pattern: The way I think about this is [比喻].
cards.quote: The way I think about this is that emotions are like a tube, let's say, and there's water moving through the tube.
cards.zh: 我自己是這樣想這件事的：情緒像一根管子，裡面有水在流。
cards.why: The way I think about this is 先聲明「這是我的思考模型」，比 This is 更容易被接受；後面接 let's say 又進一步標示這只是暫時的比喻。兩層 hedge 讓比喻不用背負「必須正確」的壓力。
swaps: The mental model I use is...
Here's the analogy I keep coming back to
cards.pmNote: 給抽象問題一個具體比喻，是策略溝通裡最省時的對齊工具。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

cards.pattern: We start our meetings with: what are you scared to say?
cards.quote: We start all of our meetings with what are you scared to say in our business?
cards.zh: 我們每場會議都從這個問題開始：在這家公司裡，你不敢講的是什麼？
cards.why: 把「請大家踴躍發言」換成一個具體到讓人不好閃躲的問題。scared to say 直接指名情緒門檻，比 any concerns? 有效十倍——後者的標準答案永遠是沉默。
swaps: What's the thing nobody wants to say out loud?
What are we all avoiding here?
cards.pmNote: 會議開場的問題設計，決定了那場會能不能碰到真問題。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

cards.pattern: If it's helpful, let me break that down a little bit.
cards.quote: And if it's helpful, let me break down the question a little bit.
cards.zh: 如果有幫助的話，我把這個問題拆開來講一下。
cards.why: if it's helpful 是英文裡最禮貌的「取得繼續講的許可」，把主導權形式上交給對方，實際上你已經接著講了。比 Let me explain 少了說教感。
swaps: If it's useful, I can unpack that
Happy to go deeper if that helps
cards.pmNote: 在會議上展開細節前先確認需求，可以避免把時間花在沒人要的深度上。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.pattern: I purposely chose the word [X] because [X] does not mean [Y], and that's a really important distinction.
cards.quote: So I purposely chose the word complicit because complicit does not mean responsible, and that's a really important distinction.
cards.zh: 我是刻意選「共謀」這個詞的，因為共謀不等於負責，這個區別非常重要。
cards.why: 先宣告「我是刻意選這個字的」，等於預先擋掉「你用詞太重」的反彈，再用 X does not mean Y 精準劃界。這是把定義權拿在手上的高階做法。
swaps: I use 'X' deliberately — it's not the same as 'Y'
The word matters here: X, not Y
cards.pmNote: 問題定義用哪個字，會決定團隊往哪個方向找解法。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.quote: So let's just pause, Lenny.
cards.zh: 我們先暫停一下。
cards.why: 用 let's（我們）而不是 you，把打斷包裝成共同行動，對方就不會覺得被叫停。加上名字更軟——這是英文裡搶回發言權而不失禮的標準做法。
swaps: Can we pause there for a second?
Let me stop us right there
cards.pmNote: 會議失焦時，打斷的時機比打斷的措辭更重要。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.quote: Does that resonate at all?
cards.zh: 這樣講有打中什麼嗎？
cards.why: resonate 問的是「有沒有共鳴」而不是「對不對」，對方就不必為了保住面子而說 yes。at all 又把門檻降到最低，連「有一點點」都算數，很難尷尬地回答不出來。
swaps: Does any of that land?
Is that anywhere close?
cards.pmNote: 驗證你的假設時，問「有沒有共鳴」比問「我說得對嗎」拿到的訊號更真。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.pattern: Let's take a step back. If I can reflect back your original question, [重述].
cards.quote: So let's take a step back. The fear is, if I can reflect back to your original question, the fear is if I go there, I don't know what's going to happen as a consequence of that.
cards.zh: 我們退一步看。如果我把你原本的問題回映給你，那個恐懼是：如果我真的往下探，我不知道會發生什麼後果。
cards.why: reflect back 是教練用語，意思是「把你的話整理後還給你」。它跟 summarize 的差別在於它承認這是「我的版本」，所以對方可以修正——是英文裡收斂發散討論最不霸道的方式。
swaps: Let me reflect that back to you
Zooming out for a second, the underlying question is...
cards.pmNote: 把散開的討論收回原始問題，是主持人最該練的一招。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.quote: Thank you for giving me more of that answer.
cards.zh: 謝謝你願意把那個答案講得更完整。
cards.why: 肯定的不是內容而是「你多說了一點」這個行為。當對方剛剛講了一段有點難堪的實話，這句是最精準的獎勵——它鼓勵的是坦白本身。
swaps: I appreciate you going there
Thank you for being that honest about it
cards.pmNote: 有人在會議上說出不好聽的真話時，公開謝他，下次才還會有人講。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.pattern: The good news / bad news is [事實].
cards.quote: And the good news bad news is that's true. That is absolutely true.
cards.zh: 好消息也是壞消息：那是真的。千真萬確。
cards.why: 把壞消息和好消息綁成同一個東西，聽者的防衛就先卸下一半。這比 unfortunately 高明，因為它沒有替對方決定該不該難過。
swaps: The good news and the bad news are the same thing
There's an upside and a downside to that, and they're identical
cards.pmNote: 報壞消息時同時指出它帶來的資訊價值，比純道歉更能推進決策。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.quote: Say more.
cards.zh: 多說一點。
cards.why: 兩個字，沒有問號，也沒有指定方向——對方會自己挑最想講的往下講。台灣人習慣問 Can you give me an example，那會把對方導到你想要的方向；Say more 不會。
swaps: Tell me more about that
Keep going
cards.pmNote: 1:1 時最好用的一句話：什麼都不引導，訊號最乾淨。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.pattern: I want to offer a different possibility. What if [替代方案]?
cards.quote: Now, I want to offer a different potential. What if what drove you was not quieting that voice, but what drove you was, oh, this is just fun?
cards.zh: 我想提供另一種可能。如果驅動你的不是想壓掉那個聲音，而是「這件事就是好玩」呢？
cards.why: offer 這個動詞是關鍵：把不同意見說成「我遞一個東西給你，你可以不拿」。搭配 What if 假設句，整段話沒有一個字在否定對方，但方向已經被換掉了。
swaps: Can I offer another way to look at it?
Here's an alternative read — what if...?
cards.pmNote: 提替代方案時用「提供」而非「反對」的框架，決策者比較不會進防衛狀態。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.quote: Now, to be clear, this is hard for me. I think it's hard for everybody.
cards.zh: 先講清楚，這件事對我來說也很難。我覺得對每個人都很難。
cards.why: 給完建議後補一句「我自己也做不好」，把 advice 從高處拉平。to be clear 在這裡不是澄清事實，而是澄清姿態——是英文裡拆掉權威感的常用開關。
swaps: For the record, I struggle with this too
I'm not saying I've got this figured out
cards.pmNote: 給建議時承認自己也在掙扎，對方採納的機率反而更高。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.pattern: Far be it from me to disagree with [權威], but I think he's wrong.
cards.quote: So far be it from me to disagree with Mike Tyson, but I think he's wrong.
cards.zh: 我哪敢跟泰森唱反調——但我覺得他錯了。
cards.why: Far be it from me to 是誇張的自貶，用來替後面的硬話買保險，語氣還帶點幽默。這種「先跪再打」的結構台灣人幾乎不會用，但在英文會議裡挑戰資深者非常好用。
swaps: Who am I to argue with X, but...
With all due respect to X, I'd push back
cards.pmNote: 挑戰高階或名人的觀點時，先明確承認地位差，反而讓內容被聽見。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.quote: So is that my legacy? Yeah, and maybe there's some ego implicit in that, but can I go on for just a bit on this?
cards.zh: 所以那算是我的 legacy 嗎？算吧，裡面可能也有一點自我——不過我可以再多講一下嗎？
cards.why: 自己主動要求延長發言時間，而且先承認「這段可能有點自戀」。just a bit 界定範圍，讓主持人容易點頭。英文會議裡想多講一段而不被打斷，這是最有效的一句。
swaps: Can I take one more minute on this?
Mind if I keep going for a beat?
cards.pmNote: 要多要一點時間就明講並給出界線，比偷偷超時更容易被允許。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.pattern: A year ago, I thought [舊看法]. We're clearly not. This is different.
cards.quote: A year ago, I thought we were going through a similar kind of transition. We're clearly not. This is different.
cards.zh: 一年前我以為我們正在經歷類似的轉型。顯然不是。這次不一樣。
cards.why: 收回立場的教科書結構：時間標記 + 舊看法 + 一句話撤回 + 新判斷。三個短句沒有一句在解釋或道歉，收得乾淨俐落，這正是英文裡改變想法該有的節奏。
swaps: I used to think X. I've changed my mind
Six months ago I'd have argued the opposite
cards.pmNote: 公開更新自己的判斷並標上時間點，是 strong opinions, loosely held 的實作方式。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.pattern: What I come back to — and I could be wrong — is [立場].
cards.quote: Now, what I come back to, and I could be wrong, but what I come back to is we're talking through a medium, a mediated experience.
cards.zh: 我一直會回到的一點——我也可能是錯的——就是：我們是透過一個媒介在對話，一種被中介過的經驗。
cards.why: and I could be wrong 插在句子中間而不是句尾，是母語者的習慣：先聲明不確定，再把立場講完，聽者就不會把它當成事後補救。what I come back to 又暗示這是反覆想過的結論，不是隨口。
swaps: I keep landing on — and I may be wrong here —
My current read, subject to change, is...
cards.pmNote: 把「不確定」放在主張前面，比放在後面更像自信而不是心虛。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.pattern: Here's what I have a problem with. First of all, [X] is a very helpful thing.
cards.quote: Here's what I have a problem with. First of all, having a growth mindset is a very, very helpful thing.
cards.zh: 我要說的是我對它的哪一點有意見。首先，擁有成長心態本身是非常非常有幫助的事。
cards.why: 先宣告「我有意見」再立刻讓步一大步，聽者的防衛值會被這個順序打亂。Here's what I have a problem with 也把批評範圍限縮成一個點，不會被理解成全盤否定。
swaps: My issue isn't with X itself — it's with how it gets used
Let me be precise about what I object to
cards.pmNote: 反對一個廣受認同的概念時，先承認它的價值再限縮攻擊面。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.pattern: So, put succinctly, [一句話結論].
cards.quote: So put succinctly, stay attached to the growth and hold mindset a little loosely.
cards.zh: 簡單講就是：緊抓成長，心態就抓鬆一點。
cards.why: 講了一大段之後用 put succinctly 明確標記「以下是懶人包」，聽的人會自動提高注意力。這個標記詞比 in summary 更口語、更有份量。
swaps: To put it simply
If I had to boil it down to one line
cards.pmNote: 任何長論述最後都該留一句能被別人轉述的版本，不然對齊只到你為止。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.pattern: Okay, I'm seeing something happen here. Every time we [情境], [模式].
cards.quote: Okay, guys, I'm seeing something happen here. Every time we get close to talking about something that's really painful, somebody makes a joke and all the energy disappears.
cards.zh: 好，我看到一個現象。每次我們快要談到真正痛的事情，就會有人開個玩笑，然後所有能量就消失了。
cards.why: 描述行為模式（every time... somebody...）而不指名任何人，讓整組人一起面對同一面鏡子。I'm seeing 又標明這只是我的觀察，不是判決。這是處理團隊動力最安全也最有效的句型。
swaps: I want to name a pattern I'm noticing
This is the third time we've done this — can we look at it?
cards.pmNote: 點名「模式」而不是點名「人」，是跨團隊卡關時唯一不會引爆的說法。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.pattern: I would argue that the more [X] you have, the more [Y] you have.
cards.quote: I would argue that the more power you have, the more moral responsibility you have to actually pause and figure out what it is that you're doing.
cards.zh: 我會主張：你握有的權力越大，你就越有道德責任停下來，搞清楚自己在做什麼。
cards.why: I would argue that 把主張標記成「經過論證的立場」而不是感想，聽者會準備接收理由。後面的 the more X, the more Y 是英文裡最好記的說理骨架，換內容就能重用。
swaps: My argument would be that...
The case I'd make is...
cards.pmNote: 資源與責任成正比的論證，是爭取或推辭跨組任務時的通用槓桿。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.pattern: How can you [期待 X] if you can't tolerate [X 的必然後果]?
cards.quote: How can you hire people whom you expect to make decisions without running them through you if you can't tolerate them making a decision that you disagree with?
cards.zh: 如果你受不了他們做出你不同意的決定，你怎麼可能招到那種不需要事事回報你就能決策的人？
cards.why: 把對方的抱怨和他自己的行為擺進同一個句子，矛盾自己浮出來，你一個字都不用評論。這種 Socratic 反問是英文裡最有力也最不失禮的挑戰方式。
swaps: You can't ask for X and also refuse Y
Those two things can't both be true — which one do you want?
cards.pmNote: 授權失敗多半不是人不行，是主管無法忍受不同意的決定。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.pattern: One thing to ask yourself is: what draws me to this in the first place?
cards.quote: One of the things to ask oneself is what draws me to this position in the first place?
cards.zh: 有個可以問自己的問題是：當初到底是什麼把我吸引到這個位置的？
cards.why: in the first place 是英文裡把時間軸拉回起點的關鍵詞組，逼人回頭看最初的動機。用 one of the things to ask oneself 包裝，等於把問題輕輕放在桌上，不指定誰要撿。
swaps: What made you take this on originally?
What was the appeal at the start?
cards.pmNote: 抱怨環境之前先問自己為何選擇它，能區分「該修的問題」和「該離開的局」。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

cards.quote: If this job were open, I'd like to be considered for it.
cards.zh: 如果這個職位有空缺，我希望能被列入考慮。
cards.why: 用假設語氣（were / I'd）把野心講出來，但不逼對方現在回應，所以被拒絕也不傷。be considered for 是被動式的關鍵：你要的是「進入名單」，不是「給我」——這個分寸台灣人很難自己抓出來。
swaps: I'd love to be in the mix if that ever opens up
Keep me in mind for that role
cards.pmNote: 沒說出口的職涯意願，主管永遠不會替你猜到。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

cards.pattern: The thing a lot of [對象] don't realize is that you can love something to death.
cards.quote: The thing that I think a lot of large companies don't realize is that you can love something to death.
cards.zh: 很多大公司沒意識到的一件事是：你可以把一個東西「愛到死」。
cards.why: love something to death 用一個反直覺的搭配，一句話擋掉「多給資源、多開會、多關注」的好意。要拒絕善意的介入時，這比 please leave us alone 有效得多。
swaps: Too much attention can kill a new product
We'd rather have less oversight and more room
cards.pmNote: 早期產品最需要的不是資源，是不被檢視的空間。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

cards.pattern: By the way, [殘酷數據]. So half of you are going to [後果]. Do you have the resilience to do that?
cards.quote: By the way, a very, very successful company for a new set of products has a 50% hit rate. So half of you are going to come back in a year and have a different job. Do you have the resilience to do that?
cards.zh: 順帶一提，一家非常成功的公司做新產品的成功率大概是五成。所以你們有一半的人一年後會換一份工作。你們有那個韌性嗎？
cards.why: 用 By the way 淡化開場，再丟出殘酷數字，最後用一個問題把選擇權交回去。這三拍是英文裡「期望管理」的完整結構：不恐嚇、不美化、要求對方自己決定。
swaps: Just so you go in with eyes open, the base rate is...
Half of these bets won't survive the year — are you okay with that?
cards.pmNote: 先講清楚失敗率再讓人選，事後就不必處理被騙的感覺。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

cards.pattern: If you had to write a spec for your career, what's in there? What are your milestones?
cards.quote: But if I said you had to write a spec for your career, what's in there? What are your milestones? What are the skills?
cards.zh: 如果我要你替自己的職涯寫一份 spec，裡面會有什麼？你的里程碑是什麼？需要哪些技能？
cards.why: 把對方每天在用的專業框架（spec）反過來套在他自己身上，一秒讓抽象的職涯焦慮變成可填的欄位。這種「借用對方的語言」是教練式提問最強的一招。
swaps: What would the roadmap for your own career look like?
If your career were a product, what's the north star metric?
cards.pmNote: 會替產品訂目標的人，常常忘了替自己訂；1:1 時借用他的框架最有效。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

cards.pattern: I noticed that you never [行為] when we [情境].
cards.quote: I asked her once, I said, "I noticed that you never answer questions when we do these presentations."
cards.zh: 我有一次問她：「我注意到，我們在做這些簡報的時候，你從來不回答問題。」
cards.why: I noticed 只陳述可觀察的行為，不含評價與推論，對方沒有東西可以否認，只能解釋。這是 radical candor 在句型層級的落實，比 You should speak up more 安全太多。
swaps: I've noticed a pattern in meetings
Something I've observed a few times now
cards.pmNote: 回饋只講觀察到的行為，對方才會告訴你背後真正的原因。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

cards.pattern: What if I called it [重新命名]? What if I called it [重新命名]?
cards.quote: What if I called it educating your manager about all the great work your team has been doing? What if I called it helping people see why your team should get more resources?
cards.zh: 如果我把它叫做「讓主管了解你的團隊做了哪些很棒的事」呢？如果我把它叫做「幫大家看見為什麼你的團隊該拿到更多資源」呢？
cards.why: 重新命名一件事，就重新分配了它的道德重量：self-promotion 變成 educating，主角從「我」換成「團隊」。用 What if I called it 而不是直接改名，等於邀請對方一起換框，抗拒最小。
swaps: What if we called it visibility instead of self-promotion?
Try thinking of it as advocating for your team
cards.pmNote: 自評與績效簡報寫的是團隊拿資源的理由，不是個人邀功。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

cards.quote: And I said, "Well, then why do you put yourself in his category instead of mine?"
cards.zh: 我就說：「那你為什麼把自己歸到他那一類，而不是我這一類？」
cards.why: 先讓對方承認一個他認同的反例，再問他為何不把自己放進去。整段沒有安慰、沒有說教，用一個問題就拆掉自我設限，是教練式提問的高階示範。
swaps: Why assume you'd be the bad version of that?
What makes you the exception in the wrong direction?
cards.pmNote: 帶人時找到對方自己認同的正面樣本，比你講一百句鼓勵有用。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

cards.pattern: I think we do a disservice when we say [說法], because it's a skill like any other.
cards.quote: I think we do a disservice when we say we're not good at speaking up because it's a skill like any other.
cards.zh: 我覺得我們說自己「不擅長發言」是在害自己，因為那跟其他技能沒有兩樣。
cards.why: do a disservice 指的是「好意造成的傷害」，用來反駁一個大家習以為常的自我開脫，語氣是心疼不是責備。把「個性」改講成 skill，責任就從天生變成可練。
swaps: Calling it a personality trait lets us off the hook
That's a skill, not a fixed trait
cards.pmNote: 把「我就是這種人」翻譯成「這是一項還沒練的技能」，才有帶人的著力點。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

cards.quote: So especially when you're meeting with a new engineering team for the first time, actually ask them, what is one thing I can do to help you this week?
cards.zh: 尤其是第一次跟新的工程團隊碰面時，真的去問他們：這禮拜我可以幫上哪一件事？
cards.why: one thing 和 this week 兩個限制詞是精髓：把一個容易被敷衍的客套問句，變成一個小到不能拒絕的具體請求。沒有這兩個限制，答案永遠是 nothing, we're good。
swaps: What's one thing I could take off your plate this week?
Give me one small thing I can help with
cards.pmNote: 新人建立信任最快的方式是先付出一次可交付的小忙。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

cards.pattern: I would like to carve [X%] of my time for [目的], and I'm happy to do this work [Y%] of the time.
cards.quote: Okay. I would like to carve 20% of my time listening and I'm happy to do this work 80% of the time.
cards.zh: 好，我想切出兩成的時間去聽，另外八成的時間我很樂意投入手上的工作。
cards.why: carve 是「切出一塊」，比 spend 更有守住邊界的意味。先講你要拿走的比例，再立刻交出剩下的比例，主管聽到的是交易而不是討價還價。
swaps: I'd like to protect one day a week for this
Can we ring-fence 20% for discovery?
cards.pmNote: 要時間時同時承諾產出比例，通過率遠高於只說「我需要時間」。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

cards.quote: Here's what I heard from all of you. I'm listening, I hear this and here's what I want to do about it.
cards.zh: 以下是我從各位那裡聽到的。我有在聽，我聽到了，接下來我打算這樣做。
cards.why: 三段式收斂：我聽到什麼 → 我確實有在聽 → 我要做什麼。中間那句看似多餘，其實是整段的關鍵——它回應的是情緒，不是資訊。
swaps: Here's what I took away from those conversations
This is what I heard, and this is what happens next
cards.pmNote: listening tour 做完一定要公開回饋摘要，否則等於沒做。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

cards.quote: And so I always say diagnose before you treat.
cards.zh: 所以我常說：先診斷，再開藥。
cards.why: 借醫療的動詞對比，四個字就把「別急著解決」講完，而且沒有指責誰躁進。這種可以被別人轉述的短語，在會議裡的傳播力遠勝一整段道理。
swaps: Let's diagnose before we prescribe
We're treating symptoms before we know the cause
cards.pmNote: 跳過問題定義直接做方案，是新任 PM 最貴的錯誤。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

cards.pattern: What they're saying is not [誤讀], it's that [真正的意思].
cards.quote: No, no, no. What they're saying is not that you're a bad product person, it's that you need to do a better job communicating or connecting.
cards.zh: 不不不。他們講的不是你是個爛 PM，而是你在溝通、在建立連結這件事上要做得更好。
cards.why: not X, it's Y 的對照結構，一句話把人身評價和行為建議切開。幫別人翻譯他收到的回饋時，這是最好用的句型——先擋掉最痛的誤讀，再放回可行動的版本。
swaps: That's feedback about the behavior, not about you
They're not questioning your judgment — they want more context
cards.pmNote: 把回饋從「你這個人」翻譯成「這個行為」，對方才有辦法改。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

cards.quote: Hey, I'm really enjoying working with you. I'm wondering is there some way I could help you that would also help me reach my goal?
cards.zh: 嘿，跟你合作我覺得很愉快。我在想，有沒有什麼事我可以幫你、同時也能幫我朝目標前進的？
cards.why: 整句的重量在 that would also：把自己的需求掛在「幫你」後面，變成雙贏的搜尋題而不是索取。I'm wondering 又讓它保持在探詢語氣，主管沒答應也不尷尬。
swaps: Is there something you need that would also stretch me in this direction?
What could I take on that helps you and builds this skill for me?
cards.pmNote: 把個人成長需求綁在主管的痛點上，是升遷談判成功率最高的框架。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

cards.quote: Two things I'd love to clarify.
cards.zh: 有兩件事我想澄清一下。
cards.why: 先報數字（two things）讓聽者知道要留多少注意力，再用 I'd love to 把「更正」講得像貢獻。這是英文簡報和會議裡最容易上手的結構標記。
swaps: A couple of things worth clarifying
Let me clean up two points
cards.pmNote: 開口前先報項目數，聽眾才知道你什麼時候會講完。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

cards.pattern: I'd be honest with people and say some patience is required. However, there is a lot you can do.
cards.quote: I would be honest with people and say some patience is required. However, there is a lot you can do. A lot is in your control.
cards.zh: 我會誠實地說：這需要一點耐心。不過，你能做的事很多，很多都在你的掌控裡。
cards.why: 報壞消息的雙拍結構：先不粉飾（patience is required），再立刻把 agency 還給對方（in your control）。少了後半句是打擊，少了前半句是畫大餅，兩句一起才是專業。
swaps: I won't sugarcoat it — this takes time. But here's what's in your hands
Realistically we're waiting. Meanwhile, here's what we control
cards.pmNote: 延期或凍結的消息一定要配上「現在能做什麼」，否則團隊只會空轉。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

cards.pattern: The first thing I did was I owned it. Yes, it's not working. It's my fault. I will deal with it.
cards.quote: Yes, it's not working. It's my fault. I will deal with it.
cards.zh: 我做的第一件事就是認下來。我說：「對，它現在是壞的。是我的錯。我會處理。」
cards.why: 三個短句、零解釋、零形容詞：承認事實、認領責任、宣告行動。台灣人（和多數人）出事時的直覺是先解釋原因，而在英文語境裡，任何在 It's my fault 之前出現的解釋都會被聽成推卸。
swaps: This one's on me. I'm on it
That was my call and it was wrong. Here's what I'm doing
cards.pmNote: 事故當下的第一句話決定你之後有沒有機會解釋來龍去脈。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

cards.pattern: This is exactly where we are. This is what we're going to do in the next hour. I will update you again at [時間].
cards.quote: This is exactly where we are. This is what we're going to do and the next hour, and this is when you'll get your next update. I will update you again at 9:00 AM.
cards.zh: 目前的狀況就是這樣。接下來一小時我們要做的是這些，下一次更新會在什麼時候。我九點會再跟你更新一次。
cards.why: 危機溝通的三欄位：現況、下一小時的動作、下次更新時間。第三欄是最多人漏掉也最關鍵的一欄——主動給下次更新時間，就是在買時間，而且對方不會來微管理你。
swaps: Status, next step, next update — I'll ping you at the top of the hour
Nothing new to report yet; next update in 60 minutes
cards.pmNote: 事故期間的節奏承諾（每小時一次）比事故內容本身更能穩住上層。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

cards.pattern: We've all been there, we know it's miserable. What can we do to help?
cards.quote: We've all been under Jeff's Eye of Sauron, we know it's miserable. What can we do to help?
cards.zh: 我們都被那道索倫之眼盯過，知道那有多難受。我們能幫上什麼？
cards.why: 先用共同經驗把對方從「犯錯的人」拉回「我們這群人」，再問要什麼幫助。少了前半句，後半句會像上級查勤；有了前半句，才是同盟。
swaps: Been there. What do you need?
We've all had one of these. How can we help?
cards.pmNote: 有人在火線上時，先表達同盟再問需求，對方才敢說出真正缺什麼。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

cards.quote: So how are you doing? I bet it's been a hard week.
cards.zh: 所以你還好嗎？我猜這禮拜很難熬吧。
cards.why: 衝突之後的修復句：不提事故、不再追責，只認可對方的處境。I bet 是英文裡替對方說出感受又不強加的句型——比 Are you okay? 更貼近，也更難拒絕。
swaps: That can't have been fun. How are you holding up?
Rough week, I imagine
cards.pmNote: 衝突後主動修補關係的人通常是層級較高的那一方，這一步決定信任會不會回來。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

cards.quote: Yeah, I messed up. But I know I'm still a good person and a good worker. Yes, I made a mistake, but I'm going to move on.
cards.zh: 對，我搞砸了。但我知道我還是個好人、也還是個好的工作者。對，我犯了錯，但我要往前走。
cards.why: 承認錯誤與維持自我價值同時成立——這是英文職場語言裡很重要、台灣人卻常常做不到的分離。連續用兩次 Yes...but 的節奏，讀起來像在對自己宣誓，可以直接照抄。
swaps: I own the mistake, but I'm not going to live in it
Bad call, not a bad career
cards.pmNote: postmortem 的目的是修系統不是修人；把羞恥留下來只會讓人隱瞞下一個錯。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

cards.quote: Paul, that's excellent leadership. I really appreciate what you're doing. Please step out of the way.
cards.zh: Paul，這是很好的領導。我很感謝你這麼做。不過請讓開。
cards.why: 先給一個具體且真誠的肯定，再下一個不容商量的指令——肯定不是為了鋪墊拒絕，而是確保對方被否決時不會誤讀成被貶低。這種「先表揚後否決」的節奏在英文高階場合很常見。
swaps: I respect you protecting your team. I still need to talk to them directly
That's the right instinct — I'm going to override it this once
cards.pmNote: 推翻部屬的判斷時先肯定他的動機，才不會讓他下次不敢再擋。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

cards.pattern: Well, two things. First, you were wrong. Second though, [轉折].
cards.quote: He said, "Well, two things. First, you were wrong. You were wrong to prioritize date over our reputation."
cards.zh: 他說：「兩件事。第一，你錯了。你不該把時程放在我們的商譽前面。」
cards.why: 先報數量再逐條講，重話就有了結構感，聽的人知道還有下一點、不會當場崩潰。You were wrong to [動詞] 這個句型精準鎖定「哪個決定錯」，而不是「你這個人錯」。
swaps: Two things. One, that was the wrong call. Two, here's what saves you
You were wrong to trade X for Y
cards.pmNote: 重話分點講並預告總數，對方才聽得完而不是聽到一半就防衛。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

cards.quote: Yes, you wrote the bug, but that's not on you. The system failed you.
cards.zh: 對，那個 bug 是你寫的，但這不算在你頭上。是制度沒接住你。
cards.why: that's not on you 是英文裡把責任從個人移回系統的標準說法，短、明確、沒有安慰的味道。先承認事實（yes, you wrote it）再免責，比一開口就說「不是你的錯」可信得多。
swaps: That's on the process, not on you
We set you up to fail there
cards.pmNote: 事故檢討時明確講出「這不是你的責任」，是留住人的關鍵一句話。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

cards.pattern: [X] is good, but [Y] is necessary.
cards.quote: And I think people don't understand that in a competitive environment, being right is good, but being quick is necessary.
cards.zh: 我覺得大家沒搞懂：在競爭環境裡，做對是加分，做得快是必要條件。
cards.why: good / necessary 的對比把兩個都「重要」的東西分成不同層級，一句話解決優先順序的爭論。這個結構可以無限套用：X is helpful, but Y is non-negotiable。
swaps: Quality is table stakes; speed is the differentiator
Nice to have versus non-negotiable
cards.pmNote: 排優先順序的爭論常常卡在「兩個都重要」，分成加分項與必要項就解開了。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

cards.quote: Beyond those cosmetics, the biggest thing I see particularly at higher levels is people talk about what they have done but not why it mattered.
cards.zh: 撇開那些表面功夫，我在比較資深的層級看到最大的問題是：大家只講自己做了什麼，不講那件事為什麼重要。
cards.why: what you did / why it mattered 是英文績效與面試語言裡最重要的一組對照。台灣人受的訓練多半停在前者，這句給了一個可以自我檢查的鉤子：講完事情就問自己 so what。
swaps: Don't tell me what you shipped — tell me what changed
Impact, not activity
cards.pmNote: 升遷簡報與面試都吃 impact；同樣一件事，量化的後果才是敘事的主詞。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

cards.quote: And what I say about that is what your manager should do and $4 will get you a cup of coffee at Starbucks.
cards.zh: 我對這件事的回答是：你主管「應該」怎麼做，加四塊美金可以在星巴克換一杯咖啡。
cards.why: 美式的招牌冷嘲句型「X and $Y will get you Z」，意思是「X 本身一文不值」。用來擋掉「這本來就該是別人的責任」這類抱怨，殺傷力強但有幽默感，屬於聽得懂就很有用、講出來要看場合的等級。
swaps: That's true, and it changes nothing
Fair — but you still have to deal with reality
cards.pmNote: 把注意力從「誰該負責」轉回「我能控制什麼」，是卡住的職涯最快的解法。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

cards.quote: Hey, I noticed that we have this problem. I fixed it.
cards.zh: 嘿，我注意到我們有這個問題，我把它處理掉了。
cards.why: 兩個短句就完成一次向上回報：發現 + 已解決。沒有請示、沒有邀功、也沒有請對方決策——這是英文裡展現 seniority 最經濟的說法。
swaps: Heads up — saw this, handled it
FYI, this came up and it's taken care of
cards.pmNote: 越資深，回報就越該從「請示」變成「知會」。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

cards.quote: We're going to get to work on that, but can you tell me how are you measuring success? We want to make sure that what we do, you consider it successful.
cards.zh: 這件事我們會開始動工，不過可以先跟我說你是怎麼衡量成功的嗎？我們想確保做出來的東西，在你眼中算是成功。
cards.why: 先用「我們會做」拿掉對方的防衛，再用「你怎麼衡量成功」把一個指定好的功能悄悄翻譯成一個問題。整句沒有一個字在反對，卻拿回了解法的主導權——這是 PM 擋需求最安全的開場。
swaps: Happy to pick this up — how will we know it worked?
Before we scope it, what does success look like for you?
We can start on that. What outcome are you hoping to move?
cards.pmNote: 把 output（做某功能）反推回 outcome（解某問題）是 empowered team 的第一步；stakeholder 給的功能其實只是他心中的一個解法假設。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

cards.pattern: Your belief is that if we [做 X]，[結果 Y] will happen. Do I have that right?
cards.quote: Your belief is that if we add buy now pay later, a lot more people will be able to buy and transact, and so it's going to pay off. Do I have that right?
cards.zh: 你的認定是：只要我們加了先買後付，會有更多人買得下去、成交量會上來，所以這筆投資划得來。我這樣理解對嗎？
cards.why: 把對方的要求複述成一句「假設」，再加上 Do I have that right? 交還發球權。假設一旦被講出口就變成可以被驗證的東西，你不必反駁，對方自己會開始鬆動。
swaps: So the assumption is that…, right?
If I'm hearing you right, you're betting that…
The thinking is …— am I reading that correctly?
cards.pmNote: 這是 assumption mapping 的口語版：把需求拆成「價值假設」，才有辦法用最小成本驗證它。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

cards.pattern: What do you think about us running an experiment? Let us try [做法] for [期間] — if it goes well, great; if it doesn't, no harm.
cards.quote: What do you think about us doing an experiment? For the next quarter or two, why don't you let us try running like this? If it goes well, great; if it doesn't, no harm.
cards.zh: 我們來做個實驗你覺得如何？接下來一兩季，讓我們試著用這種方式跑跑看。順利的話很好，不順利也沒損失，我們就退回原本的做法。
cards.why: 把「改變組織做法」這種高風險提案包裝成「實驗」，再自己先講出退場條件（no harm），主管要拒絕的成本就變得很高。台灣人常直接要求授權，忘了先幫對方把風險降到零。
swaps: Could we treat this as a two-sprint experiment?
What if we time-boxed it to one quarter and reviewed?
Would you be open to us piloting this on one team?
cards.pmNote: 組織轉型不要一次動整個 BU，先找一個 product team 當試點——風險小、可回復、有成功案例才好擴散。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

cards.quote: I've learned that some of the companies we admire are not working the way we are, and maybe we should try this.
cards.zh: 我發現我們很欣賞的那幾家公司，做事方式跟我們並不一樣，也許我們可以試試看他們的做法。
cards.why: 用「我們共同欣賞的對象」當外部權威，避免把提案變成「我覺得 vs 你覺得」的個人對決；結尾用 maybe we should 留一個很低的門檻，讓對方是「同意嘗試」而不是「承認錯誤」。
swaps: The teams we look up to do it differently — worth a look?
I noticed a pattern at companies like X; maybe there's something for us there.
cards.pmNote: 推動改變時，外部標竿（best practice benchmark）比內部主張更容易被採納，因為它把爭論從立場移到證據。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

cards.pattern: Don't get me wrong, I love [X], but [保留意見]
cards.quote: And don't get me wrong, I love those cultures, but they're all different cultures. They're very different cultures.
cards.zh: 別誤會，那些文化我都很欣賞，但它們彼此其實非常不一樣，真的差很多。
cards.why: Don't get me wrong 是英語裡最好用的「防誤解緩衝器」：先預告我不是要攻擊你喜歡的東西，再說出真正的保留。台灣人常直接接 but，聽起來像否定對方的品味。
swaps: Don't get me wrong — I'm a fan, but…
I'm not knocking it, but…
To be clear, I like it; my concern is…
cards.pmNote: 抄大公司做法時要把「文化」和「技法」拆開——Amazon 的 working backwards 可以學，Amazon 的文化不見得能移植。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

cards.pattern: If none of [可信對象] are using it, it's either snake oil or it's not proven yet.
cards.quote: If none of those companies are using it, I'm like, "Don't bother me. It's either snake oil or it's not proven yet."
cards.zh: 如果那些公司一家都沒在用，那我的反應就是：別來煩我，這東西不是江湖偏方，就是還沒被驗證。
cards.why: 拒絕時把標準（誰在用）講在前面、結論擺後面，聽起來像在套用規則而不是針對人。snake oil（蛇油＝江湖假藥）是母語者常用、台灣人幾乎講不出來的貶義詞。
swaps: If the teams we trust aren't using it, I'd wait.
Until someone credible has shipped with it, it's unproven.
That's a solution looking for a problem.
cards.pmNote: 評估新工具/新流程的最低門檻：有沒有幾支好團隊已經在真實情境下用出結果，而不是白皮書說得漂亮。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

cards.pattern: If you need to spend a little time on [X], fine — but don't spend a lot, because you need to save as much time as possible for [Y].
cards.quote: Be careful. If you need to spend a little time on the problem, fine, but don't spend a lot of time because you need to save as much time as possible to come up with the winning solution.
cards.zh: 小心一點。你要花一點時間在問題上沒問題，但別花太多，因為你得盡量把時間留給「想出會贏的解法」。
cards.why: 「fine, but」是談優先順序的黃金句型：先承認對方要的東西有價值（不是零），再用「因為要留給更重要的」轉移資源。比直接說 don't do that 溫和太多。
swaps: A little is fine; a lot is expensive.
Worth some time, not worth weeks.
Timebox it — the leverage is downstream.
cards.pmNote: problem discovery 與 solution discovery 要分開看：多數產品的勝負在解法端，過度驗證早已確知的問題等於燒掉窗口期。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

cards.pattern: You can hand off [這些]. But never [那三件核心的事].
cards.quote: Pulling off other responsibilities is no problem. It's a good thing to do, especially as you grow, but never when you touch those three sacred things.
cards.zh: 把其他職責分出去完全沒問題，隨著規模變大這反而是好事——但前提是不能碰到那三件神聖不可讓的事。
cards.why: 先大方讓步（很多事都可以拿走），再用 never 把一條線劃死。給出讓步清單會讓那條紅線顯得合理而不是難搞，這是守住範疇時最有效的結構。
swaps: Happy to give up X and Y — Z I can't move on.
Everything else is negotiable; that one isn't.
Take the rest, but that one stays with the team.
cards.pmNote: PM 三條命脈：直接接觸使用者、直接接觸工程師、直接接觸 stakeholder；把任何一條交給 product owner 或 product ops，創新就停了。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

cards.pattern: That one always makes me laugh, because [反問]
cards.quote: That one always makes me laugh because I was thinking, "Do you know how many hours a week I'd need to work if that was my only job?"
cards.zh: 這種說法每次都讓我笑出來，因為我心想：如果那真的是我唯一的工作，你知道我一週只需要上多少小時的班嗎？
cards.why: 用「這讓我笑了」＋自嘲式反問來反駁一個廣為流傳的錯誤觀念，火力很強但沒有指名任何人。幽默在英語會議裡是合法的反對武器，台灣人往往只會硬碰硬或乾脆不講。
swaps: That one always gets me, because…
I have to smile at that one — if that were true, …
That always makes me laugh; think it through and…
cards.pmNote: 「PM 只管 what、不管 how」是最常見的角色誤解——valuable 與 viable 這兩個風險本來就落在 how 裡面。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

cards.pattern: If [關鍵的人] can't be there, cancel it.
cards.quote: If the product manager and the designer are not available to be there during their product test, cancel the test. They need to be there.
cards.zh: 如果產品經理和設計師沒辦法到場，那這場使用者測試就取消。他們一定要在現場。
cards.why: 把「拒絕」寫成一條前置條件式的規則（if…, cancel it），對事不對人，下次不必再吵一次。這種「規則化的 no」是資深者最省力的擋人方式。
swaps: No decision-maker in the room, no meeting.
If the owner can't join, we move it.
Let's not run it without them.
cards.pmNote: 使用者研究的價值不在報告，在團隊親耳聽到；報告太容易被忽略，現場的震撼才會改變決策。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

cards.pattern: I hate the idea of [做法], because [理由]
cards.quote: I hate the idea of those companies that have separate product owners because product owner is just an administrative role.
cards.zh: 我很不喜歡那些另外設 product owner 的公司，因為 product owner 本質上只是個行政角色。
cards.why: I hate the idea of X 攻擊的是「這個做法」而不是「做這件事的人」——英語裡用 the idea of 當緩衝墊，強度可以很高但不會變成人身攻擊。
swaps: I'm not a fan of the idea that…
I really don't like the setup where…
The idea of splitting that role bothers me.
cards.pmNote: 把 PM 一分為二（PO 對工程、PM 對市場）看起來減負，實際上切斷了發現解法所需的資訊迴路。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

cards.pattern: Let's just say [情境設定]，and [推論]
cards.quote: Let's just say there's a product manager and nobody's ever coached this poor person, and so they really don't know much.
cards.zh: 我們就假設有一個產品經理，從來沒有人帶過他，所以他其實懂得不多。
cards.why: Let's just say 讓你把一個真實但敏感的狀況（例如「我們公司的 PM 很弱」）搬到假設世界討論，聽的人不必對號入座。談人的問題時這是最好用的去人格化裝置。
swaps: Say for the sake of argument that…
Imagine a team where…
Suppose nobody's ever coached them.
cards.pmNote: empowered team 最常失敗的一環不是流程，而是 PM 本人準備不足（不懂使用者、數據、商業、產業）。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

cards.pattern: So to your question: [重述問題]. These are the [N] things you need to do.
cards.quote: So to your question, you're a feature team. You want to give it a shot, be in a real product team. These are the four things you need to go out and do.
cards.zh: 回到你的問題：你在一支功能團隊，想試試看真正的產品團隊怎麼運作——那你要去做的就是這四件事。
cards.why: 講久了要收線時，用 So to your question 把話題拉回提問者，再用「這 N 件事」把散開的內容重新打包。這是英語會議裡把發散變收斂的標準動作。
swaps: Coming back to your question…
So, to answer what you actually asked…
Back to your point — here's the short version.
cards.pmNote: 從 feature team 轉成 product team 的四件事：拿到問題而非功能、PM 補足知識、拿到策略脈絡、學會 discovery 技法。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

cards.pattern: My purely anecdotal guess is [數字], something like that.
cards.quote: My purely anecdotal guess is maybe 10 to 15% are good product companies, something like that.
cards.zh: 我純粹憑印象猜，大概一成到一成五算是好的產品公司吧，差不多這個量級。
cards.why: 先給數字（對方要的），再用 purely anecdotal 標明資料等級，最後 something like that 留誤差。敢給數字又標清楚可信度，是資深訊號；台灣人常常是乾脆不給，反而顯得沒觀點。
swaps: Gut feel, no data behind it: maybe 10–15%.
Anecdotally, I'd guess…
Ballpark, and I could be way off…
cards.pmNote: 回答沒有資料的問題時，給出「估計值＋可信度標籤」比拒答有用，這也是 opportunity sizing 的基本禮貌。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

cards.pattern: Just to reinforce this point — what are the [N] things again? In case folks didn't catch it.
cards.quote: Just to reinforce this point, what are the three things again? In case folks didn't catch it all.
cards.zh: 為了把這個重點再壓一次——那三件事到底是哪三件？怕大家剛剛沒全部聽清楚。
cards.why: 把「我要你再講一次」包裝成「這點很重要值得再講」＋「怕別人沒聽到」，完全不暴露自己沒跟上。英文會議裡最實用的一句自保台詞。
swaps: Can we land that one again for everyone?
Worth repeating — what were the three?
Say that once more for the room.
cards.pmNote: 會議尾聲把關鍵清單複述一次，是最便宜的 alignment 動作。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

cards.pattern: [名字], you have to stop [具體行為].
cards.quote: And he's like, "Jackie, you have to stop shutting me down."
cards.zh: 他就直接說：「Jackie，你不能再這樣把我的話擋回去了。」
cards.why: 叫名字＋you have to stop＋一個動作名詞，短到沒有閃避空間。難聽的回饋在英語裡反而要更短：拉長修飾只會讓對方抓不到重點。shut someone down 精準指「當場把人堵死」。
swaps: You need to stop cutting people off.
I need you to stop shooting things down so fast.
That's the third time you've shut that down — let's not.
cards.pmNote: PM 用「效率」當理由快速否決，久了會被讀成防衛心，真正的代價是別人不再帶想法來找你。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

cards.pattern: Yes, I agree that's a real problem. Yes, we could test [做法] with users.
cards.quote: You can say, "Yes, I agree. That is a real problem. Yes, I think we could test this design with users."
cards.zh: 你可以說：「對，我同意，那確實是個真的問題。對，我覺得這個設計我們可以拿去跟使用者測。」
cards.why: 把「不做」換成兩個真心的 yes：同意問題存在、同意驗證方式。你沒有承諾任何排程，但對方感覺被接住了——這是擋需求最不傷關係的版本。
swaps: I agree the problem's real — let's test the solution.
Yes to the problem, let's validate the approach.
That pain is real; let's see what the data says.
cards.pmNote: 把 stakeholder 給的解法當成「他在描述問題的方式」，你就永遠有東西可以同意，而不必先開戰。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

cards.quote: And I can interpret their solution as a way of sharing the problem and exploring and brainstorming around that.
cards.zh: 我可以把他們提出的解法，理解成他們在用自己的方式描述問題、順便一起發想。
