cards.why: interpret A as B 是很高段的重新框架：不否定對方講的內容，只調整它的身分（從「指令」變成「線索」）。學會這一句，很多對立會直接消失。
swaps: I read that as them describing the pain.
Their fix is really a symptom report.
Behind that request there's a real problem.
cards.pmNote: 需求背後幾乎都藏著真實痛點；解法可以否決，痛點不要否決。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

cards.pattern: It might be easier if I just [做 X] — I might be able to save you some time and energy.
cards.quote: It might be easier if I just go, I might be able to save you some time and some energy if I just joined you.
cards.zh: 也許我直接去比較快，我一起進去的話，說不定可以幫你省下一些時間跟力氣。
cards.why: 想擠進一個自己沒資格參加的會議，卻把理由完全放在「幫你省事」。用 might＋just 把要求縮到最小，聽起來像順手幫忙而不是爭取權力。
swaps: Might be quicker if I just came along.
Want me to sit in so you don't have to relay it?
I could take that off your plate if I joined.
cards.pmNote: 爭取進到更高層的會議時，賣點是「減少傳話損耗」，不是「我也想聽」。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

cards.pattern: Here are the [N] questions I want you to get answered — and if they say X, ask Y.
cards.quote: Hey, you have your planning committee today. Here are the three questions I want you to go in and get answered at that committee.
cards.zh: 你今天有規劃委員會對吧？這是我希望你進去幫我問到答案的三個問題。
cards.why: 進不去的會議，就把自己的問題塞進去。用「三個問題」這種有限、具體的形式，主管容易答應；久了你就從外圍變成議程的作者。
swaps: Could you bring these two questions in for me?
If it comes up, can you ask about…?
Here's what I'd love to know from that room.
cards.pmNote: 影響力常是從「幫決策者準備問題」開始累積的，不必等到有席次。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

cards.pattern: I'd really love to become [目標] someday. What do you suggest I work on now so I'll be ready when the opportunity comes up?
cards.quote: I would really love to become a people manager someday. What do you suggest that I work on now so that I'll be ready when the opportunity comes up?
cards.zh: 我以後很想帶人。你建議我現在可以先練哪些東西，等機會來的時候我已經準備好了？
cards.why: 把野心放在未來式（someday）就不會逼主管當場評價你「現在夠不夠格」，再用 what do you suggest 把他拉到你這一邊當教練。整句沒有要求任何東西，卻同時完成了宣告目標和取得路線圖。
swaps: Down the road I'd like to grow into X — what should I be building now?
When that door opens, what would make me ready?
What gaps should I close before that comes up?
cards.pmNote: 升遷回饋要主動聚焦：不聚焦時你會收到一堆都對但無關升遷的小建議。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

cards.pattern: I agree — I've changed my mind. You're right. You saw it in a way I hadn't seen.
cards.quote: I agree, I've changed my mind. You're right. You just saw it in a way that I hadn't seen.
cards.zh: 我同意，我改變想法了。你是對的，你看到的角度是我原本沒看到的。
cards.why: 改立場時最怕顯得沒主見。這裡用「你看到的角度是我沒看到的」把轉向歸因於新資訊而非自己軟弱，既給對方面子也保住自己專業感。三句話乾淨俐落，不拖泥帶水。
swaps: You've convinced me — I hadn't looked at it that way.
Fair point, I'm changing my position.
I was wrong on that; your framing is better.
cards.pmNote: strong opinions, loosely held：立場要清楚，但新證據出現時要能公開換邊，這是資深而非動搖。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

cards.pattern: I think really [選項] is the only reasonable one, for these reasons.
cards.quote: And then our CEO gets in, and he's like, "I think really number four is the only reasonable one for these reasons."
cards.zh: 然後我們執行長進來說：「我認為真正合理的其實只有第四個，理由如下。」
cards.why: the only reasonable one 火力很強，但前面加 I think、後面立刻接 for these reasons，就從獨斷變成「我有推論、歡迎檢驗」。強勢意見要能被接受，關鍵是理由必須同句出現。
swaps: To me only option four holds up, and here's why.
I'd argue three of these are non-starters because…
I think there's really only one viable path here.
cards.pmNote: 定價這類高槓桿決策，講清楚淘汰其他選項的理由，比宣布結論更能建立共識。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

cards.quote: And he's like, "Can you create a strategy for the platform team?" And I was like, "Great, here it is." And he's like, "That's not a strategy."
cards.zh: 他問：「你能幫平台團隊做一份策略嗎？」我說：「好啊，這就是了。」他說：「這不是策略。」
cards.why: 四個字的否決，沒有任何緩衝——這種強度只有在資深、關係穩、而且接著會給定義時才能用。值得學的是它的效果：把模糊的爭論一刀切開，逼出「那什麼才算」的對話。
swaps: That's a goal, not a strategy.
That's a plan — where's the choice in it?
I don't think that clears the bar for a strategy.
cards.pmNote: 策略＝願景＋策略框架（市場、致勝賭注）＋路線圖；只有目標數字或功能清單都不算策略。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

cards.pattern: Anytime a disagreement feels like a disagreement in values, that's a sign it's really a disagreement in strategy.
cards.quote: Anytime you have these disagreements that feel really thorny or they feel like a disagreement in values, that's a sign that you really have a disagreement in strategy.
cards.zh: 每當某個爭執特別棘手、感覺像是價值觀的衝突，那通常是個訊號：你們真正在吵的是策略。
cards.why: 把僵持的衝突重新命名（不是人不合，是策略沒定），衝突就從人身層級被抬到議題層級。that's a sign that… 是把情緒轉譯成診斷的萬用句型。
swaps: If we keep relitigating this, the real gap is upstream.
This feels like values, but I think it's strategy.
Repeated fights usually mean a missing decision above.
cards.pmNote: 反覆爭同一個功能，是策略或產品原則缺席的症狀；解法是把爭論寫成一條原則，而不是一次一次投票。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

cards.pattern: If you come in on day one saying [X] is all wrong, it raises the question of why you joined.
cards.quote: But if they come in on day one saying your strategy is all wrong, raises the question of, "Well then why did you join my team if you didn't believe in my strategy?"
cards.zh: 但如果他第一天就說你的策略整個都錯了，那就會讓人想問：既然你不相信這個策略，當初為什麼要加入我的團隊？
cards.why: It raises the question of… 是把反對包成「一個自然會被問到的問題」，不是「我要質問你」。用問句回擊，殺傷力保留、姿態卻很低。
swaps: That raises a fair question…
It begs the question of why we hired for this then.
Which makes me wonder what you signed up for.
cards.pmNote: 新人前六個月先學既有策略並交付，六個月後再提策略草稿，才有信用可用。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

cards.pattern: OK, great — what does [模糊的詞] actually mean?
cards.quote: I got the feedback that I needed to be more strategic. I was like, "Okay, great. What does being more strategic mean?" And nobody could tell me.
cards.zh: 我收到的回饋是「要更有策略性」。我心想：好啊，那「更有策略性」到底是什麼意思？結果沒有人講得出來。
cards.why: Okay, great 先接受回饋、不辯解，再追問定義。這一組（接受＋要定義）能把空泛評價逼成可執行的東西，而且不會被讀成在辯護。
swaps: Happy to work on it — what would 'more strategic' look like day to day?
Got it. Can you give me an example of someone doing that well?
What would I be doing differently if I nailed that?
cards.pmNote: 收到抽象的績效回饋時，追問「具體行為」與「範例人物」，否則你會改到錯的地方。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

cards.pattern: The right answer to a narrowly scoped problem is not to invent a whole new [大東西].
cards.quote: And the right answer to these narrowly scoped defined problems is not to invent a whole new print dialogue.
cards.zh: 面對這種範圍很窄、已經定義清楚的問題，正確答案並不是重新發明一整套列印對話框。
cards.why: The right answer to X is not to Y——先立標準再排除做法，比直接說「你做太多了」不傷人。這是替別人（或自己）縮範疇時很好用的句型。
swaps: This doesn't need a redesign — it needs to ship.
The win here is doing the simple thing well.
Big creative swings are the wrong tool for this one.
cards.pmNote: 初階 PM 最常見的傷：拿到小任務卻硬做大改造，把「值得信任」的分數花掉。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

cards.pattern: That person needs to step up and be a multiplier on everybody else's work.
cards.quote: That person needs to step up more, to be somebody who's really contributing and adding and being a multiplier on the work of everybody else on their team.
cards.zh: 那個人需要更站出來一點，成為真正有貢獻、有加分，能把團隊其他人的產出放大的角色。
cards.why: step up 指出不足、multiplier 給出目標畫面，一句話同時完成批評與方向。給難聽回饋時，最好的收尾永遠是一個具體的、可以想像的角色形象。
swaps: I'd like to see you take more of the lead here.
You're adding less than you could — let's fix that.
I want you multiplying the team, not just tracking it.
cards.pmNote: PM 的績效不是自己做了多少，而是讓團隊產出被放大多少；當旁邊有強設計師時最容易退化成記錄員。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

cards.pattern: Yes it failed — but what I learned from that is [具體做法改變], and since then [結果].
cards.quote: I don't want them to leave it at, "It was a big loss." You want to say, "What I learned from that is now I always run a load test, and I've had many successful launches since then."
cards.zh: 我不希望他只停在「那是一次很大的損失」。你應該說：我從那件事學到，現在我一定會先跑壓力測試，後來的好幾次上線都沒再出過同樣的問題。
cards.why: 談失敗一定要有第三段：損失→新做法→之後的證據。少了最後那段證據，聽起來就只是懺悔；有了它，失敗反而變成能力證明。
swaps: We lost X. What changed after was Y, and it's held since.
That failure gave us the checklist we still use.
Since then I've never shipped without…
cards.pmNote: postmortem 的產出應該是一條被寫進流程的規則，不是一份心得。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

cards.pattern: I just want to make a huge caveat — this isn't a judgment on any of these.
cards.quote: And again, I just want to make a huge caveat, this is not a judgment on any of these particular perspectives. It's more like I noticed a lot of it.
cards.zh: 再強調一次，我要先加一個很大的但書：我不是在評判這些觀點的好壞，比較像是我注意到它們特別多。
cards.why: 在批評整個產業風氣之前先立一道免責聲明，把「我在觀察」和「我在批判」分開。想講重話又不想樹敵時，caveat 是最重要的前置動作。
swaps: Big caveat up front: I'm not knocking any of this.
To be clear, this isn't a criticism — just an observation.
With the obvious disclaimer that…
cards.pmNote: 產品建議大多預設了矽谷新創的脈絡；照抄到別種公司常常比不做還糟。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

cards.pattern: Both things can be true. Yes, [讓步]. However, it is true that [你的重點].
cards.quote: Both things can be true. It's like, yeah, there's nothing perfect in product. However, it is true that some companies are healthier than others.
cards.zh: 這兩件事可以同時成立。對，產品這行沒有什麼是完美的；但同樣真實的是，有些公司確實比其他公司健康得多。
cards.why: 先把對方的話完整承認一次（yeah, …），再用 however it is true that 把自己的重點放回桌上。讓步不是輸，而是換取對方接住你下一句的注意力。
swaps: Both can be true at the same time.
Sure, and at the same time…
Agreed — that said, it's still the case that…
cards.pmNote: 區分 chronic（長期慢性）與 acute（急性）問題：把慢性債還掉的公司，遇到景氣衝擊時才撐得住。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

cards.quote: Go and talk to that executive and say, "Look, I know you've told me to do this, but what would we observe if this was working versus not working? I'm here to help you with that."
cards.zh: 你可以去找那位主管說：「我知道你已經指定要做這個了，但如果它有效跟沒效，我們會分別看到什麼？這部分我可以幫你。」
cards.why: 先明確認輸（我知道這已經拍板），換取問一個真正關鍵的問題的權利，最後用「我來幫你」把自己放在同陣營。這是對付上對下命令最漂亮的一招——沒挑戰決定，只挑戰未定義的成功條件。
swaps: Decision's made, I get that — what would tell us it's working?
I'm on board. How will we know if it lands?
Since we're doing it: what signal should we watch?
cards.pmNote: 在自主權很低的組織裡，仍然可以爭取到「定義成功指標」這一格——這是把 output 文化撬開的最小施力點。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

cards.pattern: It's the difference between oversimplifying and focusing — I need to hold some things constant.
cards.quote: I think it's the difference between oversimplification and focusing. You can have a complex problem and be like, "You know what? I need to hold some things constant."
cards.zh: 我覺得差別在於「過度簡化」和「聚焦」。面對複雜問題你可以說：好，我需要先把某些變數固定住。
cards.why: 用一組對照詞（oversimplification / focusing）把「我要縮小範圍」講成方法論而不是偷懶。hold things constant 借自科學，很適合在會議上為砍範疇辯護。
swaps: Let's hold those variables constant for now.
That's focusing, not dumbing it down.
We can't move unless we freeze a few things.
cards.pmNote: 複雜系統裡要有進展，就得刻意凍結一部分變數；分不清「簡化」與「聚焦」的團隊，會在無限討論裡打轉。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

cards.pattern: That's the trillion-dollar question, so I don't really have an answer — I have a couple of thoughts.
cards.quote: That's the problem. I mean, that is the trillion dollar question so I don't really have an answer. I have a couple thoughts on it.
cards.zh: 問題就在這。這是那種價值一兆美元的問題，所以我其實沒有答案，但我有幾點想法。
cards.why: 先把問題捧高（trillion-dollar question），承認沒答案就不再像無能，而像誠實；再用 a couple of thoughts 把發言權留住。承認不知道又不失分量，全靠這個順序。
swaps: If I knew that, I'd be retired — but here's how I think about it.
No clean answer; a few observations though.
That's the hard one. I've got partial answers.
cards.pmNote: 「人 vs 流程哪個決定績效」沒有定論；能講清楚兩邊的證據，比硬給比例更有價值。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

cards.pattern: Four or five years ago I would've said [舊立場]. I used to be one of those people.
cards.quote: Four or five years ago, I would've said, well, personal skills, nothing. It's all the environment. I used to be one of those particular people.
cards.zh: 四五年前我會說：個人能力根本不重要，全都是環境造成的。我以前就是那一派的人。
cards.why: 把過去的自己拿出來當反例，是最不傷人的反駁方式——你批評的是曾經的自己，而不是現場的誰。同時也證明你會隨證據更新。
swaps: I used to believe exactly that.
Past me would've argued the same thing.
I've flipped on this over the last few years.
cards.pmNote: 對「環境決定論 vs 能力決定論」保持流動立場，才不會在招募與組織設計上做出極端決策。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

cards.pattern: A lot of this advice is common sense. That doesn't mean it's easy to put in motion.
cards.quote: It's like these things that seem so common sense are actually hard with what they're doing… a lot of the advice is common sense. That doesn't mean it's easy to put in motion.
cards.zh: 這些看起來根本是常識的東西，真的做起來很難……很多建議都是常識，但常識不代表容易落地。
cards.why: 對方還沒說出口的「這不是廢話嗎」，你先幫他說完，再把重點移到執行。搶先承認顯而易見的部分，是化解 so what 質疑的標準手法。
swaps: I know it sounds obvious — obvious isn't easy.
Simple to say, hard to run.
Everyone agrees with it; almost nobody does it.
cards.pmNote: 高績效團隊的差異往往不在知不知道，而在有沒有把常識制度化（例如 Amazon 的 bar raiser）。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

cards.pattern: The last thing I want to do is say you either have [X] or you don't.
cards.quote: The last thing I want to do is be like you have a product mindset or you don't.
cards.zh: 我最不想做的事，就是把它講成「你要嘛有產品思維、要嘛沒有」。
cards.why: The last thing I want to do is… 用「我拒絕做某件事」的方式反對一個流行說法，不必點名任何人。要拆掉別人的二分法，先宣布自己不玩這個分類。
swaps: I don't want to turn it into a binary.
I'd hate to frame it as haves and have-nots.
That's the framing I'm trying to avoid.
cards.pmNote: 把「product sense」拆成可教的能力（建模、系統思考、不確定下決策、引導），才有辦法培養人。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

cards.quote: I took us off track a little bit. I think you were going to go onto a second piece of advice.
cards.zh: 我剛剛好像把話題帶偏了一點。你原本要講的第二個建議是什麼？
cards.why: 把偏題的責任攬到自己身上（I took us off track），對方就不會覺得被指責話多。這是主持人把會議拉回主線最沒有摩擦的方式。
swaps: That's on me — you were on point two.
I derailed us; please continue.
Let's get back to where you were.
cards.pmNote: 會議主持的成本大多花在收斂；用自我歸責的方式回主線，能維持發言者的安全感。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

cards.pattern: Let me just summarize the top [N] things you shared, and then I have a two-part question.
cards.quote: But before we do that, let me just summarize maybe the top five attributes and kind of traits you just shared, and then I have a two part question around this.
cards.zh: 在進到那個之前，我先把你剛剛講的五個特質整理一次，然後我有一個兩段式的問題。
cards.why: 先預告動作（我要整理）、再預告下一步（然後我要問），聽者知道會被帶去哪裡。長討論之後不做這個動作，共識就會蒸發。
swaps: Let me play that back to make sure I've got it.
Quick recap before we move on.
So the five things I'm hearing are…
cards.pmNote: 把對方講的東西複述成編號清單，是最有效的 alignment 檢查，也順便取得議程主導權。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

cards.pattern: I'm not an expert in this — [某人] wrote about it and they're much smarter than I am.
cards.quote: And again, I'm not an expert in this and I think Erin Meyer wrote that book, The Culture Map. So you should just find what those people wrote because they're much smarter than I am about this.
cards.zh: 再說一次，我不是這方面的專家。Erin Meyer 寫過《文化地圖》那本書，你們應該直接去看他們寫的，他們比我懂太多了。
cards.why: 承認不懂之後立刻指路，就從「不知道」變成「知道去哪找」。轉介比硬答更能建立信任，而且保住了你在自己專業區的可信度。
swaps: Not my area — X has done the real work on this.
I'd point you to someone who actually knows.
I only know enough to be dangerous here.
cards.pmNote: 知道「這是一門有人專精的學問」本身就是能力；PM 的價值常在於認得出邊界並接上專家。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

cards.pattern: It's one thing to say [X]. It's a whole other thing to [真正做到的行為].
cards.quote: It's one thing to say you're spending a lot of time looking outside the building. It's a whole other thing to hear from the places you don't normally hear from.
cards.zh: 說自己花很多時間在公司外面看，是一回事；真的去聽那些你平常聽不到的聲音，完全是另一回事。
cards.why: It's one thing… it's a whole other thing… 是英語裡拆穿「自我感覺良好」最漂亮的對稱句型：先承認宣稱，再把標準提高一級。不指名、不指責，但沒人躲得掉。
swaps: Saying it and doing it are different things.
It's one thing to care; another to build a system for it.
Easy to claim, hard to evidence.
cards.pmNote: 避開 availability bias：永遠找同一批熟客講話，等於用同一組資料反覆確認自己。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.pattern: Your job is to say no to 90% of what comes your way, so you can say yes to 10%.
cards.quote: Realistically when you're a product manager, your job is to say no to 90% of things that get brought your way. And so you're saying no to 90%, so you can say yes to 10%.
cards.zh: 說穿了，當產品經理的工作就是把送到你面前的九成東西拒絕掉——你拒絕九成，才有辦法對那一成說好。
cards.why: 把拒絕定義成職務內容而不是個人態度，同時給出「為了說好」這個正當理由。要在文化上習慣說好的環境裡守住範疇，先立這個框最有效。
swaps: Every no here is protecting a yes somewhere else.
Saying no is most of the job.
We can't say yes to this without dropping that.
cards.pmNote: scope control 的本質是機會成本：每一個 yes 都在偷走另一件事的工程時間。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.quote: Is the juice worth the squeeze? And now I would say that it's pretty clear that the juice is worth the squeeze.
cards.zh: 這個果汁值得你這樣擠嗎？以現在來看，我會說很明顯是值得的。
cards.why: 一句話把 ROI 討論口語化，比 is it worth the investment 生動很多，母語者在會議上常用。台灣人講成本效益時常太正式，這句能讓你聽起來像局內人。
swaps: Is the payoff worth the effort?
Does the return justify the lift?
Is that worth the squeeze for us?
cards.pmNote: 評估投入前先問這句，能擋掉大量「做了也不會改變結果」的專案。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.pattern: First let's examine the counterfactual — let's start with the opposite of your question.
cards.quote: First let's examine the counterfactual, right? So let's start with the opposite of your question and say, "How would the world be sadder if we all just gave up on this?"
cards.zh: 我們先看反面情況吧。從你問題的相反面開始想：如果大家乾脆全都放棄這件事，世界會變得多糟？
cards.why: 被問「這東西還值得做嗎」時，不直接辯護，而是把問題倒過來問一次。反事實框架讓對方自己走到你的結論，這是最高段的接招方式。
swaps: Let's flip it: what happens if we don't?
What's the cost of doing nothing?
Take the opposite case for a second.
cards.pmNote: 辯護一項投資時，先算「不做的代價」往往比列出好處更有說服力。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.quote: Data is more like a compass than a GPS. If you look at data as a way of giving you the answer, you're always wrong. Wrong or slow, or sometimes both.
cards.zh: 數據比較像指南針，不是導航。如果你把數據當成會給你答案的東西，你不是錯就是慢，有時候兩者都有。
cards.why: 一個比喻同時完成主張與反駁（compass vs GPS），比長篇論述好記十倍。要挑戰「數據至上」文化時，用比喻比用理由安全，因為沒有人被說錯。
swaps: Data points the direction; it doesn't drive.
It narrows the uncertainty — it doesn't decide.
Think compass, not autopilot.
cards.pmNote: 資料的功能是把不確定性降到可以做下一個決策的程度，而不是取代判斷。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.pattern: It'd be better not to show up with an analysis than to show up with one that's dumb.
cards.quote: If you present data with authority and that data is ridiculous, you don't just not get benefit for that. You lose a whole bunch of brownie points.
cards.zh: 如果你很有底氣地端出一份數據，結果那份數據很荒謬，你不只是沒加到分，還會倒扣一大堆好感度。
cards.why: brownie points（好感點數）是台灣人幾乎不會用但母語者很常講的說法。整句用「不只沒好處、還倒扣」的雙層結構，把警告講得比單純說 be careful 有力得多。
swaps: A shaky analysis costs you more than no analysis.
You'll lose credibility, not just the argument.
Better to say 'I don't know yet' than to bring this.
cards.pmNote: 帶分析進會議前先自問樣本、選擇偏誤、上下游是否合理，否則被當場拆穿的代價是長期信用。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.quote: Oftentimes when I see analysis from different product leaders or even data teams, you can drive a truck through it, literally drive a truck through it.
cards.zh: 我常看到一些產品主管、甚至數據團隊做的分析，那個漏洞大到可以開一台卡車過去，真的。
cards.why: 英語裡形容論證漏洞用「洞大到可以開卡車」，比 there are holes 具體且好笑。批評分析品質時用誇飾的成語，殺傷力強但語氣還是輕鬆的。
swaps: There are holes you could drive a truck through.
That argument leaks in three places.
It doesn't hold water.
cards.pmNote: 常見的三個洞：樣本不具代表性、有選擇偏誤、只看單點沒看上下游。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.pattern: I don't really love that thinking process, just in general.
cards.quote: But the other thing is I don't really love some of that thinking process just in general.
cards.zh: 另外還有一點：那整套思考方式，我其實不是很喜歡，講一般情況啦。
cards.why: I don't really love… 是英語裡最溫和的否定之一：用喜好語氣（而非對錯）表達異議，再加 just in general 把它從針對現場的人拉開。台灣人常在這種場合直接說 that's wrong，成本高很多。
swaps: I'm not sold on that way of thinking.
That framing doesn't sit right with me.
I'd push back on the logic a bit.
cards.pmNote: 實驗效果不能長期維持，不代表當初那個效果沒有價值——可能是後續沒接住的問題。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.pattern: This idea that [X] just seems like a fantasy to me.
cards.quote: And so from my perspective, this idea that this just completely destroys the differentiation of these business process SaaS applications just seems like a fantasy, a crazy fantasy.
cards.zh: 所以就我的角度來看，「這會徹底摧毀這類商業流程 SaaS 的差異化」這種說法，聽起來根本是幻想，而且是很扯的幻想。
cards.why: 強度極高的否定，但開頭 from my perspective 與 this idea that 兩層緩衝，讓你打的是「這個說法」而不是「說這話的人」。想在英文會議上表達強烈不同意，這是安全的最高檔。
swaps: That story doesn't hold up for me.
I think that's wishful thinking.
From where I sit, that's not how it plays out.
cards.pmNote: AI 讓做出「表單＋資料庫」變便宜，反而強化既有系統的地位，因為 lock-in 來自流程不是介面。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.pattern: Nobody wants to hear it, but really it's just the hard work of [不性感的事].
cards.quote: Nobody wants to hear it. Everybody wants to just think about these really cool models and how smart they are. But really it's just the hard work of getting really good data to the LLMs.
cards.zh: 沒有人想聽這個。大家都只想談那些很酷的模型有多聰明。但說到底，這就是把好資料餵給 LLM 的苦工。
cards.why: 先承認這個訊息不討喜（Nobody wants to hear it），聽眾的防衛就會鬆掉，然後你才有空間講出真正無聊卻正確的結論。報壞消息前的最佳暖身。
swaps: This is the unglamorous part, but…
Nobody likes this answer, and it's still the answer.
It's less exciting than it sounds: it's mostly plumbing.
cards.pmNote: AI 產品 90% 的力氣花在資料管線：拿到對的、即時的、結構化的資料，模型本身反而可替換。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.quote: A decision with too little data is fatal. A decision that takes too long and collects too much data is also fatal. So it's about trying to find the balance.
cards.zh: 資料太少就下決策，是致命的；拖太久、蒐集太多資料才決策，一樣致命。所以重點是抓到那個平衡。
cards.why: 用完全對稱的兩句把兩端都封死，聽眾就不會把你的話當成偏向哪一邊。談取捨時，先證明你看得到兩種失敗，你的中間值才有說服力。
swaps: Too early is a guess; too late is a miss.
Both under- and over-researching kill you.
The risk cuts both ways.
cards.pmNote: Colin Powell 的 30/70 法則：低於三成資訊就決策太魯莽，等到七成以上才決策已經太慢。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.pattern: If you let your calendar rule you, nothing good will happen.
cards.quote: One is that if you let your calendar rule you, then nothing good will happen. It's really hard to be successful unless you find a way to force that to happen.
cards.zh: 第一，如果你讓行事曆牽著你走，就不會有什麼好事發生。除非你想辦法強迫它發生，否則很難做出成績。
cards.why: 把「拒絕會議」這件難以啟齒的事，講成一條普遍法則，你就不必針對任何一場會議說不。let X rule you 是很有畫面的說法，比 be too busy 有力。
swaps: My calendar can't be the thing deciding my priorities.
If I don't block it, it doesn't happen.
I'm protecting time for outside-in work.
cards.pmNote: 把 80% 思考時間留給「公司外面的世界」是理想值，實務上要靠固定的行事曆保護區才守得住。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.pattern: It should have been obvious, and we should have been able to call a spade a spade and speak truth to power.
cards.quote: I feel really bad because I'm like, it should have been obvious. We should have been able to call a spade a spade and I guess speak truth to power.
cards.zh: 我到現在還是很懊惱，因為這件事本來就該一眼看穿。我們應該有辦法直話直說，向上把真話講出來。
cards.why: 承擔錯誤時用 we should have been able to（我們本來做得到）而不是找藉口，語氣真誠又不自我鞭笞。call a spade a spade（有話直說）與 speak truth to power（對權力說真話）都是高分片語。
swaps: We should have named it earlier.
I should have said the quiet part out loud.
That was on us — we all saw it and stayed quiet.
cards.pmNote: 殭屍產品（zombie product）最貴的成本不是失敗，而是沒人願意在第六個月宣布它死亡。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.quote: It was pretty obvious after six months this thing was a bit of a zombie product walking, and the least I could have done is said, "This thing is dead." We could have called it dead way earlier.
cards.zh: 半年後就很明顯這是個活死人產品了，我至少可以做的，就是講一句：這個東西已經死了。我們早就該宣布它死亡。
cards.why: call it dead 是英語裡宣布終止的乾脆說法（來自急診室宣告死亡），比 we should sunset this 更果斷。報壞消息時，用最短的句子把結論放在最前面反而最有尊嚴。
swaps: Let's call it: this isn't working.
I think we should sunset it now, not in six months.
Time to pull the plug.
cards.pmNote: 砍產品要設早期的 kill criteria，否則團隊會一路投資到有人願意付錢才被迫面對。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.pattern: It's not often I use a product and think: this is 10x better than anything before it.
cards.quote: It's not often I use a product and I'm like, "This thing is 10 times better than anything that's come before it." It's one of those for me.
cards.zh: 我很少用到一個產品會覺得「這東西比之前所有的東西好上十倍」。這個對我來說就是其中之一。
cards.why: 稱讚前先講「我很少這樣」，讚美的可信度立刻上升——因為你先證明自己標準很高。這是給推薦、給肯定時最值錢的鋪陳。
swaps: I don't say this often, but…
Rarely does something clear that bar for me.
I'm hard to impress here, and this did it.
cards.pmNote: 10x better 是判斷產品能否取代既有習慣的粗略門檻，微幅改善通常換不動使用者。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.pattern: My career has been a bit like a bingo card — I've been filling in the boxes I didn't have.
cards.quote: Looking back, my career has been a little bit like a bingo card. I've always been looking to fill in boxes I didn't have filled because I felt like that would make me a better professional.
cards.zh: 回頭看，我的職涯有點像一張賓果卡。我一直在補那些還沒被填滿的格子，因為我覺得那會讓我變成更好的專業工作者。
cards.why: 用一個具體比喻把看起來很亂的資歷講成有意識的策略。面試被問「你的經歷怎麼跳這麼多」時，一個好的比喻比逐段解釋有效太多。
swaps: I've been collecting the experiences I was missing.
Each move filled a gap I knew I had.
I optimized for range, not for title.
cards.pmNote: 刻意選擇「相鄰但不同」的職位（不同銷售模式、不同使用者、不同技術層）會讓你在新問題上有更多可比對的樣式。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.pattern: I've rarely regretted going deep on something that isn't quite my job.
cards.quote: I've rarely regretted going deep in something that isn't quite my job. The worst case scenario is I've learned something new that I will never use.
cards.zh: 去深入研究那些不完全屬於我職責的東西，我幾乎沒後悔過。最糟的情況也不過是學到一個以後用不到的東西。
cards.why: I've rarely regretted… 是談自己選擇時很成熟的語氣：不吹噓成果，只講「我幾乎沒後悔」，再自己算出最壞情況有多便宜。談職涯決策時這種風險語言很有份量。
swaps: The downside is small; the upside is occasionally huge.
I've never lost by understanding the next function over.
Worst case I learn something I never use.
cards.pmNote: 最好的產品人不是 T 型而是「塗鴉型」：在好幾個不同領域都能往下鑽三層，遇到問題時能從別的角度辨識模式。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.quote: I often think about this phrase, which is people don't care what you know until they know that you care.
cards.zh: 我常想到這句話：在別人知道你在乎之前，他們不會在乎你懂什麼。
cards.why: 用 know / care 的對仗把一整套影響力理論壓成一句。這種押韻式格言在英語職場很容易被記住、被轉述，是把觀點植入別人腦中的高效載體。
swaps: Trust first, then the argument lands.
Relationship before rightness.
Being right isn't enough on its own.
cards.pmNote: 跨部門推動事情時，先確認對方的 outcome 和 incentive，你的資料才會被聽進去。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.pattern: People only do what their incentives tell them to do. You get what you set out to measure.
cards.quote: In economics, people only do what their incentives told them to do. Broadly speaking, that is what they do. You get what you set out to measure.
cards.zh: 在經濟學裡，人只會做他們的誘因叫他們做的事。大致上就是這樣。你量什麼，就會得到什麼。
cards.why: 先借一個學科當靠山（in economics），再用 broadly speaking 幫自己留退路，最後收在一句好記的結論。這種「權威＋緩衝＋金句」三段式，是把主張變成共識的標準結構。
swaps: Show me the incentive and I'll show you the outcome.
If nobody's measured on it, it won't happen.
Behaviour follows incentives, not memos.
cards.pmNote: 沒有人的 KPI 綁在終端使用者的成功上，PLG 就只會是興趣（a hobby），不會變成成果。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

cards.pattern: By definition, it's only [X] if it seems like it isn't
cards.quote: By definition it is only a tarpit if it seems like it's not. If it's just a regular idea that is hard, that is not a tarpit.
cards.zh: 照定義來說，只有在它「看起來不像陷阱」的時候，它才是陷阱。如果只是一個大家都知道很難的點子，那不叫陷阱。
cards.why: 用「By definition」把定義權搶回來，先重新界定名詞，再讓對方的反駁自動失效——這是資深 PM 面對「我覺得這個沒那麼糟」時最有力的一招：不吵事實，改吵定義。
swaps: By definition, X only counts as Y if...
The whole point of calling it X is that...
cards.pmNote: tarpit idea（焦油坑點子）＝很多人想得到、又能拿到早期正面回饋、但十年來沒人做成的題目。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

cards.pattern: I completely agree with [對方], but to look at this from a different frame, [你的角度]
cards.quote: I completely agree with what Gustav said, but to look at this from a different frame, I think is that the founders lose hope.
cards.zh: 我完全同意 Gustav 講的，但換一個框架來看，我覺得真正的原因是創辦人失去了希望。
cards.why: 先百分之百同意，再說「換個框架看」——不是反駁，而是把同一件事移到另一個座標系。台灣人常直接說 But I think...，聽起來像否定；frame 這個字讓你在不否定任何人的情況下換掉整場討論的軸。
swaps: to look at it from another angle
if you reframe it slightly
another way to cut this is
cards.pmNote: 同一組事實可以有多種 problem framing，框架選錯，後面所有解法都會歪。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

cards.pattern: If you look at [全部案例], the underlying theme is that [共同結構]
cards.quote: The way to summarize that is if you look at all the startup stories that we have at YC and all the companies we funded over all the years, the underlying theme is that rationally the founder should have given up at some point.
cards.zh: 要總結的話：如果你看 YC 所有的創業故事、這些年投的所有公司，底下共通的主題是——照理性判斷，創辦人早就該在某個時間點放棄了。
cards.why: 「the underlying theme is」是把一堆零散案例壓成一句洞見的收束句型。台灣人講案例常一路平鋪，缺的就是這種「所以底層的東西是什麼」的收尾動作。
swaps: the common thread is
what they all have in common is
the pattern underneath all of it is
cards.pmNote: 從 N 個案例抽出 pattern，是資深工作者跟資淺最明顯的差別。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

cards.pattern: The anti-pattern I see is [常見錯誤做法]
cards.quote: And so the anti-pattern I see is there are lots of founders that are very familiar with your awesome work.
cards.zh: 所以我常看到的反模式是：很多創辦人非常熟你那些很棒的內容（然後在錯的階段照做）。
cards.why: anti-pattern 是矽谷用來「批評一種做法但不指名任何人」的安全詞。你不是說「你做錯了」，你是說「這是一種已知的錯誤模式」，被指的人比較容易接受。
swaps: the failure mode I keep seeing is
the trap here is
where I see teams go wrong is
cards.pmNote: 把個案講成 anti-pattern，回饋才會變成組織知識而不是人身批評。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

cards.pattern: The prompt here is to [行動方向]
cards.quote: And so the prompt here is to try to go more off the beaten path either from your personal experience, like in the case of Brex and Retool or Whatnot.
cards.zh: 所以這裡給你的思考提示是：試著走出那條被踩爛的路，從你自己的經驗裡挖，像 Brex、Retool、Whatnot 那樣。
cards.why: 把「建議」講成 prompt（思考提示），語氣從命令降級成觸發器——你不是規定方向，你只是丟一個引子。給資深同事或創辦人建議時特別好用。
swaps: the nudge here is to
the question I'd plant is
what I'd have you go explore is
cards.pmNote: off the beaten path＝避開所有人資訊來源相同而產生的同質題目。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

cards.pattern: My tactical advice is [先做 A] versus [B]
cards.quote: I think so many folks don't know where to begin on starting a startup, and my tactical advice is start doing customer validation first versus building a PowerPoint deck.
cards.zh: 很多人根本不知道創業要從哪裡開始，我很具體的建議是：先去做客戶驗證，而不是先做一份簡報。
cards.why: tactical advice 這個標籤先幫聽眾降低期待（我不是要給你大道理），再用 A versus B 把「該做的」跟「你正在做的」直接對撞。比 You should... 少了說教味。
swaps: the practical move is to
concretely, I'd start with X rather than Y
cards.pmNote: 先預售、先驗證，再寫程式；customer validation 排在募資與美化簡報之前。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

cards.pattern: Put yourself in the shoes of [對方] and just imagine what their life is like
cards.quote: Maybe my best advice here is for founders to put themselves in the shoes of investors and just imagine what their life is like and how if you are in their shoes you would make decisions.
cards.zh: 我最好的建議大概是：創辦人去站在投資人的位置上，想像他們的日子長什麼樣、如果換成你會怎麼做決定。
cards.why: 解釋「為什麼對方會拒絕你」時，不講對方的動機（那會變成猜測與抱怨），而是請對方自己走進去演一次。這是化解怨氣、把情緒問題變成結構問題的標準手法。
swaps: flip it around and imagine you're them
run the exercise from their side of the table
cards.pmNote: 投資人說 no 多半不是不信你，而是他一年只投得下幾個。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

cards.pattern: And this is the big but, [關鍵轉折]
cards.quote: But, and this is the big but, no one has this at the early stages when they don't have a good idea and they don't have customers and it's objectively not working.
cards.zh: 但是——而且這是很大的一個「但是」——在最早期、還沒有好點子、沒有客戶、客觀上根本不 work 的時候，沒有人會有那種信念。
cards.why: 先用「this is the big but」替接下來的轉折立牌子，聽眾知道重點來了、會提高注意力。這種先預告再講的手法，在英文會議裡是掌控節奏的關鍵，台灣人幾乎不會用。
swaps: here's the caveat though
and this is the important part
with one big asterisk
cards.pmNote: 信念是結果不是前提——先有一點成績，信念才長出來。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

cards.pattern: I'm not saying [X] doesn't matter, of course it does. But [你的真正立場]
cards.quote: I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually. But trying to be super pedantic about market size when it's a pre-seed company, it's just not something I'd put a lot of thought.
cards.zh: 我不是說市場總有一天要夠大這件事不重要，當然重要。但在一家 pre-seed 公司還在糾結市場規模算得多精確，我不會花太多心思在上面。
cards.why: 先把對方的立場完整交還（of course it does），再限縮到「時機」而不是「對錯」。這是英文異議最常用的降溫結構：不否定命題，只否定它現在適用。
swaps: it's not that X is wrong, it's that it's premature
X matters eventually, just not now
cards.pmNote: 同一條建議在 seed 跟 series B 可以完全相反，先問這是給哪個階段的。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

cards.pattern: I'm not trying to diss anyone, but [批評]
cards.quote: I'm not trying to diss anyone, but you'll see things that become fashionable really quickly because someone found success in this unfashionable space and then it becomes fashionable.
cards.zh: 我不是要酸誰，但你會看到有些東西紅得很快——因為有人在一個沒人做的領域做成了，然後它就變成流行。
cards.why: diss 是很口語的「酸／貶低」。先聲明「我不是要酸誰」，等於買一張批評的保險。台灣人講到批評時常整段吞掉，這個前綴能讓你照講不誤又不樹敵。
swaps: no shade to anyone, but
I don't mean this as a knock on anyone, but
cards.pmNote: 題材的 fashionable 程度跟報酬率通常成反比。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

cards.pattern: I'm just trying to argue that [主張] is actively not helpful
cards.quote: I'm just trying to argue this advice applied to a startup that's too early is actively not helpful.
cards.zh: 我只是想主張：把這套建議套在太早期的新創身上，是「主動有害」而不只是沒用。
cards.why: 兩個關鍵：I'm just trying to argue 把強硬主張降級成一個論點（留餘地），actively not helpful 又把「沒幫助」升級成「有害」。一句話裡同時軟化語氣、強化內容，這是母語者的高階操作。
swaps: my claim is narrower than that: ...
not just unhelpful — counterproductive
cards.pmNote: 早期公司做 A/B test 與成長駭客，通常是拿後期工具解前期問題。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

cards.pattern: This is a nuanced question and it's hard to say something that'll actually be useful, but here's a couple of thoughts
cards.quote: I think this is a nuanced question and it's hard for me to say something on a podcast that'll actually be useful to people, but here's a couple of thoughts.
cards.zh: 我覺得這是個很有層次的問題，要在 podcast 上講出真的對別人有用的東西很難，不過我有幾個想法。
cards.why: 承認問題複雜、承認自己給不出通解，然後還是給——這是資深的訊號。台灣人遇到這種題目常直接給一個過度簡化的答案，或整個推掉；正確做法是「降低承諾、照樣交付」。
swaps: there's no clean answer here, but a couple of things I'd look at
I'll caveat this heavily, but
cards.pmNote: bespoke advice：需要看個案的問題，講通則反而誤導人。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

cards.pattern: I can't promise it works for everyone, but in [具體情境] it worked really well
cards.quote: Yeah, I mean, I can't promise that works for everyone, but again, in the very bespoke situation with Rujul, it worked really well.
cards.zh: 我不能保證這對每個人都有效，但在 Rujul 那個很特定的情況下，效果非常好。
cards.why: 先自己標出證據的邊界，再講成果——反而更可信。台灣人分享成功案例時常無意間過度推論（所以大家都該這樣做），這句是最短的免責＋可信度加成。
swaps: your mileage may vary, but
n of one, but it worked
I wouldn't generalize it, but in that case
cards.pmNote: 單一案例可以當靈感，不能當通則。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

cards.pattern: Just to pull on this thread a little bit more, [追問]
cards.quote: Just to pull on this thread a little bit more, what is the general advice you share there for people that also don't want to die?
cards.zh: 順著這條線再拉一下：對那些也不想死掉的人，你通常會給什麼建議？
cards.why: pull on this thread＝順著剛剛那條線再挖深。比 Can you say more? 更精準，也對對方是一種肯定（你剛剛講的那條線值得挖）。開會時追問而不打斷氣氛的最佳句。
swaps: staying on that thread for a second
I want to go one level deeper on that
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

cards.pattern: Many people quickly gravitate to [表象]. But we think about it as [本質]
cards.quote: When we talk about pricing, many people quickly gravitate to dollar figures. That's just a price point. But when we think about price, we think about it as a measure.
cards.zh: 談定價的時候，大部分人馬上跳到金額。那只是一個價格點。但我們看「價格」是把它當成一種度量。
cards.why: 重新定義一個大家以為自己懂的詞：先描述大眾的直覺反應（gravitate to），再說「但我們是這樣看的」。這是整場策略對話裡最值錢的三十秒，因為定義換了，後面的結論就跟著換。
swaps: most people jump straight to X. We treat it as Y
the instinct is to think X — we think of it as Y
cards.pmNote: 價格是價值的度量單位，不是一個數字；先問客戶願不願意付，再決定收多少。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

cards.pattern: It's not just about [大家熟的概念], it's about [升級版概念]
cards.quote: I think that the issue is, it's not just about product market fit, it is about achieving a product market pricing fit.
cards.zh: 我覺得問題在於：重點不只是 product-market fit，而是要做到 product-market-pricing fit。
cards.why: 在一個大家已經接受的名詞上加一個字，就造出自己的概念——這是矽谷造詞法的核心。用「it's not just X, it is Y」的節奏，聽眾會覺得你只是把他既有的知識往前推了一格，接受度極高。
swaps: X is table stakes; the real bar is Y
everyone talks about X — the version that matters is Y
cards.pmNote: 沒有把價格放進 PMF 驗證，你聽到的都是你想聽的。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

cards.pattern: You don't have a choice whether [X] happens. The only thing in your control is when
cards.quote: As an entrepreneur, a company, you actually don't have a choice whether you'll have a pricing conversation with your customer. The only thing in your control is when you will have it.
cards.zh: 身為創業者或公司，你其實沒有「要不要跟客戶談價格」的選擇權。你唯一能控制的是「什麼時候談」。
cards.why: 把 whether 的辯論直接關掉，只留 when——對方一旦接受前提，就已經站在你這邊了。這是說服句型裡效率最高的一種：不爭論該不該做，只討論早做還晚做。
swaps: this conversation is happening either way — the only question is when
it's not if, it's when
cards.pmNote: willingness-to-pay 對話越早做，越能反過來設計產品。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

cards.pattern: When we take a step back, there are literally only [N] types of [X]
cards.quote: When we talk about pricing strategies, we hear many buzzwords, and it's irrelevant. So when we take a step back and look at it, there's literally only three types of pricing strategies.
cards.zh: 談定價策略的時候會聽到一堆流行詞，那些都不重要。退一步看，定價策略其實就只有三種。
cards.why: 先把噪音掃掉（buzzwords, irrelevant），再宣布一個很小的數字。「literally only three」給聽眾一個可掌握的世界，是策略簡報最有效的開場。
swaps: strip away the jargon and there are really only three
at the end of the day it collapses into three options
cards.pmNote: 定價策略只有三種：skimming（高開低走）、penetration（低價衝量）、maximization（中間最大化）。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

cards.pattern: The point is not [選哪個], it's [執行你選的那個]
cards.quote: The point is not about picking, just picking one, but it's about executing the one that you actually pick.
cards.zh: 重點不是「選哪一個」，而是你選了之後有沒有真的執行到底。
cards.why: 當團隊在幾個選項上鬼打牆時，用「the point is not X, it's Y」把討論的重心整個搬走。這是主持策略會議最實用的一句——不裁決選項，直接換掉爭論的題目。
swaps: the choice matters less than the follow-through
any of these can work — what kills us is half-executing
cards.pmNote: 策略即取捨，但取捨的價值來自貫徹，不是來自比較。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

cards.pattern: How you [做法] is way more important than how much [量]
cards.quote: We usually say how you charge is way more important than how much you charge.
cards.zh: 我們常說：「怎麼收費」比「收多少」重要得多。
cards.why: 用同一個動詞（charge）做兩種問法的對比，句子短、對仗強、聽一次就記住。這種 how vs how much 的結構可以搬到很多場合：how you ship it vs how much you ship。
swaps: the model matters more than the number
we spend too long on the number and not enough on the metric
cards.pmNote: 計價單位（per seat / per mile / per tracked user）決定客戶怎麼感受價值。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

cards.pattern: The number one lesson — and I hope this is the biggest takeaway — is you cannot [X] without [Y]
cards.quote: Literally, for your product folks, the number one lesson, and I hope this is the biggest takeaway for your audience, you cannot prioritize a product roadmap without having a willingness to pay conversation.
cards.zh: 對做產品的人來說，第一號的教訓——我希望這是聽眾最大的收穫——就是：沒有做過付費意願對話，你根本沒辦法排產品路線圖的優先順序。
cards.why: 中間插入的「and I hope this is the biggest takeaway」是在替聽眾標重點，等於口頭版的螢光筆。長段落結束前用它，資訊才不會被沖走。
swaps: if you remember one thing from today, make it this
everything else is optional — this isn't
cards.pmNote: 20% 的功能帶來 80% 的付費意願，先找出那 20%。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

cards.pattern: Don't mix up [A] with [B] — those are very different things
cards.quote: Please note that don't mix transparency and fairness with being predictable. Those are very different things.
cards.zh: 請注意，不要把「透明與公平」跟「可預測」混為一談。這是兩件很不一樣的事。
cards.why: 會議裡最有價值的插話，往往不是提出新意見，而是拆開兩個被混用的概念。這句的第二段「Those are very different things」很重要——它給你的區分一個明確的收尾，不會被當成挑字眼。
swaps: let's not conflate X with Y
those two often get bundled, but they pull in different directions
cards.pmNote: 客戶要「公平」不等於要「帳單金額穩定」，兩者會導向完全不同的計價模型。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

cards.pattern: It's not about [對方擔心的壞事], it's just about [你真正在做的事]
cards.quote: So this kind of behavioral framing and nudging becomes important, it's not about deceiving your customers, but it's just about framing the products in such a way that it also appeals to the irrational side of the brain.
cards.zh: 這種行為框架跟推力很重要——它不是要騙客戶，而是把產品呈現得也能打到大腦不理性的那一面。
cards.why: 在對方開口質疑之前，先把最可能的道德指控講出來並否認（pre-emption）。這是提出爭議性做法時的標準保護動作：你先講，殺傷力就沒了。
swaps: to be clear, this isn't about tricking anyone
before anyone asks — this isn't manipulation, it's framing
cards.pmNote: 誘餌方案（decoy）與心理門檻是包裝手法，不是欺騙，但界線要自己守。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

cards.pattern: Before you [讓步], think about what value you can exchange to justify it
cards.quote: So before you price discount, think about what value can you exchange to actually justify that price discount.
cards.zh: 所以在你打折之前，先想想你可以「交換」掉什麼價值，來讓這個折扣說得過去。
cards.why: 把「讓步」重新定義成「交換」——這一個字的替換，就是談判裡守住價格完整性的關鍵。任何要求你讓步的場合都能用。
swaps: if we move on price, what do we get back?
no concession without an exchange
cards.pmNote: price integrity：折扣要用「拿掉功能」來換，否則折扣價六個月後就變成新定價。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

cards.pattern: Most people who claim to have a [X] strategy are only doing half of it
cards.quote: 90% of customers or people who we meet who claim to have a land and expand strategy are only landing. They're not expanding because they gave their farm away in the land.
cards.zh: 我們遇到宣稱自己有 land and expand 策略的人，九成其實只有 land。他們沒辦法 expand，因為一開始就把家當全給出去了。
cards.why: 挑戰假設最漂亮的方式：不說「你們沒有策略」，而是說「你們只做了策略的前半段」。對方沒有被否定，但缺口被指出來了。give the farm away（把家當全送出去）也是很道地的說法。
swaps: everyone says they do X — most stop halfway
we're landing fine; we've never actually expanded
cards.pmNote: land and expand：入門版給太多，就沒有東西留給後面的升級。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

cards.pattern: If you take that viewpoint, then [結論]. This is my strong-held belief
cards.quote: So if you take that viewpoint, then pricing needs to sit in the product function. This is my strong-held belief, one that probably won't change now.
cards.zh: 如果你接受那個看法，那定價就必須放在產品這一側。這是我很堅定的信念，大概不會再改了。
cards.why: 先把結論掛在一個前提上（if you take that viewpoint），再表態這是自己的堅定信念——條件句讓你不強迫別人，後半句讓你不顯得沒立場。台灣人常只有其中一半：不是太軟就是太硬。
swaps: follow that logic and you end up at...
that's a hill I'll die on
cards.pmNote: 定價該歸產品還是財務，取決於你認為定價是「防守」還是「設計」。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

cards.pattern: We can go deep into this — you can pull me back or ask me to go deeper
cards.quote: Yeah, we can go deep into this and you can pull me back or ask me to go deeper, whatever. It doesn't matter.
cards.zh: 這題我們可以講得很深，你隨時可以把我拉回來，或叫我再講細一點，都行。
cards.why: 在長回答之前先把「打斷我」的權力交給對方——這是英文會議裡展現從容的高階動作，也順便解決了自己講太久的風險。pull me back 這個說法台灣人幾乎想不到。
swaps: stop me whenever
wave me off if this is too much detail
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

cards.pattern: I'll try to see what I can talk about without getting too detailed
cards.quote: Sure. I will try to see what I can talk about without getting too detailed, but the thesis of the book is...
cards.zh: 好，我盡量在不講太細的前提下講一點，這本書的主軸是……
cards.why: 被問到還不能公開的東西時，不要說 I can't talk about that（會冷場），而是先答應要講、同時劃出深度上限。答應＋設限，是保密與合作之間的最佳平衡。
swaps: I can share the shape of it, not the numbers
let me stay at the level I'm allowed to
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

cards.pattern: It comes down to not [表面動作], but how deeply you understand [問題]
cards.quote: And so I think a lot of it comes down to not the things you try, but how you deeply understand the problem that's preventing someone from using your product effectively.
cards.zh: 所以我覺得關鍵不在你試了哪些招，而在你有多深地搞懂「是什麼擋住使用者用好你的產品」。
cards.why: 「comes down to not X, but Y」是把功勞從戰術移到理解的萬用句。當團隊一直在討論要做哪個實驗時，用這句把大家拉回問題本身。
swaps: the win wasn't the tactic, it was the diagnosis
less about what we tried, more about what we finally understood
cards.pmNote: 轉換率卡住時，先做質化訪談找出真正的疑慮，再設計實驗。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

cards.pattern: Your two big levers on [目標] are [A] and [B]
cards.quote: I mean your two big levers on driving a conversion are increase desire, reduce friction.
cards.zh: 驅動轉換率，你只有兩根大槓桿：提高慾望、降低阻力。
cards.why: lever（槓桿）是英文商業語彙裡描述「可操作變因」的核心字。把一堆選項壓成兩根槓桿，是讓團隊立刻能行動的講法——句子越短，執行力越高。
swaps: there are really only two dials here
everything we do falls into one of two buckets
cards.pmNote: 轉換率＝慾望 ÷ 阻力；多數團隊只做後者。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

cards.pattern: What we're trying to do is build a flywheel around [核心價值]
cards.quote: And that ultimately, we understand what makes it a must-have product. And then what we're trying to do is build a flywheel around that must-have value.
cards.zh: 最終我們要弄清楚是什麼讓它變成「非有不可」的產品，然後圍繞那個非有不可的價值，去打造一個飛輪。
cards.why: flywheel（飛輪）是英文商業裡描繪「會自己越轉越快的機制」的標準意象。用 build a flywheel around X 講願景，比 We want to grow 具體十倍，而且暗示成長是機制而不是努力。
swaps: build a loop around that value
make that moment compound
cards.pmNote: 成長飛輪：啟用 → 參與 → 推薦 → 再啟用，圍繞 must-have 價值設計。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

cards.quote: So if I got a 37%, am I going to be like, "Oh no, this would be impossible?" It's more nuanced than that.
cards.zh: 如果我拿到 37%，我會覺得「完蛋、沒救了」嗎？沒那麼一刀切。
cards.why: 「It's more nuanced than that」是英文會議裡最有教養的反對句：你沒有說對方錯，你說的是對方的版本太粗。四個字就能把一個二元問題重新打開。
swaps: it's not that binary
there's more texture to it than that
I'd resist a hard line there
cards.pmNote: PMF 的 40% 門檻是參考點不是及格線。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

cards.pattern: Just one quick interjection there — [補充]
cards.quote: Just one quick interjection there is that when I coined growth hacking, I did not think of it as a bunch of one-off hacks.
cards.zh: 這邊我快速插一句：我當初造 growth hacking 這個詞的時候，並不是指一堆一次性的小花招。
cards.why: 插話最安全的三件事：宣告很短（quick）、宣告只有一個（one）、指定位置（there）。台灣人最怕在英文會議插話，這句把打斷包裝成「幫忙補位」，幾乎不會被討厭。
swaps: quick footnote on that
one small correction before we move on
can I jump in with one thing?
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

cards.pattern: Maybe I picked the wrong [X], but at least it [正面效果]
cards.quote: And so maybe I picked the wrong term in calling it growth hacking, but I think it at least opened the conversation to getting more people thinking about growth in a different way.
cards.zh: 所以也許我當初取 growth hacking 這個名字是取錯了，但至少它打開了對話，讓更多人開始用不同的方式想成長這件事。
cards.why: 認錯 + 保住成果的雙段結構。承認的是「用詞」這個小的、可讓的部分，守住的是「影響力」這個大的部分。這比整段道歉或整段辯護都成熟。
swaps: I'd name it differently today, but
the label aged badly — the idea didn't
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

cards.pattern: I think it's [評價], but maybe I'm just being protective of my original idea
cards.quote: So I think it's an unnecessary addition, but maybe I'm just being protective of my original idea.
cards.zh: 我覺得那是多此一舉的補充，不過也可能只是我在護著自己原本的想法啦。
cards.why: 先講反對意見，再自己點出自己可能有的偏見——這叫 disclosing your bias。奇妙的是，這反而讓你的反對更有份量，因為聽的人知道你已經自己檢查過一輪了。
swaps: take this with a grain of salt, it's my own framework
I have an obvious conflict of interest here, but
cards.pmNote: RICE 的 R（reach）Sean 認為已經含在 ICE 的 I（impact）裡。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

cards.pattern: If there's anything I'd be accused of, it would be [自己的弱點]
cards.quote: And so I think if there's anything that I would be accused of, it would be being over simplifying things.
cards.zh: 如果說我有什麼會被人批評的，大概就是我把事情簡化過頭了。
cards.why: 把最可能的批評自己先講出來，而且用「被指控」這種略帶自嘲的框架——對方之後再提就沒有力道了。這是英文裡處理已知弱點的標準先手。
swaps: the fair criticism of my approach is
if you want to knock this, knock it on X
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

cards.pattern: Credit [人] with this — [事情經過]
cards.quote: Credit our CEO with this, that I shared the data with him and he basically told the product team, "We are putting a complete freeze on the product development roadmap."
cards.zh: 這件事要歸功給我們執行長：我把數據給他看，他就直接跟產品團隊說「產品路線圖全面凍結」。
cards.why: 在講自己成功案例的中途，用一句 Credit X with this 把功勞明確分出去——不只是禮貌，也讓你的敘述更可信（願意分功的人聽起來沒在膨風）。
swaps: that call was hers, not mine
hat tip to X for that one
cards.pmNote: 註冊→實際使用率從 5% 拉到 50%，同樣的通路花費才從月 1 萬美金變成月 100 萬。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

cards.pattern: I don't want to overstate it, but [你的貢獻]
cards.quote: Yeah, I mean, I don't want to overstate it, but they basically said all the early stuff we did to grow TikTok was based on your writing.
cards.zh: 我不想講得太誇張，不過他們基本上是說：TikTok 早期做的成長工作，都是照你寫的東西做的。
cards.why: 談自己的成績時最難的就是分寸。I don't want to overstate it 先自降一格，後面再把事實原封不動講完——聽起來既不吹牛也沒縮小。績效面談的萬用開場。
swaps: I won't claim more than my share, but
I had a hand in it — how big a hand, others can judge
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

cards.pattern: At first I gave the smart-ass answer '[舊立場]'. But I started finding that [新發現]
cards.quote: And at first I gave the smart-ass answer, "I don't care what they say, I care what they do." But I started finding that my experiments were so much better the more I talked to customers.
cards.zh: 一開始我回了一句欠揍的話：「我不在乎他們說什麼，我在乎他們做什麼。」但後來我發現，我越常跟客戶聊，實驗設計就越好。
cards.why: 改變立場的最佳講法：把舊的自己演出來（連當時的臭屁語氣一起），再讓證據把自己翻過來。自嘲式的 smart-ass answer 讓「我錯了」不再需要痛苦地講出口。
swaps: my glib answer back then was...
I used to push back with X — until I noticed Y
cards.pmNote: 質化與量化混用，實驗品質才會提升。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

cards.pattern: If you give a team [X], they'll take [X]. If you give them [Y], they'll take [Y]
cards.quote: But I think it's really important for it to be a time capped group conversation. And if you give a team 30 days, they'll take 30 days. If you give them six months, they'll take six months.
cards.zh: 我覺得這一定要是一場有時間上限的團體討論。你給團隊 30 天，他們就會用滿 30 天；你給六個月，他們就會用滿六個月。
cards.why: 用重複同一句型的對稱句把一個抽象的管理道理講到不可反駁。time-capped（設上限的）這個形容詞也很值得學——它把「限制」講成一種設計，不是不信任。
swaps: let's timebox this to 30 minutes
work expands to fill the time you give it
cards.pmNote: 北極星指標的討論給團隊 30 分鐘就夠，前提是原料與檢核清單齊備。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

cards.pattern: It's a great accelerant when it's already working, but it can't fix [根本問題]
cards.quote: To me, I think it's a great accelerant when it's already working, but it can't fix it if people don't want to talk about your product.
cards.zh: 對我來說，那在本來就跑得動的時候是很好的加速器，但如果根本沒人想談論你的產品，它救不了你。
cards.why: accelerant（加速劑）這個字精準劃出一種工具的能力邊界：它只能放大既有的東西。當老闆要求「加個推薦機制就會成長」時，這句是最有禮貌的擋箭牌。
swaps: it amplifies what's there; it doesn't create it
that's an accelerator, not an engine
cards.pmNote: Dropbox 推薦計畫成功的前提是它本來就有很強的口碑。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

cards.pattern: That becomes a bit of a strategic conversation of whether we want [A] or [B]
cards.quote: I think that becomes a bit of a strategic conversation of do we want to have a better chance of surviving, going after a niche that we know we can serve well?
cards.zh: 我覺得這時候就變成一個策略層級的討論了：我們是要提高存活機率、去打一個我們服務得很好的利基市場嗎？
cards.why: 當一個問題其實沒有正確答案時，最好的動作是把它「升級」成策略對話，而不是硬給答案。這句同時保護了你（我不會亂拍板）跟團隊（這件事值得認真討論）。
swaps: that's a leadership call, not a data call
this one's above my pay grade to decide alone
cards.pmNote: 小而狂熱的族群 vs 大而溫吞的族群，選哪個取決於你募了多少錢。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

cards.pattern: Why would I possibly mortgage [長期資產] for [短期小利]?
cards.quote: I had this reputation that's, like I randomly pulled the number and said, my reputation worth $5 million. Why would I possibly mortgage that reputation for $20,000?
cards.zh: 我隨便抓個數字，說我的名聲值五百萬美金。那我幹嘛為了兩萬塊去把這個名聲抵押掉？
cards.why: mortgage（抵押）把「短期得利、長期受損」的抽象概念變成金融動作，聽的人立刻感覺到代價。談任何長短期取捨（技術債、砍測試、對客戶硬拗）都能套。
swaps: that's borrowing against next year
we'd be trading a dollar of trust for a dime of revenue
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

cards.pattern: I want to put a pin in that and come back to it
cards.quote: Okay. I want to put a pin on that and come back to that because a really important topic.
cards.zh: 好，這個我先插個旗、等一下再回來講，因為這題真的很重要。
cards.why: 會議控場最實用的一句：暫時擱置一個好議題，但同時肯定它的重要性，讓被打斷的人不覺得被忽略。標準說法是 put a pin in it（Lenny 講成 on that，口語常見）。
swaps: let's park that for now
I'll come back to that — flagging it
let's table that
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

cards.pattern: [方案] might be a solution, but it can never be a problem on its own
cards.quote: You're never trying to solve a problem of simplifying. And simplifying might be a solution, but it can never be a problem on its own.
cards.zh: 你不會是在解決「簡化」這個問題。簡化可能是一種解法，但它本身永遠不會是問題。
cards.why: 這是整批語料裡最鋒利的一句。它給了你一把刀，去切開所有「把解法當成目標」的路線圖項目——把 simplifying 換成 redesign、migrate、AI 化，句子照樣成立。
swaps: that's a solution wearing a problem's clothes
what's the problem that would make this the answer?
cards.pmNote: roadmap 上寫「簡化 onboarding」＝沒定義問題；要寫的是「新用戶在第三步搞不懂要做什麼」。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.pattern: If you ever have a line item on your roadmap that says [X], please cross it out
cards.quote: But if you ever have a line item on your roadmap that says simplified onboarding, please cross it out.
cards.zh: 如果你的路線圖上有一條寫著「簡化 onboarding」，拜託把它劃掉。
cards.why: 用 please 開頭的祈使句在英文裡不是禮貌，而是一種帶感情的強調（像在求你）。擋需求時比 We shouldn't do this 更有記憶點，也不那麼官僚。
swaps: strike that line
that one doesn't survive the cut
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.pattern: That's an outlier — don't treat it as a pattern
cards.quote: Obviously never say never. Sometimes it might work, and if it worked for you, I am so glad. But that's an outlier and don't treat it as a pattern.
cards.zh: 當然，凡事沒有絕對。有時候真的會成功，如果你成功了我真的替你高興。但那是特例，不要把它當成通則。
cards.why: 先把例外整個讓給對方（甚至說我替你高興），再一刀把它釘死成 outlier。outlier / pattern 這組字是英文商業討論裡分辨「軼事」跟「規律」的標準工具，台灣人常缺這一層。
swaps: that's the exception that proves the rule
one data point isn't a trend
cards.pmNote: 改版／重新設計官網幾乎不會帶來成長，成功案例是離群值。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.pattern: Never ever once have I seen [X] produce [Y]
cards.quote: Never ever once have I seen a rebrand or redesign, especially of a marketing site, produce good performance results.
cards.zh: 我從來、一次都沒看過品牌重塑或改版——尤其是行銷官網——帶來好的成效數字。
cards.why: 把否定詞放句首造成倒裝（Never once have I seen...），這是英文裡最強的強調結構之一。用自己的親身統計當證據時，倒裝句能把「我的經驗」講出「這是規律」的份量。
swaps: not once in fifteen years have I seen
I've yet to see a single case where
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.pattern: I use it as an input, but never as a destination
cards.quote: I use it as an input into ideation, but I never use it as a destination for the result, if that makes sense.
cards.zh: 我把它當成發想的「輸入」，但絕不把它當成結果的「終點」，這樣講你懂我意思嗎？
cards.why: input vs destination 這組對比一次解決「參考競品該參考到什麼程度」這個永恆爭論。結尾的 if that makes sense 是母語者在講完抽象區分後的標準緩衝，不是真的在問你懂不懂。
swaps: it informs the work, it doesn't define it
it's a starting point, not an answer
cards.pmNote: 拆競品可以當靈感，但不能跳過使用者研究與設計流程。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.pattern: My rule of thumb: if we can't [條件], we shouldn't [行動], period
cards.quote: My rule of thumb, if we cannot collect the sample size in the month, we shouldn't test it, period.
cards.zh: 我的判準是：如果一個月內收不到足夠樣本數，那就不要測，就這樣。
cards.why: rule of thumb（經驗法則）＋句尾的 period（就這樣、不討論了）是一組黃金搭配：前者表示這是經驗不是真理（謙虛），後者表示現在不接受討論（果斷）。同時軟又硬。
swaps: my bar is simple:
hard line for me:
..., full stop
cards.pmNote: 樣本數一個月內收不齊的實驗，改用前後期比較（pre vs post）就好。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.pattern: ..., but the question is, how much time do you have to [X]?
cards.quote: Success is an output of a lot of failures, but the question is, how much time do you have to fail?
cards.zh: 成功是一堆失敗的產物，但問題是：你有多少時間可以失敗？
cards.why: 先同意一句所有人都同意的話，再用 but the question is 把真正的限制條件換上去。這是把空泛的價值觀討論（要允許失敗）拉回可管理問題（我們有幾次機會）的最快路徑。
swaps: sure — the real constraint is
agreed in principle; the binding question is
cards.pmNote: 失敗次數是資源，市場不會等你把每個坑都自己踩一遍。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.pattern: I'm very sorry to break it to you, but [難聽的事實]. I'm 99% sure of that
cards.quote: I am very sorry to break it to all of you, but your problem is not unique. I am 99% sure of that.
cards.zh: 很抱歉要這樣說，但你的問題一點都不特別。我有 99% 的把握。
cards.why: break it to someone＝把壞消息告訴某人。前面的道歉是社交緩衝，後面的 99% 卻不留餘地——先給糖再給刀，是給難聽回饋最有效的順序。台灣人常兩邊都軟，話就傳不到。
swaps: I hate to be the one to say it, but
this is going to sting, but
cards.pmNote: 你的成長問題別人解過，先去找人問，不要從零重造解法。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.pattern: Once you stand that up, it's a gift that keeps on giving and nobody can take it away from you
cards.quote: Obviously, I skew very heavily towards earned channels just because once you stand that up, that's a gift that just keeps on giving and nobody can take that away from you.
cards.zh: 我明顯偏向自有通路，因為那個東西一旦架起來，就是一份會一直給你回報的禮物，而且沒有人拿得走。
cards.why: 描繪願景不需要形容詞疊加，只需要一個對比：會一直給 vs 沒人拿得走。前半講複利，後半講防禦性——兩句話講完一個策略資產的全部價值。stand up 當動詞用（把某個機制建立起來）也很值得學。
swaps: it compounds, and it's ours
that's an asset, not a spend
cards.pmNote: Dropbox 超過 50% 的獲客來自分享機制——競爭對手買不到那些眼球。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.pattern: If you don't have [X] on your roadmap, you're going to be in real trouble over the next [時間]
cards.quote: And if you don't have them on your growth roadmap, you are going to be in some really big trouble over the next year to two years because your cost of acquisition is only going to go up.
cards.zh: 如果你的成長路線圖上沒有這些東西，未來一到兩年你會陷入大麻煩，因為你的獲客成本只會一路往上。
cards.why: 把急迫性綁在一個具體的時間窗（next year to two years）＋一個單向的趨勢（only going to go up）。沒有時間窗的警告，聽起來永遠都可以明年再說。
swaps: the window on this closes in about 18 months
this only gets more expensive from here
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.pattern: [X] can amplify [好的狀況], but [X] can't fix [壞的狀況]
cards.quote: The point is growth can amplify great product market fit and growth can help you grow faster once you are already growing. But if you are slowing down, growth is going to be absolutely helpless to do anything.
cards.zh: 重點是：成長團隊可以放大本來就好的 PMF，可以讓已經在成長的東西長更快。但如果你正在衰退，成長團隊完全無能為力。
cards.why: 拒絕一個不合理的期待，最有效的方式不是說「做不到」，而是精準定義「什麼情況做得到、什麼情況做不到」。amplify vs fix 這組動詞是關鍵：放大器不是修理工。
swaps: we can multiply what works; we can't manufacture it
hiring for this won't reverse the trend
cards.pmNote: 業績下滑時招成長負責人＝注定失敗；先讓核心產品與行銷把曲線打平。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.pattern: It's a step back, but there's a much bigger upside — and you'll have to work to get there
cards.quote: It's like a stepping stone back, but there is a much bigger room for upside that you can get to, but you are going to have to work to get to that upside.
cards.zh: 它其實是往後退一步，但後面有大得多的上升空間可以拿——只是你得努力才走得到。
cards.why: 三段式的取捨敘述：先承認退步、再指出更大的天花板、最後補一句「這不是免費的」。第三段最重要，它讓你的樂觀聽起來不是在推銷。
swaps: we're trading a local max for a shot at a global one
short-term dip, bigger ceiling
cards.pmNote: local maxima vs global maxima：改版的價值在打開新天花板，不在改版當下的數字。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.pattern: Give yourself [X] at the minimum, ideally more like [Y]
cards.quote: Give yourself two to three months at the minimum, ideally more like six months, to really optimize it back to a good standing where it can potentially outperform.
cards.zh: 至少給自己兩到三個月，最好是六個月，把它優化回到好的水準、甚至超越原本的表現。
cards.why: 談時間資源時同時給下限與理想值，比只給一個數字聰明：對方要砍，也只能砍到你的下限。而 Give yourself 的語氣是替對方著想，不是在跟對方要東西。
swaps: three months buys us X; six months buys us Y
the floor is two months — I'd argue for six
cards.pmNote: 改版之後要預留三到六個月的優化期，這段常被團隊忘記編進計畫。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.pattern: It has to come from knowing you don't know everything and the humility to say 'I need help'
cards.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
cards.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。
cards.why: 後半句是關鍵：It actually earns you a lot more credit than you think——直接對抗「求助＝示弱」的直覺。對害怕在英文環境暴露不懂的台灣人，這句是心理支撐也是實用句。
swaps: asking buys you more credibility than bluffing
I'd rather look green now than wrong later
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.pattern: Let's do a workshop first. I have this problem — I think you can help me fix it
cards.quote: Say, "Hey, let's have a workshop first. I have this problem. I think that you can help me fix it."
cards.zh: 你就說：「嘿，我們先辦一場工作坊吧。我手上有這個問題，我覺得你可以幫我解。」
cards.why: 請教高手時不要問「可以跟你聊聊嗎」，而是帶著一個具體問題並指定形式。這三句話的結構是：提議形式 → 給出問題 → 說明為什麼是你。短、具體、有誠意。
swaps: can I bring you a real problem to work on together?
I'd rather pay you for one working session than a intro chat
cards.pmNote: 找顧問／advisor 前先付費做一場工作坊，等於實戰面試。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.pattern: I want to call an audible here — [改變議程]
cards.quote: And kind of on a note, I want to call an audible, and so we were going to talk through all of your favorite frameworks.
cards.zh: 順著剛剛那個點，我想臨時改一下流程——我們原本要把你最愛的框架全部走一遍。
cards.why: call an audible 來自美式足球（四分衛在開球前臨時改戰術），現在是會議室裡「臨時變更議程」的標準說法。用它比 Let's change the plan 更有掌控感，也順便顯示你是有意識地改，不是失控。
swaps: let me audible here
I'm going to switch gears on the agenda
change of plan — bear with me
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.pattern: To make this even more concrete for people, can you [具體要求]?
cards.quote: To make this even more concrete for people that are starting to like, oh, shit I got to do this. Can you just give us a list that doesn't have to be exhaustive?
cards.zh: 為了讓大家更具體一點——那些正在想「糟糕我得開始做了」的人——你可以給我們一個清單嗎？不用列很完整沒關係。
cards.why: 要求對方講具體時，先把理由掛在「聽眾」身上（for people），不是「我聽不懂」。後面的 doesn't have to be exhaustive 是降低對方負擔的關鍵——你越說不用完美，對方越願意馬上給。
swaps: can you ground that in an example?
off the top of your head, what would that look like?
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

cards.quote: And so what I'm hearing is when you come into a project and the way you simplify is you start putting together a doc that describes these things you're talking about...
cards.zh: 所以我聽到的是，你進到一個專案時，你簡化的方式就是先寫一份文件，把你剛講的那些東西寫下來。
cards.why: 「So what I'm hearing is…」是英文會議裡最安全的確認句：它把「我可能聽錯」的責任攬在自己身上，而不是質疑對方講不清楚。台灣人常直接說 "You mean...?"，聽起來像在挑錯；這句則同時完成「我有在聽」＋「請幫我確認」兩件事。
swaps: What I'm taking away from this is...
If I'm following you correctly...
So the way I understood that is...
cards.pmNote: 在跨職能會議裡覆述對方的話，是最低成本的對齊 (alignment) 動作——它讓誤解在會議中就暴露，而不是在交付前才爆炸。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.quote: Just to double click on that one real quick, so what you're describing for the visual is you're presenting here's our options, here's our three options on a slide.
cards.zh: 這點我很快追一下——你剛說的那個視覺化，意思是你把三個選項放在一張投影片上對吧？
cards.why: 「double click」是矽谷會議的高頻動詞，意思是「把這一點放大來看」。加上 "real quick" 等於先承諾「我不會佔太久」，所以打斷不會惹人厭。這是台灣人最缺的一招：不是搶話，而是宣告「我只借三十秒」。
swaps: Can I double click on that for a second?
Let me pull on that thread real quick
Quick follow-up on that before we move on
cards.pmNote: 會議中即時追問細節，比會後私訊確認省下一整輪往返。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.pattern: I'm going to come back to X. I want to take a tangent to Y.
cards.quote: I'm going to come back to what you've learned about what makes super successful PMs, what makes you really successful. I want to take a tangent to Zuck.
cards.zh: 成功 PM 的特質這題我等一下會繞回來。我想先岔題聊一下 Zuck。
cards.why: 厲害在「先寄放、再岔題」：他不是隨便跳題，而是當場替被跳過的議題留一個位子，讓對方知道「你講的沒被丟掉」。這是主持人控場的核心技巧——會議的議程焦慮，多半來自「不知道還會不會回來談」。
swaps: Let's park that and come back to it
I want to bookmark that — first, a quick detour
Hold that thought, I want to go sideways for a second
cards.pmNote: 把離題「命名」出來（tangent / detour），比硬壓住離題更能維持會議節奏。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.quote: And this may not be a direct answer to the question, but it didn't really necessarily come from Mark.
cards.zh: 這可能不算直接回答你的問題，不過這件事其實不見得是 Mark 起頭的。
cards.why: 先自曝「我知道我沒正面回答」，反而讓聽者放心——因為最惱人的不是答非所問，是講的人沒發現自己答非所問。面試、被老闆抽問時特別好用：它買到繼續講下去的許可。
swaps: This is a bit adjacent to your question, but...
I'm going to answer a slightly different question first
Let me come at that from another angle
cards.pmNote: 當問題本身框錯了，資深的人不會硬答，而是先標示「我要換個框」。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.quote: And stop me if I'm getting too wonky, I can really get into this.
cards.zh: 如果我講得太細節控你就打斷我，這個主題我可以講到停不下來。
cards.why: 把「要不要繼續聽」的控制權主動交給對方，是專業感很強的一招——講細節前先給對方煞車。"wonky" 指「鑽進技術細節的書呆子勁」，母語者常用來自嘲。台灣人往往一路講到底，或乾脆不敢展開；這句讓你可以放心展開。
swaps: Cut me off if this is too in the weeds
Tell me if this is more detail than you need
Stop me if I'm going too deep here
cards.pmNote: 簡報時主動交出中斷權，比事後道歉「講太久」更有掌控感。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.pattern: Before we wrap, is there anything we haven't covered that you wanted to cover?
cards.quote: So before we get to our very exciting lightning round, is there anything else that we haven't covered that you wanted to cover or share?
cards.zh: 在進到最後的快問快答之前，還有什麼我們沒聊到、但你想講的嗎？
cards.why: 會議結尾的標準收口句。它做兩件事：宣告「快結束了」（讓大家收心），同時開最後一扇門（避免有人帶著沒講的話離開）。台灣人常用 "Any questions?"，那是要別人問你；這句是請對方補你漏掉的。
swaps: Anything we should have talked about and didn't?
Before we close out — anything I missed?
Is there anything you were hoping I'd ask?
cards.pmNote: 收尾前留一個「補件視窗」，能撈回會後才被提出的隱藏需求。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.pattern: Oh, one thing I forgot — [X] is that...
cards.quote: Oh, one thing I forgot that I learned from Guy Rosen, he is our chief security officer, is when you have three options and a recommendation...
cards.zh: 喔對，我忘了講一件我從 Guy Rosen（我們資安長）那邊學到的：當你有三個選項加一個建議的時候⋯⋯
cards.why: 話題已經往前走了，還想補一段——"one thing I forgot" 是最不失禮的回頭插話法。它把插話包裝成「我的疏漏」而不是「你講得不完整」。順帶示範一個母語習慣：人名後面立刻補職稱，讓聽眾不必猜這人是誰。
swaps: Sorry, one thing I meant to mention earlier
Oh — I should have said this before
Can I back up for one second? I skipped something
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.pattern: I don't love X. It's [problem].
cards.quote: In terms of evaluating the options, I don't love pros and cons. It's a flat list of text. It's hard to just get the big picture from that.
cards.zh: 在評估選項這件事上，我不太喜歡用優缺點列表。它就是一串平鋪的文字，很難一眼看到全貌。
cards.why: 「I don't love X」是英文裡殺傷力最小的否定：不是「這是錯的」，是「我個人不偏好」。但後面立刻接一句具體理由，所以不會顯得任性。台灣人反對時常兩極——要嘛不講，要嘛講成 "That's not good"；這個句型剛好落在中間。
swaps: I'm not a huge fan of...
I've never loved...
That's never quite worked for me because...
cards.pmNote: 否定一個既有做法時，一定要立刻給替代方案，否則只是製造真空。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.pattern: If there's a decision, I need three options and a recommendation.
cards.quote: So if there is a decision, I need three options and I need a recommendation that should hopefully help focus the meeting.
cards.zh: 如果這場會要做決定，我要三個選項加一個推薦方案，這樣才有辦法讓會議聚焦。
cards.why: 會議前設「入場費」的句型：不是拒絕開會，而是說清楚「符合什麼條件我才開得下去」。"help focus the meeting" 是很體面的理由包裝——你不是在刁難，你是在保護大家的時間。
swaps: Can you come with a recommendation, not just options?
I'd like a point of view, not just a menu
What would you do, if it were your call?
cards.pmNote: 「三選項＋一推薦」是主管最愛的提案格式：既展示你想過取捨，又不把決策丟回去給對方。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.pattern: Who's owning this? / Every workstream has a single-threaded owner.
cards.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
cards.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。
cards.why: "own" 當動詞用（誰 own 這件事）是矽谷會議的日常，台灣人常直譯成 "Who is responsible for this?"，語氣偏究責；"Who's owning this?" 問的是歸屬，不是罪責。散會前問這句，是把口頭共識變成可追蹤決議的最短路徑。
swaps: Who's the DRI on this?
Who's driving this one?
Whose name goes next to this?
cards.pmNote: single-threaded owner（單一負責人）＝ Amazon 的 DRI 概念：一件事只能有一個人的名字，兩個人負責等於沒人負責。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.quote: I often go into a project, everyone's operating at a PhD level, I'm coming in at a kindergarten level...
cards.zh: 我常常進到一個專案時，大家都在博士班的水準討論，而我是幼稚園程度進來的。
cards.why: 這是「問笨問題」的通行證。她不是說「我不懂」（示弱），而是說「我是新進場的人」（角色說明）——把知識落差重新框成情境問題，不是能力問題。對非母語者尤其好用：你聽不懂時，可以借這個框自然要求對方降階解釋。
swaps: Can you take me back to first principles on this?
Assume I know nothing here — walk me through it
Let me ask the naive question
cards.pmNote: 資深的人敢問基本問題，因為簡化本身就是產出：問題被拆到幼稚園程度，通常也就找到真正的癥結。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.pattern: X is not for X's sake — it's ultimately to [benefit].
cards.quote: Sometimes I feel the need to defend that the process is not for process' sake, it's ultimately to help us all move faster and work better.
cards.zh: 有時候我得替流程辯護一下：流程不是為了流程而存在，它最終是要讓大家跑得更快、做得更好。
cards.why: 「not for X's sake」是預先拆掉對方最可能的攻擊角度：對方還沒說「你在搞官僚」，你已經先替他說了，再翻轉成效益。這叫 pre-empting——先講出反對意見，反對意見就失去殺傷力。
swaps: This isn't process for the sake of process
I'm not adding this to add ceremony — it's so that...
The point isn't the doc, the point is...
cards.pmNote: 推流程時，一定要把它翻譯成「更快」而不是「更嚴謹」，否則工程團隊會直接判死刑。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.pattern: You can imagine [audience] hearing this and thinking...
cards.quote: You can imagine an engineer hearing me talk about how to run a meeting and all the canonical docs and just be like, "What? This sounds terrible."
cards.zh: 你可以想像一個工程師聽我在講怎麼開會、講那堆權威文件，心裡大概是：「蛤？這聽起來超糟。」
cards.why: 自己先演出反對者的台詞，還用對方的語氣（"What? This sounds terrible."）。這比「有些人可能不同意」高明得多——它證明你真的懂對方的痛，聽眾就會願意聽你解釋。會議中被質疑前先自嘲，等於把子彈接走。
swaps: I know how this sounds to an engineer
Some of you are probably thinking...
If I were sitting where you are, I'd be rolling my eyes
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem 的口語版：先把最強的反對意見說出來，再回應它。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.pattern: It doesn't mean we agree — it means we have the same understanding of the facts.
cards.quote: Extreme clarity means everyone's on the same page. It definitely doesn't mean that they all agree with each other, but they just have the same understanding of the facts.
cards.zh: 極度清晰的意思是大家在同一頁上。它絕對不是說大家都同意彼此，而是大家對事實的理解是一致的。
cards.why: 「It doesn't mean X, it means Y」是英文最有效的定義句型，專治雞同鴨講。這句本身也解決一個台灣職場常見誤會：把「對齊」當成「要大家同意」。對齊的門檻其實只到事實層，不到立場層。
swaps: Alignment isn't agreement
We don't have to agree, but we do have to be looking at the same facts
Let's separate the facts from the positions
cards.pmNote: 把會議切成「事實層」與「立場層」：事實不一致造成的爭吵最浪費時間，而且最容易解決。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.quote: "Where can I learn what I need to learn about this project?" I ask five different people, get five different answers. That is unacceptable.
cards.zh: 我要去哪裡搞懂這個專案？我問五個人，得到五種答案。這是不能接受的。
