cards.why: 描述「團隊沒對齊」最生動的一句話，而且結構可複製：用一個具體場景取代抽象抱怨。台灣人常說 "There is no alignment"，聽的人無感；"five people, five answers" 讓每個人腦中都浮現畫面。
swaps: Ask three people and you get three roadmaps
Everyone has a different version of the truth here
There's no single source of truth on this
cards.pmNote: canonical doc（權威文件）：一個專案只能有一份「總表」，其他文件都從它連出去。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.quote: I think the thing you really need to know is that for under 16-year-olds, if they want to change any of these defaults, they're going to have to get their parents' permission.
cards.zh: 我覺得你真正需要知道的是：未滿 16 歲的用戶如果想改這些預設值，必須先拿到父母同意。
cards.why: 在一堆細節裡替聽眾標紅線。母語者很習慣用這種「資訊分級」句型帶聽眾——不是全部倒給你，而是先告訴你哪一句最重要。台灣人簡報常平鋪直敘，缺的就是這種語氣上的粗體字。
swaps: If you only remember one thing, it's this
The headline here is...
The part that actually matters is...
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.pattern: One of the development areas for me is...
cards.quote: Candidly, one of the development areas for me, and it could be downstream because I do have this analogy of how to be a PM, is that the growth feedback or the constructive feedback for me is really learning when to lead from the front more.
cards.zh: 老實說，我自己的成長項目之一——這可能跟我對 PM 的那套比喻有關——別人給我的建設性回饋是：我要學會什麼時候該站到前面帶。
cards.why: 談自己的弱點時，母語者不用 weakness，而用 development area / growth feedback / constructive feedback，把缺點放進「還在長」的框架。面試「你的缺點是什麼」時，這組詞就是分水嶺。"lead from the front" 也是台灣人想不到的說法。
swaps: An area I'm actively working on is...
The feedback I keep getting is...
Where I still have room to grow is...
cards.pmNote: 績效面談把缺點講成「發展方向」，比講成「我不擅長」更容易換到資源與教練。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.quote: If there's nothing here, totally cool. But is there something that you changed Mark's mind about?
cards.zh: 如果沒有的話完全沒關係。不過，有沒有哪件事是你改變了 Mark 的想法的？
cards.why: 問敏感問題前先給對方一個下台階，對方就不必為了面子硬編一個答案。這在跨文化會議特別重要：台灣人被問到答不出來時容易硬撐，而母語者其實習慣先鋪「可以說沒有」。
swaps: Feel free to pass on this one, but...
No pressure if nothing comes to mind, but...
This might be a dead end, but I'm curious...
cards.pmNote: 使用者訪談同理：先允許受訪者說「沒有」，資料才不會被禮貌污染。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

cards.quote: I still may insert myself and say, "Hey, let me pause here for a second and try to capture what has been said." This is what I've heard.
cards.zh: 我還是會切進去說：「欸，我先暫停一下，把剛剛講的整理一下。」以下是我聽到的。
cards.why: 這是整批素材裡最值錢的一句。它同時解決台灣人在英文會議的兩個痛點：插不上話、以及不知道怎麼展現貢獻。你不需要提出新想法，只要當那個「按暫停＋做總結」的人——Anneka 說，別人會直接把這個動作認定為「有策略思維」。
swaps: Let me play back what I'm hearing
Can I stop us here and summarize?
Before we go further — here's where I think we are
cards.pmNote: 在發散的討論裡做即時 summarization，是最容易被誤認為策略能力的行為（她的原話：people actually view that as strategy）。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

cards.pattern: Is everyone in agreement, or is there some dissent about where we've landed?
cards.quote: Is everyone in agreement with that or is there some dissent about whether that's an accurate portrayal of where we've landed with this conversation?
cards.zh: 大家都同意嗎？還是有人覺得我這樣描述我們的結論並不準確？
cards.why: 總結完一定要用問句結尾，否則就變成「我替大家做決定」。關鍵在 "or is there some dissent"——主動邀請反對，讓沉默的人有位子。"where we've landed"（我們落在哪）是會議收斂的標準說法，台灣人幾乎不會用。
swaps: Does that land for everyone?
Anyone see it differently?
Is that a fair read of where we are?
cards.pmNote: 結論以問句收尾，能把「表面同意、會後翻案」的風險提前引爆。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

cards.pattern: I'm not going to interrupt the flow — I'll just summarize in chat what I've heard.
cards.quote: I'm not going to interrupt the flow conversation. I'm just going to summarize in Zoom chat this is what I've heard, and this is what I think we're saying in this conversation.
cards.zh: 我不打斷大家的討論節奏，我直接在 Zoom 聊天室整理一下我聽到的、以及我認為我們在談的東西。
cards.why: 給「真的插不進話」的人一條後門：把總結打在聊天室，通常會被主持人念出來、拉回主線。對非母語者是黃金策略——書寫沒有口音、沒有搶麥壓力，卻拿到同樣的存在感。
swaps: Dropping a quick summary in the chat
I'll put my read in the chat so I don't derail us
Noting in chat — feel free to correct me
cards.pmNote: 遠端會議的低風險發言管道：chat 的門檻遠低於搶麥，但被引用的機率很高。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

cards.pattern: I agree with 90% of that — I'm 10% off.
cards.quote: But then inviting people to discuss and say "Yes," or "No, I agree with 90% of that or 10% off."
cards.zh: 然後邀請大家討論，回一句「同意」，或者「不完全，我同意九成，有一成不太一樣」。
cards.why: 用百分比表達部分不同意，是英文會議極常見、中文卻很少的招。它避免了 yes/no 的二元對立，也自動把討論聚焦到那 10%——不用重新吵整件事。台灣人自己想不出來，但學會後馬上能用。
swaps: I'm with you on most of that, except...
I'd agree with everything but the last part
90% yes — let me push on the other 10%
cards.pmNote: 把異議量化，能防止一個小分歧升級成全案重議。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

cards.quote: Hey, look, I know this is what you're trying to do, but maybe instead of looking at option A here of how we go about tackling this, we should have explored these three other options instead.
cards.zh: 欸，我知道你想達成的是什麼，只是與其走 A 這條路，也許我們該把另外三個選項也攤開來看。
cards.why: 反對老闆的標準結構：先確認他的目標（我知道你要什麼），只反對手段（不是 A 這條路）。台灣人反對時容易連目標一起否定，聽起來像不服；這句把爭點縮到「方法」，老闆的面子完全不受傷。
swaps: I'm bought into the goal — I'd challenge the approach
Same objective, different path: what if we...
Can we pressure-test the mechanism, not the goal?
cards.pmNote: 跟創辦人 disagree 前先還原他的 objective：多數「爛點子」其實是好目標配錯手段。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

cards.pattern: What's the hill I'm going to die on?
cards.quote: What's the hill that I'm going to die on and is this something that I can shift or is this something that is not worth shifting?
cards.zh: 哪座山是我願意死守的？這件事我推得動嗎？還是根本不值得去推？
cards.why: "the hill to die on" 是英文職場最常見的取捨隱喻，台灣人聽得懂但幾乎不會主動用。它把「該不該堅持」變成一個可以放上桌面討論的問題，而不是私下悶著生氣。
swaps: Is this a hill worth dying on?
Is this a two-way door or a one-way door?
Do I spend capital here, or save it?
cards.pmNote: 產品領導的核心不是每場都贏，而是選對要贏的那幾場——政治資本是有限資源。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

cards.pattern: I heard this piece of feedback, and here's what it made me think about our strategy — what do you think?
cards.quote: I was talking to security leaders in our customer advisory board recently and I heard this piece of feedback and this is what it made me think about our strategy, what do you think about that?
cards.zh: 我最近跟客戶顧問委員會的資安主管聊，聽到一個回饋，這讓我重新想我們的策略——你怎麼看？
cards.why: 資深的人挑戰下屬的策略時，不會直接說「這錯了」，而是「丟一個資料點＋問你怎麼看」。她的理由很直白：她一開口，房間裡就沒人敢反駁。這個句型把「主管的意見」降級成「一個可以被反駁的假設」。
swaps: Here's a data point that's been nagging me — how does it square with your plan?
Let me put a hypothesis on the table
I might be wrong, but here's what I keep hearing
cards.pmNote: 位高的人講話會壓縮討論空間，所以要刻意把結論降級成假設（seed an assumption），保留反駁的餘地。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

cards.quote: I care so much about you and I'm giving you this feedback because I want you to be successful and I want you to be able to reach the pinnacle of what I know you can accomplish.
cards.zh: 我非常在乎你，我給你這個回饋是因為我希望你成功、希望你能走到我知道你能到的高度。
cards.why: 重點在她強調的一件事：這段話要「明講出來」，不能只是希望對方感受到。台灣主管習慣用暗示和婉轉，結果對方只接收到批評沒接收到善意。把動機說白，是硬回饋能被聽進去的前提。
swaps: I'm telling you this because I think you can go further than this
This comes from a good place — I want you to win
I wouldn't spend this time if I didn't think you had it in you
cards.pmNote: radical candor：關心對方 × 直接挑戰。少了前半段，後半段就只是攻擊。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

cards.pattern: This is how you're being perceived — which may not be what you're intending.
cards.quote: Hey, well this is how other people perceive you including me, but maybe this is not what you are intending...
cards.zh: 其他人——包括我——是這樣看你的，但這可能不是你原本想呈現的樣子。
cards.why: 把「你是這樣的人」換成「你被這樣看」，對方就不會為了辯護人格而關上耳朵。而且它自帶一個善意假設：你的本意是好的，只是傳達出了落差。討論就自然轉向「怎麼改變觀感」這個可執行的問題。
swaps: The perception is X — I don't think that's your intent
Here's how it's landing, which may not be how you meant it
The gap I see is between intent and impact
cards.pmNote: 回饋談「觀感落差」而非「本質缺陷」，對方才有可改的著力點。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

cards.pattern: All feedback is valid — that doesn't mean you need to act on all of it.
cards.quote: Actually, all feedback I think is valid. People's feelings are valid, but it doesn't mean that you need to do something about all of those things.
cards.zh: 其實我覺得所有回饋都是有效的。別人的感受都是真的，但這不代表你每一項都得去處理。
cards.why: 「承認＋但不照做」的標準句型。先給對方情緒上的完全認可（valid），再把行動決定權留給自己。台灣人常誤以為承認對方有道理就等於答應要改；這句示範兩者可以拆開。
swaps: That's fair, and I'm still going to prioritize elsewhere
I hear it, but it's not where we're putting the effort
Valid — just not a must-have this quarter
cards.pmNote: 回饋分 must-have 與 nice-to-have：must-have 太多時，nice-to-have 就是明確地不做。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

cards.quote: How do I make this idea one click better? It's not about how do you do something radically, radically different, but taking ideas and then making it slightly better, slightly better.
cards.zh: 我要怎麼把這個想法再往上推一格？重點不是做出天差地遠的東西，而是接手別人的想法，再讓它好一點點。
cards.why: "one click better" 是很好用的提案框：你不是推翻別人，你是在他的基礎上加值。這讓「提出想法」變成低風險行為——尤其適合會議上不敢拋大構想的人。
swaps: Can I build on that?
What if we took that one step further?
Yes — and here's a small twist
cards.pmNote: 策略常不是憑空生出來的大點子，而是把現有的想法一格一格往上推（betterment）。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

cards.pattern: As long as the decision is 70% right, you can iterate on the rest.
cards.quote: And as long as your decision is like 70% right, you can iterate on that 20, 30% in either direction, but if you don't commit, then you don't actually get any new information that is high fidelity and high quality.
cards.zh: 只要決策有七成對，剩下的兩三成你都可以往任一邊修；但你不下注，就拿不到任何高品質的新資訊。
cards.why: 用一個數字（70%）把「先決定再修正」變成可以說出口的原則，而不是聽起來很草率的直覺。開會卡在分析癱瘓時，這句是最有效的推進器。
swaps: Let's make the call and learn our way to the rest
We're at 70 — that's enough to move
The cost of not deciding is higher than deciding wrong
cards.pmNote: 不做決定＝零學習。承諾之後拿到的資料，品質遠高於假設階段的推演。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

cards.pattern: Before I give feedback: what do you want to do? Where do you want to go?
cards.quote: Sometimes I even start the conversation by asking them, "What do you want to do? Where do you want to go in your career?"
cards.zh: 有時候我甚至會用這個開場：「你想做什麼？你的職涯想往哪走？」
cards.why: 給回饋前先問目標，回饋就從「我對你的評價」變成「我幫你導航」。同一件事，對想當 CPO 的人跟想當技術專才的人，回饋內容完全不同——不先問，回饋就注定錯位。
swaps: Where are you trying to get to?
What does the next version of your career look like?
Before I dive in — what would be most useful to you?
cards.pmNote: 1:1 先校準對方的目標函數，回饋才有槓桿。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

cards.quote: Let me refine that a little bit more. It's more about giving people the information that they can use for decisions that they alone are good at...
cards.zh: 我把那個講法再修得精準一點。重點比較是：給人們他們才擅長的那類決策所需要的資訊。
cards.why: 當別人幫你總結卻總結歪了，直接說 "That's not what I meant" 會讓對方難堪。"Let me refine that" 把糾正包裝成「我來把它磨得更準」——是你在補完，不是他理解錯。這招在英文會議每天都用得到。
swaps: Let me sharpen that a bit
Close — let me put it slightly differently
I'd nuance that one degree
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

cards.quote: So I think about it as designing an interface and make it an extension of yourself rather than a black box on its own that you just need more information to. Is that helpful?
cards.zh: 所以我把它想成在設計一個介面，讓它成為你的延伸，而不是一個你只能不斷餵資料的黑盒子。這樣講有幫到你嗎？
cards.why: 講完一段長解釋後回頭確認，把「你聽懂了嗎」（帶著居高臨下）換成「我講得有用嗎」（責任在講者）。這個責任轉移是母語者的細膩處，台灣人常用 "Do you understand?"，語感其實很傷人。
swaps: Does that answer it?
Is that the level you were after?
Did that land?
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

cards.pattern: So just to kind of recap — you want X, you want Y.
cards.quote: So just to kind of recap, you want it to feel like it's core and critical to the company. You want it to feel like it's everyone's success.
cards.zh: 所以簡單複述一下：你希望它讓人覺得對公司是核心、關鍵的；你希望它是所有人的成功。
cards.why: "just to kind of recap" 裡的 kind of 是關鍵的緩衝詞——它讓總結聽起來像隨手整理，而不是「我來替你定調」。台灣人講英文常缺這類軟化詞，導致語氣比本意強硬。
swaps: So if I zoom out for a second...
Let me play that back
Quick recap before we move on
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

cards.quote: For folks that haven't worked at a company with this kind of on the ground ops team, can you just unpack what that is?
cards.zh: 對於沒待過有這種第一線營運團隊的人來說，你可以幫忙拆解一下那是什麼嗎？
cards.why: 這是「我聽不懂但不想顯得沒跟上」的最佳解：把問題掛在別人身上（for folks who haven't...），你就從「不懂的人」變成「替大家問的人」。"unpack" 也比 "explain" 更專業、更不像在挑戰對方沒講清楚。
swaps: Can you unpack that a bit for the room?
For those of us not close to this — what does that mean in practice?
Say more about what that looks like day to day
cards.pmNote: 會議裡沒人敢問的術語，通常有一半的人也不懂——先問的人反而拿到主持權。
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

cards.quote: And so we had this idea that we came up with that would do it. I'm not going to let that one out.
cards.zh: 我們後來想到一個做得到的點子。那個我就不外流了。
cards.why: 拒絕透露而不失禮的漂亮示範：語氣輕鬆、不解釋、不道歉。台灣人碰到不能講的事常支支吾吾或編理由；"I'm not going to let that one out" 反而顯得有分寸又有趣。
swaps: That one I'll keep to myself
I'll have to leave that one out
Can't go into that one, sorry
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

cards.pattern: Now, don't get me wrong — [credential that pre-empts the misread].
cards.quote: Now, don't get me wrong, I've built the experimentation platform at Lyft. I'm a guy who loves data and loves using it and looking at experiments.
cards.zh: 先別誤會我的意思——Lyft 的實驗平台就是我建的。我是個超愛用數據、愛看實驗的人。
cards.why: 當你批評某件事（這裡是「只看數據」），聽眾很容易把你歸類成反對派。"Don't get me wrong" 立刻堵住這條誤讀，還順手把自己的資歷放上桌。批評與立場切割，論點才站得住。
swaps: To be clear, I'm not anti-data
Don't hear this as me saying X
I say this as someone who...
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

cards.quote: I think some controversy is necessary and so I may be at a different point on that one.
cards.zh: 我覺得某種程度的爭議是必要的，所以這一題我的位置可能跟大家不太一樣。
cards.why: 把「我不同意」重寫成「我站的位置不同」——不預設誰對誰錯，只是座標不同。這是英文裡殺傷力最低的異議表達之一，非常適合對上級或客戶用。
swaps: I might land somewhere different on that
I probably sit further along that spectrum
I hold that one a bit differently
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

cards.quote: Where I've seen people get lost is they assume that if you do that alone, it will work.
cards.zh: 我看過很多人卡住的地方是：他們假設光做這件事就會成功。
cards.why: 指出對方的錯誤假設，卻不指名對方——主詞是「我看過的人」，不是「你」。這個第三人稱轉移是拆假設時最好用的緩衝，會議上幾乎不會引起防衛。
swaps: The trap I see teams fall into is...
Where this usually breaks down is when people assume...
The mistake I keep seeing is...
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

cards.pattern: Something I caution people against is...
cards.quote: Something I caution people against though is don't use the data alone to figure out who the marginal user is.
cards.zh: 不過有件事我會提醒大家小心：不要只靠數據去判斷誰是邊際使用者。
cards.why: "caution against" 比 "don't do" 專業得多，語氣是提醒不是命令。它把你放在「有經驗、替你擋坑」的位置，而不是「來管你」的位置——資深感就是從這種措辭累積出來的。
swaps: One thing I'd be careful about here is...
The thing I'd watch out for is...
I'd push back gently on...
cards.pmNote: marginal user＝差一步就會轉換的那群人；找到他們就找到最高槓桿的優化點。
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

cards.quote: Those are just numbers I'm putting out there. It's always going to be a gut call based on where you are.
cards.zh: 那些數字只是我隨口丟出來的。這終究是看你所在的位置做的直覺判斷。
cards.why: 他剛講完 80/20 的分配，主持人追問「這是你的原則嗎」，他立刻承認那是隨口說的。這一招保護你不被自己的舉例綁架——台灣人被追問時常硬撐把即興數字說成方法論，反而失信。
swaps: Don't quote me on the exact split
That's directional, not precise
I'm making that number up to illustrate the shape
cards.pmNote: 報數字時要標示信心水準：拍腦袋的比例就說是拍腦袋的，別讓它變成別人的規劃基準。
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

cards.quote: Okay, good tangent, I wanted to chat about your learnings at Facebook.
cards.zh: 好，這段岔題不錯——我想聊聊你在 Facebook 學到的東西。
cards.why: 把離題拉回主線的最短句：先肯定（good tangent），再直接轉。先給一句正面標籤，轉場就不會顯得你在嫌人家講太久——這是台灣人主持英文會議最常缺的兩秒鐘。
swaps: Great detour — let's get back to...
Love that, and I want to make sure we cover...
Good rabbit hole. Coming back to the agenda...
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

cards.quote: Okay. I know I have to let you go and you have to get back to real work.
cards.zh: 好，我知道我該放你走了，你還有正事要忙。
cards.why: 結束會議的體面說法：把「時間到了」翻譯成「我尊重你的時間」。"let you go" 是母語者收尾的固定用法，台灣人通常只會說 "Time is up"，語感生硬又像在趕人。
swaps: I want to be respectful of your time
I'll give you your time back
Let's not run over — last thing before we close
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

cards.quote: Okay, that's a difficult and different question.
cards.zh: 好，這是個困難、而且性質不太一樣的問題。
cards.why: 被問到棘手問題時，先替問題貼標籤，等於合法地買到三秒鐘思考時間，還順便暗示「答案不會簡單」。比 "Um... let me think" 專業非常多。
swaps: That's a harder question than it looks
That's a fair question, and a tricky one
Let me think about how to answer that properly
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

cards.pattern: The hardest part isn't getting into their shoes — it's taking my own off.
cards.quote: The hardest part of it is they say getting in somebody else's shoes. The hardest part is taking my own shoes off.
cards.zh: 大家都說最難的是站到別人的鞋子裡。其實最難的是先把自己的鞋脫掉。
cards.why: 改寫一個人人都會的老比喻，就是母語者製造記憶點的手法。這句在跨團隊卡關的場合特別好用——它把「同理心」講成一個具體動作，而不是道德要求。
swaps: I have to put my own agenda down first
Before I can hear you, I have to stop arguing in my head
Step one is letting go of what I came in wanting
cards.pmNote: 跨團隊衝突多半不是資訊不對稱，而是雙方都沒放下自己原本要的東西。
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

cards.quote: Now can I jump in here, please? Because then people are like, "But how do I do this?"
cards.zh: 我可以在這邊插一句嗎？因為接下來大家一定會問：「那我到底該怎麼做？」
cards.why: 插話的黃金結構：請求＋理由。"please" 讓它保持禮貌，"Because..." 立刻交代插話的價值，對方就不會覺得被搶麥。台灣人插話常只有請求沒有理由，於是聽起來像打斷。
swaps: Can I come in on that?
Mind if I jump in here?
Sorry — can I add one thing before we move on?
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

cards.quote: I'm going to jump in real quick just to highlight what you're talking... what you just said, which I think is extremely important and powerful, and people might kind of move on too quickly.
cards.zh: 我很快插一下，只是想把你剛剛講的那句畫個重點，我覺得那非常重要、非常有力量。
cards.why: 最容易被接受的插話理由：不是要反對，是要把對方的話放大。稱讚型插話幾乎零風險，而且能讓你在會議裡累積存在感——對不敢搶話的人來說是最好的第一步。
swaps: Can I underline that for a second?
I want to make sure that doesn't slide by
Let me flag that — it's the key point here
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

cards.quote: Help me understand more what your concerns are. Are your concerns around reliability when you move faster?
cards.zh: 幫我多理解一下你的顧慮是什麼。你擔心的是加快之後穩定性會出問題嗎？
cards.why: 碰到阻力時，最有效的不是反駁而是「請對方教我」。"Help me understand" 把姿態放低，卻同時逼對方把模糊的反對具體化。第二句再給選項，讓不擅表達的人有梯子可下。
swaps: Walk me through what's worrying you
What's the concern underneath that?
Say more — what would make this feel safe?
cards.pmNote: 反對意見多半是模糊的焦慮；把它逼成具體問題，才有辦法設計解法。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

cards.pattern: What do you mean by this? Are you talking about X? Are you talking about Y?
cards.quote: Okay, what do you mean by this? Are you talking about inner and outer loop? Are you talking about friction?
cards.zh: 好，你指的是什麼意思？你講的是內外迴圈嗎？還是講摩擦成本？
cards.why: 光問 "What do you mean?" 常換到一句更含糊的回答。厲害的是後面連續丟兩三個具體選項——讓對方用「選」的，而不是用「重講一次」的。這對非母語者尤其有效：你不必聽懂全部，只要問對選項。
swaps: When you say X, do you mean A or B?
Which of these are we actually talking about?
Give me the concrete version of that
cards.pmNote: 80% 的專案走偏，起因是主管一句沒被追問的模糊指令。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

cards.pattern: They're related concepts that people conflate — so, related but different.
cards.quote: I think they're very related concepts that people sometimes conflate, but I see them as being different. So related, but different.
cards.zh: 我覺得這是常被混用的相關概念，但我把它們看成不同的東西。所以是——相關，但不同。
cards.why: "conflate"（把兩件事混為一談）是台灣人幾乎不用、但會議裡超常出現的動詞。最後那句三字收尾 "related, but different" 示範母語者的節奏感：長句解釋完，用一個極短句釘住。
swaps: People use those interchangeably, but they're not the same thing
Adjacent, not identical
Same neighborhood, different house
cards.pmNote: canonical nomenclature：先把詞定義好再討論，否則整場會都在為同一個詞吵不同的意思。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

cards.pattern: I will admit I only have [X] top of mind.
cards.quote: So I will admit I only have the 2019 benchmarks top of mind.
cards.zh: 我得承認，我腦中現在只記得 2019 年那版基準數字。
cards.why: "top of mind"（此刻記得起來的）是漂亮的限縮詞：她沒說「我不知道」，而是精確標示自己資訊的邊界。這是專家承認不足的方式——縮小範圍，而不是否定自己。
swaps: Off the top of my head...
I'd have to check the latest, but as of last I looked...
Don't hold me to the current numbers
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

cards.pattern: I can't tell you why. If I were to guess / I would surmise...
cards.quote: In a research paper, we'd have a discussion section, and this is where you get to guess. I would surmise, and we do this in the report, that it's probably because retail went through the retail apocalypse, right.
cards.zh: 我沒辦法告訴你原因。在論文裡這叫討論章節，也就是可以猜的地方。我的推測是——報告裡也是這樣寫的——大概是因為零售業經歷了那場零售末日。
cards.why: 把「知道」與「猜」明確分開，反而讓人更信任你。她甚至先示範分界（這一段是可以猜的），再開始猜。台灣人被問到不確定的事時常含糊帶過，聽起來像在唬；這種明講分界的方式是資深訊號。
swaps: I don't have data on that — but my hypothesis would be...
If I had to guess, and this is a guess...
That's speculation on my part, but...
cards.pmNote: intellectual honesty：把事實、推論、猜測分層說清楚，是資料型工作者最重要的信用來源。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

cards.pattern: The common knowledge was X. Turns out that's not right.
cards.quote: The common knowledge was that you had to have at least a two-week wait for change approvals in order to get that stability. Turns out that's not right. It was just kind of an old wives' tale, right.
cards.zh: 過去大家都認為，變更審核至少要等兩週才能確保穩定。結果那是錯的。那就是個以訛傳訛的老說法。
cards.why: 推翻共識的標準三段式：先複述共識（讓大家點頭）→ 一句短的翻轉（Turns out that's not right）→ 貼標籤（old wives' tale）。攻擊的是「集體迷思」而不是在場任何人，所以沒人需要防衛。
swaps: The received wisdom is X — the data says otherwise
That's the folklore. It doesn't hold up
We all believed that. It turned out not to be true
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

cards.quote: You know what, I'll say yes and, right.
cards.zh: 這樣說吧，我要用「是，而且」來回答。
cards.why: "yes, and" 來自即興劇，現在是矽谷會議的固定用法：先接受對方的前提，再加上你的補充——實質上是不同意，但語感是共建。台灣人想不到可以用一個「劇場術語」當作反對的外衣。
swaps: Yes — and here's the wrinkle
True, and also...
I'd say both things are true
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

cards.quote: One, I hate to be this person, but I'll point to a few of my papers.
cards.zh: 第一，我很不想當那種人，但我還是要推薦一下我自己的幾篇論文。
cards.why: 自我推薦最尷尬的一刻，用 "I hate to be this person" 先自嘲就化解了。這是英文裡處理「自誇焦慮」的通用開關——台灣人多半選擇乾脆不提自己的成果，結果貢獻沒人知道。
swaps: At the risk of being that guy...
Shameless plug, but it's genuinely the best source
Forgive the self-reference —
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

cards.quote: I know we'll talk more about this, but let me go back to the question I was going to ask...
cards.zh: 我知道這個我們等下會再聊，不過讓我先回到我原本要問的問題。
cards.why: 回到議程的乾淨句型：前半句先安撫（這題沒被丟掉），後半句才拉回。少了前半句就會像在打斷；有了前半句，對方會覺得你在幫忙管時間。
swaps: Let's come back to that — first, the question I parked
Holding that thought, back to where we were
We'll return to this. To finish the earlier point...
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

cards.pattern: This is a great segue to something I was going to get to later — let's just get into it.
cards.quote: This is a great segue too, something I was going to get to a little bit later, but let's just get into it, which is the DORA framework...
cards.zh: 這剛好可以順下去——我本來排在比較後面，不過我們直接進去談吧，就是 DORA 框架。
cards.why: 議程可以往前調，但要說出來。這句把「我臨時改順序」講成「你的話剛好接得上」，等於把主導權的行使包裝成順水推舟——主持會議時最實用的一種面子工程。
swaps: You've teed up my next question perfectly
That's a natural bridge to...
Let's jump ahead in the agenda since we're here
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

cards.quote: You can't fund everything. You don't get to pick everything.
cards.zh: 你沒辦法什麼都投資。你也沒有權利什麼都選。
cards.why: 兩個短句、平行結構、沒有任何緩衝——擋需求時偶爾就是需要這種硬度。注意她用的是 "you"（泛指所有人），所以聽起來像原則，不像針對某個人。
swaps: If we fund everything, everything fails
Saying yes to this means saying no to that
We don't have the capacity to bet on all of it
cards.pmNote: 策略的本質是取捨：全部都做＝全部都做不好。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

cards.pattern: This is where I'm data informed, not data driven.
cards.quote: Now this is where I'm data informed, and I'm not data driven.
cards.zh: 這就是我所謂的「被數據啟發」，而不是「被數據驅動」。
cards.why: 一組字的差別（informed vs driven）就劃出立場，而且不必否定數據的價值。當你要在數字之外做判斷、又不想被說「憑感覺」時，這句是最省力的辯護。
swaps: The data has a vote, not a veto
I let the numbers inform the call, not make it
Data in one hand, judgment in the other
cards.pmNote: 數據給你一個選項清單（class of options），最後那一步還是人的判斷。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

cards.pattern: Instead of getting mad at [person], we can say: this was problematic — what's wrong here?
cards.quote: Instead of getting mad at Lenny for his really stupid idea or getting mad at Nicole because this was a really bad idea, we can say, "This was problematic. What's wrong here?"
cards.zh: 與其去氣 Lenny 出了個爛點子、或氣 Nicole 這主意很糟，我們可以說：「這裡有問題。是哪裡出錯了？」
cards.why: 對事不對人的具體操作法：把爭論的對象從「人的名字」搬到「框裡的東西」。她甚至拿自己當反例（getting mad at Nicole），主動把自己放進可被批評的位置，房間的防衛心就降下來了。
swaps: Let's put the problem on the whiteboard, not on a person
The idea failed, not the person
What broke here — not who broke it
cards.pmNote: 把假設寫成外部化的框（四宮格、假設卡），失敗時就能檢討框而不是檢討人。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

cards.quote: And if you're on different pages, you're heading in completely different directions.
cards.zh: 如果大家不在同一頁上，那就是往完全不同的方向前進。
cards.why: 一句話講完「沒對齊的代價」，而且是可以直接搬去說服老闆開對齊會議的說法。"on the same page / on different pages" 是英文職場最高頻的對齊隱喻，台灣人聽得懂卻很少主動用。
swaps: We're solving two different problems right now
We're not aligned on what 'done' means
Let's make sure we're pointed at the same thing
cards.pmNote: 對齊做在前面是幾小時，做在後面是幾個月的返工。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

cards.pattern: I'm not saying that's the thing that made it happen, but I will say [後續發生的事實]
cards.quote: And I'm not saying that's the thing that made it happen, but I will say very quickly after that, we became very close partners and ultimately they acquired me.
cards.zh: 我不是說就是因為這件事才成的，但我可以說，那之後我們很快就變成很緊密的夥伴，最後他們把我們買下來了。
cards.why: 把「因果」降級成「時序」——先主動放棄過度歸功（I'm not saying that's the thing that made it happen），再用 but I will say 把事實原封不動放上桌。結果是聽者自己去連因果，你既拿到功勞又完全沒有吹牛的姿態。這是英語職場「講成績」最高階的一招。
swaps: I won't claim that caused it, but the timeline speaks for itself
I can't prove the two are connected, but what I can tell you is...
cards.pmNote: 談 impact 時，只要你講的是 correlation 而非 causation，就該用這種降級句型——否則被追問「你怎麼證明」會很難看。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.pattern: The short of it is [三個關鍵字]. And the longer version is that...
cards.quote: The short of it is, it was a promise to myself, and COVID, and Uber doing layoffs. And the longer version is that, when I joined Uber, before Uber I was...
cards.zh: 簡單講，就是我對自己的一個承諾、COVID，還有 Uber 裁員這三件事。比較長的版本是，我剛進 Uber 之前……
cards.why: 先給一個「三個名詞」的壓縮版答案，再自己開權限講長版。對聽者是禮貌（你隨時可以喊停），對講者是保險（就算被打斷，重點已經送出去了）。台灣人面試最常見的死法就是直接進入長版、講到一半被打斷，結論還沒出來。
swaps: The short answer is X. The longer answer is...
Short version: X. Want the long version?
cards.pmNote: 這是 BLUF（bottom line up front）的口語版；PM 對高層報告一律先給 short of it。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

cards.pattern: I picked you because [具體理由]. Do you mind spending a couple of minutes and just giving me some thoughts on this?
cards.quote: I picked you because I really trust you to be a sound source of truthful advice and give me some feedback. So I really value that. Do you mind spending a couple of minutes and just giving me some thoughts on this?
cards.zh: 我會找你，是因為我真的很信任你會給我誠實的建議跟回饋，這對我很有價值。可以請你花個幾分鐘，給我一點想法嗎？
cards.why: 三段結構：說明為什麼是你（不是群發）→ 講出你重視的價值 → 把 ask 縮到「a couple of minutes / some thoughts」這種心理成本極低的量詞。台灣人請教常犯的錯是問題很大、理由很空，對方讀完不知道要回什麼。
swaps: I'm reaching out to you specifically because...
Would you be up for giving me your quick take on this?
cards.pmNote: Ada 稱這套流程為 curiosity loop：好問題＋精選對象＋輕量 ask＋事後回報結果。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

cards.pattern: I love what I'm doing here, and I would also like to [想要的]. And here's what I'm interested in.
cards.quote: It might actually mean a proactive conversation with your manager or the leadership to say, "I love what I'm doing here, and I would also like to learn a little bit more. And here's what I'm interested in."
cards.zh: 這可能只是主動找主管或高層談一次，跟他說：「我很喜歡現在做的事，同時我也想再多學一些，這是我有興趣的方向。」
cards.why: 關鍵在 and，不是 but。「I love X, but I want Y」會被聽成抱怨，「I love X, and I would also like Y」是把新需求疊加在肯定之上。結尾再用 here's what I'm interested in 把球做給對方——你不是丟問題，你是丟一份可執行的清單。
swaps: I'm happy where I am, and I'd love to stretch into...
This is working well for me — and here's where I'd like to grow next
cards.pmNote: 要成長機會前先確認自己現在的產出無可挑剔；否則這句會被讀成「本份沒做好還想挑工作」。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

cards.pattern: I wouldn't have gotten [成果] if I had just [被動的預設路徑]
cards.quote: It was just such a rare opportunity, but I wouldn't have gotten those opportunities if I just let them promote me or I followed a strategy where I was just focused on trying to get the biggest title.
cards.zh: 那真的是很難得的機會，但如果我當初只是讓他們幫我升職、或只想著拿最大的頭銜，我根本拿不到那些機會。
cards.why: 用「反事實」（counterfactual）講成績：不說「我很厲害所以拿到 X」，而說「如果我沒有做那個選擇，我就拿不到 X」。功勞落在你的判斷力上，聽起來像在分析而不是在誇耀。這是亞裔講者最好用的一招。
swaps: None of that would have happened if I'd taken the default path
That only came about because I deliberately chose not to...
cards.pmNote: 面試的 STAR 裡，Action 最有說服力的講法就是講「你放棄了什麼預設選項」。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

cards.pattern: I'm here to [你真正的目的]，even if it costs [別人以為你要的東西]
cards.quote: I even told my manager this when I first came in, "I'm here to learn to be a better founder." So if I can make my LinkedIn experiences match to that, that would be a huge win for me independent of promotion, or compensation.
cards.zh: 我一進去就跟我主管講了：「我來這裡是為了學會怎麼當一個更好的創辦人。」所以只要 LinkedIn 的經歷能配上這個目標，對我就是大勝利，跟升職或薪水無關。
cards.why: independent of promotion, or compensation 這半句是全句的重量所在——你先放棄了對方最容易拿來跟你交換的籌碼，反而讓你的請求變得可信、也讓主管不需要防你。「a huge win for me」則把個人目標翻譯成對方聽得懂的成敗語言。
swaps: I'm optimizing for learning here, not title
What I want out of this role is X — the promotion piece is secondary
cards.pmNote: 跟主管講清楚你要什麼，主管才有辦法把對的專案給你；沒講的人只會拿到剩下的專案。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

cards.pattern: I respect you so much as [角色]. I want to tell you that [我這一端的觀察落差]
cards.quote: I shared a lot of my impressions with her and I told her, "I respect you so much as an operator. I want to tell you that in the physical meeting that we had together, there was this disparity on how I would've potentially perceived you."
cards.zh: 我把我的印象跟她說了：「我非常尊敬你作為一個經營者的能力。我想跟你講，我們那次實體見面時，我對你的印象跟我原本認識的你有落差。」
cards.why: 整句都掛在「我」上：my impressions、how I would've perceived you。沒有一句是「你錯了」，全部是「我這一端看到什麼」，對方沒有東西可以反駁、也不必防衛。disparity（落差）比 problem 更中性，把事實留給對方自己去解讀。
swaps: I want to name something I noticed, and it's just my read
There's a gap between how I know you and how you came across that day
cards.pmNote: radical candor 的操作定義：先證明你在乎（care personally），才有資格直接挑戰（challenge directly）。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

cards.quote: Her reaction was like, "Oh my God, Ada. No one has ever connected the dots for me. Thank you so much."
cards.zh: 她的反應是：「天啊 Ada，從來沒有人幫我把這些點連起來。真的太謝謝你了。」
cards.why: 接難聽回饋的高分答案。connect the dots 把對方定位成「幫我補上了缺的那條線」，而不是「指出我的缺點」——你不但沒有防衛，還把這次回饋重新定義成一份禮物。往後對方會更願意告訴你真話。
swaps: That's the first time anyone's put it that way — thank you
I really appreciate you saying the hard thing
cards.pmNote: 回饋的供給量取決於你上一次怎麼接。接得好，別人下次才敢講。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

cards.pattern: If you had asked me [某個時間點], it would've been [當時的答案]. Now, I have a couple asterisks on top of it.
cards.quote: If you had asked me when I first started the company, it would've been an enthusiastic hell yes. I totally recommend. Now, I have a couple asterisks on top of it.
cards.zh: 如果你在我剛創業的時候問我，答案會是超級肯定的「絕對推薦」。現在的話，我會加上幾個但書。
cards.why: 改變立場的標準句型：先誠實還原舊立場（而且講得很生動：enthusiastic hell yes），再用 asterisks（星號、但書）這個視覺化的名詞承接。asterisk 比 but 高明得多——它暗示主結論還在，只是要看註腳，不是自打嘴巴。
swaps: A year ago I'd have said X without hesitating. These days I'd caveat that
My answer used to be a flat yes — now it comes with conditions
cards.pmNote: strong opinions, loosely held：更新立場時保留舊立場的合理性，別假裝自己一直都是對的。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

cards.pattern: Roll it forward six months — what have you accomplished?
cards.quote: I ask them, "What are your goals when it comes to coaching? Roll it forward six months, what have you gotten done in your coaching experience."
cards.zh: 我會問他們：「你找教練的目標是什麼？把時間快轉六個月，那時候你在教練這件事上完成了什麼？」
cards.why: roll it forward 是教練式提問的萬用開關：把對方從「我現在很卡」的情緒狀態，硬拉到未來的完成式，逼出可驗收的具體成果。動詞用 gotten done 而不是 want——want 會拿到願望，done 才會拿到標準。
swaps: Fast-forward six months — what does good look like?
Play it out: it's December and this worked. What happened?
cards.pmNote: 同樣的問法可以用在 kickoff：把 OKR 從願望改寫成「季末我們會看到什麼」。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

cards.pattern: It's not [壞] because [善意的理由], it's [壞] because it's not [真正的缺陷]
cards.quote: And it's not bad because it's not well-intentioned, but it's bad because it's not contextual.
cards.zh: 它不好，不是因為對方沒有善意，而是因為它沒有考慮你的處境。
cards.why: 先幫被批評的對象洗清動機，再把矛頭精準對到結構問題上。這個 not X because A, but because B 的雙層結構，讓你可以在完全不得罪人的情況下說出很重的判斷。台灣人常見的講法是直接說 it's bad advice，殺傷力大又沒說清楚壞在哪。
swaps: The issue isn't intent, it's fit
Nobody's wrong here — the advice just doesn't account for your situation
cards.pmNote: 評估外部建議先問一句「這個建議預設了什麼 context」，多數建議的失效點都在 context 而不在邏輯。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

cards.pattern: This is one potential solve of [對方的問題]
cards.quote: I sat for about a half a day and I thought, I think I can help here, drew out an org chart, put my name on the top, walked into my boss's office and said, "This is one potential solve of your marketing organization question."
cards.zh: 我想了大概半天，覺得我應該幫得上忙，就畫了一張組織圖，把自己放在最上面，走進我主管辦公室說：「這是你那個行銷組織問題的其中一個解法。」
cards.why: one potential solve 是精準的自我降級：不是「這是解法」而是「這是解法之一」，主管保有否決權，你的提案就不會變成逼宮。另外注意 solve 在矽谷被當名詞用（a solve），比 solution 更輕、更像草稿。
swaps: Here's one way this could work
This is one shape it could take — happy to sketch others
cards.pmNote: 要一個新職位／新組織，最短路徑是替決策者把組織圖畫好；你不是在要，是在幫他省下思考成本。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.pattern: That's solving a problem for the company. That's not solving [自己的問題].
cards.quote: That's solving a problem for the company. That's not solving a career growth issue for an individual. And I think people who want to be promoted need to think in that orientation versus the other.
cards.zh: 那是在解決公司的問題，不是在解決個人的職涯成長問題。想升遷的人要用前面那種角度思考，不是後面那種。
cards.why: 兩個對稱的短句就完成了一次視角切換的教學。X, not Y 的並列句在英語裡是最有力的定義工具——不解釋、不論證，直接把兩個選項擺在一起讓對比自己說話。爭取任何東西前，先把它翻譯成公司的問題。
swaps: Frame it as a gap in the org, not a gap in your résumé
Make the ask about the business, not about you
cards.pmNote: 升遷提案的黃金格式：這個職位不存在造成公司什麼損失＋為什麼我是填補這個洞的最低風險選項。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.pattern: Look, your span of control — you have [數字] direct reports, you need leverage here. I have [你的籌碼].
cards.quote: Instead of saying, "Look, your span of control, you have nine direct reports, you need leverage here. I have a lot of credibility with this side of the product organization. I think we could be doing more if this position existed."
cards.zh: 換成這樣講：「你看你的管理幅度，你手下有九個直屬，你需要有人幫你分擔。我在產品組織這一邊累積了不少信任。我覺得如果有這個職位，我們可以做得更多。」
cards.why: 三步：指出對方的痛（span of control 是個可量化的管理術語）→ 陳述你的獨特資產（credibility with…）→ 用 we could be doing more 把好處收回到團隊。全程主詞在 you 跟 we，只有中間那句短短用了 I。
swaps: You're stretched across nine reports — that's where I can take load off
The bottleneck is your bandwidth; here's what I can absorb
cards.pmNote: span of control（管理幅度）是要求開新主管職時最有效的量化依據。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.pattern: The way you are operating is not meeting [標準]. I believe you can operate differently, but it is your responsibility to do so.
cards.quote: I said, "The way you are operating is not meeting our leadership expectations. If you do not change, you cannot be part of this organization anymore. I believe you can operate differently."
cards.zh: 我跟他們說：「你們現在的做事方式沒有達到我們對領導者的期待。如果不改變，你們就不能繼續留在這個組織。我相信你們有能力用不同的方式做事。」
cards.why: 三拍：事實（not meeting expectations）→ 後果（cannot be part of…）→ 信任（I believe you can）。少了第三拍就是威脅，少了第二拍就是空話。注意用 the way you are operating 而不是 you are bad，罵的是行為模式不是人。
swaps: This isn't meeting the bar. It has to change, and I think you're capable of changing it
I'm telling you straight because I think you can turn this around
cards.pmNote: 績效談話一定要包含「後果」跟「我相信你做得到」兩句，缺一不可——只講後果會逼走人，只講相信會沒人動。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.pattern: Saying [直白版] is much kinder than [委婉版]
cards.quote: And I honestly think saying, "You are not doing a good job," is much kinder than, "I think you can improve on this aspect or that aspect."
cards.zh: 老實說我覺得直接講「你做得不夠好」，其實比「我覺得你在某某方面可以再進步」還要仁慈。
cards.why: 把 kind 這個字重新定義：仁慈＝讓對方知道真實處境，不是讓對話當下好過。台灣人習慣把 kind 等同於婉轉，這句直接把兩者切開。搭配 Brené Brown 的 "Clear is kind"，是英語職場給重話時最常引用的正當性來源。
swaps: Clear is kind
Vague feedback isn't kindness, it's avoidance
cards.pmNote: 回饋含糊會讓當事人以為只差一點，錯過真正調整的時間窗；模糊的溫柔是遲來的殘忍。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.quote: And that means being very clear when people are not meeting expectations, making it very clear that questioning ideas is not questioning innate talent.
cards.zh: 這代表在別人沒達到期待時要講得很清楚，同時也要講清楚：質疑一個想法，不等於質疑一個人的天賦。
cards.why: 一句話就把「對事不對人」翻成可以直接說出口的英文。開會前先講這句，等於預先幫團隊裝上一層防護，之後你怎麼挑戰想法都不會被讀成人身攻擊。台灣人多半只在心裡想，沒有把這條規則說出來。
swaps: I'm poking at the idea, not at you
Attack the problem, not each other
cards.pmNote: 把這句寫進團隊的 working agreement，比事後道歉有效十倍。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.pattern: Is [X] going to happen? Probably not. Are [Y] going to shift? Yes. Could it happen faster than we anticipate? Probably.
cards.quote: Is it going to eliminate PMs next year? Probably not. Are the ratios between PMs and other teams going to shift over time? Yes. Are the skills required going to shift? Yes. Could they shift much faster than we all anticipate? Probably.
cards.zh: 明年就會取代 PM 嗎？大概不會。PM 跟其他團隊的比例會不會變？會。需要的技能會不會變？會。會不會變得比我們預期的快很多？很可能。
cards.why: 自問自答（rhetorical Q&A）把一個含糊的大問題拆成四個可以各自回答的小問題，每題只給一到兩個字。這是面對「你怎麼看 AI」這種爛問題的最佳武器：你不必有完整答案，也顯得非常有結構。
swaps: Let me break that into three questions...
Short term? No. Medium term? Almost certainly.
cards.pmNote: 面對不確定的趨勢，把問題拆成「會不會發生 / 什麼會變 / 多快」三軸，比直接下判斷安全也更有用。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.pattern: I tend to be very short-term pessimistic and very long-term optimistic
cards.quote: At the highest level, I tend to be very short-term pessimistic, although I'll frame that short-term pessimistic and very long-term optimistic.
cards.zh: 從最高層次看，我大致上是短期悲觀、長期樂觀的。
cards.why: 用「時間軸」而不是「程度」來拆立場，一句話同時容納兩個相反的判斷而不矛盾。I tend to be 是再加一層自我限定，讓這變成傾向而非教條。被問任何趨勢題都可以套。
swaps: Bearish this year, bullish this decade
I'm cautious on the timeline, not on the direction
cards.pmNote: 區分「方向對不對」跟「時間到了沒」是策略討論最常混淆的兩件事。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.pattern: Is it [高標準]? No. Does it need to be? No.
cards.quote: It's making what I would consider real money. Is it a venture scale thing? No. Does it need to be? No. I have a ambitious but not audacious goal for ChatPRD.
cards.zh: 它有在賺我認為是真的錢。是那種創投等級的規模嗎？不是。需要是嗎？也不需要。我對 ChatPRD 的目標是有企圖心，但不到誇張。
cards.why: 先自己問出最尖銳的質疑（Is it venture scale?）再自己否認，然後補上 Does it need to be? 把整個評分標準推翻掉。ambitious but not audacious 這種「調節形容詞對」是英語裡設定期待值的漂亮手法。
swaps: Is it huge? No. Was it meant to be? Also no.
It's meaningful money — not life-changing money, and that's fine
cards.pmNote: 側專案先講清楚成功的定義，才不會被別人的 KPI 綁架。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.pattern: I agree with you. Now, I think it's [你要補的那一塊] though...
cards.quote: I agree with you. I totally agree with you. Now, I think it's the human aspect though of boldness, seeing the future in a way that a thing trained on priors cannot.
cards.zh: 我同意你，完全同意。不過我覺得，人的那一塊——那種膽識、那種能看見未來的能力，是只學過去資料的東西做不到的。
cards.why: 先給滿分同意（而且重複一次加強誠意），再用 Now... though 開一個新的維度。這不是反駁，是加碼——對方的立場完整保留，你的觀點疊在上面。台灣人常直接跳到 but，聽起來像前面的同意是假的。
swaps: Totally with you. The piece I'd add is...
Yes — and the part that keeps nagging me is...
cards.pmNote: "Yes, and" 比 "yes, but" 在會議裡多買到 30 秒的注意力。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.pattern: That is an artificial timeline introduced by [某個系統]. It's not a real thing.
cards.quote: That is an artificial timeline introduced by Google Calendar or whatever calendar you use. It's not a real thing, and so I want to put us on real timelines.
cards.zh: 那只是 Google 日曆——或你們用的任何行事曆——生出來的假期限，它不是真的。所以我希望我們回到真正的時間軸上。
cards.why: 把一個大家默認的東西（下次開會再決定）點名為「某個工具的副產品」，assumption 就瞬間失去正當性。artificial / real 的對比是拆假設最省力的一組詞：你不必證明它錯，只要證明它不是天生的。
swaps: That deadline is an artifact of the calendar, not the work
Who set that date, and what actually depends on it?
cards.pmNote: 組織的節奏會不自覺對齊會議節奏；把決策日期跟會議日期脫鉤是最便宜的加速手段。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.pattern: Bring the clock speed one click faster: if you think it needs to be done this year, it needs to be done this half.
cards.quote: I communicate to my leaders that my expectation is they bring in the clock speed one click faster, which means if you think something needs to be done this year, it needs to be done this half.
cards.zh: 我會跟我的主管們講，我的期待是把時鐘往前撥一格：如果你覺得某件事今年要做完，那就是這半年要做完。
cards.why: 一個具體到可以當場執行的比喻（one click faster），加上一組階梯範例，讓抽象的「要更快」變成任何人在說出日期前都能自我檢查的動作。這是把價值觀翻譯成行為的示範句。
swaps: Pull it in by one increment
Whatever date you're about to say, move it up one notch
cards.pmNote: 設定節奏比催進度有效：讓「一格」變成團隊語言，你就不用每次都當壞人。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.pattern: People think I'm hired to [表象]. In fact, I say I'm hired to [真正的任務].
cards.quote: People often think that I get hired into later stage companies because I'm supposed to teach them how to operate like a big company, and in fact, I say I'm hired to remind them they can operate like a startup.
cards.zh: 大家常以為，公司找我去後期階段是要我教他們怎麼像大公司一樣運作；但其實我都說，我是被找去提醒他們，他們還可以像新創一樣運作。
cards.why: 「別人以為 A，其實我是 B」是自我定位最漂亮的一次翻轉，把一句自介變成一個觀點。注意動詞從 teach 換成 remind——remind 預設能力本來就在，只是被忘了，比 teach 少了說教味。
swaps: I'm not here to add process — I'm here to take it away
The job isn't to make us bigger, it's to make us faster
cards.pmNote: 空降主管的第一場自介決定接下來半年的抗拒程度：先定義你不是來做什麼。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.quote: I think the other thing is really asking yourself, "What do I do that no one else in this organization can do?" There are lots of things that I do that other people in the organization can do.
cards.zh: 另外一件事是問自己：「我做的哪些事，是這個組織裡其他人做不到的？」我做的很多事，其實別人也能做。
cards.why: 把「我的價值」這種模糊自評，換成一個可證偽的問題：可替代 vs. 不可替代。談加薪、談升遷、談範疇時，答案就是你唯一的籌碼。後半句主動承認多數工作可被取代，反而讓前半句更可信。
swaps: Where am I genuinely hard to replace?
What's the work only I can do at this company right now?
cards.pmNote: Claire 稱之為 zone of genius；作法是把上季行事曆全部分類，只留最頂那一格。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.pattern: I never want to be a bottleneck for [組織]
cards.quote: The third thing on pace is personal SLA. I never want to be a bottleneck for the organization.
cards.zh: 節奏的第三件事是個人的 SLA。我從來不想成為組織的瓶頸。
cards.why: personal SLA 把服務業的術語（回應時效承諾）搬到個人身上，是矽谷主管很愛用的自我要求語。bottleneck 則是一個所有工程師都秒懂的比喻：你不是慢，你是卡住整條線。用在自我檢討或替別人設期待都成立。
swaps: I don't want to be the blocker here
My turnaround shouldn't be what slows this down
cards.pmNote: 主管的回應速度會被整個組織拿來當上限；你慢一天，下游慢一週。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.quote: It sounds wonderful, having one person to deal with across all these functions. — It is and isn't. I'll just say, I've done both.
cards.zh: 「有一個人統管這些功能聽起來很棒。」——是也不是。我只能說，兩種我都做過。
cards.why: 三個字擋掉一個過度簡化的結論，而且完全不失禮。It is and isn't 保留了對方一半的正確性，再用 I'll just say 開場自己的版本。在被引導性問題（leading question）逼到牆角時，這是最好的緩衝墊。
swaps: Yes and no
It depends more than people think
cards.pmNote: 被問「這樣做是不是比較好」時，先確認前提是否成立，再回答好壞。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.pattern: I'm a [立場] apologist, unabashedly.
cards.quote: And I'm a sales-led product apologist unabashedly, which is, I think that it is okay to listen to the market and to be commercially oriented in products.
cards.zh: 我毫不掩飾地是「業務導向產品」的辯護者——我覺得傾聽市場、讓產品帶商業考量，是可以的。
cards.why: apologist 在這裡不是道歉，是「公開替某個不受歡迎立場辯護的人」。自稱 apologist + unabashedly，等於先承認自己的立場是少數派，反而奪走對方嘲笑你的空間。這是在同溫層裡講異見的標準開場。
swaps: I'll defend this one, unpopular as it is
I know this is heresy in product circles, but...
cards.pmNote: product-led vs sales-led 不是道德問題，是市場結構問題；企業軟體多數是後者贏。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.pattern: I raised my hand and I said, "I'll [接下這件事]. I think I know what we need."
cards.quote: And I raised my hand and I said, "I'll IC this. I think I know what we need."
cards.zh: 我就舉手說：「這個我自己下去做。我大概知道我們需要什麼。」
cards.why: raise my hand 是英語職場「自願接下」的固定說法（不是真的舉手）。IC 當動詞用（individual contributor→「我自己捲袖子做」）是矽谷主管的自貶式炫技。後面接 I think I know，保留一點不確定，避免變成打包票。
swaps: I'll take this one myself
Let me own this — I have a rough idea of the shape
cards.pmNote: 主管親自 IC 一個小專案，是最快取得團隊技術信任的方式。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

cards.quote: But now I am making more in compensation that I made at Uber. Part of it is just luck, part of this is situational.
cards.zh: 但我現在的收入比在 Uber 的時候還高。其中一部分純粹是運氣，一部分是時機造成的。
cards.why: 先把最硬的數字結論放上桌，再馬上分掉功勞。part of it… part of this… 的雙拍節奏比單一句 I was lucky 有說服力——它暗示你認真分析過成因，只是誠實地承認有幾份不屬於你。講成績最怕聽起來像全靠自己。
swaps: Timing had a lot to do with it
A good chunk of this was circumstance, not skill
cards.pmNote: 在績效回顧裡自己先講出外部因素，比讓主管替你講出來好。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

cards.pattern: I had a spreadsheet where I listed, for every [產出], how much [指標] moved a week later.
cards.quote: I had a spreadsheet that I maintained for the first year of the publication, where I listed, for every article, how much did my annual revenue go up a week later. So tracking what was the impact.
cards.zh: 電子報第一年我維護了一份表，把每一篇文章對應到一週後年營收增加了多少。就是在追蹤 impact。
cards.why: 把「我有做事」變成「我有一份把每個動作對應到數字的紀錄」。for every X, how much did Y move 是量化影響力的通用模板；結尾一句 So tracking what was the impact 把工程細節翻譯回商業語言，是簡報時的必要收尾。
swaps: I tracked each launch against the metric a week out
Every shipped feature got mapped to a number
cards.pmNote: 沒有 baseline 的 impact 都是故事；先建表，再談貢獻。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

cards.quote: And this sounds like a fairytale. And if you do this, I guarantee you're not going to get the same results. In fact, you'll probably see way smaller numbers.
cards.zh: 這聽起來像童話。如果你照做，我可以保證你不會拿到一樣的結果——很可能數字會小很多。
cards.why: 講完自己的漂亮成績後，主動拆掉倖存者偏誤。這句的社交效果極強：它同時證明你誠實、也證明你懂統計，還讓聽眾不會因為做不到而暗自討厭你。分享成功經驗時最缺的一句話。
swaps: My numbers aren't a template — they're one data point
Don't take this as a playbook; the conditions were unusual
cards.pmNote: 拿 case study 說服人時，先講清楚哪些前提不可複製，論點反而更站得住。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

cards.pattern: What I didn't tell you is that there was at least [N] years of accidental work behind this.
cards.quote: What I didn't tell is that there was at least six years of accidental work behind this. I started a blog six years before... Actually, I've always been blogging since I graduated.
cards.zh: 我沒講的是，這背後至少有六年、不是刻意規劃的累積。我在那之前六年就開始寫部落格了——其實我從畢業就一直在寫。
cards.why: What I didn't tell you is… 是把敘事拉回真相的開關，等於自己承認前面那版是簡化過的。accidental work（不是刻意為之的累積）這個搭配很少見，卻精準描述了大部分職涯真相：不是規劃來的，但確實是做出來的。
swaps: What that story leaves out is the six years before it
The overnight part took about six years
cards.pmNote: 說自己的成功故事時，補上「看不見的準備期」會讓故事更可信、也更有用。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

cards.pattern: I wish I could tell you [完整答案], but the best advice I have is still [別人的], except I have less conviction.
cards.quote: So there was years of work, and I wish I could tell you how to build a successful newsletter, but the best advice I have is still what Jeff Atwood does, except I have less conviction.
cards.zh: 所以那是好幾年的累積。我很希望能告訴你怎麼做出一份成功的電子報，但我最好的建議還是 Jeff Atwood 那一套——只是我沒有他那麼有把握。
cards.why: 承認不知道的高階版本：不是說「我不知道」，而是「我能給的最好答案是別人的，而且我的信心比他低」。except I have less conviction 這種對自己信心程度的量化，是英語裡表達知識誠實最優雅的方式之一。
swaps: I don't have a better answer than X, and I hold it loosely
The honest answer is I'm less sure than I sound
cards.pmNote: 資深的訊號不是知道更多，是能精確描述自己的不確定程度。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

cards.pattern: Don't get me wrong, I'm not trying to [對方擔心的事]. But [你的保留].
cards.quote: Again, don't get me wrong, I'm not trying to talk people out of doing it. But for me, a lot of this was luck.
cards.zh: 先說清楚，我不是想勸大家不要做。但對我來說，這裡面有很大一部分是運氣。
cards.why: don't get me wrong 是英語裡最實用的預防針：先否認對方可能誤讀的那個版本，再放出真正的保留意見。有這半句，後面的 but 就不會被聽成潑冷水。台灣人常常直接講 but，然後花五分鐘解釋自己不是那個意思。
swaps: To be clear, I'm not saying don't do it
I'm not trying to discourage anyone here — but
cards.pmNote: 提出風險前先聲明你支持這個方向，風險才會被當成建議而不是抵制。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

cards.pattern: I don't want to say [重話], but it's kind of true.
cards.quote: So this might mean that I think... I don't want to say that if you don't have experience, don't start one, but it's kind of true. So become an expert somewhere, somehow, before you start.
cards.zh: 我不想說「沒經驗就別開始」這種話……但其實有點是真的。所以動手前，先想辦法在某個地方變成專家。
cards.why: 把重話包在「我不想這樣說」裡再送出去——句子講完了，責任卻分掉了一半。but it's kind of true 這個補刀是關鍵：它承認自己剛剛做了什麼，反而顯得誠實而不是狡猾。
swaps: I hate to put it that bluntly, but roughly, yes
That sounds harsher than I mean it, though it's not wrong
cards.pmNote: 給殘酷但有用的建議時，先示意你知道它很殘酷，接受度會高很多。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

cards.pattern: So a downside we haven't mentioned, but I'm just going to call it out, is [X].
cards.quote: So a downside we haven't mentioned, but I'm just going to call it out, is holiday.
cards.zh: 有一個我們還沒提到的缺點，我就直接講出來——就是休假。
cards.why: 把一個沒人提的議題塞進對話的正規做法：先標記它是「我們還沒講的」（表示你在追蹤整場討論），再用 I'm just going to call it out 取得發言權。just 讓這個動作看起來很輕，實際上你剛剛改變了議程。
swaps: One thing nobody's said yet, and I'll just say it:
Can I put one more item on the table?
cards.pmNote: 會議裡沒人願意講的那件事，通常就是決策真正卡住的地方。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

cards.pattern: You said something really important, and I want to double down on that.
cards.quote: And one last thing to touch on, you said something really important about pull, and I want to double down on that.
cards.zh: 還有最後一件事，你剛剛講到「拉力」那個點很重要，我想把它再放大講。
cards.why: 接話的最佳姿勢：先把功勞給對方（you said something really important），再宣告你要做的動作（double down＝加碼、放大，源自 21 點的加倍下注）。你講的其實是自己的內容，但整段聽起來是在延伸別人的觀點。
swaps: I want to build on what you just said
Let me pull on that thread a bit
cards.pmNote: 會議裡要讓自己的觀點被採納，最省力的路徑是掛在別人已經被接受的觀點上。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

cards.pattern: I just felt this pull — I was able to double down on it.
cards.quote: I just felt this pull, of this huge interest of people caring about this. The point was, I was able to double down on this pull.
cards.zh: 我就感覺到一股拉力——一大群人真的在乎這件事。重點是，我有辦法對這股拉力加碼。
cards.why: pull 當名詞用（市場拉力、需求拉力）是矽谷特有的說法，台灣人幾乎不會這樣講，通常只會說 demand。felt a pull 帶有「我沒去推，是它把我拉過去」的意味，正好對應 product-market fit 的體感描述。
swaps: There was real pull from the market
People were pulling this out of me faster than I could push it
cards.pmNote: push 要靠行銷預算，pull 才是真需求；分不清這兩者的團隊會一直加行銷卻沒有留存。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

cards.quote: One is people set this goal, I want to be promoted the next thing, or I want to lead this big project. And those are bad goals, because it's not in your control. A good goal is what you can do.
cards.zh: 有一種是設「我要升到下一級」或「我要主導那個大專案」。這些是壞目標，因為不在你的掌控裡。好目標是你自己做得到的事。
cards.why: 用「掌控權」單一維度把目標分成兩類，判準乾淨到可以現場套用。not in your control 是英語裡談目標設定的核心慣用語；台灣人通常說「不切實際」，但那是在談難度，講不到真正的問題。
swaps: Set inputs you control, not outcomes you don't
Own the behaviour, not the verdict
cards.pmNote: 個人 OKR 用可控的輸入指標；輸出指標留給組織層級。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

cards.quote: And I'm now doing stuff that I love, and in some strange way, I guess it even pays better.
cards.zh: 我現在在做我喜歡的事，而且莫名其妙地，好像還賺得更多。
cards.why: in some strange way + I guess 兩層減震器，把一句相當高調的話（收入超過大廠主管）壓到聽起來像是連自己都覺得不可思議。這正是英語裡「炫耀而不像炫耀」的核心技術：把驚訝的位置留給自己。
swaps: Somehow it's worked out better than the day job
Oddly enough, the numbers ended up higher
cards.pmNote: 談待遇或成果時，用「連我自己都意外」的框架，比用「我早就知道」少樹敵。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

cards.pattern: I'll tell the story that is kind of true — and also the real deal behind it.
cards.quote: I'll tell the story that is kind of true, and people will think it's amazing, and also the real deal behind it.
cards.zh: 我先講那個「差不多是真的」的版本，大家會覺得很厲害；然後再講背後真正的狀況。
cards.why: 先預告自己要講兩個版本，等於在故事開始前就買到了信任。kind of true 這種對真實度的自我標註在英語裡很自然，中文直譯成「有點真」會怪，實際上要翻成「差不多是真的」。the real deal 指的是真正的內情。
swaps: Here's the polished version — then I'll tell you what actually happened
Let me give you the highlight reel first, then the messy bit
cards.pmNote: postmortem 也適用：先講對外的說法，再講內部真正的因果，兩者的差距本身就是資訊。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

cards.pattern: I'll be honest, I didn't really enjoy [某段經歷]. It felt a bit too [形容詞].
cards.quote: I'll be honest, I didn't really enjoy being a manager of managers. It felt a bit too abstract. I didn't like being in the meetings, not doing the work.
cards.zh: 老實說，我沒有很喜歡當「管理主管的主管」。感覺有點太抽象了。我不喜歡一直在開會、卻沒有真的在做事。
cards.why: 面試裡講不喜歡的經歷，安全格式是：I'll be honest（宣告誠實模式）→ didn't really enjoy（用 really 弱化，不是 hated）→ 給一個關於工作性質的具體理由，而不是關於人的抱怨。整段沒有一個字在怪別人。
swaps: Honestly, that layer wasn't a fit for me
I found I missed being close to the work
cards.pmNote: 面試被問「你為什麼離開管理職」，把答案定位在工作型態偏好，不要定位在組織或人。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

cards.pattern: As [職稱], I have a team of folks who are really passionate about [使命]
cards.quote: As head of fan monetization, I have a team of folks who are really passionate about figuring out new ways to help artists and fans connect and also figure out ways to make those connections result in new monetization opportunities for the artists.
cards.zh: 我的職稱是 head of fan monetization，我帶一群很熱衷於「幫藝人跟粉絲建立連結」的人，同時想辦法把這些連結變成藝人新的收入來源。
cards.why: 介紹職務不列職掌，而是講「我的團隊在乎什麼＋要把什麼變成什麼」。這種句型讓一個乾巴巴的頭銜變成一個有方向的故事，也自然帶出你的價值主張。台灣人自介常見的 I'm responsible for A, B and C 完全沒有這個效果。
swaps: My team's job is to turn X into Y
I run the group that's trying to answer: how do we...?
cards.pmNote: 團隊介紹用 mission statement 格式（把什麼變成什麼），比列功能清單更容易被記住與轉述。
cards.episode: Monetizing passions, scaling marketplaces, and stories from a creator economy vet | Camille Hearst (Spotify, Patreon, Apple, YouTube)

cards.pattern: Which actually brings me to the flip side of the question you asked, which was [原問題]
cards.quote: Which actually brings me to the flip side of the question which you asked what is the hardest part.
cards.zh: 這剛好把我帶回你問的另一半問題——最難的部分是什麼。
cards.why: 講到一半發現自己離題時的優雅回收：不道歉、不說 sorry I digressed，而是把離題說成一條通往下半題的路（brings me to）。flip side of the question 是「同一個問題的另一面」，適用所有「最好／最壞」「優點／缺點」的雙問。
swaps: Which loops me back to the second half of your question
That's a natural bridge to what you asked about the downside
cards.pmNote: 被問雙問題時先答一半，再用 bridge 回收另一半，比一開始就宣告「我分兩部分回答」自然。
cards.episode: Monetizing passions, scaling marketplaces, and stories from a creator economy vet | Camille Hearst (Spotify, Patreon, Apple, YouTube)

cards.pattern: There's no way you can [趨勢A] and [趨勢B] and not see [結果] emerge.
cards.quote: There's no way that you can lower the cost of content creation and increase the scale of distribution and not see this emerge, this creator economy I think emerge.
cards.zh: 你不可能同時把內容製作成本壓低、又把發行規模放大，然後這個東西——創作者經濟——不出現。
cards.why: 把主張寫成「雙重否定的必然性」：不是「我覺得會發生」，而是「這兩件事同時成立，它不發生才奇怪」。論點的重量從個人判斷轉移到結構條件上，反對者必須先推翻你的前提才能反駁你。
swaps: If cost goes down and reach goes up, this outcome is basically arithmetic
You can't have both of those and not get this
cards.pmNote: 機會評估最有力的說法是「結構已經改變」，不是「市場很大」。
cards.episode: Monetizing passions, scaling marketplaces, and stories from a creator economy vet | Camille Hearst (Spotify, Patreon, Apple, YouTube)

cards.pattern: The second piece of advice I would give: I think we should have [做法] from the beginning.
cards.quote: And then the second piece of advice I would give I think we should have been talking to potential acquirers from the beginning and sharing our vision and what we were trying to accomplish because we started those quite late in our journey as a company.
cards.zh: 我要給的第二個建議是：我覺得我們一開始就該去跟潛在的收購方聊，分享我們的願景跟想達成的事。我們啟動得太晚了。
cards.why: 把自己的失誤包裝成給別人的建議（advice I would give），既承擔了錯誤，又立刻把它轉成對聽者有用的東西。we should have… from the beginning 的完成式虛擬語氣是承擔錯誤的標準時態，比 we made a mistake 有建設性得多。
swaps: If I were doing it again, I'd start that conversation on day one
The thing I'd fix: we were late to that
cards.pmNote: postmortem 的產出格式最好是「下次的建議」，因為它天然強迫你把教訓寫成可執行的動作。
cards.episode: Monetizing passions, scaling marketplaces, and stories from a creator economy vet | Camille Hearst (Spotify, Patreon, Apple, YouTube)

cards.pattern: We're working on something cool. It aligns with what you're doing. Maybe there's a partnership here.
cards.quote: Or if the meeting is not under the context of buying it all, it's like, "We're working on something cool. We have a great vision. It aligns with what you're doing. Maybe there's a partnership here."
cards.zh: 或者那場會根本不是在談收購，而是：「我們在做一件很酷的事，我們有很好的願景，跟你們在做的方向對得上。也許這裡有合作的空間。」
cards.why: 真實目的是被收購，開場卻只講 alignment 跟 partnership。Maybe there's… 這種弱化到極致的提議句，讓對方可以毫無壓力地回應——而你需要的其實只是在對方腦中留下位置。這是英語商務裡最常見的迂迴前置動作。
swaps: There might be something here worth exploring together
Not pitching anything — just think our directions overlap
cards.pmNote: 被收購的前置作業是關係，不是流程；等你要賣的時候才第一次見面，估值一定吃虧。
cards.episode: Monetizing passions, scaling marketplaces, and stories from a creator economy vet | Camille Hearst (Spotify, Patreon, Apple, YouTube)

cards.pattern: What drew me to [領域] probably was maybe accidental at the beginning.
cards.quote: What drew me to that side of the business probably was maybe accidental at the beginning. Just again, coming from this musical family and background, I always had a natural interest in helping artists make a living.
cards.zh: 會被那一塊業務吸引，一開始大概、應該說算是偶然吧。不過我出身音樂家庭，本來就對「幫藝術家養活自己」這件事有興趣。
cards.why: probably was maybe accidental 疊了三層不確定，聽起來像在回憶而不是在包裝履歷——這種「講得不完美」的誠實感反而建立信任。接著馬上補上真正的內在動機，讓偶然變成有跡可循。面試講職涯轉折非常好用。
swaps: Honestly, it started out as an accident
I fell into it — though looking back it wasn't random
cards.pmNote: 職涯敘事不必假裝一路規劃好；「偶然＋一以貫之的動機」比「精心設計」更可信。
cards.episode: Monetizing passions, scaling marketplaces, and stories from a creator economy vet | Camille Hearst (Spotify, Patreon, Apple, YouTube)

cards.pattern: Where I started really understanding [X] was actually [某段經歷]
cards.quote: But where I started understanding deeply the dynamics of the marketplace was actually my experience and the one job I've had that not been in the creator or art or these big consumer platforms.
cards.zh: 但我真正開始深入理解市集的運作機制，其實是在那份唯一不屬於創作者、藝術或大型消費平台的工作裡。
cards.why: 分裂句（cleft sentence）把「哪一段經歷」推到句子的焦點位置，強迫聽者等你揭曉。actually 更暗示答案跟大家猜的不一樣。履歷上最不起眼的那份工作，用這個句型就能變成你能力的來源。
swaps: The place I actually learned this was...
Funnily enough, the job that taught me most was the odd one out
cards.pmNote: 面試要凸顯一段冷門經歷，先用 cleft 句把它放進聚光燈，再解釋它為什麼是關鍵。
cards.episode: Monetizing passions, scaling marketplaces, and stories from a creator economy vet | Camille Hearst (Spotify, Patreon, Apple, YouTube)

cards.pattern: As a leader you are in the hot seat — if these things don't pan out, it's on you and not on your team.
cards.quote: So it's someone that as a leader, you are in the hot seat and you can take accountability. So if some of these things don't pan out, it's on you and not on your team, and give your team permission to fail.
cards.zh: 身為領導者，你就是坐在火線上、要負起責任的人。如果這些事沒成，那是你的責任，不是團隊的責任——同時給團隊失敗的許可。
cards.why: it's on you 是英語裡承擔責任最短的說法（比 I take responsibility 有力，因為它是描述事實而非宣告態度）。give your team permission to fail 則把承擔翻譯成一個可以發給別人的具體物件：許可。
swaps: If it fails, that's on me
The downside risk sits with me, not with the team
cards.pmNote: 要團隊挑高風險題目，必須先公開宣告失敗的帳算在誰頭上。
cards.episode: Monetizing passions, scaling marketplaces, and stories from a creator economy vet | Camille Hearst (Spotify, Patreon, Apple, YouTube)

cards.pattern: Tell me about something you're really proud of — and take me through the process.
cards.quote: I like to ask people to tell me about something they're really proud of that they accomplished and take me through the process and talk to me about why they're proud of it.
cards.zh: 我喜歡請對方講一件他真的很自豪的成就，帶我走過整個過程，並告訴我為什麼他覺得自豪。
cards.why: 面試官這題其實在問三件事：你做了什麼、你怎麼做的、你的評分標準是什麼。作答時三個都要給——尤其最後一個 why I'm proud，多數人漏掉，但那才是暴露你 what good looks like 的地方。take me through 是「帶我走一遍」的標準說法。
swaps: Walk me through something you're proud of
The part I'm proudest of is... and here's why
cards.pmNote: 回答時把「為什麼自豪」放在最後當收尾，等於主動告訴面試官你的品質標準。
cards.episode: Monetizing passions, scaling marketplaces, and stories from a creator economy vet | Camille Hearst (Spotify, Patreon, Apple, YouTube)

cards.quote: You should have 30 seconds for your play. Right? Don't ask me, I'm not a lawyer.
cards.zh: 應該有個三十秒的合理使用吧？別問我，我又不是律師。
cards.why: 先給出直覺答案，再用一句自嘲把責任推乾淨。這比一開始就說 I don't know 有用得多——你還是貢獻了資訊，只是標好了信心水位。I'm not a X, but… 這個句型在英語會議裡是拋出跨領域意見的通行證。
swaps: I'm not a lawyer, but my read is...
Take that with a pinch of salt — outside my lane
cards.pmNote: 跨領域發言先標註自己的資格邊界，別人才會把你的話當輸入而不是結論。
cards.episode: Monetizing passions, scaling marketplaces, and stories from a creator economy vet | Camille Hearst (Spotify, Patreon, Apple, YouTube)

cards.pattern: I'll have a hot take on this: for the vast majority of people, they probably do not need [X].
cards.quote: I'll have a hot take on this, and it's something that I share to people when I talk to them about coaching. But my hot take is that for the vast majority of people, they probably do not need a coach.
cards.zh: 我對這件事有個比較嗆的看法，這也是我跟人聊教練時會講的：對絕大多數人來說，其實不需要教練。
cards.why: I'll have a hot take on this 是先貼標籤再開槍：告訴聽眾接下來這句是刻意挑釁的、不是共識，對方就會用「聽意見」而不是「被冒犯」的模式接收。而且說這句的人是教練本人，自斷財路反而建立可信度。
swaps: Unpopular opinion, but...
This is going to sound odd coming from me, but...
cards.pmNote: Ada 稱這種自我拆台為 anti-sell：先講清楚你的服務不適合誰，剩下的人才會真的買。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

cards.pattern: Do you take it as [對事的解讀], or do you take it as [對人的解讀]?
cards.quote: So if your partner comes to you and says that marketing plan or that product roadmap that you put together, not good, do you take it as the plan is not good and let's talk about what we can actually do to fix it?
cards.zh: 如果你的夥伴跟你說，你做的行銷計畫或產品路線圖不好，你會理解成「這份計畫不好，我們來談怎麼修」嗎？
cards.why: 用一個二選一的問句，讓對方自己看見他選了哪一種解讀。do you take it as A, or do you take it as B 比直接說「你太玻璃心」有效一百倍，因為選擇權還在對方手上。這是教練式提問的骨架。
swaps: Which reading are you going with here?
Is that about the work, or about you?
cards.pmNote: 跨職能衝突多半來自「對事的批評被讀成對人」，先對齊解讀方式再談內容。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

cards.quote: So the ability to be really truth seeking and take the most respectful interpretation when you're giving feedback to focus on trying to get to a smart good outcome that benefits the business.
cards.zh: 所以那種追求真相、並且在給回饋時採取「最善意的解讀」的能力，目標是導向對生意有利的好結果。
cards.why: take the most respectful interpretation（常縮寫 MRI）是矽谷團隊的固定用語，指刻意選擇對方動機的最善意版本。它不是要你天真，而是一條協作紀律：先假設善意，衝突才有辦法談內容而不是談態度。
swaps: Assume positive intent
Let's give that the most generous reading and go from there
cards.pmNote: 非同步協作（Slack、文件留言）的誤讀率極高，MRI 幾乎是遠距團隊的必備預設值。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

cards.pattern: I gave myself this rule where I had to [具體動作] before I could [離開/結束]
cards.quote: So I gave myself this rule where I had to go out once a week for a couple of months, go to an external event, and I would count out 10 business cards.
cards.zh: 所以我給自己訂了一條規則：連續幾個月每週出去一次，去參加外部活動，然後數出十張名片。
cards.why: 談自己的成長不講心態，講「我替自己設計了什麼規則」。I gave myself this rule where… 這個句型把抽象的自律變成可驗證的機制，面試官會直接判斷你是一個會自己搭鷹架的人。台灣人常說 I forced myself to，那只講了意志力。
swaps: I set myself a hard rule:
I built a little forcing function for myself
cards.pmNote: 改變行為靠機制不靠意志：把想做的事變成有終止條件的規則（十張名片發完才能走）。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

cards.quote: I did that a couple of weeks in a row, and it was horrible. It was really awful, but it got a lot better.
cards.zh: 我連續做了好幾週，超痛苦，真的很難受，但後來好很多了。
cards.why: 承認過程很糟（而且用了兩次強烈形容詞）再翻轉，比一路正向的敘述可信得多。it got a lot better 是很輕的收尾，沒有誇大成功——這種「不誇張的翻轉」正是英語面試裡描述成長曲線最舒服的比例。
swaps: The first few times were rough, and then it wasn't
I was bad at it, publicly, for about a month
cards.pmNote: Ada 稱這套為 eating your vegetables：分辨「我討厭它」是因為不擅長還是真的不合，要先做滿十次。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

cards.pattern: Here are [N] options. Can you pick your top two and tell me why?
cards.quote: So in your case, I said, "Here are nine topics. Can you pick your top two and tell me why you like them?"
cards.zh: 以你這次來說，我就是問：「這裡有九個主題，可以請你挑出你最喜歡的兩個，然後告訴我為什麼嗎？」
cards.why: 把開放題改成選擇題，把回覆成本壓到最低——這是提高回覆率的關鍵。and tell me why 那半句才是真正要的東西：選項揭露偏好，理由揭露判準。少了 why，你只會拿到一堆沒有資訊量的票數。
swaps: Which two jump out, and what makes them work for you?
Rank your top three — one line each on why
cards.pmNote: 好問題的三個條件：具體、能引出理由、不帶引導（不要先講你自己傾向哪個）。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

cards.pattern: Hi, my name's [X]. I just wanted to say thank you for [具體的事].
cards.quote: I said, "Hi, my name's Camille. I'm interning here this summer. It's my first day. I just wanted to say thank you for spending your time doing that speech for us on Saturday."
cards.zh: 我說：「嗨，我叫 Camille，今年夏天在這裡實習，今天是我第一天。我只是想跟你說謝謝，謝謝你週六花時間為我們做那場演講。」
cards.why: 跟大人物搭話的完整劇本：名字＋身分＋為什麼此刻在這裡＋一句具體的感謝，然後結束。I just wanted to say… 用 just 跟過去式把整段降級成「不佔你時間」，而且不要任何東西（不合照、不加聯絡方式），所以對方沒有防備的理由。
swaps: I just wanted to introduce myself and say thanks for X
No ask — I just wanted you to know that talk landed for me
cards.pmNote: 建立人脈最低成本的一步是「不帶請求的感謝」；有請求的初次接觸成功率低很多。
cards.episode: Monetizing passions, scaling marketplaces, and stories from a creator economy vet | Camille Hearst (Spotify, Patreon, Apple, YouTube)

cards.pattern: There's two ways of [規劃/思考這件事]. The way that you can [X] is you can [做法 A]... And the alternate is [做法 B].
cards.quote: So I guess there's two ways of planning. The way that you can plan is you can dream of what is the perfect vision of the future, what future do you want to exist in, what would you like the world to look like?
cards.zh: 我覺得規劃大概分兩種。一種是你去夢想那個最完美的未來——你想活在什麼樣的未來裡？你希望這個世界長什麼樣子？
cards.why: 開場先報數量（two ways），聽眾馬上知道要接兩個框、不會迷路；接著不下定義，改用三個並列的 what 問句把「願景」變成對方可以自己回答的東西。母語者講願景很少說「我的願景是⋯」，而是丟問句讓人走進去。
swaps: There are basically two ways to go about this.
You've got two options here — one is..., the alternate is...
cards.pmNote: 這就是 backcasting：從理想終局往回推，而不是從現有資源往上疊。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: It seemed really impossible that [現狀] would [持續下去]. And it just seemed so apparent to me that in the future it was going to be completely different.
cards.quote: And it seemed really impossible that it would stay on the desktop, it would stay really complicated. And it just seemed so apparent to me that in the future it was going to be completely different.
cards.zh: 它會一直留在桌機上、一直這麼複雜，這件事在我看來根本不可能。我當時就覺得很明顯，未來一定會完全不一樣。
cards.why: 兩句都用 seem（it seemed impossible / it seemed so apparent to me），把一個沒有證據的主觀判斷講得像是事情本來就擺在那裡。強度夠但留了退路——不是 I'm sure，是「在我看來很明顯」。台灣人常在這裡二選一：不是不敢講，就是講成 I'm 100% sure。
swaps: It seemed obvious to me that this couldn't last.
It felt inevitable that in a few years this would look completely different.
cards.pmNote: 講 vision 的力道來自「現狀不可能持續」的判斷，不是來自「我很有信心」。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: Could I [做到那件事]? I had absolutely no idea.
cards.quote: Could I build that future? I had absolutely no idea
cards.zh: 我做得出那個未來嗎？我完全不知道。
cards.why: 自問自答式的認錯：問句先替聽眾把懷疑問出來，再用 absolutely no idea 老實承認。效果是坦率而不是心虛——因為承認的是「能力」，前後包夾的都是「方向很篤定」。直接說 I don't know 會斷氣，這樣說反而加分。
swaps: Could we actually pull it off? No idea at the time.
Did I know how? Absolutely not.
cards.pmNote: 願景要篤定、路徑可以承認未知——把不確定性放在 how，不要放在 why。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: You kind of want to have a ladder that goes all the way up to [終極願景], and then you want to have rungs that just work its way up step by step.
cards.quote: You kind of want to have a ladder that goes all the way up to the moon, which is your crazy, wild vision. And then you want to have rungs that just work its way up step by step.
cards.zh: 你會希望有一把直達月球的梯子，那就是你那個瘋狂的大願景。然後你要有一階一階的橫桿，讓人可以一步一步往上爬。
cards.why: 一個意象同時裝下兩件常被拆開講的事：梯子＝遠到不合理的目標，橫桿＝可執行的每一步。用 ladder / rungs 這種有內建結構的比喻，比講 vision and milestones 更容易讓人記住並自己往下推。
swaps: You need a ladder to the moon, and then rungs you can actually climb.
Set the destination absurdly far out, then define the very next rung.
cards.pmNote: vision → mission pillars → 年度目標，就是這把梯子的橫桿。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: And it doesn't matter how small [第一步] is or how seemingly inconsequential, if it is working towards [那個未來].
cards.quote: And it doesn't matter how small that first step is or how seemingly inconsequential if it is working towards that future that you want to will into existence
cards.zh: 第一步有多小、看起來多微不足道，都沒關係——只要它是朝著你想召喚出來的那個未來走。
cards.why: 先主動承認對方會有的異議（這步小到很好笑），再用 if 子句把價值判準換成「方向」而不是「大小」。will something into existence 是母語者講願景的高頻搭配，台灣人幾乎不會用，但一講出來層次立刻不同。
swaps: It doesn't matter how small the first step is, as long as it points the right way.
However trivial that first move looks, it counts if it's in the right direction.
cards.pmNote: 評估第一個里程碑要看方向對不對，不是看規模夠不夠有面子。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: What is wild success for [X]? And then equally, what is terrible failure for [X]?
cards.quote: And I think an exercise we often do is what is wild success for X, or what is wild success for Y? And then equally, what is terrible failure for those things?
cards.zh: 我們常做的一個練習是：這件事的「誇張級成功」長什麼樣？然後同樣重要的，它的「災難級失敗」又長什麼樣？
cards.why: wild success / terrible failure 這組對照把模糊的目標一次夾出邊界，比 goal 或 KPI 更能逼出真實想法。And then equally 是關鍵：宣告下一句和上一句一樣重要，聽眾就不會把失敗那題當補充題敷衍過去。
swaps: What does wild success look like here? And equally, what does disaster look like?
Best case in ten years? And the version we'd hate?
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem 的正向孿生：同時定義成功與失敗，團隊才對得齊。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: The thing that I love about [一個看起來很嚇人的東西] is that you feel completely inadequate before it.
cards.quote: And I think the thing that I love about a crazy big goal is that you feel completely inadequate before it.
cards.zh: 我最喜歡「瘋狂大目標」的一點，就是站在它面前你會覺得自己完全不夠格。
cards.why: The thing I love about X is that [聽起來像缺點的東西]——用讚美句型裝一個負面詞，聽眾會頓一下、然後被迫重新理解那個詞。這是英文裡最省力的翻轉手法，適合任何你想幫某個「缺點」平反的場合。
swaps: What I love about this constraint is that it makes us uncomfortable.
The best part of a goal like that is that it's obviously out of reach.
cards.pmNote: 目標要大到讓團隊不敢照舊做法交差，才會逼出新解法。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: They would say, "[反對意見]." And I would say, "[立場]." And I'd add a new page in my deck that [直接回答那個反對].
cards.quote: So they would say, "Oh, your market's not big enough." And I would say, "It's going to be huge." And I'd add a new page in my pitch deck that said how big the market I believe was.
cards.zh: 他們會說：「你的市場不夠大。」我就說：「它會變超大。」然後我就在簡報裡加一頁，講我認為這市場有多大。
cards.why: 三拍結構：對方說什麼 → 我當場怎麼回 → 我事後改了什麼。第三拍才是重點，它把「被打槍」轉成「我的簡報變強了」，讓整段聽起來像進度報告而不是抱怨。講被拒絕的經驗一定要有第三拍，否則就只是訴苦。
swaps: They'd push back on X, and the next version of the deck answered X.
Every objection we heard twice became a slide.
cards.pmNote: 把重複出現的反對意見「pre-answer」進簡報前段，能省掉六小時的來回解釋。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: The first few pages became much more problem-based, because if people don't understand the problem then they can't care about your solution.
cards.quote: And so then the first few pages became very much more problem-based because if people don't understand the problem then they can't understand or care about your solution.
cards.zh: 所以前面幾頁後來就大改成以「問題」為主，因為人如果不懂那個問題，就不可能懂、也不可能在乎你的解法。
cards.why: 用一個 because 子句同時解釋「我改了什麼」和「為什麼非改不可」，而且理由是關於聽眾的心理、不是關於自己的偏好。can't understand or care 兩個動詞並列，把「聽不懂」和「不在乎」綁成同一件事——這正是台灣人簡報最常踩的坑：直接跳進解法。
swaps: We lead with the problem now, because nobody cares about a solution to a problem they don't feel.
If the problem isn't clear, the solution can't land.
cards.pmNote: problem statement 沒對齊，後面所有的 roadmap 討論都是空轉。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: It's kind of like [比喻]. And if you go and take [別人的做法] and stick it in [你這裡], it's probably not going to look very matched.
cards.quote: And it's kind of building a house that you want every brick in the house to match. And if you go and try and take some bricks from someone else's house and stick it in your house, it's probably going to not look very matched.
cards.zh: 這有點像蓋房子，你會希望每一塊磚都是搭的。如果你跑去人家家裡搬幾塊磚塞進自己家，看起來大概就是不搭。
cards.why: 反對「照抄大公司做法」卻完全沒有點名任何人，也沒有說 that won't work——只描述一個誰都看得出來不對勁的畫面，再用 probably 和 not very matched 收尾。要在會議上擋掉別人帶進來的舊公司 playbook，這是殺傷力最低、成功率最高的講法。
swaps: Borrowed practices tend not to match the rest of the house.
That worked there because of everything else that was true there.
cards.pmNote: 引進外部流程前先問：我們是不是也要引進讓它成立的那些前提？
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: Often people have [使命] kind of on the wall somewhere, and then what they're actually doing and the way they actually spend their time is in a very different direction.
cards.quote: Often people have a mission that's kind of on the wall somewhere and then what they're actually doing and the way they actually make money and the way people actually spend their time is in a very, very different direction from that original mission.
cards.zh: 很多公司的使命就掛在牆上某個地方，可是他們真正在做的事、真正賺錢的方式、大家真正把時間花在哪，跟那個使命的方向差超多。
cards.why: 三個 actually 連發（actually doing / actually make money / actually spend their time），一次把「說的」和「做的」拉開對照。actually 在英文口語裡就是揭穿的訊號詞，用它比用 but 或 however 更不像指控、卻更有力。
swaps: The mission is on the wall; the roadmap says something else.
What we say we're about and where the time actually goes are two different things.
cards.pmNote: 檢查策略是否真實：看時間與預算的流向，不要看願景頁。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: Just because [X] is all the rage and [某群人] really like it doesn't necessarily mean it should be front and center.
