cards.quote: Just because AI is all the rage and investors really like AI doesn't necessarily mean it should be front and center
cards.zh: AI 現在很紅、投資人也很愛，但這不代表它就該擺在最前面。
cards.why: Just because A doesn't mean B 是英文最好用的拆假設句型：先大方承認 A 是真的（不跟人吵事實），只否定那個沒人講出口的推論。加上 necessarily 又再軟一層，聽起來像在提醒而不是打臉。
swaps: Just because everyone's doing it doesn't mean it's right for us.
That it's popular doesn't automatically make it a priority.
cards.pmNote: 熱門技術要進 roadmap，判準是「有沒有幫使用者把事情做完」，不是「投資人愛不愛聽」。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: One of the most important things we did was we didn't really worry about [對手] at all. We just asked where is there a gap that we can uniquely fill.
cards.quote: One of the most important things that we did was we didn't really worry about competitors at all. We actually just saw where is there a gap in the market that we can uniquely fill
cards.zh: 我們做過最重要的一件事，就是根本不太管競爭對手。我們只看市場上哪裡有一個缺口，是我們可以獨一無二補上的。
cards.why: 先講「我們刻意不做什麼」再講「我們只做什麼」，一放一收就把策略講完了。uniquely fill 的 uniquely 是重點，它把 gap 從「沒人做的事」升級成「只有我們能做的事」——少了這個字，整句就變成單純的市場空白論。
swaps: We spent almost no time on competitors and all of it on the gap.
The question wasn't who else is here, it was what only we can do.
cards.pmNote: 競品分析容易變成 feature 對照表；真正該產出的是「我們獨有的缺口」。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: We're literally smack bang in the middle of that Venn diagram of [A] and [B], rather than making our customers have to make a choice between those two.
cards.quote: And what Canva really does is we're literally smack bang in the middle of that Venn diagram of creativity and productivity, rather than making our customers have to make a choice between those two suites.
cards.zh: Canva 真正在做的事，就是不偏不倚站在「創意」跟「生產力」這兩個圈的交集正中央，而不是逼客戶在兩邊二選一。
cards.why: 定位一句話講完：座標（Venn diagram 的交集）＋ 敵人（逼客戶二選一）。rather than 後面接的不是競品名字，而是客戶的痛，所以聽起來是在幫客戶說話而不是在自誇。smack bang in the middle 是很口語的加強語，可換成 right in the middle。
swaps: We sit right at the intersection of A and B.
Instead of asking people to pick a side, we cover both.
cards.pmNote: positioning 的黃金句型：先給座標，再給你替使用者消除的那個選擇題。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: You fast-forward [50 年] and you say: Are we in a safer world? Is this the [X] that we want?
cards.quote: Are we in a safer world? Is the world the place that we want our kids to grow up in? Is this the humanity that we want?
cards.zh: 我們有活在一個更安全的世界嗎？這是我們想讓小孩長大的世界嗎？這是我們要的人類文明嗎？
cards.why: 三個平行問句、一句比一句大（safer → our kids → humanity），完全不下結論。願景講到最後不給答案而給問句，聽者才會自己回答「不是」——那個「不是」由他們自己講出來，說服力才夠。
swaps: Fast-forward five years — is this the product we'd be proud of?
Is this the team we want to be in three years' time?
cards.pmNote: long-term vision 的檢查點：把時間軸拉遠到現有 KPI 全部失效，剩下的才是真的方向。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: Rather than just being fearful of [你擔心的事], I started to think what would the alternative be?
cards.quote: And then rather than just being fearful of the things that I'm worried about for society and for humanity, I started to think what would the alternative be?
cards.zh: 與其一直害怕那些我替社會、替人類擔心的事，我開始想：那另一種版本會長什麼樣？
cards.why: 把「反對什麼」轉成「想要什麼」的標準轉軸句。Rather than being fearful of X 先承認情緒是真的（不裝理性），再用 I started to think 把自己從受害者切換成設計者。抱怨型的同事最需要被丟這一句。
swaps: Instead of listing what worries us, let's describe the version we'd want.
Rather than fighting the thing we hate, what's the alternative we'd build?
cards.pmNote: 把 risk list 翻成 target state，團隊才有東西可以往前做。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: It's not something that I alone can achieve. I'd like to help change [X]. I'd like to help change [Y].
cards.quote: But I think that I'd like to change that. I'd like to help change the mood. I'd like to help change the way we're thinking about things.
cards.zh: 但我會想去改變這件事。我想幫忙改變那個氛圍。我想幫忙改變我們思考事情的方式。
cards.why: 三句 I'd like to 排比把野心堆高，但第二句起插進 help（我只是幫忙，不是我一個人扛），姿態瞬間壓低。野心大＋姿態低是英文講願景最難的平衡，這個 help 就是那顆調節鈕。
swaps: I'm not going to solve this alone, but I'd like to help shift how we think about it.
I'd like to help move the conversation, not own it.
cards.pmNote: 跨部門提大方向時，用 help 當動詞可以避免踩到別人的地盤。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

cards.pattern: It was like [遠處的蘑菇雲] — you see it, but you don't hear or notice it.
cards.quote: But weirdly, it was like you see the videos where there's the mushroom cloud in the distance. You see it. But you don't hear, or notice it.
cards.zh: 但很怪，那感覺就像影片裡遠方升起的蘑菇雲。你看得見。可是你聽不到，也沒真的感覺到。
cards.why: 三句短到不能再短，節奏是「畫面 → 停 → 反轉」。You see it. 獨立成句就是刻意的停頓，讓聽眾以為講完了，下一句 But you don't hear it 才把整個意思翻過來。要描述「威脅已經來了但當時沒人有感」，這比任何形容詞都準。
swaps: You could see it coming and still not feel it.
It registered visually, but nothing actually changed for us.
cards.pmNote: 競品發表當下往往看不出數據影響；真正的衝擊是綁定與迭代後才出現。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.pattern: People write about [X] like it's [一槍斃命的散彈]. Later I would learn it's more of a [慢慢絞緊的蟒蛇].
cards.quote: When, later, I would learn it's more of a boa constrictor.
cards.zh: 後來我才學到，它比較像一條蟒蛇慢慢把你絞緊。
cards.why: 媒體把競爭寫成「散彈槍一轟」，他改用蟒蛇——換比喻就是換模型，兩個比喻的差別剛好就是時間軸，而時間軸正是他的論點。要糾正別人對一件事的理解，找一個比對方更精準的比喻，比列三點理由有效十倍。
swaps: People talk about it like a single event; it's actually a slow squeeze.
It's not a shock, it's a slow compression.
cards.pmNote: 被大廠夾擊很少是單次事件，而是綁定＋迭代累積出的擠壓，數據上要看趨勢不是看發表日。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.quote: I'd say that was the beginning of chapter two where it was we went from the company that could do no wrong to the company that could do no right, which was a big flip.
cards.zh: 我會說那就是第二章的開始——我們從「怎麼做都對」的公司，變成「怎麼做都錯」的公司，整個翻過來。
cards.why: 只換一個字（wrong→right）就把整段起落講完，這是英文裡最省字的對比法。而且 could do no wrong / could do no right 兩個都是現成慣用語，母語者一聽就懂；台灣人多半會講成 people used to love us, now they criticize everything，長三倍又沒力。
swaps: Overnight we stopped being the team that could do no wrong.
The narrative flipped completely.
cards.pmNote: 敘事（narrative）本身會影響招募、留才與媒體，是需要主動管理的資產。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.pattern: Suddenly [一個很小很具體的畫面：員工不想再穿公司的 T-shirt 了].
cards.quote: You've started this company, it's been super successful, and then suddenly your employees don't want to wear your T-shirt anymore.
cards.zh: 你創了這家公司，它一路很成功，然後突然間，員工不想再穿你們公司的 T-shirt 了。
cards.why: 「士氣崩了」是抽象的，「員工不再穿公司 T-shirt」是看得見的。母語者講低潮幾乎一定會落到一個生活畫面上，聽眾才會有身體感。挑細節的原則：要能被拍下來，而且不需要解釋。
swaps: People stopped putting the company on their LinkedIn headline.
Nobody was handing out referrals anymore.
cards.pmNote: 士氣的領先指標常常是這種小訊號，比 engagement survey 早三個月出現。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.pattern: [強大的外部對手] did not kill us. We killed ourselves.
cards.quote: And he's looked at me, he laughed at and snorted and he's like, "Microsoft did not kill us. We killed ourselves."
cards.zh: 他看著我，笑了一聲、鼻子哼了一下，說：「不是微軟弄死我們的。是我們自己弄死自己的。」
cards.why: 兩句話、同一個動詞（kill）、主詞對調，就把責任從外部搬回內部。這種句型的威力在於它先幫對方講出那個最好用的藉口，再一刀否決——比直接說 we made mistakes 更難反駁，因為它示範了「我已經想過怪別人這條路了」。
swaps: The market didn't beat us — we beat ourselves.
That wasn't done to us. We did it to ourselves.
cards.pmNote: postmortem 開場先把外部因素講完再封起來，剩下的時間才會花在可控項上。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.pattern: The root cause was that I was too busy firing to aim, and then I thought I would do my aiming on [週末／假期].
cards.quote: I was too busy firing to aim, and then I thought I would do my aiming on vacations and things like that.
cards.zh: 我太忙著開槍，忙到沒空瞄準；然後我還以為瞄準這件事可以放到放假的時候再做。
cards.why: firing / aiming 是同一個動作系統的兩端，用它們就不必解釋「執行 vs 思考」的差別。第二句更狠：不是不知道要瞄準，是把瞄準排到了不可能發生的時段——這是承認錯誤時最高階的一手，你連自己的自欺都說出來了。
swaps: I was executing far more than I was deciding.
I kept deferring the thinking to a week that never came.
cards.pmNote: 策略時間如果沒有排進行事曆，就等於不存在。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.pattern: [挑戰] is not optional. You're going to be challenged, but [受苦] is optional.
cards.quote: I think the hardest thing for a founder, challenge is not optional. You're going to be challenged, but the suffering is optional.
cards.zh: 對創辦人來說最難的是：挑戰不是選項，你一定會被挑戰；但要不要痛苦，是選項。
cards.why: 把兩件常被綁在一起的事拆開，用同一個字（optional）當支點。這個句型可以套到任何你想幫人卸下不必要負擔的場合：加班、被罵、改版都適用。難度在於必須先承認前半是真的，否則後半會變成風涼話。
swaps: The deadline isn't negotiable; the panic is.
Pressure comes with the job. Misery doesn't have to.
cards.pmNote: 高壓專案的溝通重點：把不可控（挑戰）與可控（工作方式）明確分開。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.quote: Yeah, every time you move up a league, your reward is a stronger and better opponent and potentially more unlevel playing field.
cards.zh: 每升上一個聯盟，你的獎賞就是一個更強的對手，而且場地可能還更不公平。
cards.why: reward 這個字用得很反常——獎賞應該是好事，這裡卻接一個壞消息，一句話就把「成功會帶來更難的問題」講完。要安慰正在被降維打擊的團隊，這比 it's normal to struggle 有力太多。後面接 Easy to say, hard to do 可以再把姿態放低。
swaps: The prize for winning is a harder game.
Every level up buys you a tougher opponent.
cards.pmNote: 產品做起來之後的競爭強度是階梯式跳升的，資源規劃要提前一級。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.pattern: Owning it ends up being more painful in the short run, but some painful hours can save painful years.
cards.quote: And just owning things ends up being more painful in the short run, but then some painful hours can save painful years.
cards.zh: 把責任認下來，短期一定比較痛；但幾個難熬的小時，可以省下難熬的好幾年。
cards.why: hours / years 同字根對照（painful hours → painful years），把成本效益比壓進四個字裡。前半先老實承認會痛（不假裝認錯很容易），後半才給理由——順序反過來就會變成說教。
swaps: It costs more today and a lot less over the year.
A hard conversation now beats a hard quarter later.
cards.pmNote: 壞消息越早上報越便宜，這是期望管理的核心算式。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.pattern: Why do I have [1 個 X] at home and [10 個 X] at work? Why is it easier to [大範圍的事] than [自己身邊的事]?
cards.quote: Wait, why do I have 1 search box at home, and 10 search boxes at work? Why is it easier to search all of human knowledge than my company's knowledge?
cards.zh: 等等，為什麼我在家只有一個搜尋框，在公司卻有十個？為什麼搜全人類的知識，比搜我自己公司的知識還簡單？
cards.why: 兩個 Why 問句都內建一組荒謬的對照（家裡 vs 公司、全人類 vs 一間公司），完全不需要下結論，聽眾自己就得出「這不合理」。定義問題最有效的方式不是描述它，是找到一組讓它顯得荒謬的對照。
swaps: Why is the consumer version of this better than the one we pay for?
Why does this get worse every year instead of better?
cards.pmNote: 好的 problem statement 通常長得像一個沒人能回答的 Why。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.quote: We should probably not do things that would've been invented by everybody else 10 minutes later. Where are the problems that are not solving themselves?
cards.zh: 我們大概不該去做那些晚十分鐘別人也會做出來的東西。真正該問的是：哪些問題是不會自己被解決的？
cards.why: 先給一條刪除規則（不做什麼），再給一個定位問句（做什麼）。not solving themselves 是很漂亮的判準——它把「市場空白」重新定義成「連時間都解決不了的空白」，門檻一下子拉高，而且很好在會議上重複引用。
swaps: If someone else would build it anyway, it's not ours to build.
Which of these problems won't fix itself in two years?
cards.pmNote: 選題判準：這個問題會不會被平台方、時間或競爭者自然解決？會的話就別投人力。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.pattern: When you open up your laptop in [2030], what do you see?
cards.quote: In deciding to turn Dropbox into this lab for distributed work, we're like, "Okay, when you open up your laptop in 2025, 2030, what do you see?"
cards.zh: 我們決定把 Dropbox 變成遠距工作的實驗室時，問的是：「二〇二五、二〇三〇年，你打開筆電的那一刻，看到的是什麼？」
cards.why: 願景問題落到一個具體動作（打開筆電）跟一個具體感官（看到什麼），團隊就答得出來。相對地「五年後我們想成為什麼」這種問法只會收到空話。要讓 vision workshop 有產出，先把問題縮到一個畫面。
swaps: What's on the screen when they start their day in 2030?
Walk me through their first five minutes three years from now.
cards.pmNote: product vision 的可操作版本＝使用者未來某一天的具體場景，不是形容詞的堆疊。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.pattern: [某個 buzzword] means a lot of things to a lot of people. So it's a bit of a Rorschach test — the part that resonates with me is [你的定義].
cards.quote: So founder mode means a lot of things to a lot of people. So it's a bit of a Rorschach test
cards.zh: 「founder mode」這個詞，每個人講的都不太一樣，有點像羅夏克墨漬測驗——但真正打到我的部分是⋯⋯
cards.why: 會議上有人丟出一個大家其實各自解讀的流行詞時，這句可以在不否定任何人的前提下，把定義權接過來。a Rorschach test 是關鍵——它委婉地說「這個詞現在是空的，投射什麼進去都可以」，然後你才填自己的內容。
swaps: That term means different things to different people — the way I use it is...
Let me say what I mean by that, because it's used pretty loosely.
cards.pmNote: 跨團隊對齊的第一步永遠是把共用名詞定義下來，否則所有共識都是假的。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.quote: And then you flip to your development areas because no one calls them weaknesses.
cards.zh: 然後你翻到「待發展面向」那一頁——因為沒人會直接叫它「缺點」。
cards.why: 用一句自嘲式的旁白拆穿職場委婉語，既表示你懂遊戲規則，又不刻薄。實用價值很直接：英文職場一律講 development areas / growth areas，台灣人常照字面說 weaknesses，在 360 或 1:1 裡聽起來會過重。
swaps: your growth areas — nobody says weaknesses out loud
the development section, as it's politely called
cards.pmNote: 回饋要能被接住，用詞的溫度跟內容一樣重要；先降溫再給料。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.pattern: [聰明人] have a really fast rationalization hamster — they can convince themselves that here's how they were technically right even though clearly they were wrong.
cards.quote: smart people have a really fast rationalization hamster. They can convince themselves that, well, here's how they were technically right even though clearly they were wrong
cards.zh: 聰明人腦裡那隻「合理化的倉鼠」跑得特別快，他們有辦法說服自己「技術上我其實是對的」，即使明明就錯了。
cards.why: rationalization hamster 是自創的具象化說法，把抽象的認知偏誤變成一隻在跑滾輪的動物，聽一次就忘不掉。而且 technically right 這個搭配本身就是英文職場的暗語——說某人 technically right 幾乎等於說他錯了。
swaps: Smart people are unusually good at explaining away their own misses.
The smarter the person, the faster the rationalization.
cards.pmNote: 面試資深職位時，比起「知道什麼」更該測「能不能承認自己判斷錯過」。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.quote: So I think finding ways to take responsibility or always have a mindset of what if I were a hundred percent responsible for this? What if it was no one else's fault?
cards.zh: 我覺得要一直找辦法把責任接下來，常常問自己：如果這件事百分之百是我的責任呢？如果完全不是別人的錯呢？
cards.why: 用假設語氣（What if）而不是斷言（It was my fault），所以不必真的相信這是事實也能用——他後面也承認 those things are never true。這讓「扛責任」變成一種思考工具而不是自虐，開檢討會時特別好用。
swaps: Let's assume for a minute this was entirely on us — what would we change?
If none of the external stuff existed, what's still our problem?
cards.pmNote: postmortem 的高產出設定：先假設 100% 內部歸因，把可控項全撈出來再談外部因素。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.pattern: The only thing our customers have really meaningfully seen from us in [三年] is [a price increase]. What are we doing?
cards.quote: Look, we haven't shipped any. Last three years, the only thing our customers have really meaningfully seen from our product is a price increase. What the hell are we doing?
cards.zh: 你看，我們什麼都沒出。過去三年，客戶從我們產品上真正感受到的只有一件事：漲價。我們到底在幹嘛？
cards.why: 把難聽的話換算成「客戶視角的唯一事實」，就沒人能辯——不是我覺得你們不夠好，是客戶三年只收到一次漲價。最後那個問句不是要答案，是把不舒服留在房間裡。內部要打破自我感覺良好時，這是最短路徑。
swaps: From the customer's side, the only change in two years was the price.
Let's be honest about what shipped and what didn't.
cards.pmNote: 組織自嗨的解毒劑：把內部成果單換算成「使用者實際感受到的變化」。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.quote: So first of all, when you're in the early innings, you'll actually get more useful advice often from your peers because they're going through the same thing.
cards.zh: 首先，在很前期的階段，你從同輩那裡拿到的建議其實比較有用，因為他們正在經歷一模一樣的事。
cards.why: in the early innings（棒球用語＝比賽還很前面）是矽谷高頻慣用語，台灣人幾乎不會用但一講就很到位。這句的實用性在於它給了一個選 mentor 的判準：不是找最資深的，是找階段最貼近的。
swaps: Early on, peers give better advice than veterans.
For this stage, I'd rather ask someone who did it last year.
cards.pmNote: 建人脈梯隊：同階段 1-2 人、領先 2 年、領先 5 年、領先 20 年，各問不同層級的問題。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.pattern: A year from now, what will I wish I had been learning today? Two years? Five years?
cards.quote: always be working back from, in one year from now, what will I wish I had been learning today? Two years, five years?
cards.zh: 永遠從未來往回推：一年後的我，會希望今天的我在學什麼？兩年後呢？五年後呢？
cards.why: working back from 是這句的骨架，把提問的時間原點從現在搬到未來，答案就會完全不同。後面只丟兩個名詞（Two years, five years?）當追問，是很自然的口語省略——不必重複整句問句。
swaps: What will next year's version of me wish I'd started today?
Working back from a year out, what's missing now?
cards.pmNote: 個人成長曲線要跑在公司成長曲線前面，這個問句是它的操作版本。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

cards.pattern: Hopefully I don't come off as [對方可能的誤解]. I'm not saying that at all. What I'm saying is [你真正的意思].
cards.quote: Hopefully, I don't come off as encouraging everyone to be like me. I'm not saying that at all. What I'm saying is, this is a way to be.
cards.zh: 希望我聽起來不是在鼓吹大家都要跟我一樣。我完全不是那個意思。我要說的是：這是一種活法。
cards.why: 三拍拆誤會：先點名可能的誤讀（come off as）、再切斷（I'm not saying that at all）、最後才給正確版本（What I'm saying is）。整段最重的字是 a way——不是 the way，一個冠詞就把主張從教條降成選項。
swaps: I don't want this to come across as X. What I mean is Y.
To be clear, I'm not arguing for X — I'm saying X is one option.
cards.pmNote: 提出非主流做法時先自曝可能的誤讀，可以擋掉一半的反對意見。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

cards.pattern: What's interesting is that [某群人] has found a way to make the most [adj] [X] the least [adj].
cards.quote: What's interesting is that Silicon Valley has found a way to make the most profitable style of business the least profitable.
cards.zh: 有趣的是，矽谷居然有辦法把全世界最好賺的生意做成最不賺錢的生意。
cards.why: 同一個形容詞的最高級正反並排（the most profitable / the least profitable），矛盾自己會跳出來，不必加任何評論。開頭 What's interesting is 又把一句很嗆的批評包成觀察，語氣立刻降溫——這是英文裡最好用的「毒藥包糖衣」。
swaps: We've somehow turned the cheapest thing to build into the most expensive.
It's impressive how the easiest market to win became the hardest.
cards.pmNote: 軟體毛利本來就高，燒錢燒到不賺錢是選擇問題，不是產業結構問題。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

cards.pattern: [X] is not just a stepping stone — [X] is a great destination itself.
cards.quote: Small is not just a stepping stone, small is a great destination itself.
cards.zh: 「小」不只是通往別處的墊腳石，「小」本身就是一個很好的終點。
cards.why: not just a stepping stone / a great destination 是一組現成的空間隱喻，用來替任何「被當成過渡狀態」的東西平反：小團隊、資深工程師不轉管理、產品不擴張都能套。重點在 itself——沒有它，這句就只是說小也不錯。
swaps: This isn't a phase we're trying to get out of.
Staying at this size is the plan, not a stage.
cards.pmNote: 不是每個產品線都要規劃成長路徑；有些的正確目標就是穩定與高毛利。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

cards.pattern: This is not an estimate of time, it's an appetite. It doesn't sound like that much of a different word, but it really is.
cards.quote: So this is not an estimate of time, it's an appetite, which is a radically different approach. It doesn't sound like that much of a different word, but it really is.
cards.zh: 這不是「時間估算」，這是「胃口」——做法完全不一樣。聽起來只是換個字，但差別真的很大。
cards.why: 換掉一個名詞就換掉整套邏輯：estimate 是「這要多久」，appetite 是「我願意花多久」，因果方向相反。第二句先替聽眾說出他的懷疑（聽起來只是換字），再堅持（but it really is），比直接解釋更有說服力。
swaps: We're not estimating this, we're budgeting it.
The question isn't how long it takes — it's how long it's worth.
cards.pmNote: fixed time, variable scope：時間先鎖死，範圍才是變數，這是 Shape Up 的核心。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

cards.pattern: There's nothing easier than promising [work] later — and the further away it is, the easier it is to promise.
cards.quote: There's nothing easier than promising work later.
cards.zh: 沒有什麼比「答應以後再做」更容易的事了。
cards.why: 八個字擋掉「那放到 Q4 好不好」。它攻擊的是「承諾」這個行為本身而不是對方的需求，所以不會撕破臉；接下來那句 the further away it is, the easier it is to promise 用比較級連動，把心理機制講成公式，聽者會自動想到自己剛才差點答應的事。
swaps: Committing to something six months out costs nothing today — that's the problem.
The easiest promise to make is the one that's furthest away.
cards.pmNote: 「by the end of the year」是最危險的承諾句型，成本為零、代價全在未來。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

cards.pattern: Keep working the way you're working, but on some low-criticality project, try this new method on that.
cards.quote: So what we often encourage people to do is keep working the way you're working, but some future project, some low criticality project, try this new method on that.
cards.zh: 我們常建議的是：現在的做法照舊，但挑一個之後的、沒那麼要緊的專案，在那上面試新方法。
cards.why: 推新做法時最大的阻力是風險，這句直接把風險拿掉：不動現況、只在低風險的地方試。keep... but... 的結構讓對方不必先否定自己現在的做法就能點頭，成功率比「我們改用 X 吧」高很多。
swaps: Let's not change anything critical — let's try it on the next low-stakes project.
Same process for now; I'd just like one small project to pilot this.
cards.pmNote: 流程變革要先降低 criticality；在關鍵專案上試新方法失敗一次，就再也不會有第二次機會。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

cards.pattern: I don't like the word [X] — how do you feel after a [X]?
cards.quote: I don't like the word sprint because how do you feel after a sprint? Exhausted.
cards.zh: 我不喜歡「衝刺」這個詞——你衝刺完是什麼感覺？累爆。
cards.why: 拆一個用久到沒人再想的詞：不吵它的定義，而是問它的字面經驗，然後自己答一個字（Exhausted.）。這種一字回答是英文口語的重錘，比講一整句解釋更有停頓感，也留給對方反駁的空間。
swaps: I'd avoid that word — think about what it literally describes.
What does that word actually imply about how we work?
cards.pmNote: 團隊語彙會塑造行為：叫 sprint 就會一直衝，叫 cycle 才會有節奏與冷卻期。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

cards.pattern: We ask people "What do you think?" We don't say "What do you know?"
cards.quote: What we ask people in general is we say, what do you think? We don't say, what do you know? We often say, what do you think?
cards.zh: 我們一般會問人「你怎麼想？」我們不會問「你知道什麼？」我們最常問的就是「你怎麼想？」
cards.why: 把兩個看起來差不多的問句擺在一起比，差別就出來了：know 要求證據、think 要求判斷。而且他刻意重複第一句收尾，是很自然的口語強調法（A → not B → A）。要讓資淺同事願意開口，換這個動詞就夠了。
swaps: I'm not asking what the data says — what do you think?
What's your read on this?
cards.pmNote: 1:1 裡問 what do you know 會得到報告，問 what do you think 才會得到判斷。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

cards.quote: And one of the things I'll often ask is, if you had another couple days, what would you do with this?
cards.zh: 我很常問的一個問題是：如果再多給你幾天，你會拿這個東西做什麼？
cards.why: 假設性問句把人從「辯護已交付的東西」切換成「想下一步」，答案會露出他真正的品味和存貨。面試、design review、1:1 都能用，而且因為是假設，對方不會覺得是在被挑毛病。
swaps: If we gave this another week, where would it go?
What's the version of this you didn't have time to build?
cards.pmNote: 評估設計師／PM 的深度，看他手上還有沒有「沒放進去的下一層想法」。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

cards.pattern: The more massive an object, the more energy it takes to change its direction. This is why [大公司] move slowly.
cards.quote: The more massive an object, the more energy it takes to change its direction. This is why big companies move slowly.
cards.zh: 物體越重，要改變它的方向就要越多能量。這就是為什麼大公司動得慢。
cards.why: 借一條沒人會反駁的物理定律，再用 This is why 一句話落到組織上。這種「定律＋落地」的兩句組合，能讓一個主觀判斷聽起來像推論結果；而且對方要反駁，得先反駁牛頓。
swaps: Momentum is real — the bigger the team, the more energy a turn costs.
You can't turn a big ship on a dime.
cards.pmNote: 組織轉向的成本跟規模成正比，改流程要估的是能量不是時間。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

cards.quote: I'm like, "I'm not surprised to hear that. Tell me how you did it."
cards.zh: 我就說：「我一點都不意外。你跟我說說你們是怎麼做的。」
cards.why: 對方抱怨「你的方法沒用」，這兩句既不辯護也不道歉：I'm not surprised 穩住場面又暗示問題可能在執行，Tell me how you did it 直接把對話推進到事實層。台灣人在這種場合最常見的反應是先道歉或先解釋，兩者都會失去診斷的機會。
swaps: That doesn't surprise me — walk me through what you actually did.
Makes sense. How did you run it?
cards.pmNote: 有人說某個做法失敗時，先問執行細節再談方法論，八成問題出在前者。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

cards.pattern: What's the worst that can happen? You've got to be at peace with the worst that can happen.
cards.quote: which is just the idea of negative visualization. What's the worst that can happen? You got to be at peace with the worst that can happen.
cards.zh: 這就是「負面預想」：最糟會發生什麼事？你必須跟那個最糟的結果和平共處。
cards.why: 把風險提問跟心理準備綁成一組（問完還要 be at peace with），所以不會停在嚇人。at peace with 是關鍵搭配——不是 accept、不是 prepare for，而是「不再抗拒」，語氣冷靜很多。提案被質疑風險時用這句可以把對話從恐懼轉成盤點。
swaps: Let's name the worst case and decide if we can live with it.
If this fails completely, what have we actually lost?
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem 的私人版；能接受最壞情況，決策速度會快很多。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

cards.pattern: We use words to establish a perspective. And if those are the words that are in your head, then you feel like [結果].
cards.quote: We use words to establish a perspective in a way of thinking about the world. And if those are the words that are in your head, then you feel like it's this war.
cards.zh: 我們用字詞來建立一種看世界的角度。如果你腦袋裡裝的是那些字，你就會覺得這是一場戰爭。
cards.why: 要改團隊文化卻不想講大道理時，從用詞下手：先給機制（字詞建立視角），再給後果（你會覺得這是戰爭）。整段沒有一句是罵人的，但把「攻佔市場、殲滅對手」這類講法的代價說清楚了。
swaps: The words we pick shape how we see the work.
If that's the vocabulary, that's the mindset we'll end up with.
cards.pmNote: 團隊慣用語是文化的先行指標；改語言比改流程便宜。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

cards.pattern: Why are we always looking to [極端的對照組] to tell us how to run our business?
cards.quote: Why are we always looking to Navy SEALs to tell us how to run our business?
cards.zh: 我們為什麼老是要去看海豹部隊怎麼做，來決定自己公司該怎麼經營？
cards.why: 用一個誇張但真實存在的類比對象（海豹部隊）逼出情境落差——他後面那句 what you're doing is you're making B2B accounting software 才是真正的重擊。要拆掉「某某大廠都這樣做」的論點，先把那個對象的情境放大到荒謬即可。
swaps: Why do we keep borrowing playbooks from a completely different context?
That works for them because their stakes are nothing like ours.
cards.pmNote: 抄大公司做法前先問：他們的限制條件跟我們一樣嗎？
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

cards.pattern: I want to provide an alternative, not a competitor. If it's not an alternative, it doesn't need to exist.
cards.quote: If it's not an alternative, it doesn't need to exist.
cards.zh: 如果它不是一個「另一種選擇」，那它根本沒必要存在。
cards.why: 十個字的判準句，可以直接拿去砍需求：這個功能只是把別人做過的再做一次嗎？If it's not X, it doesn't need to exist 這個框架很萬用，換掉 X 就能定義任何團隊的存在門檻。
swaps: If it's the same thing again, why build it?
Unless it offers a genuinely different approach, it shouldn't ship.
cards.pmNote: differentiation 不是功能多寡，而是「是否提供一種不同的做法」。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

cards.pattern: People act like [X] is the worst thing that can happen to you. That's not even in the top 10.
cards.quote: People act like having a startup fail is the worst thing that can happen to you. And man, that's not even in the top 10.
cards.zh: 大家都把「創業失敗」講得像是人生最慘的事。老實說，那連前十名都排不進去。
cards.why: 先精準複述大家的預設（People act like...），再用一個帶數字的說法一口氣打掉（not even in the top 10）。not even in the top 10 比 that's not true 有力太多，因為它暗示你手上有一份更慘的清單——聽眾會等著你講下去。
swaps: Everyone treats that as the disaster scenario. It isn't even close.
That's not the worst outcome here — not by a long way.
cards.pmNote: 風險排序要重排：比「這個專案失敗」更糟的通常是「這個專案不死不活拖兩年」。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.quote: Well, first of all, thank you for saying all that. That's giving me too much credit, but I like the idea that it's going to balance out the too little credit I ostensibly get somewhere else, that's great.
cards.zh: 首先謝謝你這樣說。你太抬舉我了——不過我喜歡這個說法，就當作是補回我在別的地方被低估的部分吧。
cards.why: 被公開稱讚時最難的是既不推掉也不照單全收。這裡的解法是先謙虛（too much credit），再用一個俏皮的會計比喻（跟別處被低估的互相抵銷）把讚美收下來。台灣人多半只做前半段，結果整段對話停在尷尬的推辭。
swaps: That's very generous — I'll take it to offset the times nobody noticed.
Too kind, but I'll happily bank that one.
cards.pmNote: 績效面談收到讚美時，接住它並接一句事實，比一直說 no no no 更有利。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.pattern: Did they succeed because of [那個做法], or in spite of it?
cards.quote: Exactly. Did they succeed because of that or in spite of that?
cards.zh: 沒錯。他們成功是「因為」那個做法，還是「儘管」有那個做法？
cards.why: 十二個字拆掉所有的成功學案例。because of / in spite of 是一組現成的反義介系詞，擺在同一個問句裡就形成完整的二分——對方必須提出證據才能回答，而通常他沒有。會議上有人搬出大公司案例時的萬用回應。
swaps: Was that the cause, or did it work despite that?
How do we know that's what made the difference?
cards.pmNote: benchmark 的最大陷阱：把倖存者的所有行為都當成成功原因。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.pattern: All the advice used to be of the form, "[名人] once did this thing, so if you do it too, you'll be like [名人]." Well, he also [一個明顯無關的細節].
cards.quote: All the advice used to be of the form, "Steve Jobs once did this thing, so if you do it too, you'll be like Steve Jobs." And it's like, well, he also wore the black turtleneck.
cards.zh: 以前的建議都是這個格式：「賈伯斯做過這件事，所以你也做，你就會變成賈伯斯。」我就想說，那他還穿黑色高領毛衣呢。
cards.why: 歸謬法的教科書範例：不否定前提，只是照著同一套邏輯再推一個明顯荒謬的結論。of the form 這個說法把對方的論點抽象成一個公式，等於先聲明「我要拆的是結構不是你這個人」，殺傷力大但衝突感低。
swaps: By that logic we should also copy their office layout.
That argument proves too much.
cards.pmNote: 案例式建議要先問：這個做法在他們身上生效的前提條件，我們有嗎？
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.pattern: I'm not telling you that you should [做 X]. I'm just saying that is what it's called when [情況].
cards.quote: It's like, "well, I'm not telling you that you should pivot. I'm just saying that is what it's called when you change the strategy, but try to have fidelity to the vision."
cards.zh: 我不是在叫你去 pivot。我只是說，當你改策略但盡量守住願景的時候，那件事就叫這個名字。
cards.why: 把「描述」和「主張」明確切開，是化解無謂爭執最快的一招——對方以為你在逼他做某事，你只是在替一個現象命名。I'm not telling you... I'm just saying... 這組句型在任何被誤會成施壓的場合都能用。
swaps: I'm not recommending it — I'm just naming what's happening.
That's a description, not a proposal.
cards.pmNote: 團隊反彈某個名詞時，先確認他們反對的是名字還是那件事本身。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.pattern: Please tell me the better [說法／做法] and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea.
cards.quote: And I always write them back and say like, "Please tell me the better term and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea."
cards.zh: 我都回信說：「請你告訴我更好的講法，然後把它推廣開，我就會改用。這主意很好。」
cards.why: 被批評時不辯護、直接把球丟回去，而且丟得很誠懇（It's a great idea 不是諷刺）。這招的實際效果是把「抱怨者」變成「要負責提案的人」，八成的人就此收手；真的提案的那兩成，你也真的得到了東西。
swaps: If you've got a better framing, I'll switch to it — genuinely.
Send me the better version and I'll use it.
cards.pmNote: 接住反對意見的高效版：把否定轉成一個具體的交付要求。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.quote: That's the whole ball game. No one had to lose in order for us to win.
cards.zh: 這才是重點。我們要贏，不需要有人輸。
cards.why: 十個字解散一場零和框架。當兩個團隊互相指責、或有人硬要把討論變成路線之爭時，這句話把賽局重新定義；前面加一句 That's the whole ball game（這才是關鍵）先立場再落句，節奏很穩。
swaps: This doesn't have to be zero-sum.
Our win doesn't require their loss.
cards.pmNote: 跨團隊卡住時先檢查是不是被架成零和；多數資源衝突其實有第三解。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.pattern: "[對方指控你漏掉的東西], you say?" — and you take notes — "Oh, interesting."
cards.quote: I'd be like, "X, Y, Z, you say?" And I'd be like taking notes, "Oh, interesting."
cards.zh: 我會說：「X、Y、Z 是嗎？」然後一邊做筆記，一邊說：「喔，有意思。」
cards.why: 「名詞＋you say?」是把對方的指控原封不動複誦回去的懶人句型，效果是降速＋表示你聽進去了。搭配動作（做筆記）跟一個不表態的評語（Oh, interesting），整段完全沒有防衛姿態，但也沒有答應任何事。
swaps: X and Y, you say? Let me write that down.
Interesting — say more about Z.
cards.pmNote: 使用者罵你少了什麼功能時，那份清單本身就是最便宜的 roadmap 訊號。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.quote: So, I don't really care how high quality the initial MVP is because quality is defined by the customer. And if we don't know who our customer is, we literally don't know what the word quality means.
cards.zh: 所以第一版的 MVP 品質多高，我其實沒那麼在意，因為品質是由客戶定義的。如果我們連客戶是誰都不知道，我們根本不知道「品質」這兩個字是什麼意思。
cards.why: 把爭執從形容詞（夠不夠好）拉到定義層（誰有資格定義「好」），對方就沒得吵了。literally 在這裡不是口頭禪，是強調「這不是修辭，是字面意思」——用對的話很有力，用錯就變油。
swaps: Good is relative to a user. Which user?
We can't judge quality until we know who it's for.
cards.pmNote: craft 之爭多半是 target user 沒對齊之爭；先定義使用者再談品質標準。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.pattern: If you're asking whether you should [做重大決定], you probably know the answer already.
cards.quote: So first of all, if you're asking whether you should pivot or not you probably know the answer already.
cards.zh: 首先，如果你在問「該不該轉向」，你八成心裡已經有答案了。
cards.why: 不回答問題，改回答「你會問這個問題」這件事本身——這是教練式對話最高階的一手。probably 跟 already 都是緩衝，讓這句不至於太篤定；拿掉它們就會變成不禮貌的斷言。
swaps: The fact that it's a question probably answers it.
If you have to ask, you've mostly decided.
cards.pmNote: 評估 product-market fit 時，「有沒有餘裕開會討論這件事」本身就是訊號。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.pattern: The fact that you have time to ask me this question already tells me the answer.
cards.quote: People call me sometimes they're like "I want to know if I have product market fit." Well, the fact that you have time to call me and ask me this question already tells me the answer.
cards.zh: 有人打給我說：「我想知道我們有沒有 PMF。」嗯，你有空打這通電話問我，這件事本身就給了答案。
cards.why: 把「行為」當證據，而不是把「說法」當證據——他沒聽你的數據，只看你有沒有空。這種以行為推論狀態的句型（the fact that you... already tells me...）在英文裡非常有份量，因為它不可反駁。
swaps: The fact that we're debating this tells me where we are.
If it were working, you wouldn't have time for this call.
cards.pmNote: PMF 的體感判準：真的抓到的時候，忙到沒空自我懷疑。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.pattern: Everyone go around the room and say: "If I could start this over again, the thing I wish we were doing was ___."
cards.quote: Now that you've agreed among yourselves that you're going to do that for a fixed period of time, everyone go around the room and say, "If I could start this company over again the thing I wish we were doing was."
cards.zh: 既然大家已經同意用一段固定的時間來試，那就一個一個講：「如果能重來一次，我希望我們在做的是＿＿＿。」
cards.why: 會議設計的兩個關鍵都在這句：go around the room（每個人都要講，不能躲）＋一個未完成的句子（不必自己組織語言，填空就好）。而且用假設語氣包裝，講出「我早就想換方向」不會像背叛。
swaps: Let's go around: if we were starting today, what would we be building?
Everyone finish this sentence — the thing I'd rather we were doing is...
cards.pmNote: 重大轉向前先做一輪匿名或輪流表態，常會發現大家早就想同一件事但都不敢先開口。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.quote: And one of my main takeaways of that entire process is that it's always too early until it's too late.
cards.zh: 我從那整段過程裡學到最重要的一件事是：這種事永遠都「太早」，直到它「太遲」。
cards.why: 七個字裝下一個完整的機制：每一次單獨看都太早，加總起來就變成太遲。too early / too late 的對仗讓它像諺語一樣好記，要推動任何「現在做沒感覺、以後做來不及」的事（技術債、治理、文件化）都可以直接引用。
swaps: Every single time it's premature — right up until it's impossible.
There's never a good moment, and then the moment's gone.
cards.pmNote: 架構債、資安、治理這類事沒有「剛剛好的時機」，要用日曆而不是用時機來排。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.pattern: Don't ask them "Should I do it?" Ask them "Can you give me the pros and cons of doing it?"
cards.quote: And don't ask them, "Should I do it?" Ask them, "Tell me for each thing, can you give me the pros and cons of doing it?"
cards.zh: 不要問他們「我該不該做？」要問他們「每一個做法的利弊分別是什麼？」
cards.why: 同一件事、兩種問法，收到的東西完全不同：問「該不該」拿到的是對方的偏好（而且通常是最保守那個），問「利弊」拿到的是你自己判斷所需的材料。Don't ask X, ask Y 的對照結構讓建議很好記也很好轉述。
swaps: I'm not asking for a recommendation — I want the trade-offs.
Walk me through the upside and downside of each option.
cards.pmNote: 找專家要的是選項的成本結構，決策權留在自己身上。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.quote: Thank you for advising me on the pros and cons. You work for me, you're my lawyer. I'd like to implement this thing.
cards.zh: 謝謝你把利弊分析給我。你是替我工作的、你是我的律師。我決定要做這件事。
cards.why: 聽完專業建議之後仍然拍板的標準三步：先謝（承認對方的專業）、再定位（誰對誰負責）、最後宣布（I'd like to，不是 I want）。台灣人最常卡在第二步，結果被顧問或資深同事的偏好牽著走。
swaps: I appreciate the analysis. I've made the call — let's go with this.
Noted, and I'd still like to move forward with it.
cards.pmNote: 顧問／專家給的是選項與風險，決策責任仍在 DRI 身上，這個界線要講出來。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.pattern: You can't have it both ways. Are you [自己吹的那個大話]? Well, then you have [對應的責任].
cards.quote: It's like you can't have it both ways, buddy. Are you the Superman who's reordering the whole world to your whim? Well, then you have moral responsibility for the outcomes.
cards.zh: 你不能兩邊都要。你到底是不是那個要照自己意思重排整個世界的超人？是的話，結果的道德責任你就得扛。
cards.why: 抓住對方前後不一致（募資時說要改變世界、被追責時說只是個小廠商），用 You can't have it both ways 一句封住，再用一個 Are you...? 問句逼他選邊。這是英文裡處理雙重標準最直接的句型，語氣重，用在有把握的場合。
swaps: You can't claim both of those at once.
Pick one — either it's transformative or it's just a tool.
cards.pmNote: 對外宣稱的野心大小，會決定外界對你的責任標準，兩者要同時規劃。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.pattern: Given that it's not knowable what's going to happen, the thing that makes sense is to pick actions today that make sense in a wide variety of future scenarios.
cards.quote: The thing that makes sense is to pick actions today that make ethical sense in a wide variety of future scenarios and do those.
cards.zh: 比較合理的做法是：挑那些在很多種未來版本裡都說得通的行動，今天就去做。
cards.why: 承認不確定卻不癱瘓的標準解法——不是預測未來，而是找「哪個未來成立都不會後悔」的動作。a wide variety of future scenarios 這個說法很好用，因為它把「我不知道」轉成一個具體的篩選條件。
swaps: Let's do the things that hold up whichever way this goes.
We can't predict it, so let's pick no-regret moves.
cards.pmNote: 高度不確定時的決策原則：no-regret moves 優先，可逆決策快做、不可逆決策慢做。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.quote: Great. Tell me a situation where that best practice would not be applicable.
cards.zh: 很好。那你跟我說一個「這個最佳實務不適用」的情境。
cards.why: 先給一個廉價的肯定（Great.）再丟出真正的問題，落差本身就是壓力測試。這題測的不是知識而是理解深度——真的會用的人講得出邊界，只背過的人講不出來（他說大部分人答不出來）。面試、招募、找顧問都適用。
swaps: When would you not do it that way?
Where does that framework break down?
cards.pmNote: 面試判斷「真懂 vs 背過」的通用題：請對方講出方法論的失效條件。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.pattern: Not to be too [哲學／戲劇化／悲觀] about this, but it really goes right to the issue of [一個很大的主題].
cards.quote: and not to be too spiritual about this, but it really goes right to the issue of ego identification
cards.zh: 不是想把這件事講得太玄，但它真的直接踩到「自我認同」這個問題。
cards.why: 在商業場合要拋出一個偏哲學／情緒／價值觀的主張時，這個前綴先替聽眾說出他們的顧慮（你是不是要開始講心靈雞湯了），拿到許可後再講。not to be too X about this, but... 可以換成 not to get too philosophical / not to be dramatic，是英文會議裡極高頻的軟化裝置。
swaps: Not to get too philosophical, but this is really about identity.
At the risk of sounding dramatic, this goes deeper than process.
cards.pmNote: 把「情感／認同」議題帶進工作討論前先加一層 hedge，接受度會高很多。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

cards.pattern: It's felt like [大家的直覺]. But actually, if you look for evidence of that, you basically can't find it.
cards.quote: It's felt like we've been in a time of great technological change. But actually, if you look for actually evidence of that, in statistical evidence of that, analytical evidence of that, you basically can't find it.
cards.zh: 大家都覺得這幾十年科技變化很快。但你真的去找證據——統計上的、分析上的——其實根本找不到。
cards.why: 先用 it's felt like 把對方的直覺說出來（而且說得很同情），再用 but actually + if you look for evidence 把戰場從「感覺」換到「證據」。攻擊的是資料不是人，所以對方不會防衛。
swaps: The perception is that X. The data tells a different story
It feels true, but I couldn't find anything that backs it up
cards.pmNote: 推翻團隊共識前，先把共識講得比對方還準，接受度會高很多。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

cards.pattern: Everything I've just described is just a straightforward extrapolation of [基本原理]. I'm not making any bold predictions.
cards.quote: And again, everything I've just described, by the way, is just a very straightforward extrapolation of very basic economics. I'm not making any bold predictions of what I just said.
cards.zh: 我剛剛講的這一整串，其實只是最基本的經濟學往下推而已。我沒有在做什麼大膽預測。
cards.why: 講完一個聽起來很狂的結論後，馬上把它降級成「這只是常識往下推」。先自己拆掉「你太樂觀／你在唬爛」這顆炸彈，對方就很難用「這只是你的猜測」來反駁。
swaps: None of this requires a leap—it's just following the numbers
I'm not predicting anything exotic here, just applying the basics
cards.pmNote: 提大膽提案時，把推論鏈拆成「每一步都很無聊」，比把結論講得很興奮更有說服力。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

cards.pattern: I've been wrong about tons of things, but I [幽默地說自己把證據藏起來了].
cards.quote: I was going to start by saying, I've been wrong about tons of things, but I buried those out back behind the shed.
cards.zh: 我本來想說，我看走眼的次數多到數不清啦，只是那些我都埋在後院工具間後面了。
cards.why: 被大力稱讚時，母語者不會謙虛地否認，而是用一個誇張的玩笑承認自己也有很多失敗——既接住讚美又不顯得自滿。台灣人習慣講「沒有啦哪有」，在英語職場會顯得沒自信。
swaps: I've been wrong plenty of times too—those just don't make the highlight reel
For every one of those there are five you haven't heard about
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

cards.pattern: I've come much more around to [某人]'s point of view. I would argue that quite a bit differently today than I did.
cards.quote: By the way, I will say on the Peter one, I've come much more around to Peter's point of view. I would probably argue that one quite a bit differently today than I did, and I would give his view, I think, a lot more credit.
cards.zh: 順帶一提，Peter 那場辯論，我現在比較站到他那邊了。同樣的題目今天要我講，我會講得很不一樣，也會給他的看法多很多分數。
cards.why: 改變立場的三段式：come around to someone's view（承認位移）→ argue it differently today（把改變歸給時間而不是自己蠢）→ give his view more credit（給對方加分）。全程沒有一句「我錯了」，但誠意十足。
swaps: I've moved a long way toward his position on that
If I were making that argument today, I'd frame it very differently
cards.pmNote: 公開改變立場是資深訊號；重點是把新資訊當主詞，而不是把自己當被告。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

cards.pattern: Everybody wants to talk about [表層現象], but really, what you want to look at is [底層單位].
cards.quote: Everybody wants to talk about job loss, but really, what you want to look at is task loss, the tasks changing.
cards.zh: 大家都在談工作被取代，但真正該看的是「任務」被取代——是任務在變。
cards.why: 一句話把討論的分析單位換掉，這是資深的人最常用的一招。Everybody wants to talk about X 不否定對方，只說那不是最有用的切面；whatt you want to look at 又把建議包成中性的「該看的」而不是「你錯了」。
swaps: The conversation is about X, but the unit that actually moves is Y
I'd reframe it: it's less about X, more about Y
cards.pmNote: framing 決定討論走向——換掉分析單位，比在原本的單位上贏辯論有效十倍。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

cards.pattern: I could have been pretty good at [A], or pretty good at [B], but being [A] who understood [B] made me spectacularly great at [成果].
cards.quote: He said, "I could have been a pretty good cartoonist or I could have been pretty good at business, but the fact that I was a cartoonist who understood business made me spectacularly great at making Dilbert."
cards.zh: 他說：「我可以當個還不錯的漫畫家，也可以當個還不錯的商業人，但因為我是一個懂商業的漫畫家，才讓我把呆伯特做到無人能及。」
cards.why: pretty good at A / pretty good at B / spectacularly great at 的三拍節奏，把「跨界」這個抽象概念變成可以量的落差。母語者很愛用 the fact that I was X who understood Y 這個結構來描述自己的獨特定位。
swaps: Either alone would have been fine; the combination is what made it work
It took someone with both skills to pull that off
cards.pmNote: 談職涯定位時，講「兩個領域的交集」比講「我很強」更難被反駁。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

cards.pattern: He used to tell people, "[一句格言]". What that means essentially is [白話翻譯].
cards.quote: He used to tell people, he said, "The key for career planning is," he said, "don't be fungible." He's an economist and so that was economic speaking. What that means essentially is don't be replaceable.
cards.zh: 他都跟人說：「職涯規劃的關鍵就是，別讓自己可被替換。」他是經濟學家，所以講得比較術語。白話講就是：別讓自己是可以隨便換掉的那個人。
cards.why: 先丟術語再自己翻譯，是英語會議裡最實用的一組動作：術語讓你顯得懂行，緊接著的 what that means essentially is 讓沒跟上的人不必舉手發問，等於幫全場保住面子。
swaps: In plain English, that just means...
The non-jargon version of that is...
cards.pmNote: 用了任何專有名詞，下一句就要自己翻譯——這是主持會議的基本禮貌。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

cards.pattern: There's this rush to judgment upfront where people say, "It's therefore obvious that [X]."
cards.quote: There's this rush to judgment upfront where people say, "Oh, it's therefore obvious that X, Y, Z. It's obvious that the moats are going to be in this area of the technology, but not in this other area."
cards.zh: 一開始大家都會急著下判斷，說「所以顯然就是 X、Y、Z」、「顯然護城河一定在這一塊，不會在那一塊」。
cards.why: 不點名任何人，而是把對手的立場模仿出來（用 people say + 引號），再讓那個語氣自己聽起來太滿。這比直接說「你太武斷」安全得多，是英語裡最常見的軟性反駁。
swaps: There's a lot of premature certainty around this
People jump straight to "and therefore obviously..."
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem 時先蒐集大家的「顯然」，那通常就是最大的風險清單。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

cards.pattern: I'll just run this as a thought experiment and you can see what you think, but [問題].
cards.quote: I'll just run this as a thought experiment and you can see what you think on this, but it's like, are AI models themselves defensible?
cards.zh: 我把它當成一個思想實驗丟出來，你自己判斷——AI 模型本身到底有沒有護城河？
cards.why: 先把提案降級成「思想實驗」，等於預先聲明「我還沒押注在這上面」，別人反駁時就不是在打你的臉。you can see what you think 又把決定權交還給對方，開會拋新方向時最安全的開場。
swaps: Let me float something and you tell me if it holds up
Purely as a hypothetical—what if...
cards.pmNote: roadmap 會議第一次拋新方向，用「思想實驗」包裝可以避免太早被逼表態。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

cards.quote: And so again, it's just like, I don't know, my view is I need to put a big discount on my forecasting ability on this one.
cards.zh: 所以這一題，我的看法是：我得把自己的預測能力先打一個大折扣。
cards.why: 用金融語彙 put a discount on 講自謙，聽起來像在做風險定價而不是在示弱。這種「用專業框架講自己的限制」是英語職場承認不確定最漂亮的方式。
swaps: I'd weight my own prediction pretty lightly here
My track record doesn't buy me much confidence on this one
cards.pmNote: 對外給預估時主動標示信心水準，比事後解釋為什麼估錯便宜得多。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

cards.pattern: I don't think I can predict that. I think a much better use of my time is [替代做法].
cards.quote: It's like, I don't think I can predict that. I think a much better use of my time is being very flexible and adaptable at a time like this.
cards.zh: 我不覺得我預測得了那個。我覺得我的時間花在保持彈性、快速調整上，回報高得多。
cards.why: 拒絕回答一個問題時，不要只說做不到，要立刻交出你打算改做什麼。a much better use of my time 把「我不做」翻譯成「我在做更有價值的事」，主導權還在自己手上。
swaps: That's not a call I can make—what I can control is...
Rather than guess at that, I'd rather spend the time on...
cards.pmNote: 擋需求的標準句型：先說做不到什麼，再說改做什麼，永遠不要只留前半段。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

cards.pattern: The nature of [X] is we just don't know all the answers, and that's okay. The right way to deal with that is [做法].
cards.quote: And then just the nature of the future is like we just don't know all the answers and that's okay. And then the right way to deal with that is to run as many experiments as possible.
cards.zh: 未來的本質就是我們不會知道所有答案，這沒關係。面對這件事正確的做法，是盡可能多跑一些實驗。
cards.why: and that's okay 這三個字是整句的關鍵——它把不確定從問題變成前提，後面的策略才站得住。少了它，「我們不知道」只會讓人焦慮。
swaps: We're not going to have certainty here, and that's fine—so we optimize for learning speed
Given we can't know, the strategy is to buy information cheaply
cards.pmNote: 策略就是取捨：不確定性高的時候，選項價值大於準確度。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

cards.pattern: I don't think there's any reason to assume that [大家默認的上限] is the cap on anything.
cards.quote: And the reason for that is, I don't think there's any reason to assume that human skill level is the cap on anything.
cards.zh: 原因是：我不覺得有任何理由要假設「人類的能力水準」就是天花板。
cards.why: I don't think there's any reason to assume 把舉證責任推回給對方——不是我要證明可以更高，是你要證明為什麼不行。這是拆隱含假設最省力的一句。
swaps: Who says that's the ceiling?
Nothing forces that number to be the limit
cards.pmNote: first principles 的入口通常是一句「這個上限是誰定的？」
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

cards.pattern: I love this answer. So what I'm hearing is, essentially, [一句話重述].
cards.quote: I love this answer. So what I'm hearing is, essentially, if you're amazing at any of these three roles, you will do well.
cards.zh: 我很喜歡這個回答。所以我聽到的意思，簡單講就是：這三個角色你任何一個做到頂尖，都會過得很好。
cards.why: so what I'm hearing is 是英語會議裡的萬用安全帶：既確認理解、又不必承認自己剛剛沒聽懂。前面加一句 I love this answer 讓重述不像考試，而像接話。
swaps: Let me play that back—you're saying...
If I'm following you, the takeaway is...
cards.pmNote: 對齊（alignment）不是問「你懂嗎」，是自己重述一遍讓對方修正。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

cards.pattern: My most controversial opinion is that [X] is as big a deal as [Y]. And only as big a deal as [Y].
cards.quote: My most controversial opinion is that I think that AI is as big a deal as the internet or mobile. And only as big a deal as the internet or mobile.
cards.zh: 我最有爭議的一個看法是：AI 跟網路、行動裝置一樣重大——而且也「只」跟它們一樣重大而已。
cards.why: 同一句話重複一次、只換一個字（and only），前半段拉攏樂觀派、後半段一秒打臉狂熱派。這種「重複＋一字反轉」是英語裡最漂亮的立場宣告技巧。
swaps: It's a huge deal—and no bigger than the last huge deal
As big as X. Exactly as big as X, and no bigger
cards.pmNote: 先給對方一半的認同再收回另一半，比一開始就唱反調更容易被聽完。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.pattern: I don't think it's particularly productive to argue whether [A or B]. Those aren't productive conversations.
cards.quote: I don't think it's particularly productive to say, "Well, is it 20% bigger than the internet or 100%?" Those aren't productive conversations.
cards.zh: 去爭「它比網路大 20% 還是 100%」我覺得沒什麼意義，那種對話不會有產出。
cards.why: 不說對方講錯，而說這個「對話」沒有生產力——把否定對準議題而不是人。particularly 這個副詞讓語氣軟一級，是英語裡標準的緩衝副詞。
swaps: I'm not sure that debate takes us anywhere useful
That's an argument we can't settle and don't need to
cards.pmNote: 會議上最貴的成本是辯論一個無論結果如何都不改行動的問題。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.pattern: One of the comments was "[別人的酸言]", which is slightly facetious, but also kind of true.
cards.quote: One of the comments was, "Benedict, this is 80 slides of saying we don't know," which is slightly facetious, but also kind of true.
cards.zh: 有人留言說：「Benedict，你這 80 張投影片就是在講『我們不知道』。」講得有點壞，但也算是實話。
cards.why: 自己把最刺的批評唸出來，再用 slightly facetious, but also kind of true 半接下來。這招同時做到三件事：顯得有幽默感、拆掉對方的火力、還讓「我們不知道」變成刻意的結論。
swaps: Someone called it X—unfair, but not entirely wrong
That's a cheap shot, and it's also basically accurate
cards.pmNote: 預先講出對你最不利的一句話，會場上就沒人需要幫你講了。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.pattern: What's the hard part of the job? Is it [表面工作]? Or is it something else?
cards.quote: What's the hard part of the job? Is the hard part of the job writing the code line by line? Is the hard part of the job giving you the SKU, or making the PowerPoint?
cards.zh: 這份工作真正難的部分是什麼？是一行一行寫程式嗎？是把貨號調出來、把投影片做出來嗎？
cards.why: 連續三個同構的問句（都以 Is the hard part of the job 開頭），節奏本身就在暗示答案是「都不是」。用問句串起來的論證，聽眾會覺得結論是自己推出來的。
swaps: Where does the difficulty actually live in this job?
Which part of this is the part you're really paid for?
cards.pmNote: 拆自動化風險前先問「難的部分在哪」，答案通常不在被自動化的那一段。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.pattern: Young people won't believe this, but before [X], [誇張的舊苦日子]. And now thanks to [X], [反諷的結果].
cards.quote: Young people won't believe this, but before Excel, junior investment bankers worked really long hours. And now thanks to Excel, Goldman's associates will work at lunchtime on Fridays.
cards.zh: 年輕人可能不信，Excel 出現以前，投行的菜鳥可是要加班到很晚的。現在多虧有了 Excel，高盛的 associate 禮拜五中午就能下班了。
cards.why: 整句是反話：大家都知道投行現在更操。用一個假裝正經的歷史敘述把「效率提升＝工時減少」這個假設笑掉，比直接反駁有力十倍。young people won't believe this 是講反話的招牌開場。
swaps: Remember how X was supposed to give us all more free time?
Funny how that efficiency never showed up in anyone's calendar
cards.pmNote: 效率工具通常提高產出而不是減少工時（Jevons paradox）——排期時別把節省的時間當成可回收。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.pattern: It's all the other stuff. [顯眼的產出] is just the task, but that's not what you hired them for.
cards.quote: It's all the other stuff. And the PowerPoint is just like the task, but that's not what you hired them for.
cards.zh: 價值在其他所有事情上。投影片只是那個「任務」，但那不是你花錢請他們來做的事。
cards.why: 把對方看得見的產出降格成 the task，再用 that's not what you hired them for 把價值移到看不見的地方。這句可以原封不動搬去回應「這功能 AI 一天就做得出來」。
swaps: The deliverable isn't the value—it's the residue of the value
You're not paying for the artifact, you're paying for the judgment
cards.pmNote: 被質疑「這個外包／AI 也能做」時，先分清楚 task 跟 job 的界線。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.pattern: [某產業] do not think of themselves as being in the business of [不起眼的實際工作], but that was what they actually did.
cards.quote: Record companies do not think of themselves as being in the business of manufacturing small pieces of plastic, but that was what they actually did.
cards.zh: 唱片公司從來不覺得自己是在做小塑膠片的生意，但他們實際上做的就是這個。
cards.why: in the business of 是英語商業裡定義「你到底在賣什麼」的固定說法。前後兩句刻意矛盾（他們以為 vs 實際上），把一個公司的自我認知與現金流來源拆開，是最狠也最有禮貌的一種質疑。
swaps: They thought they were selling X; they were actually selling Y
Nobody there would say they were in the Y business, but that's what the P&L says
cards.pmNote: 問「我們實際上在賣什麼」比問「我們的願景是什麼」更能預測誰會被顛覆。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.pattern: I think one needs to be a little bit cautious on what [人] says. And that's setting aside the cynical view that [難聽的解讀], which I don't believe at all.
cards.quote: So, I think one needs to be a little bit cautious on what Dario says. And that's setting aside the cynical view that he's just doing that department stock, which I don't believe at all.
cards.zh: 我覺得對 Dario 講的話要保留一點。而且我這裡還先撇開那種比較酸的解讀——說他只是在替自家股價講話——那我完全不相信。
cards.why: one needs to be cautious 用非人稱主詞把批評講得像通則。真正高明的是後半句：主動把更難聽的攻擊講出來，同時聲明自己不採用——既讓聽眾想到那個可能，又保住了風度。
swaps: I'd take that with a pinch of salt—and I'm not even going down the cynical route
There's an unkind reading of this that I don't buy, so let's set it aside
cards.pmNote: 反對高層意見時，把「立場利益」講出來但明說自己不採信，殺傷力與安全性兼具。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
cards.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。
cards.why: 用一個對稱句解釋為什麼恐慌是結構性的：看得見的一定是損失。這種「不對稱可見性」的論證，換掉主詞就能用在裁員、砍功能、換技術棧任何場合。
swaps: The losses are visible on day one; the gains only show up later
We can name what goes away; we can't name what replaces it yet
cards.pmNote: 報壞消息時主動說明「新機會現在講不出具體名字」，比硬編一個更可信。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.pattern: You don't have to believe [激進前提] to believe that [結論].
cards.quote: So you don't have to believe in any of that stuff to believe that this is a giant deal.
cards.zh: 你完全不用相信那一整套說法，也可以相信這件事非常重大。
cards.why: 把結論跟最容易被攻擊的前提脫鉤，讓懷疑派也能點頭。這是說服光譜上最有效的一句話：降低對方買單所需要的信仰量。
swaps: You can reject the whole thesis and still land in the same place
None of that has to be true for this to matter
cards.pmNote: 提案時把「必須先同意的前提」壓到最少，過關率最高。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.pattern: Obviously if [極端個案], then you're really pissed off. But that's a [別的問題]. That's not a [我的問題].
cards.quote: Now, obviously if you live in a small town and they capped the well and gave all the water to the data center, then you're really pissed off. But that's a planning problem. That's not a data center problem.
cards.zh: 當然，如果你住在小鎮上，井被封了、水全給了資料中心，那你當然火大。但那是都市規劃的問題，不是資料中心的問題。
cards.why: 先把對方的情緒完整承認（you're really pissed off，用他的語氣講），再用兩個短句把問題重新歸類。承認情緒但不承認歸因——這是接住反對意見最乾淨的一組動作。
swaps: That's a real complaint, but it's a policy issue, not a product issue
Totally fair to be angry about that—it's just a different root cause
cards.pmNote: 接住反對時，先驗證感受、再爭論歸因，順序反了就會被當成迴避。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.pattern: Now that may be completely wrong. Imagine having this conversation about [X] in [年份]—what would you have got right?
cards.quote: Now that may be completely wrong, and one of the points I make in the presentation is like, imagine having this conversation about the internet in 1997, what would you have got right?
cards.zh: 當然，這可能完全錯。我在簡報裡就有提到：想像我們在 1997 年談網路，你當時猜對過幾題？
cards.why: 剛講完一個很篤定的推論就自己補一句 that may be completely wrong，是英語論述型講者的紀律：立場要硬，信心要標示。後面的歷史類比讓自謙有依據，不是客套。
swaps: I could be completely wrong about this
Ask me again in five years and I'll probably wince
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.pattern: You can say [時髦標籤] all you like—it's [本質].
cards.quote: We're all sitting talking about it, and Tate says, "It's a low margin reseller, one time sells." "You can say dotcom all you like, it's a low margin reseller."
cards.zh: 大家在車上討論，Tate 說：「它就是個低毛利的經銷商，一次性買賣。你要講幾次『.com』都可以，它還是個低毛利經銷商。」
cards.why: You can say X all you like 是英語裡專門用來剝掉包裝的句型：不否認標籤，只是宣告標籤不改變經濟結構。重複同一個判斷兩次，讓它變成定論。
swaps: Call it AI-native if you want—the unit economics are the same
The label changes; the margin structure doesn't
cards.pmNote: 評估新商業模式，先把行銷詞拿掉看毛利結構。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.pattern: Somebody said the problem with me is my answer to everything is "it depends". Yeah, it does. It depends.
cards.quote: I remember somebody on social media said the problem with Benedict is his answer to everything is it depends. It's like, yeah, it does. It depends.
cards.zh: 我記得有人在社群上說：Benedict 的問題就是他對什麼都回答「看情況」。呃，本來就是啊。就是看情況。
cards.why: 面對嘲諷最強的回應不是辯解，是完全同意再重複一次。Yeah, it does. It depends. 兩個短句把批評變成立場宣告，對方的攻擊反而幫你打了廣告。
swaps: Guilty. It really does depend
That's the criticism, and I'll own it
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.pattern: I should just wind back on what you just said—[修正對方的前提].
cards.quote: Well, I should just wind back on what you just said. So on average, nobody died in World War I. Great.
cards.zh: 我得先把你剛剛那句話往回拉一點。用平均來看，一次大戰沒有人死掉嘛，很好。但你如果是 1914 年的十九歲男生，有三分之一機率回不來。
cards.why: wind back on what you just said 是一個很有禮貌的煞車片語：不說你錯，只說「我們倒回去一點」。接著他用「平均來說一戰沒人死掉」這種荒謬的算法，再補上「但你如果是 1914 年的十九歲男生，有三分之一機率回不來」——一句話拆掉「整體來看沒事」這種安慰式論述。
swaps: Let me push back on the framing there for a second
Before we move on—averages hide the thing that matters here
cards.pmNote: 看到「平均沒問題」的指標，先問分佈：受害最深的那一群是誰。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.pattern: Don't [自我感覺良好的迴避]—that gives you a great feeling of moral superiority, but it's not going to help.
cards.quote: The only answer I think one can have is, don't stick your head in the sand and say, "I hate all of this stuff," because that gives you a great feeling of moral superiority.
cards.zh: 我覺得唯一的答案是：別把頭埋進沙子裡說「我討厭這些東西」，因為那只會讓你很有道德優越感。
cards.why: 不罵對方逃避，而是精準說出逃避帶來的好處（道德優越感）——把對方的心理動機講穿，比指責更難反駁。這是給難聽回饋時最鋒利也最不失禮的角度。
swaps: Refusing to engage feels principled, but it doesn't move you forward
That position is comfortable, and it costs you
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.pattern: A really interesting takeaway here is that your sense is [重述對方的預測].
cards.quote: A really interesting takeaway here is that your sense is over time the foundational model companies, their margins will get squeezed, and the bigger opportunities in the application layer.
cards.zh: 所以一個很有意思的結論是：你的判斷是，長期來看基礎模型公司的毛利會被壓縮，比較大的機會在應用層。
cards.why: 用 your sense is 而不是 you said，把重述框成「我理解的你的判斷」——留了修正空間，也避免把對方的推測講成斷言。這是複述別人立場時最安全的動詞。
swaps: So your read is that...
If I'm capturing it right, your expectation is...
cards.pmNote: 會議紀錄裡把「判斷」跟「事實」用不同動詞標開，後面追責才不會失真。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

cards.quote: And that's the classic explanation of what they do. So, they sell a data platform. So, that's the capsule answer, but there's lots to unpack in there.
cards.zh: 這是最制式的講法：他們賣的是一個資料平台。這是濃縮版的答案，但底下還有很多可以拆。
cards.why: 先給一個 30 秒版本，再宣告「還有很多可以拆」，等於把節奏交還給對方決定要不要深入。台灣人回答大問題常一路講到底，用 capsule answer 這個標記會顯得結構清楚很多。
swaps: That's the short version—happy to go deeper on any part
That's the elevator answer; there's a lot underneath it
cards.pmNote: 面對高層先給壓縮版答案，再問要不要展開，是最省時間的匯報結構。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.pattern: The companies that attract talent put out a distinctive bad signal—it has to turn some people off. That's the key of a good bad signal.
cards.quote: He thinks that a lot of the best recruiters in the world or the companies that attract talent, they put out this distinctive bad signal and it has to turn some people off. That's the key of a good, bad signal.
cards.zh: 他認為最會吸引人才的公司，都會刻意放出一個「不討喜的訊號」，而且一定要有人被勸退。這才是好的壞訊號的重點。
cards.why: good, bad signal 這種故意的矛盾詞組，逼聽眾停下來重新解讀，正是它值錢的地方。用 it has to turn some people off 把「勸退」講成功能而不是副作用，一句話就把價值觀定位講完了。
swaps: If nobody's put off by it, it isn't doing its job
The filter only works if it actually filters
cards.pmNote: 定義團隊價值觀時，最重要的一句是「這裡不適合誰」。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.quote: So the idea is, basically, you write up a two-page plan for the project. You invite three or four smart folks who don't know anything about the project and their job is just to tear apart your plan.
cards.zh: 做法是：你先寫一份兩頁的專案計畫，然後找三四個完全不懂這個專案的聰明人來，他們的任務就是把你的計畫拆爛。
cards.why: their job is just to tear apart 把「被批評」制度化成一個有職稱的角色，所以沒有人是在針對你。要在英語團隊裡導入任何批評機制，這個「指派任務」的講法最好用。
swaps: Their only job in the room is to find the holes
We assign people to argue against it on purpose
cards.pmNote: murder board／pre-mortem：找不懂脈絡的人來拆，比找懂的人來背書有價值。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.pattern: "[人人都同意的原則]" is not a good principle, because nobody can reasonably disagree with it.
cards.quote: They would write principles such as move fast and I would always be, "Everyone likes to move fast." It is not a good principle actually because nobody can really disagree with this reasonably.
cards.zh: 他們會寫「快速行動」這種原則，我都會回：誰不喜歡快速行動？那其實不是好的原則，因為沒有人會合理地反對它。
cards.why: 用一個測試取代爭論：「有沒有人會合理地反對？」沒有的話它就不是原則、只是廢話。給對方一把尺，比直接說「你寫得很空」有建設性得多。
swaps: If the opposite sounds insane, it's not a real principle
A principle only counts if someone could sensibly argue the other side
cards.pmNote: 寫 principles 或 tenets 時，每一條都要能寫出一個合理的反面版本。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.pattern: They've accomplished very difficult goals in very hostile environments. And it turns out that [對照場景], that's actually a very useful skill.
cards.quote: They tend to have accomplished very difficult goals in very hostile environments. And it turns out that when you're starting a somewhat chaotic tech company, that's actually a very useful skill to have.
cards.zh: 這些人習慣在極度不友善的環境裡把很難的目標做出來。結果發現，開一家有點混亂的科技公司，這剛好是非常有用的能力。
cards.why: and it turns out that 是英語裡「意外發現」的標準連接詞，讓一個非直覺的招聘決定聽起來像被資料驗證過，而不是老闆的偏好。
swaps: As it happens, that maps almost perfectly onto...
Turns out that's exactly the muscle you need when...
cards.pmNote: 招募差異化人才時，要講清楚「他們原本的環境」跟「我們的環境」哪裡同構。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.pattern: The job is not just to [X]. It is not just to [Y]. It is to actually [真正的目標].
cards.quote: But then the job of the forward deployed engineer is not just to deploy software. It is not just to sell software. It is to actually solve the problem.
cards.zh: 前線工程師的工作不只是把軟體部署上去，也不只是把軟體賣出去，而是真的把問題解決掉。
cards.why: 兩個 not just 疊出節奏，最後一個 It is to actually 落地。三段式否定＋肯定是英語裡定義角色最有力的結構，用來回答「這個職位到底在幹嘛」百試百靈。
swaps: The deliverable isn't the software, it's the outcome
We're not measured on shipping it—we're measured on it working
cards.pmNote: 定義角色時用「不是什麼」開頭，比列職責清單更能對齊期待。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.pattern: The error people make more often than not is [X]. That's the mistake I've seen more than the other way around.
cards.quote: And I think the error that people make more often than not is they are actually too stuck on their own product vision. That's the mistake I've seen a little bit more actually than the other way around.
cards.zh: 我覺得大家最常犯的錯，是太黏著自己原本的產品願景。這個錯我看到的，其實比反過來的那種多一點。
cards.why: 把批評講成一個群體現象（the error people make），對方就不必對號入座。再用 more than the other way around 承認兩種錯都存在，只是比例不同——這種比例式判斷比絕對判斷容易被接受。
swaps: The more common failure mode is the opposite of what people expect
In my experience people over-index on their original thesis
cards.pmNote: 客戶說的痛點跟你的產品願景衝突時，先假設客戶是對的。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.pattern: There's no hard and fast rule, but you need to have this matrix of options in your mind and be very deliberate about which one you're going with and why.
cards.quote: So yeah, no hard and fast rule, but I think it's always you need to have this matrix of options in your mind and be very deliberate about which one you are going with and why.
cards.zh: 沒有什麼鐵則，但你腦中要有一張選項矩陣，而且要很清楚自己選了哪一格、為什麼。
cards.why: 被問到「有沒有標準答案」時最好的回法：先承認沒有（no hard and fast rule），再把價值放在「有意識地選」。deliberate about which one and why 把要求從答案轉成流程，聽起來專業又不敷衍。
swaps: There's no formula—what matters is knowing which trade-off you took
It's situational, but the choice should never be accidental
cards.pmNote: 沒有最佳解時，決策品質等於「你有沒有明確知道自己放棄了什麼」。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.pattern: Sorry, this is a little bit dark, but [不舒服的類比].
cards.quote: As a very simple example, sorry, this is a little bit dark, but how restaurants want to turn over tables as fast as possible in order to maximize for the day? Hospitals actually want to do the same with patients.
cards.zh: 舉個很簡單的例子——抱歉這個講法有點黑暗——餐廳希望翻桌越快越好，好把一天的收益拉高。醫院對病床其實也是同一件事。
cards.why: sorry, this is a little bit dark 是一個預警標籤：先幫聽眾準備好情緒，他們就不會把你的冷血歸咎到人格上。要講不討喜但真實的商業邏輯時，這個緩衝幾乎是必備的。
swaps: This is going to sound cynical, but...
Forgive the blunt framing, but the economics work like this
cards.pmNote: 理解客戶產業，要從「他們怎麼算錢」而不是「他們怎麼自我介紹」開始。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.pattern: There's so much advice on this and you read it and think "this is super obvious". Then when you live it, you're like, "this is why people say this".
cards.quote: I think with hiring, it's funny, man, there's so much hiring advice online and you read it and you're like, "Yeah, this is super obvious." And then when you live it, you're suddenly like, "Aah, this is why people say this."
cards.zh: 招人這件事很好笑，網路上一堆建議，你看的時候都覺得「這不是廢話嗎」。等你真的經歷過，才會突然懂「喔，原來大家是這個意思」。
cards.why: 自己先講出「這聽起來很廢」，讀者／聽者就不會替你講。用 read it vs live it 的對比把老生常談重新充電，是分享常識型結論時最重要的一道手續。
swaps: It sounds obvious until it happens to you
Everyone knows this; almost nobody has felt it
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.quote: You ask questions like, what's the hardest you've ever worked to get something done and why? And that does differentiate a lot of people, a lot of people don't actually have a great answer to that.
cards.zh: 你可以問這種問題：你這輩子為了完成某件事最拚的一次是什麼？為什麼？這題真的很能分辨人，很多人其實答不太出來。
cards.why: 先給問題、再給這題的診斷價值（能分辨什麼、大部分人會怎麼卡住）。介紹面試題時附上「答不出來代表什麼」，聽眾才知道怎麼用，而不是只抄一個題目。
swaps: Tell me about a time you went well past what was asked
What's the most effort you've ever put into something nobody made you do?
cards.pmNote: 行為面試題的重點不是答案內容，是對方有沒有具體到細節。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.pattern: And then there's this question of: would you rather be in the room making this better, or not?
cards.quote: And then there's this question of, well, would you rather be in the room and making this better or not?
cards.zh: 然後就有一個問題：你是寧願待在那個房間裡把它變好，還是乾脆不在？
cards.why: 把道德爭議轉成一個只有兩個選項的選擇題，而且兩個選項都由對方承擔後果。用問句而不是主張，讓聽眾自己走到你要的位置，反彈最小。
swaps: Is walking away actually the higher-impact choice here?
Does opting out make the outcome better or just make you cleaner?
cards.pmNote: 遇到「該不該參與」的爭議，先問「不參與的話結果會變好嗎」。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.pattern: You sort of want to say to them, "Hey, are you thinking about [他們在迴避的後果]?"
cards.quote: So you have engineers now who are working on optimizing short form videos for higher engagement, and you sort of want to say to them like, "Hey, are you thinking about what this is doing to the brains of young children?"
cards.zh: 現在有一群工程師在優化短影音的互動率，你會有點想跟他們說：「欸，你有想過這對小朋友的腦袋在做什麼嗎？」
cards.why: you sort of want to say to them 是一層很好用的緩衝：把尖銳的話講出來，但框成「我有點想說」而不是「我現在正在對你說」。sort of 再降一級語氣，整句就從指控變成感嘆。
swaps: Part of me wants to ask them whether...
You almost want to stop them and say...
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.pattern: It turned out my comparative advantage in a lot of ways was [別人不想碰的那塊].
cards.quote: But it turned out, look, my comparative advantage in a lot of ways was the networks I'd built and the experience I'd had in engaging with the messy parts of the world.
cards.zh: 但後來發現，我真正的比較利益，其實是那些人脈，還有跟這個世界最麻煩的那些地方打交道的經驗。
cards.why: comparative advantage 是經濟學詞，用來講自己的強項時特別好：它承認「我不是每件事都比別人強」，只是說「相對來說我在這塊最划算」。談成績時最不招人反感的措辭。
swaps: Where I'm actually differentiated is...
My edge isn't raw skill, it's the terrain I know
cards.pmNote: 談自己的價值時用「相對優勢」而不是「我最強」，可信度高很多。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.pattern: You have to aim for [最高標準]. You have to make something better than that. That should be your goal—not something you feel is good enough.
cards.quote: And he would say, you have to aim for Chartres. You have to make something that is better than that. That should be your goal, not to just turn in something that's what you feel is good enough.
cards.zh: 他會說：你要對準夏特大教堂。你要做出比它更好的東西。那才是你的目標，而不是交出一個你自己覺得「還可以」的作品。
cards.why: 用一個具體到不能再具體的標的（那座教堂）取代抽象的「追求卓越」，三個短句層層加碼，最後用 good enough 當反例收尾。設定標準時，指著一個實體遠比形容詞有效。
swaps: Benchmark against the best thing ever made in this category, not against last quarter
Don't aim for shippable, aim for the thing people still study in twenty years
cards.pmNote: 把品質標準綁在一個具體的參照物上，團隊才不會各自解讀「夠好」。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.pattern: I think [不流行的主張]. I think this is a somewhat contrarian view within [某圈子], maybe not outside it.
cards.quote: I think going to college is great. I think this is a somewhat contrarian view within tech, maybe not in the broader economy.
cards.zh: 我覺得念大學很棒。我知道這在科技圈算是個有點逆風的看法，在一般社會可能就還好。
cards.why: 先講立場，再標示「這在哪個圈子算逆風」。這個座標定位讓聽眾知道你不是狀況外，而是明知故犯——講不受歡迎的意見時，這一句能省下一半的辯護。
swaps: I know this isn't the popular take in this room
This puts me in the minority here, and I'll stand by it
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.quote: I'm going to mirror back the tips you just shared, and there's actually a secondary tip that I think is the more interesting piece.
cards.zh: 我把你剛剛給的建議重述一遍——而且我覺得裡面藏了一個更有意思的第二層建議。
cards.why: mirror back 是「原樣反射回去」的說法，比 summarize 更強調忠實。加上 the more interesting piece，你在複述的同時也加了值，這是會議裡把角色從記錄者變成參與者的關鍵一句。
swaps: Let me reflect that back—and add what I think the real insight is
Playing that back to you, plus the part I think you buried
cards.pmNote: 總結別人的話時順手指出「最有價值的其實是第二點」，比純複述有影響力。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

cards.pattern: I'll just say it as plainly as possible: they don't care about you. They care about [他們真正在服務的對象].
cards.quote: The editor, the writer, I'll just say it as plainly as possible, they don't care about you. They don't care about you. They care about their reader, or their listener, or their viewer.
cards.zh: 編輯也好、記者也好，我把話講到最白：他們不在乎你。他們真的不在乎你。他們在乎的是他們的讀者、聽眾、觀眾。
cards.why: I'll just say it as plainly as possible 是講重話前的許可證，先宣告「接下來會很直接」，聽者就會把它當事實而不是攻擊。緊接著把同一句重複一次，是英語口語裡最強的加粗方式。
swaps: Let me put this bluntly
I'll be as direct as I can about this
cards.pmNote: 跨部門協作時先搞清楚對方真正被誰考核，需求才推得動。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.pattern: Think about [X] the same way you think about [Y]: you do it when you know what it's for.
cards.quote: Think about press the same way that you think about raising money, which is to say you do it when you know what the money is for, and you should do it when you know what the press is for.
cards.zh: 把「找媒體報導」想成「募資」：你會在知道這筆錢要幹嘛的時候才去募，那你也該在知道這次曝光要幹嘛的時候才去找。
cards.why: 借用對方已經有紀律的領域（募資）來規範他還沒有紀律的領域（公關），一句話就把標準搬過去。which is to say 是把類比講成明確規則的橋接詞。
swaps: Treat it like hiring—you don't open a req until you know the gap
Same rule as fundraising: know the use of funds first
cards.pmNote: 任何資源投入前先寫下「這一輪要換到什麼」，否則無法判斷成敗。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.pattern: I respect that, and I relate to it. But "[對方的理由]" is not a good tactical decision for your business.
cards.quote: I respect that, and I relate to it in some ways with my own trying to get attention for my own work. But, "I deserve this" that's not a good tactical decision for your business.
cards.zh: 我尊重這種心情，我自己在推廣作品時也有過。但「我值得」不是一個好的商業決策理由。
cards.why: 先承認情緒（respect / relate to），再把它從決策依據裡剔除。關鍵在 not a good tactical decision——不否定感受本身，只否定它作為決策輸入的資格。這是給難聽回饋時最乾淨的切法。
swaps: I get the feeling, but it isn't a business reason
That's completely understandable—it's just not a criterion
cards.pmNote: 擋需求時把「情緒是真的」跟「情緒不能當排序依據」分兩句講。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.pattern: Was it that hard to [做那件小事]? No. But scale that out.
cards.quote: Was it that hard to come up and talk to me at the conference? No. But scale that out.
cards.zh: 好，那走過來跟我講兩句話有多難？不難。但你把這件事乘上去看——像這樣的信他到底寄了幾封？
cards.why: 對方一定會回「這又沒花多少力氣」，所以先自己承認（No），再用 scale that out 把單次成本乘上頻率。這是拆「反正很便宜」型反對意見的萬用招。
swaps: Individually it's cheap. Multiply it by fifty and it isn't
One of these costs nothing. That's not the number that matters
cards.pmNote: 評估瑣事成本要看總量，不看單次——這也是技術債累積的主因。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.pattern: The way I think of [我們] is that it's not even a [類別]. It's a [重新定義].
cards.quote: The way that I think of Entrepreneur is that it's not even a magazine about business. It's a magazine about thinking.
cards.zh: 我自己是這樣看《Entrepreneur》的：它根本不是一本講商業的雜誌，而是一本講「怎麼想事情」的雜誌。
cards.why: not even a X 的 even 是關鍵，它預設對方本來就會把你歸到 X 類，然後直接跳過那個層級。用兩句話重新定義自己的產品類別，是產品定位最短的講法。
swaps: We're not really a project management tool—we're a decision log
Think of it less as a product and more as a habit
cards.pmNote: 產品定位講「我們不是什麼」通常比「我們是什麼」更快讓對方抓到差異。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.quote: And so what I'm looking for when somebody reaches out is did they make some interesting counterintuitive decision that solved a problem in their business, and I'll emphasize in.
cards.zh: 所以我在找的是：他有沒有做過什麼有趣、反直覺的決定，解決了他公司「內部」的問題——我要特別強調是「內部」。
cards.why: I'll emphasize in 這種「我要特別強調這個介係詞」的講法，是英語裡處理最容易被誤解的一個字的標準動作。台灣人講英文很少停下來標記單字，但這一秒往往省掉整輪來回。
swaps: —and the word doing the work there is "internal"
I want to underline that one word
cards.pmNote: 寫需求規格時，最容易出事的通常是一個介係詞或量詞，值得單獨標註。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.pattern: Don't confuse [表面指標] with actual success.
cards.quote: So don't confuse posting press releases even on very big websites with actual success.
cards.zh: 所以不要把「新聞稿被大網站登出來」跟真正的成功搞混。
cards.why: don't confuse A with B 是英語裡拆虛榮指標最短的句型，一句話就能在會議上把 vanity metric 擋掉。重點在於它不指責任何人，只指出兩件事被混為一談。
swaps: Let's not mistake activity for impact
Coverage isn't the same as being read
cards.pmNote: 定義成功指標時，先列出三個最容易被誤當成功的虛榮指標。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.pattern: What you want in [某個角色] is someone who traffics in one thing, and that is [核心資產].
cards.quote: What you want in an actual PR person is someone who traffics in one thing, and that is relationships.
cards.zh: 你要找的公關，是那種只靠一件事吃飯的人——關係。
cards.why: traffics in 是很精準的動詞（以某物為交易標的），用它把一個職位的核心價值壓成一個名詞。要人要預算時，先把「這個角色唯一不可取代的東西」講出來，說服力最強。
swaps: The one thing that role has to bring is X
You're not buying hours, you're buying access
cards.pmNote: 要 headcount 時，論證要落在「這個角色唯一提供的東西」，不是工作量。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.pattern: You should like it when [對方] pushes back and says "[反對意見]". That's someone you should hire.
cards.quote: You should like when a PR person pushes back on you and says, "You know what? I don't think that your story is right for that publication. Here's why." That's someone you should hire.
cards.zh: 當一個公關回你「老實說，我覺得你的故事不適合那家媒體，原因是這樣」，你應該要高興。這種人才值得聘。
cards.why: 把「被拒絕」重新標記成「值得付錢的訊號」，用 that's someone you should hire 一句收尾。要在團隊裡鼓勵反對意見，最有效的不是說「歡迎批評」，而是明確說出「會這樣做的人我們會留下來」。
swaps: The ones who tell you no are the ones worth keeping
Pushback is the service, not a failure to deliver it
cards.pmNote: 想要團隊敢講真話，就要公開獎勵第一個說「這個方向不對」的人。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.pattern: So I would expect that it would be possibly very reasonable that [結論] might not be [X] right now.
cards.quote: So I would expect that if you have a startup and that startup is not B2B in some way, that it would be possibly very reasonable that business publications might not be your target right now.
cards.zh: 所以我會預期，如果你的新創不算 B2B，那商業媒體現在可能不是你該鎖定的對象——這樣想其實滿合理的。
cards.why: 一句話裡疊了四層緩衝（would expect / possibly / very reasonable / might not），語意其實是「不要去」。這是英語顧問式建議的極端示範：越是要否定對方的計畫，緩衝疊得越厚。台灣人常直接說 you shouldn't，語氣會硬三級。
swaps: It might well be that this isn't the right channel for you yet
I'd probably question whether that's where your audience is
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.pattern: These reach millions of people. That does not mean your [X] is going to be read by millions of people.
cards.quote: These are reaching millions of people, their websites get many, many, many millions of unique visitors each month. That does not mean that your story is going to be read by millions of people.
cards.zh: 這些媒體確實觸及上百萬人，網站每個月幾百萬不重複訪客。但這不代表你那篇報導會被上百萬人看到。
cards.why: 先把對方期待的數字完整講一遍（甚至幫他放大），再用 that does not mean 把它跟他真正在意的結果切開。管理期待時，最有效的做法是承認大數字為真、只否定它的推論。
swaps: The reach is real. Your share of it won't be
Big audience, small slice—those are different numbers
cards.pmNote: 期望管理：讓對方保有大數字，只把「這跟你有關的部分」拆出來講。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.pattern: Did we get anything from that? The answer is no, like nothing. But you better believe that every [場合] includes the link.
cards.quote: Did we get anything from that story in Variety? The answer is no, like nothing. But you better believe that every email we send out to every potential advertiser, to every partner, includes the link.
cards.zh: 那篇 Variety 的報導有帶來什麼嗎？完全沒有。但你可以放心，我們寄給每個潛在廣告主、每個合作方的信裡，一定都附上那個連結。
cards.why: 先誠實承認直接成效是零，再把價值移到第二層用途。you better believe that 是很有畫面的口語強調（你最好相信＝我當然有做）。承認失敗再翻盤，比一開始就吹更可信。
swaps: Direct impact? Zero. Second-order value? Enormous
It moved no numbers. It opens every door
cards.pmNote: 談成效時把「直接指標」跟「第二層用途」分開講，避免被單一數字定生死。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.pattern: There is literally no magic answer to that. I wish that there was, but there is not. The closest I can give you is [替代答案].
