cards.quote: I mean, look, there is literally no magic answer to that. I wish that there was, but there is not. There's no format.
cards.zh: 老實說，這題沒有什麼神奇答案。我也希望有，但就是沒有。也沒有什麼固定格式。
cards.why: I wish that there was, but there is not 這句多餘的重複，作用是表達「我知道你想要答案，我也很遺憾」——先處理失望，再處理資訊。之後接 the closest I can give you 交出次佳解，整段就不會空手。
swaps: There's no formula here—I wish I had one for you
No silver bullet. The nearest thing I can offer is...
cards.pmNote: 說「不知道」之後一定要接「我能給的最接近的東西是」，否則等於沒回答。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.pattern: I hate [大家以為你要的東西]. I love [你真正要的東西].
cards.quote: I hate success stories. I love problem solving stories. And that's why when I talk to an entrepreneur, I expect them to be really open about that stuff.
cards.zh: 我討厭成功故事。我喜歡解決問題的故事。所以我跟創業者聊的時候，會期待他們願意把難的部分講出來。
cards.why: 兩個四個字的對句，把一整套編輯標準壓縮成八個字，對方聽完立刻知道該給你什麼。要傳達偏好時，「我討厭 A、我喜歡 B」的極簡對比比任何說明段落都有效。
swaps: Spare me the highlight reel—show me the mess
Wins bore me. Recoveries don't
cards.pmNote: review 或 postmortem 邀請別人講真話時，先明說你想聽的是問題不是成果。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.quote: But Fred got his press because sometimes, and here's the lesson, sometimes you are not the story, but you can be part of the story.
cards.zh: Fred 之所以拿到報導，是因為——這就是重點——有時候你本身不是那個故事，但你可以是故事的一部分。
cards.why: and here's the lesson 是插在句子中間的標記，等於在說「接下來這句要抄下來」。後半句的 not the story / part of the story 只換一個介係詞，就把一個策略講完了。
swaps: You don't have to be the headline to be in the piece
Aim to be the example, not the subject
cards.pmNote: 打不進主場的時候，先找一個正在被討論的趨勢，把自己放進去當案例。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.pattern: You have to know that there's a chance it could blow up in your face. That's the price you're paying for [好處].
cards.quote: You have to go into this being vulnerable and you have to know that there's a chance that it could blow up in your face. That's the price that you're paying for reaching their audience.
cards.zh: 你得帶著會受傷的心理準備進來，而且要知道這件事有可能整個炸在你臉上。這就是你為了觸及他們的受眾所付的代價。
cards.why: That's the price you're paying for X 把風險明確標價，讓對方自己決定要不要買。談取捨時最強的一句話，因為它不勸阻也不鼓勵，只是把帳算清楚。
swaps: That's the cost of admission for this channel
That downside is baked into the upside—you can't buy one without the other
cards.pmNote: 講取捨時把代價講成價格（price of X），比講成風險更容易讓對方做決定。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.pattern: I want to run a theory by you. Do you think the reason you [做了X] is actually because of [Y]?
cards.quote: I'll say, "I want to run a theory by you. Do you think that the reason why you are really interested in this or you made that decision is actually because of this other thing that you told me a little bit about?"
cards.zh: 我會說：「我想跟你對一個猜測。你會這麼在意這件事、或做了那個決定，會不會其實是因為你剛剛提到的另一件事？」
cards.why: run a theory by you 把一個很私人的推測包成待驗證的假設，對方可以否認而不必尷尬。這招在 1:1 帶人時特別好用：你證明自己有在聽，又不強加詮釋。
swaps: Can I test a hunch on you?
Tell me if this is off—I wonder whether the real driver here is...
cards.pmNote: 1:1 帶人不給答案，但可以給一個「假設」讓對方自己驗證或推翻。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.pattern: Okay, so let me summarize things that you've taught us so far. One is [X]. Two is [Y].
cards.quote: Okay, so let me summarize things that you've taught us so far. One is think about publications that go to people that will buy your thing. Two is don't think of it broad thing.
cards.zh: 好，我來把你目前教我們的整理一下。第一，挑那些會接觸到你買家的媒體。第二，不要只想到媒體這個層級。
cards.why: let me summarize things that you've taught us 這個措辭把總結變成致謝，對方不會覺得你在搶話。編號（One is / Two is）讓聽眾知道還有幾點，也逼自己收斂。
swaps: Let me recap where we've landed so far
So far I've got three things—stop me if I've missed one
cards.pmNote: 長會議每 20 分鐘做一次編號小結，決議品質會明顯提升。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

cards.pattern: Inherent in your question is this assumption that [對方沒說出口的前提]. And so I'm going to reject that premise, because [你的理由].
cards.quote: Well, inherent in your question is this assumption that design takes more time. And so I'm going to kind of reject that premise, because I don't think design takes more time.
cards.zh: 你這個問題裡本身就藏了一個假設：做設計會比較花時間。我要先否掉這個前提，因為我不覺得設計比較花時間。
cards.why: 不去回答問題，而是先把問題底下的假設挖出來擺上桌，再明講「我要拒絕這個前提」。這是英語會議裡最高階的反駁：你沒有反對任何人的立場，你只是指出大家都沒察覺的預設。kind of 是關鍵緩衝，把「拒絕」變成半步後退。
swaps: There's an assumption baked into that question that I'd want to challenge
Before I answer, can I push on the premise a bit?
cards.pmNote: 被問「這要花多久」時，先確認問題本身有沒有錯誤前提——很多 roadmap 爭論其實是前提之爭，不是估時之爭。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.pattern: [X] isn't useful as a decision-making tool, because nobody would ever argue the opposite.
cards.quote: They're not useful as decision-making tools because nobody would ever argue the opposite. Nobody ever sat in a meeting and said, "Oh, forget clear. Let's try to make it as confusing as possible."
cards.zh: 這些東西沒辦法拿來做決策，因為根本不會有人主張反面。從來沒有人在會議上說：「別管清楚了，我們把它做得越難懂越好。」
cards.why: 拆穿廢話的通用檢驗法：能不能想像有人主張反面？不能，就代表這句話沒有決策力。第二句用一個荒謬的假想台詞把論證演出來，比抽象講理有力十倍。
swaps: That's not a real criterion—nobody's going to argue for the opposite
If the opposite of your principle sounds insane, it isn't a principle
cards.pmNote: 設計原則要能砍掉選項才有用；「簡單、清楚、快」這種沒人反對的詞，只是標語不是準則。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.pattern: You're focused on [對方的框架] and I'm just going to push back.
cards.quote: You're focused on recent and I'm just going to push back. No, there's nothing terribly recent.
cards.zh: 你一直扣在「最近」這個點上，我要反過來擋一下——沒有，最近沒什麼特別的。
cards.why: 先把對方問題裡的限制條件講出來（You're focused on X），再宣告自己要反駁。先命名再反對，對方不會覺得被突襲；push back 是英語職場最安全的「我不同意」動詞，比 disagree 輕、比 I think 有力。
swaps: You're framing this as X—let me push back on that
I'm going to push back on the question itself
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.pattern: [對方用的那個詞] doesn't feel quite right to me, because [那個詞] feels like [A]. And that's different from [B].
cards.quote: Yeah, sorry. Buy-in doesn't feel quite right to me, because buy-in feels like, oh, I've come to agree with you. And that's different from it's a part of me.
cards.zh: 抱歉，我覺得「buy-in（買單）」這個詞不太對。buy-in 聽起來像「我最後被你說服了」，那跟「這東西本來就是我的一部分」是兩回事。
cards.why: 不反對想法，只反對用詞——這是最低風險的異議。doesn't feel quite right to me 把客觀爭論降級成主觀語感，對方幾乎不可能生氣；接著用 A feels like…that's different from… 把兩個概念的差距拉開。
swaps: I'd use a different word there—X suggests Y, and that's not quite it
"Alignment" doesn't feel like the right word to me
cards.pmNote: buy-in（事後被說服）和 ownership（一開始就在場）是兩種團隊狀態，交付品質差很多。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.pattern: Many of my [同行] will push back on this and they'll say [對方論點], and that's a solid argument as well.
cards.quote: And many of my design friends will push back on this and they'll say design should be its own thing and it should be an independent group and we should have three co-equal branches of government, and that's a solid argument as well
cards.zh: 我很多設計圈的朋友會反對，他們會說設計應該獨立成一個部門，跟產品、工程三權分立——那也是很有道理的論點。
cards.why: 自己先把最強的反方論點講出來，而且承認它成立（that's a solid argument as well）。搶先講反對意見會讓聽者覺得你思考過全局，後面你講自己的立場時可信度直接翻倍。台灣人習慣藏起反例，反而顯得沒想清楚。
swaps: A lot of people will disagree with me here, and honestly they've got a point
The counterargument is X—and it's a good one
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem 的口語版：把反對意見先講掉，比等對方講出來再接招容易十倍。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.pattern: Although I know this will frustrate [某群人], I just haven't been able to figure out how [X] works.
cards.quote: And although I know this will frustrate some of my friends, I just haven't been able to figure out how that works for design.
cards.zh: 我知道這樣講會讓一些朋友不爽，但我真的還沒想通這件事在設計上要怎麼運作。
cards.why: 承認不知道 + 承認會惹到人，兩個示弱疊在一起，反而變成資深訊號。I just haven't been able to figure out 的重點在 been able to——它把「我不懂」講成「我努力過但還沒解」。
swaps: I know this isn't a popular view, but I haven't cracked it
This will annoy some people, but I don't have a good answer here
cards.pmNote: 設計團隊該不該背數字，業界至今沒有共識；不要假裝有標準答案。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.pattern: I would kind of defer to you on that, honestly. You've [對方的優勢], so you have a much broader set of information you're working with.
cards.quote: Yeah, look, I would kind of defer to you on that, honestly. You've talked to a lot more people across a lot more companies, so you have a much broader set of information you're working with.
cards.zh: 老實說這題我聽你的。你跟更多公司、更多人聊過，你手上的資訊面比我廣太多。
cards.why: defer to you 不是投降，是「在這個題目上我把發言權讓給你」，而且立刻給出讓權的具體理由。這招讓你在不知道答案時仍然顯得判斷力清楚——你知道誰該回答這題。
swaps: I'd defer to you here—you've got far more data points than I do
You're closer to this than I am, so I'll take your read on it
cards.pmNote: 跨部門會議中主動 defer 一次，往往換來對方下次在你的地盤 defer 給你。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.quote: But if a PM came to me with something that was drawn and kind of fully baked, my response was like, thanks for giving me that. Now I know exactly what we're not going to do.
cards.zh: 如果 PM 拿一張畫得很完整的圖來找我，我的回應是：謝謝你給我這個，現在我很清楚我們「不會」做成這樣。
cards.why: 用感謝當包裝，把拒絕塞在第二句。fully baked（做到全熟）是很有畫面的行話，指「別人已經幫你決定完的方案」。這句的殺傷力來自反差，但也因為有 thanks 開頭而不至於變成人身攻擊。
swaps: That's helpful—now I know one direction we won't take
Appreciate the sketch. I'll treat it as one option to rule out
cards.pmNote: PM 給 designer 的應該是問題與限制，不是解法；給了解法等於把對方降級成畫圖的人。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.pattern: You don't give them [太大的範圍] and you don't even give them [中等範圍]. You give them something more like [剛好的範圍].
cards.quote: You don't give them an airport tarmac and you don't even give them a football field. You give them something more like a basketball court, a sort of scale at which they can do their design thing.
cards.zh: 你不會給他們一整條機場跑道，連足球場都不該給。要給的是差不多籃球場那種大小——大到能發揮，小到能收斂。
cards.why: 把抽象的「範圍要多大」換成三個一路縮小的具體場地，聽的人不用思考就能感覺到尺度差。談 scope 時最難的就是量化，這種遞減式比喻是母語者的標準解法。
swaps: Not a blank cheque, not a straitjacket—somewhere in between
Give them guardrails, not a tiny box
cards.pmNote: 設計需要限制才跑得快；限制不足和限制過度一樣傷產出。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.pattern: If you give [對象] a lot of [問題], they're going to [後果], and honestly, that's your fault as the [對方的角色].
cards.quote: And if you give designers a lot of ambiguity, they're going to spend a lot of time spinning around, and honestly, that's your fault as the client.
cards.zh: 你丟一堆模糊的東西給設計師，他們就會一直空轉——老實說，那是你這個「業主」的問題。
cards.why: 把責任歸屬藏在因果句尾，而不是開頭指著人罵。honestly 在這裡是「我要說重話了」的訊號燈，而 as the client 給了對方一個角色而不是罪名——你批評的是他的職責履行，不是他的人格。
swaps: That's on us as the people writing the brief
Honestly, that one's on the requester, not the team
cards.pmNote: 設計拿到模糊的 input，卻被要求交出精確的 output——這種不對稱是多數 design churn 的根源。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.pattern: It's not that [對方] couldn't [做那件事], it's just I need you to play that position.
cards.quote: It's not that one of my PM counterparts couldn't bring a lot to the design table, it's just I need you to play that position.
cards.zh: 不是說 PM 對設計沒有貢獻——他們當然有；只是我需要你守住你的位置。
cards.why: It's not that X, it's just Y 是英語裡「擋人但不貶低人」的專用句型：前半句先確認對方有能力，後半句把拒絕轉成分工需求。台灣人常直接講「這不是你的守備範圍」，殺傷力大很多。
swaps: It's not that you can't—it's that I need you covering your own base
Not a capability question, a role question
cards.pmNote: Bob 的棒球比喻：二壘手不會去補一壘；每個人守好自己的位置，整個場才守得住。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.pattern: Let me back up and just dissect a little bit the way you described [X]—you described it in [某種] terms.
cards.quote: Let me back up and just dissect a little bit the way you described design, you described it in really tactical terms.
cards.zh: 先讓我退一步，拆解一下你剛剛描述設計的方式——你講的是很戰術層次的東西。
cards.why: 回答之前先動手拆對方的用詞，等於重新定義整場對話的地基。Let me back up 是英語會議裡最有用的一句話：它買到時間、拿回主導權，而且聽起來像謹慎不像抗拒。
swaps: Can I back up for a second and unpack how you framed that?
Before I answer, let me pull apart the way you're defining it
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.pattern: Look for places where the team keeps having the same debate over and over, and have it once, get it done, and put it behind you.
cards.quote: So I'd say practically just try to look for places where it seems the team's having the same debate over and over and have it once, get it done, and put it behind you.
cards.zh: 很實際的做法是：找出團隊一再重複爭論的那幾件事，把那場辯論一次辯完、定案、然後永遠翻過去。
cards.why: 三個祈使短句連發（have it once / get it done / put it behind you），節奏本身就是說服力。這是英語裡把「制度化」講得有畫面的標準做法：不是 let's document it，而是把它「放到身後」。
swaps: Let's settle this once so we never have to relitigate it
We keep relitigating this—can we decide it for good today?
cards.pmNote: 重複出現的辯論＝缺一條 tenet；Bob 說 tenet 是決策工具，principle 只是標語。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.pattern: It's not about me, it's about the idea. And don't be afraid to stand behind [那個想法].
cards.quote: It's not about you, it's about the idea. And don't be afraid to stand behind the idea.
cards.zh: 重點不是你，是那個想法。而且不要怕站在那個想法後面。
cards.why: 專治華人的「自我推銷罪惡感」：把發聲的主體從自己轉到 idea 上，你就不是在自誇，而是在替一個想法出頭。這一句在 LinkedIn 貼文、公開簡報、爭取資源時都能當開場的心理許可。
swaps: I'm not promoting myself, I'm advocating for this idea
Put the idea forward, not yourself
cards.pmNote: Bob 引 NASA 的 John Hobolt：好想法需要有人賭上職涯去當 champion，否則會躺在那裡幾十年。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.pattern: What I'm usually looking for is do they have a story as to why [他們相信某件事]?
cards.quote: What I'm usually looking for is do they have a story as to why they believe in design?
cards.zh: 我通常在找的是：他們講不講得出一個故事，說明自己為什麼相信設計？
cards.why: 把抽象的評估標準壓成一個可驗證的動作：不是問「你重不重視設計」，而是看對方有沒有「故事」。另外注意 What I'm looking for is do they…——口語裡嵌入問句不做倒裝，是母語者的自然講法，台灣人常錯寫成 whether they have。
swaps: What I want to hear is whether they can tell me a story about why
The test for me is: is there a story behind the belief?
cards.pmNote: 面試公司時問「你們為什麼相信設計」，答不出故事的公司多半是事後才把設計嫁接上去。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.pattern: I want to make sure I've got air cover from [最高層], because [沒有的話會怎樣].
cards.quote: I want to make sure I've got air cover from the highest people in the company setting the culture.
cards.zh: 我要確定最高層那些定文化的人會幫我掩護。
cards.why: air cover（空中掩護）是英語職場核心行話：不是要預算、要人，而是要「上面挺你」這種看不見的資源。台灣人談判時常只敢要具體資源，忘了政治掩護本身就能開口要。
swaps: I need top-level cover on this one
I want to know leadership will back this when it gets hard
cards.pmNote: 接高風險專案前先確認 air cover 來源，比談 headcount 更決定成敗。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.pattern: I came in thinking I was supposed to [做法], which is [那個做法的特徵].
cards.quote: I came in thinking I was supposed to behave the way I behaved at Apple, which is very direct, fighting hard.
cards.zh: 我進去的時候以為我該照在 Apple 的那一套來——非常直接、硬碰硬地爭。
cards.why: I came in thinking… 把錯誤定位成「當時的認知」，而不是「我這個人有問題」。承認失誤而不自我否定，是英語裡談失敗經驗最安全的框架，面試講 failure 時直接可用。
swaps: I walked in assuming the same rules applied, and they didn't
My mistake was importing the old playbook wholesale
cards.pmNote: 換公司時要帶走的是價值觀，不是行為模式——同一種強度在 A 公司叫投入，在 B 公司叫攻擊性。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.pattern: I agree—[重述對方的顧慮] sounds like a high bar, and in some ways it is. [然後轉折].
cards.quote: I agree, look, having your soul at every little checkbox sounds like a high bar and in some ways it is.
cards.zh: 我同意，聽著，要求每一個小勾選框都灌注靈魂，聽起來標準很高，某種程度上也確實是。
cards.why: 先說 I agree，再把對方的話原封不動重述一次，最後承認 in some ways it is——三層讓步之後才轉折，對方已經沒有防衛的理由。台灣人反駁常跳過重述，對方會覺得沒被聽懂。
swaps: Fair—that does sound like a lot, and in some ways it is
You're right that it's a high bar. Here's why I'd still hold it
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

cards.quote: We are about to launch something and then for example I or someone else goes to look at it and sees, "Oh, this doesn't feel right and we should fix it so I don't think we should launch this now."
cards.zh: 我們正要上線，然後我或別人去看了一眼，就會說：「這感覺不對，應該修一下，我覺得現在還不能上。」
cards.why: 喊卡的三段式：感覺判斷（doesn't feel right）→ 行動（we should fix it）→ 結論（I don't think we should launch）。關鍵在把主觀感受先講出來當理由，而不是硬找數據——在品質議題上，這反而更有說服力。
swaps: Something's off here—I'd rather hold the release
This isn't ready. Let's fix it before it goes out
cards.pmNote: Linear 沒有 A/B test 也不設功能指標，上不上線靠團隊試用後的直覺判斷。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

cards.quote: In those stages, the experience can be a little janky or it's not that polished, but we're okay with it because we are saying, "It's not finished. We just want to get your feedback early so we can make it better."
cards.zh: 那個階段體驗可能有點卡、不太精緻，但我們可以接受，因為我們有先講清楚：「這還沒完成，我們只是想早點拿到你的回饋，好把它做得更好。」
cards.why: janky 是矽谷高頻口語（能動但粗糙），台灣人幾乎不會用。整句的語用價值在「先降期待、再要回饋」——把未完成品講成刻意的邀請，客戶的不滿就變成參與感。
swaps: Heads up, it's rough around the edges—that's on purpose
This is an early cut; we want your reaction before we polish it
cards.pmNote: beta 邀請信的標準框架：先聲明未完成、再說明為什麼現在給你看、最後只要一件事（回饋）。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

cards.pattern: People think [X] is about [Y]. The downside with that mindset is that [代價].
cards.quote: I think sometimes people think that craft is about perfecting things and perfecting them in a very organized way or very early on. The downside with this perfection mindset is that it can be sometimes hard to put anything out because nothing is ever fully perfect.
cards.zh: 大家常以為所謂「工藝」就是把東西做到完美，而且要很有條理、很早就開始做。這種完美心態的代價是：你可能什麼都出不了貨，因為沒有東西是真正完美的。
cards.why: 不否定對方的價值觀，只指出它的副作用。The downside with this mindset is… 讓你可以反對一個「政治正確」的信念（追求品質）而不被貼上「不重視品質」的標籤。
swaps: The failure mode of that mindset is...
I get why people believe that. The cost is...
cards.pmNote: Linear 的做法是又快又修：第一週就把粗版推到 production，只給內部看。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

cards.pattern: There's definitely a trade-off. [對方的做法] is more efficient—[但我們選另一邊的理由].
cards.quote: There's definitely a trade-off. I think sometimes when companies specialize roles a lot it's because it's more efficient.
cards.zh: 這確實有取捨。公司把角色切得很細，通常是因為那樣比較有效率。
cards.why: 先承認 trade-off 存在，再主動把對手選項的優點講清楚。這是談優先順序時的信任開關：你證明自己知道放棄了什麼，接下來的選擇才會被當成判斷而不是偏好。
swaps: There's a real trade-off here, and I want to name it
The other approach is genuinely more efficient—we're choosing something else
cards.pmNote: 角色切太細會讓每個人只執行不思考；Linear 刻意讓工程師與設計師承擔部分 PM 職責。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

cards.pattern: This is the scope of it for now and we're okay launching this. But we know that this is not the fully figured out version.
cards.quote: So I think a lot of times we just think, okay, this is the scope of it for now and we are okay launching this and the execution is good. But we know that this is not the fully figured out version.
cards.zh: 很多時候我們就是這樣想：現階段範圍就到這裡，執行品質夠好，可以上。但我們知道這還不是完整想通的版本。
cards.why: 把「已完成」和「已想通」拆開來各自宣告，是資深 PM 的招牌動作。for now 與 not the fully figured out version 一前一後，讓上線這件事不必等於承諾終局，也堵住了「所以這樣就好了嗎」的追問。
swaps: This is v1 scope; we're deliberately not solving the rest yet
Good enough to ship, not the end state
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

cards.pattern: People use [X] too much because they're afraid: will I make the wrong choice? They're using [X] to make the choice for them.
cards.quote: I think sometimes people use data a lot or too much because they're worrying or they're afraid that, will I make the wrong choice? And I'm using data to make the choice for me.
cards.zh: 我覺得有時候大家用數據用得太兇，是因為他們在怕：萬一我選錯了怎麼辦？於是就讓數據替他們做決定。
cards.why: 把對方的行為重新歸因到情緒（fear）而不是理性，是拆假設最有效的一刀。注意他沒說「數據沒用」，只說「你在用它逃避決定」——攻擊動機而不是攻擊工具，對方很難反駁。
swaps: I wonder if we're reaching for data because we don't want to own the call
Are we measuring this, or are we hiding behind the measurement?
cards.pmNote: Karri：「至少那個決定是我們做的，不是數據幫我們做的。」錯了可以改，但決策權要留在人手上。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

cards.quote: And then we're like, "Well, does it help the customers? Does it help the product?" This sounds like a side quest to me, and basically means we shouldn't do it.
cards.zh: 然後我們就會問：「這對客戶有幫助嗎？對產品有幫助嗎？」這聽起來像支線任務，那基本上就是不該做。
cards.why: 用一個電玩比喻（主線 vs 支線）建立團隊共用的擋需求語彙——一旦大家接受這個詞，拒絕就不再是人跟人的衝突，而是分類問題。This sounds like X to me 也把判斷降級成個人觀感，留了台階。
swaps: Feels like a side quest—fun, but not the main line
Is this on the critical path, or is it a nice-to-have?
cards.pmNote: 在團隊裡建立一個共用的拒絕詞彙（side quest / main quest），比每次重新辯論省 90% 的力氣。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

cards.quote: Or I always have this question, is this important to do now or is it important to maybe do later?
cards.zh: 我一直用的一個問題是：這件事是「現在」重要，還是「以後」才重要？
cards.why: 把 yes/no 的爭論偷換成 now/later 的爭論。對方要的東西你沒有否定它的價值，只重新談時間——這是英語擋需求最不傷感情的一招，也讓你保留了之後真的要做的餘地。
swaps: Not whether, but when
Is this a now problem or a later problem?
cards.pmNote: 把優先順序爭議從價值判斷轉成時序判斷，對方比較不會覺得自己的需求被否定。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

cards.pattern: We know that eventually we need [X], but we don't need it today. So we just say no to that.
cards.quote: And we know that eventually we need to get it, but we don't need it today. So we just say no to that.
cards.zh: 我們知道遲早得弄那個，但今天不需要。所以我們就直接說不。
cards.why: 先承認需求的正當性（eventually we need it），再用時間切割拒絕當下。第三句刻意講得極短乾脆——前面鋪墊夠了，拒絕就不必再解釋。長篇解釋反而會讓對方覺得有討價空間。
swaps: We'll need it one day, just not this quarter
Yes eventually, no now
cards.pmNote: Linear 早期直接跟客戶說「我們還沒有 SOC 2，之後會有」，多數客戶回答 that's fine。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

cards.pattern: Why was this decision made? Why do you think it was made? Do you think it was the right decision, or did you agree with it?
cards.quote: It's like why was this decision made? Why do you think the decision was made? And I might ask, "Do you think it was the right decision or did you agree on it?"
cards.zh: 像是：這個決定為什麼會做？你覺得為什麼會這樣決定？然後我可能會問：你覺得那是對的決定嗎？你當時同意嗎？
cards.why: 三連問一路往內收：事實 → 對方的推測 → 對方的立場。最後一問把人逼到必須表態，但因為前面兩問已經暖過場，感覺是好奇不是逼問。面試與 1:1 通用。
swaps: What was the thinking behind that? Would you have done it differently?
Why do you think they went that way—and did you buy it?
cards.pmNote: Linear 用這組問題測「產品感」：有沒有觀點、能不能講出理由，比技能本身重要。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

cards.pattern: Go slow to go fast. Urgency is important, but too much urgency means [代價].
cards.quote: Go slow to go fast. I think urgency is important, but then sometimes you have too much urgency and you are rushing things.
cards.zh: 先慢才會快。急迫感很重要，但有時候急過頭，你就開始趕，結果反而要回頭重修。
cards.why: 四個字的矛盾句當標題，後面立刻補一句承認對立面的價值（urgency is important）。英語職場很吃這種「口號 + 立刻自我平衡」的結構：口號負責被記住，平衡句負責不被當成偏執。
swaps: Slow is smooth, smooth is fast
Measure twice, cut once
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

cards.pattern: What I'm hearing is basically [你的理解]. Is that right?
cards.quote: What I'm hearing is basically you give those responsibilities to the engineers, designer, and maybe other functions within the team. Is that right?
cards.zh: 我聽到的意思基本上是：你們把那些責任分給工程師、設計師，可能還有團隊裡其他角色。我理解對嗎？
cards.why: 英文會議裡沒聽懂卻不想顯得跟不上，這句是最安全的解法：你不是在問「你剛剛說什麼」，而是在展示你的理解版本。basically 讓你的複述不必精準，Is that right? 把驗證的責任交回對方。
swaps: So if I'm following, you're saying X—is that fair?
Let me play that back: X. Did I get that right?
cards.pmNote: 會議中每 10 分鐘做一次 playback，是最便宜的對齊機制。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

cards.pattern: So just to summarize so far, you have no [A], you have no [B], you have essentially no [C].
cards.quote: So just to summarize so far, you have no metrics, you have no experiments, you have essentially no PMs, just one product leader.
cards.zh: 所以先總結一下：你們沒有指標、沒有實驗、基本上也沒有 PM，只有一個產品負責人。
cards.why: 三個平行的 you have no… 排比，把一堆零散資訊壓成一個有衝擊力的畫面。essentially 是關鍵保險絲——第三項並非完全成立，用一個副詞就避免了被更正。
swaps: So to recap where we are: no A, no B, essentially no C
Let me pull the threads together—here's what I'm taking away
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

cards.pattern: That was a tangent, but I want to come back to [原本的主題].
cards.quote: Awesome, that was a tangent because I could not go in that direction, but I want to come back to design again and craft.
cards.zh: 很棒，剛剛那段是離題——我實在忍不住問——但我想拉回設計跟工藝這條線。
cards.why: 主動把自己剛剛的離題命名為 tangent，等於向全場宣告「我知道我們跑掉了，現在收回來」。控場的權力來自命名：你講出偏離，就重新拿回議程。
swaps: Sorry, that was a bit of a detour—back to the main thread
Parking that one. Where we were is...
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

cards.pattern: A lot of people see [X] as [簡化的看法]. What you're describing is more of [更細緻的看法].
cards.quote: A lot of people see product market fit as this binary, "I have it or I don't." What you're describing is what I often hear, it's more of this spectrum of more and more confidence.
cards.zh: 很多人把 PMF 看成二元的：不是有就是沒有。而你在描述的，是我常聽到的另一種——它比較像一條逐漸累積信心的光譜。
cards.why: 把對方沒說清楚的話升級成一個對比架構（binary vs spectrum），再掛回對方名下。這是會議裡最高價值的貢獻：你沒有新資訊，但你讓對方的模糊直覺變成一個團隊可以引用的概念。
swaps: Most people treat this as either/or; you're framing it as a spectrum
So it's less a yes/no and more a matter of degree
cards.pmNote: PMF 要按分眾談：對早期新創有、對 Fortune 500 沒有，是完全正常的狀態。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

cards.quote: It's actually not. It's not. So many people are used to it and they think that it's just how it is, but it's actually not.
cards.zh: 其實不是。真的不是。太多人習慣了，就以為事情本來就是這樣——但其實不是。
cards.why: 重複三次 it's actually not，中間夾一句解釋為什麼大家會誤會（they're used to it）。英語裡拆「這是常態」型假設的標準節奏：先否定、給同理、再否定一次。重複本身就是強調手段，台灣人常改用更長的句子，反而弱。
swaps: Everyone assumes that's just how it works. It isn't
That feels like a law of nature. It's actually a choice someone made
cards.pmNote: 系統之間的依賴多半是可以拆的；好的工程領導的價值就是讓一塊系統能獨立被改。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: I'll quote [某人]: "[一句畫面感強的俗諺]"
cards.quote: So, I think I'll quote Bob Moesta, who's been on your show a couple times, "You can't put 10 pounds of crap in a five pound bag."
cards.zh: 我引 Bob Moesta 一句話：「你沒辦法把十磅的東西塞進五磅的袋子。」
cards.why: 借別人的嘴講難聽話，是英語職場的標準避雷做法：話的粗俗歸原作者，判斷歸你。畫面感越強的俗諺越好用——它會被會議室其他人重複引用，你的立場就自動擴散了。
swaps: As someone once put it, you can't fit a quart into a pint pot
There's a saying I like here:
cards.pmNote: 把巨大專案丟給團隊說「六週內自己砍 scope」不是授權，是推責。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: This is a tricky one. So, you're right that [對方說對的部分], but the thing is, in real life, [現實].
cards.quote: This is a tricky one. So, you're right that it's implied, but the thing is, in real life, if you make a commitment and you get alignment that we are going to spend six weeks of engineering time building this thing…
cards.zh: 這題很麻煩。你說得沒錯，那個確實是言下之意，但問題是，現實裡如果你已經做出承諾、也拿到共識要花六週工程時間……
cards.why: 三層緩衝之後才反對：先標記難度（This is a tricky one）、再確認對方哪裡對（you're right that）、最後用 but the thing is, in real life 把戰場從理論拉到現場。台灣人想反駁權威時，這是最完整的安全句型。
swaps: That's the theory, and it's right—in practice it breaks down because...
Yes and no. On paper that's true; in real life...
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: We can't just cut [已承諾的核心] and say we shipped on time. That's going to kill everybody's morale.
cards.quote: We can't just cut the scope and say, "Oh, well now, we managed to ship inside of six weeks." That's going to kill everybody's morale.
cards.zh: 我們不能就這樣砍掉範圍，然後說「你看，我們六週內出貨了」。那會把所有人的士氣打死。
cards.why: 反對一個「表面上達標」的解法時，最有力的理由不是邏輯而是後果，而且是人的後果。kill everybody's morale 是英語裡少數可以在會議上直接拿來當否決理由的情緒詞。
swaps: Shipping on time by gutting it isn't a win
That's a technically-on-time, actually-demoralising outcome
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: You probably know what happens when [產物] makes first contact with [另一個團隊]. There's a reality check that happens there.
cards.quote: So you probably know about what happens when the Figma file makes first contact with the engineering team. There's a reality check that happens there and very often, there's a back to the drawing board.
cards.zh: 你大概知道 Figma 檔第一次「接觸」到工程團隊時會發生什麼事。那裡會有一次現實檢驗，而且常常整個打掉重來。
cards.why: makes first contact 借自軍事／科幻，把交付講成一次會出事的遭遇戰。前面加 you probably know，讓聽者站在「我們都懂」的同一邊——描述共同痛點時，先建立同盟再描述傷口。
swaps: You know what happens when the design finally hits engineering
That's where it collides with reality
cards.pmNote: back to the drawing board（打掉重來）是英語職場高頻片語，值得整組背下來。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: I often use this analogy: [日常場景]. You can have [表面完美的東西], but if you haven't checked [底層的隱藏條件], it's going to drastically change the cost.
cards.quote: I often use this analogy of if you're doing a home renovation, you can have the most beautiful rendering of the new bedroom. But if you haven't checked if there's electricity in that wall there or not, it's going to drastically change the cost and the time and everything.
cards.zh: 我常用一個比喻：你在裝修房子，臥室的效果圖可以做得美到不行。但如果你沒去確認那面牆裡到底有沒有電線，成本跟時間都會整個變樣。
cards.why: I often use this analogy of… 直接宣告接下來是比喻，聽者立刻切換到「聽故事」模式。比喻本身選了一個對方一定有經驗的場景（裝修），而且精準對應到技術債：漂亮的表面 vs 牆裡看不見的東西。
swaps: The analogy I keep coming back to is...
Think of it like renovating a house you haven't opened the walls on
cards.pmNote: shaping 的核心就是「先開牆看管線」——在承諾時間之前把未知拆出來。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: It's not [大而模糊的名詞]. It's [具體到可執行的描述].
cards.quote: So, what you can see here is it's not like, what is a calendar? It's not a calendar. It's a two-month dot grid with scrolling agenda view underneath.
cards.zh: 所以你看，重點不是「什麼叫行事曆」。它不是一個行事曆，它是「兩個月的圓點格線，下面搭一個可捲動的議程檢視」。
cards.why: 先否定那個大詞，再用一句精準到可以動手的描述取代它。這一招同時完成兩件事：擋掉無限膨脹的期待，並讓工程師當場知道要蓋什麼。名詞越大越危險，是英語產品討論的共識。
swaps: We're not building "search"—we're building X, Y and Z
Let's stop saying dashboard and say what it actually is
cards.pmNote: 專案名稱如果是一個名詞（calendar / dashboard），就代表還沒 framing 完。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: I've got to tell you, the dominant failure case that I see in the real world is always, again and again, [根因].
cards.quote: I got to tell you, the dominant failure case that I see in the real world is always, again and again, not enough detail.
cards.zh: 我得說，我在現實世界裡看到的主要失敗模式，一次又一次都是同一件事：細節給得不夠。
cards.why: I got to tell you 是「我要講一句你可能不愛聽的話」的訊號。in the real world 與 again and again 把個人意見升級成觀察樣本——沒有數字，卻建立了經驗權威。
swaps: Honestly, the most common failure mode I see is...
Nine times out of ten, the root cause is the same thing
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: I can understand why the hair stands up on the back of your neck thinking about that.
cards.quote: But I can understand why the hair stands up on the back of the neck a little bit thinking about it because, of course, if you give a senior engineer like, "Here's how I want you to go implement the schema"…
cards.zh: 但我理解為什麼你一想到這個就會汗毛豎起來——畢竟你如果去跟資深工程師說「這個 schema 我要你這樣實作」……
cards.why: 先替對方把還沒說出口的生理反應講出來。用身體感覺（hair stands up）而不是抽象的 concern，對方會覺得「他真的懂我在怕什麼」，接下來的反駁就進得去。
swaps: I get why that makes people bristle
I know that sets off alarm bells—let me explain
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: It's not a universal thing. [X] is a dial that we can turn, and it depends on [變數].
cards.quote: But what's really interesting is it's not a universal thing. The amount of detail that the team is going to feel helps them is a dial that we can turn that depends on who's on the team.
cards.zh: 但有趣的是，這件事沒有通則。要給多少細節其實是一個可以轉的旋鈕，看團隊裡是誰。
cards.why: a dial we can turn 把 A/B 二選一的爭論轉成連續刻度，爭論立刻消失——大家不再爭立場，而是一起找刻度。這是英語裡化解「該多還是該少」型爭執最漂亮的一個比喻。
swaps: It's a dial, not a switch
There's no universal answer—it slides depending on the team
cards.pmNote: 資淺工程師需要更多細節才敢動手，資深的則相反；細節量該按人調，不是按流程調。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: It's not like now we're screwed. Now we can have a really cool conversation about trade-offs.
cards.quote: And now, it's not like, "Okay, now, we're screwed and the project is going to be bigger." Now, we can have a really cool conversation about trade-offs.
cards.zh: 所以現在不是「完了，這專案要爆了」。現在我們可以來一場很棒的取捨對話。
cards.why: 壞消息出現時把它重新標籤成機會。先把大家腦中最糟的解讀原句念出來（now we're screwed），再直接否定並替換——因為對方那句話已經被說出口，反駁才有著力點。
swaps: This isn't a disaster—it's the conversation we needed to have
Good news: we found it now, not in week four
cards.pmNote: 早期發現複雜度是好事；同一個發現出現在 build 第四週就是災難。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: By the way, I'm being very mean to [X] so far in this conversation. There is a time when it's the right time for [X].
cards.quote: By the way, I'm being very mean to Figma so far in this conversation. There is a time when it's the right time for the Figma file.
cards.zh: 順帶一提，我到目前為止對 Figma 有點太兇了。Figma 檔是有它對的時機的。
cards.why: 自己承認立場偏頗，等於預先拆掉對方「你就是討厭 X」的反擊。being mean to 是很輕鬆的自嘲用詞，把一場可能變成派系之爭的討論拉回技術層面。
swaps: I've been unfair to X here—it does have its place
To be clear, I'm not anti-X; I'm anti-X-too-early
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: It's [完成的定義] if we can give this to [某人] and they say, "Yeah, I know what to go do now."
cards.quote: So maybe this is a way to come back to your question about what's the output of the shaping session, it's like it's shaped if we can give this to a technical person and they say, "Yeah, I know what to go build now."
cards.zh: 所以回到你剛剛問的「shaping session 的產出是什麼」：判準是——把它交給一個技術的人，他會說「好，我知道要蓋什麼了」。
cards.why: 先明講「這是在回你剛剛的問題」（長篇回答後的必要收線），再用一句對方會講的台詞當驗收標準。把抽象的完成定義換成一個可觀察的行為，是英語裡定義 done 的最佳實務。
swaps: The test is whether the builder says "I know what to do now"
Coming back to your question—here's the acceptance criterion
cards.pmNote: 定義 done 時用「誰會說出什麼話」，比用文件清單更難鑽漏洞。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: I would say wait until it hurts more. If [不熟悉] is the big problem, then maybe things are fine.
cards.quote: I would say wait until it hurts more. If the unfamiliarity is the big problem with it, then maybe the things are fine.
cards.zh: 我會說：等到更痛再來。如果你最大的問題只是「不熟悉」，那可能表示現在其實還好。
cards.why: 把自己的方法論往外推。勸人不要買你在賣的東西，是最強的可信度動作；語言上的關鍵是給出一個判準（痛感 vs 陌生感），讓拒絕聽起來像診斷而不是謙虛。
swaps: Honestly, don't change until the pain is real
If it's just unfamiliar rather than painful, leave it alone
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.quote: Of course, I don't want to be cruel to the people who are putting their hearts into that work, because the Figma file is beautiful. It's just coming a little early.
cards.zh: 當然，我不想對那些真心投入的人太苛刻——那些 Figma 檔真的很漂亮。只是它來得太早了一點。
cards.why: 把批評從「品質不好」改成「時機不對」，是保住對方尊嚴的最短路徑。三段結構：宣告不想傷人 → 具體稱讚 → 用一句極輕的話點出問題（just / a little 兩個減壓詞疊用）。
swaps: The work is good—it's just landing at the wrong point in the process
Nothing wrong with it. It's premature, not bad
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.quote: You write this document and I'm sorry, who actually reads it? You know what I mean? I know it's painful, but it's like that.
cards.zh: 你寫了那份文件——不好意思，但到底有誰真的會讀？你懂我意思吧？我知道這很刺耳，但事實就是這樣。
cards.why: I'm sorry 插在句中，不是道歉而是「我要說實話了」的減震器。結尾 I know it's painful, but it's like that 承認對方會不舒服卻不收回主張——承認情緒、不撤回內容，是英語說重話的標準收尾。
swaps: Sorry to be blunt, but does anyone actually read these?
I know that stings, but that's the reality
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: Well, I understand what the [某某] critique is supposed to be. The thing is, [你的反轉].
cards.quote: Yeah. Well, I understand what the feature factory critique is supposed to be.
cards.zh: 嗯，我理解「功能工廠」這個批評原本想講的是什麼。
cards.why: is supposed to be 這三個字很毒：它同時表示「我懂這個說法的原意」和「但它沒有真的成立」。想質疑一個流行術語又不想顯得沒讀書時，這是最省力的開場。
swaps: I know what that critique is meant to capture
I take the point behind the term, but
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: Imagine: [極端的對照場景]. No such thing as [你們每天在忍的事]. Never.
cards.quote: Yeah. Imagine, no such thing as a request from sales, yeah? No such thing as pressure of like, "We need this thing in order to upsell or to close this deal." Never.
cards.zh: 你想像一下：完全沒有業務來提需求，好嗎？也完全沒有那種「我們需要這個功能才能升級方案、才能成交」的壓力。從來沒有。
cards.why: 用 Imagine 開頭把聽者拉進一個他沒經歷過的世界，再用 No such thing as… 連續否定他每天在忍的事，最後單字成句的 Never 收尾。解釋「為什麼別人的做法在你這裡行不通」時，這比列差異清單有效太多。
swaps: Picture a world where nobody's asking you for a deal-blocker feature
Now imagine none of that pressure exists. That was their setup
cards.pmNote: 抄別人的流程前先看他們的前提：Basecamp 沒有業務團隊，所以工程時間從不被搶。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: I've got to tell you, I had no idea how unique we were until I was outside.
cards.quote: I got to tell you, I had no idea how unique we were until I was outside and there are so many things.
cards.zh: 我得說，直到我離開之後，我才知道我們當時有多特殊——太多事情都是。
cards.why: 承認自己曾經把特例當通則，是寫過書、給過建議的人最需要的一句話。until I was outside 把認錯講成視角變化，而不是能力不足——既保住權威，又贏得信任。
swaps: I didn't realise how unusual our setup was until I left
I was taking a lot of things for granted that turned out to be rare
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

cards.pattern: To set the answer up, I'll give you a super brief history of [背景].
cards.quote: To set the answer up, I'll give you a super brief history of Make Time.
cards.zh: 為了鋪陳我的答案，我先講一段 Make Time 的超簡短來歷。
cards.why: 先宣告「我要繞路，但這是為了回答你」。台灣人在英文會議裡最怕的就是講一長串背景卻讓人以為離題；一句 to set the answer up 就買到了一段合法的鋪陳時間，super brief 又預告了長度。
swaps: Quick bit of context before I answer
Let me set that up with 30 seconds of background
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.pattern: The problem is not [大家以為的問題]. They usually know that. The problem is [真正的問題].
cards.quote: The problem is not like what should my goal be or how should I figure out what to do with my life? They usually know, but it's very hard to actually make time for those things.
cards.zh: 問題不在於「我的目標該是什麼」或「我這輩子要幹嘛」。這個大家其實都知道。問題是很難真的挪出時間去做那些事。
cards.why: 定義問題的標準動作：先否定一個大家預設的問題，再指出真正的痛點。中間插一句 they usually know 是關鍵——它證明你調查過，不是在憑空重新定義。
swaps: It's not a clarity problem, it's an allocation problem
People know what matters. What they can't do is protect the time for it
cards.pmNote: problem statement 寫壞的第一名死法：解決一個大家早就解決了的問題。
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.pattern: And I don't mean to sound like I'm above it all and have figured it all out. It still [你也還在犯的事].
cards.quote: And I don't mean to sound like I'm above it all and have figured it all out. It still drives my stress
cards.zh: 我不是想擺出一副「我早就超脫了、全都想通了」的樣子。那件事到現在還是讓我很焦慮。
cards.why: 教別人做某件事時最容易失去的就是可信度。這句先否認自己站在制高點，再承認自己仍受同樣困擾——聽眾從「被說教」切換成「同一條船」。給建議、做內部分享、寫文件開頭都能用。
swaps: I'm not saying I've cracked this—I still fall into it
Not preaching from the mountain here; I struggle with it too
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.pattern: At the top of the interview you asked, "[原問題]" And I'll frame my answer in those terms.
cards.quote: At the top of the interview, Lenny, you asked, "What do most people get wrong when they think about this productivity, time management, whatever?" And I'll frame my answer in those terms.
cards.zh: Lenny，你一開始問過：「大家在生產力、時間管理這些事情上最常搞錯什麼？」我就用那個框架來回答。
cards.why: 回頭引用對方半小時前的問題，等於證明你一直在聽，也讓長回答有了正當理由。I'll frame my answer in those terms 更是控場：接下來用「我的框架」講，但功勞掛在對方問題上。
swaps: Going back to what you asked at the start—let me answer it in those terms
You asked earlier about X; I'll use that frame
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.pattern: At any given point in time, I probably give myself a [等第], and sometimes it's a [更低的], and sometimes it's an A.
cards.quote: So at any given point in time, I probably give myself a B to B-, and sometimes it's a C and sometimes it's a D, and sometimes it's an A, and I'm really plugging away, but it's totally an ongoing challenge.
cards.zh: 任何時間點上，我大概給自己 B 到 B-，有時候 C、有時候 D，偶爾也有 A，我真的一直在努力，但這就是個持續的挑戰。
cards.why: 用學校成績當自評尺度，讓誠實變得輕鬆且具體。給一個區間而不是單點（B to B-），再列出高低兩端，聽起來是誠實而不是自貶。績效面談被問「你覺得自己做得如何」時很好用。
swaps: On a good week it's a B; on a bad week, honestly a D
I'd give myself a solid B-minus and I'm still working at it
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.pattern: And one core idea I don't think we've mentioned yet is that [你的重點].
cards.quote: And one core idea I don't think we've mentioned yet is that we strongly believe in people's intuition about how they should spend their time if they have the chance.
cards.zh: 還有一個核心想法我覺得我們還沒提到：我們非常相信一個人只要有機會，他自己知道時間該花在哪。
cards.why: 母語者講不停時要切進去，最安全的入口不是「我可以說一下嗎」，而是宣稱有一個「還沒被提到」的東西。I don't think we've mentioned yet 把插話轉成補漏，沒有人會拒絕補漏。
swaps: One thing we haven't touched on yet is...
Can I add one piece that hasn't come up?
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.pattern: [A] could be like [情境A]. [B] could be like [情境B]. They're in the same family, but they're cousins.
cards.quote: Satisfaction could be like, "I know this thing has to get done, and I got it done." Joy could be like, "Man, that was great." And they're in the same family, but they're cousins.
cards.zh: 「滿足」比較像：我知道這件事非做不可，而我做完了。「喜悅」比較像：哇，那真的太棒了。它們算同一家族，但只是表親。
cards.why: 分辨近義詞的最佳範本：不查字典，而是各給一句情境台詞，再用一個親屬比喻定位距離（same family, but cousins）。要向老外解釋兩個中文近義詞、或聽懂他們在細分什麼時，這句可以直接搬。
swaps: They're related, but they're not the same thing
Same neighbourhood, different houses
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.quote: Well, thank you for sharing the real talk. I think you made the right choice.
cards.zh: 謝謝你講了實話。我覺得你那個選擇是對的。
cards.why: real talk 是英語裡對「坦白講不好聽／不好意思的事」的專門讚美，比 thank you for sharing 精準得多。有人在會議上自曝失敗時，這一句能確保下次還有人願意講真話。
swaps: Appreciate the honesty—that's not easy to say out loud
Thanks for the candour
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.pattern: There's great research on this, but for now just trust me: [你的主張].
cards.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
cards.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。
cards.why: 手上沒有引用來源、又不想顯得心虛時的標準做法：宣告證據存在、承認現在不展開、請對方暫時信任。for now 是關鍵——它把「不提供證據」框成時間安排，而不是心虛。white-knuckle（握到指節發白地硬撐）也是很值得學的動詞。
swaps: There's solid research behind this—happy to send it after
I'll spare you the citations for now, but the evidence is there
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.pattern: And that's totally fine, because you're being deliberate about it, rather than [僵化的做法].
cards.quote: And then there'll be some other thing that happens that causes you to reinstall it, and that's totally fine, because you're being deliberate about it and you're paying attention.
cards.zh: 然後某天會發生某件事讓你又把它裝回來——那完全沒問題，因為你是刻意這樣做的，你有在注意。
cards.why: 帶人時最有用的一句：先預告對方會退步，再預先赦免。that's totally fine, because… 把判準從「有沒有做到」換成「有沒有意識」，讓對方不會因為一次失敗就整套放棄。
swaps: That's fine—as long as it's a decision and not a drift
Falling off is fine; noticing is the whole skill
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.pattern: So yeah, anyway, sorry, that's just a rant, but [收回重點].
cards.quote: So yeah, anyway, sorry, that's just a rant, but you should try it.
cards.zh: 總之，抱歉，剛剛那段只是我在碎念——但你真的該試試看。
cards.why: 自己講太久之後的標準煞車：把剛剛那段命名為 rant（一時激動的長篇），道歉，然後用一句話把重點壓回去。台灣人講太久常直接停住讓場面尷尬；這句能把失控轉成有意識的收尾。
swaps: Anyway—rant over. The point is X
Sorry, I got on a soapbox there. Short version:
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.pattern: Well, first a pairing, and then one more. The pairing is [A] and [B].
cards.quote: Well, first a pairing, and then one more. The pairing is reset expectations and slow your inbox.
cards.zh: 好，先講一組配套的，再講一個。配套的是：重設期待，還有讓你的收件匣慢下來。
cards.why: 開口前先報數量與結構，聽者就知道要等多久、怎麼記。first…and then one more 是最輕量的路標，比 firstly/secondly 自然，適合口語會議。
swaps: Two that go together, then a bonus one
I've got a pair here, plus one extra
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.pattern: Just saying "because" dramatically boosted [結果]. We're suckers for explanations, all of us.
cards.quote: And just saying because dramatically boosted the percentage of the time that a person would let them cut the line. We're suckers for explanations, all of us.
cards.zh: 光是講出「因為」，別人讓他插隊的比例就大幅上升。我們每個人都吃「解釋」這一套。
cards.why: 先給實驗結果，再用一句自嘲式通則收尾（把自己也算進去：all of us）。be a sucker for X（對 X 沒抵抗力）是高頻口語。實務含意也很重要：擋需求時記得補一個 because，理由本身合不合理反而次要。
swaps: People will accept almost anything with a "because" attached
We're all wired to accept a reason, even a weak one
cards.pmNote: 拒絕或延後需求時一律附理由；有 because 的拒絕接受度遠高於同樣內容的無理由拒絕。
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.pattern: It seems like it would be a big deal because [表面理由], and that is true. But the real power of it is [更深的理由].
cards.quote: And it seems like it would be a huge deal because it changes others expectations, and that is true. But the real power of it is in changing our own expectations about what we are going to do.
cards.zh: 看起來它之所以有用，是因為它改變了別人的期待——這也沒錯。但它真正的威力，在於改變我們自己對自己的期待。
cards.why: 先確認那個顯而易見的理由成立（and that is true），再說「但真正的力量在別的地方」。這個兩段式讓你不必否定任何人，就把討論拉到更深一層——說服資深聽眾時特別有效。
swaps: That's the obvious benefit, and it's real. The bigger one is...
Everyone sees the first-order effect; the second-order effect is where it pays
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.pattern: So to replay the system overall: [A] is about [X], [B] is about [Y].
cards.quote: So to replay the system overall highlight is about the thing you want to make time for today. The most important thing today, laser is about creating barriers to distraction.
cards.zh: 把整套系統再跑一遍：highlight 是你今天最想騰出時間做的那件事；laser 是替干擾設路障。
cards.why: replay 這個動詞比 summarize 更口語、也更精準——它暗示「照原樣再放一次」而不是加入你的詮釋。長會議尾聲重述架構時，用「一個詞 + is about + 一句話」的模組，聽者最容易記住。
swaps: Let me replay the whole thing quickly
To put the pieces back together: A does X, B does Y
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.pattern: For what it's worth, we're not really motivated to [對方以為你的動機]. We just hope it works for you.
cards.quote: For what it's worth, we're not really motivated to try to create a self-improvement empire. This is not our full-time job. We just hope it works for you and is useful.
cards.zh: 順帶一提，我們並不是想搞一個自我成長帝國。這不是我們的正職。我們只是希望這對你有用。
cards.why: For what it's worth 是英語裡「這句話你可以不採納」的最輕開場，用來降低推銷嫌疑剛好。主動否認自己的商業動機、並補一句「不想買書我們懂」，反而讓推薦更容易被接受。
swaps: For what it's worth, we're not trying to sell you anything here
If you don't want to buy the book, we get it
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.pattern: So I've used up basically all our time on [A]. What I think we do is [調整方案].
cards.quote: So I've used up basically all our time talking about Make Time. I think we should have a follow-up episode just to talk about Sprint. What I think we do is let's cut off the lightning round.
cards.zh: 我基本上把時間都花在 Make Time 上了。我覺得我們該再錄一集專門講 Sprint。現在我的想法是：閃電問答就先砍掉。
cards.why: 會議超時的完整處理三步：承認是自己造成的（I've used up）、給議題一個未來的家（follow-up）、當場提出砍哪一段。台灣人常只做第一步一直道歉，母語者的重點在第三步：立刻提出取捨方案。
swaps: We're out of time on this—here's what I suggest we drop
I've eaten the clock. Let's park X and take Y offline
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

cards.quote: Hey, here's what I'm seeing and tell me what's going on for you.
cards.zh: 我先講我這邊看到的狀況，然後換你講講你那邊發生了什麼事。
cards.why: 用 what I'm seeing 把「觀察」跟「評價」切開——不是你有問題，是我看到一個現象；後半句立刻把發言權交還對方，讓他不必先防衛。台灣人常一開口就是「你是不是哪裡沒做好」，對方馬上關門。
swaps: Here's what I'm noticing — what's your read on it?
Let me share what I'm observing, and then I want your side.
cards.pmNote: 難談的 1:1 一律用雙向開場：先講觀察，再問對方版本，通常會發現你們對「他的職責」根本認知不同。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.quote: I always start with, "Does this person actually know what you expect of them?" If not, go back to step one.
cards.zh: 我一定先問一句：這個人到底知不知道你對他的期待是什麼？如果不知道，那就回到第一步。
cards.why: 把「人的問題」硬轉成「期待有沒有講清楚」，等於幫對方保留面子的同時把責任拉回管理者身上。go back to step one 是英語職場很好用的收尾——不指責，直接指出下一步。
swaps: First question I ask is whether expectations were ever made explicit.
Before we call it a performance issue — has anyone actually told them what good looks like?
cards.pmNote: 80% 的「績效問題」其實是角色與成功定義沒講清楚，先修結構再檢討人。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.pattern: The rule is you snorkel before you scuba — [X]% of problems come from [結構層], not from the people.
cards.quote: The rule with the Waterline Model, which is very memorable, is you snorkel before you scuba. So, 80% of problems on teams actually happen because of structural issues or dynamics issues.
cards.zh: 這個模型的規則很好記：先浮潛，再深潛。團隊上八成的問題其實出在結構或運作方式，不是出在人。
cards.why: 一句口訣（snorkel before you scuba）把抽象的診斷順序變成畫面，開會時丟出來所有人立刻懂。母語者很愛用這種押韻／對比型 rule of thumb 來擋掉「先怪人」的直覺。
swaps: Let's check the shallow stuff before we go deep on personalities.
Start at the surface: goals, roles, expectations — then look at people.
cards.pmNote: 團隊卡住的排查順序：結構（目標／角色／期待）→ 運作（決策／衝突）→ 人際 → 個人。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.pattern: You feel like a broken record — "I've said this [45] times." Turns out no one heard you the first [43].
cards.quote: You feel like a broken record, right? You're like, "I've said this 45 times." Turns out no one heard you the first 43.
cards.zh: 你會覺得自己像跳針的唱片：「這件事我講過四十五次了。」結果是前四十三次根本沒人聽進去。
cards.why: 用「45 次 / 43 次」這種具體假數字製造幽默，把「重複講很煩」正常化成領導者的本分。broken record 是母語者抱怨自己重複時的固定說法，台灣人多半只會說 I said it many times。
swaps: I know I sound like a broken record, but let me say it one more time.
At the risk of repeating myself for the tenth time —
cards.pmNote: 策略與角色定義要一講再講；你覺得囉唆的那一刻，通常才剛開始被聽見。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.pattern: Strategy should hurt — if you're not making trade-offs that are painful, you're not actually helping people prioritize.
cards.quote: Strategy should hurt is a much better way to explain it to people which is, if you're not making trade-offs that are painful, you are not actually helping people prioritize their time.
cards.zh: 「策略應該要會痛」是更好的說法：如果你做的取捨一點都不痛，那你根本沒在幫大家決定時間該花在哪。
cards.why: 把抽象的「策略」綁到一個身體感受（hurt），一秒讓人判斷自己有沒有真的在做策略。if you're not... you are not actually... 是英語裡很兇但不針對人的反證句型。
swaps: If the roadmap didn't hurt to write, it isn't a roadmap.
A strategy that costs you nothing isn't a strategy.
cards.pmNote: 設目標時「不做什麼」要跟「要做什麼」一樣明確，否則團隊會自己幫你排優先順序。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.pattern: Two people owning [X] is no one owning [X]. One person owns it — who is it?
cards.quote: Two people owning a goal is no one owning a goal. One person owns the goal, who is it?
cards.zh: 兩個人一起扛一個目標，等於沒人在扛。這個目標只能有一個人負責——是誰？
cards.why: 先用「A=B」的悖論句把模糊狀態講死，再用一個五個字的問句逼出名字。會議收尾要定 owner 時，這比 "who wants to take this?" 有力十倍。
swaps: Shared ownership is no ownership. Whose name goes next to this?
Let's put one name on it — who's the DRI?
cards.pmNote: 一個目標一個 owner，而且不能是 CEO 自己；沒有名字的目標等於沒設。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.pattern: I have a bone to pick with [X]. It's obviously been really helpful for [A and B], but...
cards.quote: I definitely have a bone to pick with OKRs. I feel like it's obviously been a really helpful framework for Google and others.
cards.zh: 我對 OKR 是真的有意見。當然啦，它對 Google 那些公司顯然是很有用的框架——
cards.why: have a bone to pick with 是「我有帳要算」的口語說法，先亮出立場再馬上讓一步（obviously been really helpful），讓後面的批評聽起來像持平判斷而不是唱反調。
swaps: I've got some issues with how we use OKRs — useful framework, wrong application.
I'll push back on OKRs a bit, with all due respect to the framework.
cards.pmNote: 目標的本質是溝通工具；一百行的 OKR 試算表對誰都沒有製造清晰。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.pattern: Don't come to me for [X] — I'm not the person to ask about [Y].
cards.quote: I always say to people don't come to me for management 101, I'm not the person to ask on how to run the most effective one-on-one with your people.
cards.zh: 我常跟人講：管理入門的東西不要來問我，怎麼把一對一開得最有效率，我不是那個該問的人。
cards.why: 把「拒絕」講成「界定專業範圍」，完全不帶歉意也不失禮。台灣人拒絕時容易繞一大圈道歉，母語者直接說 I'm not the person to ask，反而顯得有自知之明。
swaps: That's outside my wheelhouse — you'd want to ask someone else.
I'm the wrong person for that one, but I can point you to who isn't.
cards.pmNote: 把自己的守備範圍講清楚，比什麼都接下來再做不好有用。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.pattern: Your job is not to have all the answers — it's to get good at finding them.
cards.quote: Your job as manager and a leader is not to have all the answers. It is not to have all the answers, it is to get good at finding them.
cards.zh: 你當主管、當領導者的工作不是要有全部的答案。真的不是——是要變得很會把答案找出來。
cards.why: 重複同一句（It is not to have all the answers）製造強調，是英語口說裡的 anaphora；再用 not X, it is Y 把職責重新定義。承認不知道的時候，這句可以先鋪路。
swaps: My job isn't to know — it's to make sure we find out fast.
Leadership isn't having answers, it's building the path to them.
cards.pmNote: 變動越快的公司，越是「會探索的人」贏，不是「已經知道的人」贏。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.pattern: There is literally no faster way to [demoralize X] than [Y].
cards.quote: There is literally no faster way to demoralize high performers than going back on a promise.
cards.zh: 要讓高績效的人瞬間心死，沒有比毀約更快的方法了。
cards.why: no faster way to X than Y 是英語裡最有力的警告句型之一，用最高級把後果講到底，卻不需要指名道姓。literally 在口語裡是強調詞，不是「字面上」。
swaps: Nothing kills trust faster than walking back a commitment.
The quickest way to lose your best people is to promise what you can't control.
cards.pmNote: 招人時不要承諾你控制不了的事（title、穩定、永遠不會有人壓在你上面）——那是寄給未來自己的炸彈。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.pattern: My mantra that almost always leads in the best direction is [A], not [B].
cards.quote: My mantra that almost always leads in the best direction is serve the business, not the people.
cards.zh: 我幾乎每次靠它都能做出對的決定，那句口訣是：服務這門生意，不是服務個別的人。
cards.why: 先幫這句話上一層保險（almost always leads in the best direction），再丟出可能刺耳的 A not B。政治角力時，把判準拉到「對公司最好」這個大家都同意的層次，等於抽掉個人恩怨。
swaps: The question I fall back on is what's right for the business.
Let's optimize for the company here, not for anyone's comfort.
cards.pmNote: 跨團隊卡住時，把爭執升級到「對公司最好的做法是什麼」，人的問題常常就自己散了。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.pattern: Direct is kind. It feels easier to avoid it, but [代價].
cards.quote: Direct is kind. And it feels kind or, really, honestly, easy to avoid these things or to work around them.
cards.zh: 直說才是善意。避開不談、繞過去，感覺很體貼，其實只是比較輕鬆而已。
cards.why: 三個字的口號式句子（Direct is kind）在英語職場是給難聽話撐腰的萬用開場；後半句用 it feels kind... easy 拆穿「體貼」其實是「怕麻煩」。
swaps: Being clear is being kind.
I'd rather be direct with you than let this drag on.
cards.pmNote: 不處理的人會變成船底的藤壺——拖慢整艘船，而且拖越久越難拔。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.quote: What escalation is, "We disagree. Neither one of us has enough power to make this decision. Let's go to someone who does."
cards.zh: 所謂升級是這樣講的：「我們兩個看法不同，而且我們誰都沒有權限拍板，那就找有權限的人。」
cards.why: 三句話拆成「事實／限制／提議」，完全不談對錯也不帶情緒，所以對方不會覺得你要去告狀。台灣人怕 escalate 被當成打小報告，關鍵就在有沒有這句 neither one of us has enough power。
swaps: This one's above both our pay grades — let's take it up together.
We're deadlocked and neither of us owns this call. Who does?
cards.pmNote: escalation 是工具不是失敗；卡在同層級互推時，主管的存在就是為了解鎖。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.pattern: And I'm like, "Could you possibly do that with [更小的數字]?"
cards.quote: And I'm like, "Could you possibly do that with 100 people?"
cards.zh: 我就會問一句：「這件事有沒有可能用一百個人就做完？」
cards.why: 不否定對方的計畫，只把數字換小然後丟回去。Could you possibly...? 表面是禮貌的可能性提問，實際上是逼對方自己去證明那個數字的必要性。
swaps: Is there a version of this that works with half the headcount?
What would it take to do this with the team we already have?
cards.pmNote: 人數成長超過一倍，你就快到來不及去重複的職缺與重疊的職責。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.pattern: [X] does not actually make you [Y]. We think it does. It does not.
cards.quote: More people does not actually make you faster. We think it does. It does not.
cards.zh: 人多不會讓你變快。我們都以為會，但真的不會。
cards.why: 三段式節奏：主張、承認共同直覺、再否定一次。第三句只有三個字，等於用停頓當鎚子。母語者在打破常識時很愛這種短句重擊。
swaps: Adding headcount doesn't buy speed. It feels like it should. It doesn't.
More resources won't fix this — we assume they will, and they won't.
cards.pmNote: 資源不足反而讓團隊只做高優先的事；先問「有沒有可能不加人」。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.pattern: You're sitting there thinking "this is a dumb question" — then you ask it and it turns out it wasn't.
cards.quote: You're sitting in the meeting and you're like, "This is a dumb question. Everyone's going to think I'm an idiot." But then you get brave and you ask it and it turns out it wasn't a dumb question.
cards.zh: 你坐在會議裡想：「這問題也太蠢，問了大家會覺得我是白痴。」結果你鼓起勇氣問了，才發現根本不是蠢問題。
cards.why: 用引號直接把腦內小劇場演出來（英語口說的 quotative like），聽眾馬上有共感。這段話本身也是一個社交許可：講完就可以接著問那個問題。
swaps: This might be a basic question, but I'd rather ask it than guess.
Probably a dumb question — what does that acronym actually mean?
cards.pmNote: 會議裡沒人敢問的問題，通常是所有人都想問的；問它就是在製造清晰。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.pattern: My superpower is being a professional [moron]: "Do we have goals? Why are we having this meeting?"
cards.quote: I always say that my superpower is being a professional moron. Because I'm the one that shows up in a room and is like, “Do we have goals? Why are we having this meeting?”
cards.zh: 我常說我的超能力就是當一個專業級的蠢蛋。我就是那種進到會議室會問：「我們有目標嗎？我們現在在幹嘛？這個會到底為什麼要開？」
cards.why: 先自嘲（professional moron）取得社交許可，才敢連丟三個直球問題。這是非母語者最該偷學的招：用降低自己的姿態，換取問最基本問題的權利。
swaps: Let me play dumb for a second — what's the goal of this meeting?
At the risk of asking the obvious: what are we actually deciding today?
cards.pmNote: 會議發散時，把大家拉回「我們今天要決定什麼」通常比任何議程都有效。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

cards.pattern: In [six months], if I'm telling you what to do, I've hired the wrong person.
cards.quote: In six months, if I'm telling you what to do, I've hired the wrong person.
cards.zh: 半年後如果還是我在告訴你要做什麼，那就是我當初找錯人了。
cards.why: 把標準講成「我的失敗」而不是「你的失敗」，壓力同時落在雙方身上，卻沒有一句話在威脅對方。這是英語管理語言裡很高竿的一種責任互換。
swaps: A year from now you should be setting the agenda, not me.
If I'm still unblocking you every week in six months, I've done this wrong.
cards.pmNote: 用這條標準面試，你會自動去找有 judgment 跟自主性的人，而不是找執行者。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.pattern: Look, I don't have time to sugarcoat any feedback — the best people I work with are the ones who tell me I'm messing up.
cards.quote: Look, I don't have time to sugarcoat any feedback, and frankly, the best people I've worked with are the people who come into one-on-ones with me and yell at me and tell me I'm messing up.
cards.zh: 老實說，我沒空把回饋包糖衣；而且說真的，我合作過最好的人，都是會在一對一裡對我吼、直接說我哪裡搞砸了的人。
cards.why: sugarcoat（裹糖衣）是給難聽話開場的關鍵字；後半句立刻把「直說」跟「我最欣賞的人」綁在一起，等於預先授權對方也可以這樣對你。
swaps: I'm not going to sugarcoat this — here's what I saw.
I'd rather be blunt than polite here, and I want the same from you.
cards.pmNote: 先建立雙向可以直說的關係，之後給難聽回饋才不會被當成人身攻擊。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.pattern: Tell me about one of the biggest mistakes you've made — truly, the more painful the better — and how you work differently now.
cards.quote: I asked them, think about one of the biggest mistakes you've made, truly, the more painful the better. And tell me what the mistake was.
cards.zh: 我會請對方想一個自己犯過最大的錯——說真的，越痛越好——然後告訴我那個錯是什麼。
cards.why: the more painful the better 這個插入語直接把「可以講真的」寫進題目裡，破解制式的假答案。英語裡 the more X the better 是很順的邀請結構，中文直譯反而會像在為難人。
swaps: Walk me through a decision you got badly wrong — the more painful the better.
What's a mistake that actually changed how you work?
cards.pmNote: 面試只考一件事的話，考 growth mindset：他能不能反省、接受回饋、把錯變成原則。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.quote: And guess what? It's all okay. It's not a loss, it's a lesson.
cards.zh: 然後你知道嗎？那都沒關係。那不是損失，那是一課。
cards.why: not a X, it's a Y 的押韻對句（loss / lesson）讓認錯不變成自責。承認失敗後補這一句，可以把場面從尷尬拉回可以往前走的狀態。
swaps: We didn't lose the quarter, we bought information.
Call it tuition, not failure.
cards.pmNote: 事後檢討的語氣決定下次還有沒有人願意冒險；把失敗定義成學費是最低成本的做法。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.quote: She used to have this saying, which is like, "Repetition doesn't spoil the prayer."
cards.zh: 她有一句話我一直記著：「重複並不會壞了那句禱告。」
cards.why: 用一句諺語替「一直重複講」正名，講完就不必再為囉唆道歉。引用別人的話（She used to have this saying）也讓你不必自己扛這個主張。
swaps: I'll say it again — repetition is the job.
You can't over-communicate a priority.
cards.pmNote: 願景與目標要對上、對下、對外一直重複；你講到膩的時候，組織才剛聽到第一次。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.quote: The way I would say it is, say you're going to do the thing, say that you're doing the thing, and then say that you did it.
cards.zh: 我的講法是：先說你要做這件事，做的過程中說你在做，做完再說你做完了。
cards.why: 三拍節奏加上刻意重複 the thing，讓一個管理原則變得像口訣一樣記得住。中間那步最值錢——它給主管一個「其實不用做了」的插話點。
swaps: Flag it, work it, close the loop.
Tell them what you'll do, tell them you're doing it, tell them it's done.
cards.pmNote: 向上管理不是拍馬屁，是讓對方有機會在你做錯方向前喊停。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.pattern: People who don't want to draw attention tend to get lost in organizations — so if that describes you, just remember to say what you did.
cards.quote: I think those people tend to get lost in organizations. So if that describes you, just remember to say what you did.
cards.zh: 這種人在組織裡很容易被淹沒。所以如果你就是這種人，記得一定要把你做過的事講出來。
cards.why: if that describes you 是一個很體貼的點名方式——不指著誰，但被說中的人自己會對號入座。內向者要學會的不是變外向，只是「把做完的事說出口」。
swaps: Quick recap of what shipped this week, in case it got lost in the noise.
I don't love self-promotion, but I want to make sure this lands: we shipped X.
cards.pmNote: 績效面談前先累積一份「說過會做／做了／做完」的紀錄，成績就不用臨時掰。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.pattern: Give two people different charges — [grow it] and [protect the craft]. That tension is extremely healthy.
cards.quote: It's really important to give two people on your team different charges. One is like go grow the product and the other one is maintain that design, that craft. That tension is extremely healthy.
cards.zh: 團隊裡要刻意讓兩個人扛不同的任務：一個負責把產品做大，另一個負責守住設計跟質感。這種張力其實非常健康。
cards.why: healthy tension 是英語職場把「衝突」正名的關鍵詞——衝突不是壞事，是刻意設計出來的制衡。主持會議時可以用它讓兩邊安心繼續吵。
swaps: This disagreement is by design — that's a healthy tension, not a problem.
I want someone in the room whose job is to argue the other side.
cards.pmNote: 團隊也是產品：刻意配置互補（甚至互斥）的角色，決策品質才會拉開。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.pattern: Just like you wouldn't [fly a plane without instruments], why would you [run a product without instrumentation]?
cards.quote: This sounds, again, very simple but just like how you wouldn't fly a plane without instruments, why would you run your products without understanding the instrumentation and how it's doing.
cards.zh: 這聽起來很簡單，但就像你不會沒有儀表就開飛機一樣，為什麼你會在完全不看數據的情況下經營產品？
cards.why: 先自己承認 sounds very simple 卸掉對方的防備，再用一個沒人會反對的類比把結論逼出來。反問句（why would you...）讓對方自己說出答案，比直接主張更難反駁。
swaps: You wouldn't drive at night without headlights — same logic here.
We'd never ship code without tests; why do we ship features without metrics?
cards.pmNote: 從 1 到 10 的階段最該做的事：把所有東西量起來，通常會發現一半的行為根本沒 log。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.pattern: [Name]'s really special. I've got to just take a moment to give her a giant shout out — she is the only person I've worked with who [X].
cards.quote: Joanne's really special. I got to just take a moment to give her a giant shout out. She is the only person that I've worked with that has as much technical depth as she does have product taste.
cards.zh: Joanne 真的很特別。我一定要停下來大聲說一下她有多厲害——她是我合作過唯一一個技術深度跟產品品味一樣強的人。
cards.why: take a moment to give a shout out 是英語公開稱讚的標準動作：先宣告要停下來讚美（製造焦點），再給一個具體到不能複製的理由。台灣人稱讚常停在 she's great，沒有那個「唯一」的比較級。
swaps: Quick shout out to Ray — he's the reason this shipped on time.
I want to call this out publicly: nobody else on the team could have done that.
cards.pmNote: 公開稱讚要具體到「別人做不到的那一點」，否則只是客套，起不了帶動士氣的作用。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.pattern: Honestly, I'm more proud of [the team I built] than [the products].
cards.quote: I'm so proud of, honestly, the team that I built there more than the products.
cards.zh: 老實講，比起那些產品，我更以我在那裡帶出來的團隊為榮。
cards.why: 把 honestly 插在句中而不是句首，是母語者強調真心的節奏；more than 的比較讓稱讚有份量——你放棄了更亮眼的功績來讚美人。
swaps: The thing I'm proudest of isn't the launch, it's the people.
Ask me what I'd put on my resume — it's this team.
cards.pmNote: 領導者的長期成績是「離開後那些人去了哪」，不是當時 ship 了什麼。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.quote: Look, I won't claim to be an expert on this at all, but I think that with every technology that's come out, we've been able to harness it and it takes a lot of harnessing.
cards.zh: 我先講，我完全不敢說自己是這方面的專家，但我覺得每一種新技術出來，我們最後都有辦法駕馭它，只是那個駕馭要花很多力氣。
cards.why: I won't claim to be an expert 不是示弱，是先把自己的可信度範圍畫好，之後的意見就變成「一個有經驗的人的判斷」而不是「專家宣稱」。台灣人常用 I'm not sure，語感上弱很多。
swaps: I'm no expert here, but my read is —
Take this with a grain of salt since it's outside my area, but...
cards.pmNote: 承認知識邊界是資深訊號；重點是承認完之後仍然給出明確判斷。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.pattern: I love that you're starting with a spicy question — let me share some more context behind it.
cards.quote: I love it that you're starting with a spicy question here and let me share some more context behind it.
cards.zh: 我很喜歡你一開始就丟這麼辣的問題，讓我先把背後的脈絡補一下。
cards.why: 被問到尖銳問題時，先誇問題（spicy question）再爭取鋪陳空間，等於用一句話同時降溫、拖秒數、掌控框架。這比 that's a good question 高明，因為它承認了問題的攻擊性。
swaps: That's a spicy one — let me give you the context first.
Fair challenge. Before I answer, let me set some background.
cards.pmNote: 被 exec 當場質疑時，先給脈絡再給答案，可以避免答案被斷章取義。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.pattern: If you're [doing the shortcut], you're missing the point. You can't [empathize] with a summary.
cards.quote: I think that to anyone out there who's doing user interviews and then saying, hey ChatGPT, summarize the takeaways, you're missing the point. You can't empathize with the summary.
cards.zh: 如果你做完使用者訪談，轉頭就叫 ChatGPT 幫你摘要重點，那你就搞錯重點了。你沒辦法對一份摘要產生同理心。
cards.why: you're missing the point 是英語裡最直接但仍可接受的糾正；後面那句短短六個字（can't empathize with the summary）把抽象的損失講成一個具體不可能的動作，殺傷力很大。
swaps: Reading the transcript isn't the same as sitting in the room.
You can automate the notes, you can't automate the empathy.
cards.pmNote: 使用者研究的價值在「你自己感受到那個痛」，不在那份重點整理。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.pattern: It pains me to say this, but really [the uncomfortable truth].
cards.quote: And at Uber, I learned this because, it pains me to say this, but really the price and the ETA at Uber was the product.
cards.zh: 我在 Uber 學到這件事——講出來我自己都有點痛——但價格跟預估時間，那才是 Uber 真正的產品。
cards.why: it pains me to say this 事先承認「這句話對我也不好受」，讓聽者把注意力放在事實而不是說話者的立場。要講一個大家不想聽的結論時，這是很好的緩衝。
swaps: I hate to say it, but the data doesn't support our theory.
This one hurts to admit — the feature isn't what moved the number.
cards.pmNote: 有時候你精雕細琢的介面根本不是產品；先確認什麼才是使用者真正在消費的東西。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.quote: There's a saying that Mike and Kevin had at Instagram which is we may not be right, but at least we're not confused.
cards.zh: Instagram 的 Mike 跟 Kevin 有一句話：我們不見得是對的，但至少我們不是一團混亂。
cards.why: we may not be right, but at least... 用讓步句把「決策不確定」跟「方向清楚」分開處理，是在不確定中仍然要求執行力時最好用的一句。
swaps: We might be wrong, but we won't be vague.
I'd rather be clearly wrong than fuzzily right.
cards.pmNote: 猶豫不決的代價通常高於選錯；先定一個方向，再用數據修正。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.pattern: You have to obsess over [the details of craft] while simultaneously having the wisdom of which details don't actually matter.
cards.quote: It's important to obsess about the details of craft, while simultaneously having the perspective and wisdom of which details don't actually matter.
cards.zh: 你要對細節的講究到近乎偏執，同時又要有那個判斷力，知道哪些細節其實根本不重要。
cards.why: while simultaneously 把兩個看似矛盾的要求綁成同一個能力，是英語裡描述「資深」的常用結構。台灣人容易講成 but also，力道弱一半。
swaps: Care about everything, and know what to let go of.
Sweat the details that matter — and be ruthless about which ones don't.
cards.pmNote: 資淺 PM 卡在「什麼都想做好」，資深 PM 的差別在知道哪些地方可以不做好。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

cards.pattern: You earn their trust by asking them to do one of two things: either you teach me, or I help you.
cards.quote: You earn their trust by asking them to do two things. One, you're either going to teach me or I'm going to help you.
cards.zh: 取得信任的方法就是給對方兩個選項：要嘛你教我，要嘛我來幫你。
cards.why: 把「我想跟你搞好關係」轉譯成兩個對方都不吃虧的具體請求，任何一邊他都不好拒絕。teach me / help you 這組對仗把「主動示弱」變成一個交易。
swaps: Either I learn from you or I take work off your plate — your call.
I'd love an hour of your time; if you don't have it, put me to work instead.
cards.pmNote: 新進公司先去找那個最有影響力、最吵的人，把他的信任借到自己身上。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

cards.pattern: Look, I just hired [X]. Super rockstar. But he knows nothing about [our business] — I'd love for you to teach him some things.
cards.quote: Look, I just hired Lenny. Super rockstar. But he knows nothing about that business, nothing about how we work — I will love for you to teach him some things.
cards.zh: 我會說：「這是我剛找進來的 Lenny，超強，做過這些那些。可是我們這門生意他一無所知，公司怎麼運作也不懂，很希望你能教他一些東西。」
cards.why: 先抬（super rockstar）再壓（knows nothing），對方就不會覺得你在推一個麻煩給他，而是被邀請去塑造一個高潛力的人。這是替下屬引薦的標準句法。
swaps: She's excellent, but brand new to how we operate — could she learn from you?
I'd love for you to shape how he thinks about this space.
cards.pmNote: 讓有影響力的人「共同持有」新人的成長，之後他就很難公開說這個新人不行。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

cards.pattern: He's just got to sit in the meetings you're in, quiet, observe. No stress, nothing to give.
cards.quote: He's just got to sit in meetings you are, quiet, observe, just by observing you, he will be a rockstar. No stress, nothing to give.
cards.zh: 他只要坐在你會出席的會議裡，安靜、看就好，光是看你怎麼做他就會變很強。你完全不用出力，也不用有壓力。
cards.why: No stress, nothing to give 這六個字把對方的成本降到零，是說服忙人答應最關鍵的一句。台灣人請人幫忙時常反而強調「不會耽誤你太多時間」，遠不如直接說「你什麼都不用做」。
swaps: Zero prep needed on your side — she'll just be a fly on the wall.
You don't have to do anything differently; he'll just shadow you.
cards.pmNote: 跟忙碌的 stakeholder 建關係，先設計一個他成本為零的接觸方式。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

cards.pattern: Is it okay if I show you an alternative way of doing that?
cards.quote: And I said, "Is it okay if I show you an alternative way of communicating that?"
cards.zh: 我就說：「我可以示範一種不一樣的講法給你看嗎？」
cards.why: 先要許可再示範，把糾正變成一份禮物而不是評判；alternative way 也刻意避開「你錯了」的預設。對上位者給回饋，這句幾乎是萬用鑰匙。
swaps: Would it be useful if I showed you another way to frame that?
Mind if I try saying the same thing differently?
cards.pmNote: 多數人不是不想改，是沒看過別的做法有效；示範比說教有用。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

cards.pattern: First of all, I don't think I can [keep working with you] given [this]. But I need to understand why you [do X].
cards.quote: I was like, "First of all, I don't even think I can work with you anymore given this environment you're creating, but I need to understand why you are talking to your team like that."
cards.zh: 我就說：「老實講，看到你製造出來的這種氣氛，我覺得我沒辦法再跟你合作下去了。但我還是想先搞懂，你為什麼會這樣跟你的團隊講話。」
cards.why: 先亮出最重的底牌（我可能不做了），再馬上轉成一個真誠的提問，讓對方在震撼中還有台階可下。but I need to understand why 是把對峙轉成對話的樞紐。
swaps: I'm not sure I can be part of this, but help me understand where it's coming from.
This is a line for me — and I still want to hear your reasoning.
cards.pmNote: 要求對方改變前，先確認你有沒有理解他為什麼一直這樣做。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

cards.pattern: Doing [X] is the [報告者]'s job, but getting better at [X] is the manager's job.
cards.quote: Doing product management is a product manager's job, but getting better at product management is the manager's job, is the coach's job.
cards.zh: 把產品管理做出來，是 PM 的工作；讓 PM 在產品管理上變得更強，那是主管的工作、教練的工作。
cards.why: 同一個名詞（product management）配上 doing / getting better at 的對比，一句話重新劃分責任。這種「做 vs. 變強」的對仗在英語管理場合非常好記也很難反駁。
swaps: Shipping is their job; growing them is mine.
They own the work — I own whether they get better at the work.
cards.pmNote: 主管的日常工作是 coaching，不是自己下去解題；解題的人只會養出微管理。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

cards.pattern: Let me tell you what a [director] does — because I'm promoting you to do the job, not to learn the job.
cards.quote: Let me tell you what a director does. And you're going to work with me over the next couple of months to do those things because I am promoting you to do the job, not to learn the job.
cards.zh: 我先跟你講總監到底在做什麼。接下來這幾個月你要跟我一起把那些事做一遍——因為我升你是要你來做這個職位，不是來學這個職位。
cards.why: to do the job, not to learn the job 用同一個動詞結構做對比，把升遷的門檻講得極清楚卻不帶羞辱。想爭取升遷時反過來用也成立：我想先做，再談 title。
swaps: Start doing the role now; the title follows the evidence.
I'd rather you practise the job before you have to survive it.
cards.pmNote: 最適合學當 VP 的時機，是你還不是 VP 的時候——犯錯成本最低。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

cards.pattern: I can teach most things, I can coach a lot of things — but [arrogance] is very, very challenging.
cards.quote: Most of I can teach, I can coach a lot of things, but that arrogance, that ego, those "I walk alone" kinds of things, those are very, very challenging and disruptive to a team culture.
cards.zh: 大部分東西我都能教、都能帶，但那種傲慢、那種自我、那種「我一個人走」的姿態，非常難處理，而且會傷到團隊文化。
cards.why: 先大方承認「絕大多數我都能教」，再把唯一的例外點出來，讓這個否定顯得客觀。those "I walk alone" kinds of things 用引號把一種態度具象化，比 arrogant 更有畫面。
swaps: Skills I can teach. The attitude I can't.
Everything else is coachable — this part isn't.
cards.pmNote: 面試可以放過技能缺口，不能放過拒絕協作的傾向。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

cards.pattern: Just because they can use it doesn't mean they will buy it. Just because they can use it doesn't mean they will choose it.
