cards.quote: Just because somebody can use your product doesn't mean that they will buy it. Just because they can use it doesn't mean they will choose it.
cards.zh: 會用你的產品，不代表他會買。會用，也不代表他會選你。
cards.why: Just because A doesn't mean B 是英語拆解錯誤推論最乾淨的句型，連用兩次形成節奏，聽起來像在拆一顆一顆的假設。反駁「使用者測試分數很高」這類數據時特別好用。
swaps: Usability isn't demand — passing a usability test isn't a purchase.
Just because they said yes in the survey doesn't mean they'll pay.
cards.pmNote: 四種風險裡最常被跳過的是價值風險：能用 ≠ 想要 ≠ 願意付。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

cards.pattern: All [25] have to want the same thing. If one person's out, you just don't do it at all.
cards.quote: All 25 have to want the same thing. If one person's out, you just don't do it at all.
cards.zh: 二十五個人得要的是同一件事。只要有一個人不要，那這個東西就整個不做。
cards.why: 用一條事先講好的規則來拒絕，而不是用個人判斷——擋需求時對方無法把不滿投射到你身上。這是把「說不」外包給制度的典型英語說法。
swaps: Our bar is unanimous demand; this one didn't clear it.
If it's not wanted by all of them, it doesn't go in.
cards.pmNote: 被要求加功能時，最強的回擊是「跟你一樣的 25 個人沒有它也很滿意」。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

cards.pattern: The ultimate definition of [love for our product] is they're willing to put their reputation on the line by telling people about it.
cards.quote: The ultimate definition for me today of the love that somebody has for our product is they're willing to put their reputation on the line by telling people about it.
cards.zh: 對我來說，一個人有多愛你的產品，最終極的定義就是：他願意拿自己的名聲去替你背書，主動跟別人講。
cards.why: 把一個模糊的字（love）重新定義成一個可觀察的行為，是英語裡「操作型定義」的標準寫法。put their reputation on the line 比 recommend 重得多，因為它點出對方的風險。
swaps: The real signal isn't the score — it's whether they'll vouch for us publicly.
If they won't put their name on it, they don't love it.
cards.pmNote: PMF 的指標不是滿意度，是有沒有人願意當可以打電話去問的 reference customer。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

cards.pattern: Most people don't like [X] because they haven't experienced good [X].
cards.quote: I think most people don't like product managers often because they haven't experienced good product managers.
cards.zh: 我覺得多數人不喜歡 PM，多半是因為他們沒遇過真正好的 PM。
cards.why: 不否認對方的情緒，只把原因換掉——從「這個角色沒用」變成「你的樣本有問題」。這種 reframe 是接住整組人負評時最省力的一招。
swaps: The problem isn't the role, it's the ones they've worked with.
People hate meetings because they've never been in a good one.
cards.pmNote: PM 的信任來自能力：對客戶、資料、產業、生意比別人懂，別人才會讓你決定做什麼。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

cards.pattern: Wow, would you give me [$X] to solve this problem?
cards.quote: And my first question to him as a product guy is like, "Wow, would you give me a million dollars to solve this problem?"
cards.zh: 身為做產品的人，我第一個問題是：「哇，那你願意花一百萬美元讓我解掉這個問題嗎？」
cards.why: 用一個誇張的數字把「你有多痛」轉成一個可以回答的問題，對方猶豫的那個秒數就是答案。前面加一個 Wow 讓這個逼問聽起來像興奮而不是刁難。
swaps: What would you pay to make this go away tomorrow?
Is this a 'nice to have' or a 'write a cheque' problem?
cards.pmNote: 問題值不值得解，最快的測法是問對方願意付多少；含糊的回答就是不夠痛。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

cards.pattern: What is the action you can take next to counter-program the narrative you're afraid this person has of you?
cards.quote: I try to focus them less around whatever happened and more on what is the action that you can take next to counter program the narrative that you are afraid that this other person has of you.
cards.zh: 我會把他的注意力從「已經發生的事」拉開，改放到：你接下來可以做什麼動作，去反寫你擔心對方對你形成的那個印象。
cards.why: counter-program（原本是電視台排檔的用語）把「挽回形象」變成一個主動的動作，而不是解釋或爭辯。focus them less around X and more on Y 也是很好用的引導句型。
swaps: What's one thing you could do this week that tells a different story?
Instead of correcting the record, let's change the next data point.
cards.pmNote: 在組織裡，關於你的敘事是靠後續行為改寫的，不是靠澄清郵件。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.quote: I challenge it and I say, "First of all, I don't think there's evidence for that. Is there evidence for that? And even if there is, it doesn't really matter."
cards.zh: 我會直接反問：「首先，我不覺得這件事有任何證據。你有證據嗎？就算有好了，其實也不重要。」
cards.why: 先否定、再把否定改成問句交還對方、最後用 even if 把整個爭點作廢——三步一氣呵成。even if X, it doesn't matter 是英語裡最有效率的收束法，直接跳過辯論。
swaps: Do we actually have evidence for that? And even if we do, would it change what we do next?
That's an assumption. Even granting it, I'm not sure it matters.
cards.pmNote: 帶人時要挑戰負面推論，不要只是同理——同理會讓對方陷得更深。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.pattern: Wanted to build on this idea you had today. I really liked that idea, by the way. I saw this research about [相關的東西]...
cards.quote: I very quickly just sent her a note that said, "Wanted to build on this idea you had today. I really liked that idea, by the way. I saw this article, I saw this research about this other emerging thing."
cards.zh: 我很快就傳了一則訊息給她：「想接著你今天那個想法往下延伸。順帶一提，我真的很喜歡那個點子。我看到一篇研究提到另一個正在浮現的現象……」
cards.why: Wanted to build on... 這個省略主詞的開場是英語職場訊息的標準寫法（省略 I，顯得輕快不正式）；by the way 把讚美放在附帶位置，反而比正面稱讚更可信。
swaps: Building on what you raised today — here's a related angle.
Quick follow-up on your idea from the meeting, plus something adjacent I found.
cards.pmNote: 會議上表現失常，用一封「延伸你的想法」的短訊補救，比任何解釋都有效。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.pattern: This isn't funny. This is a serious issue for a lot of people — I think we should take it seriously.
cards.quote: This isn't funny, Hilary. This is a serious issue for a lot of people, and it's an emerging problem in some cases. And I think we should take it seriously.
cards.zh: 這不好笑。這對很多人來說是很嚴重的問題，而且在某些地方正在惡化。我覺得我們應該認真看待。
cards.why: 當場糾正而不攻擊人：先否定行為（this isn't funny），再給理由，最後用 I think we should 把大家拉回同一陣線。整段沒有一個 you。
swaps: I don't think that's a joke — this matters to a lot of our users.
Let's not laugh this one off; I'd like us to take it seriously.
cards.pmNote: 會議中糾正氣氛，越早越好；隔天再說會變成翻舊帳。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.pattern: I'm not interested in litigating what already happened when we can move forward.
cards.quote: I'm not interested in litigating the things that happened already when we can move forward.
cards.zh: 已經發生的事我沒興趣再打官司，我們可以往前走。
cards.why: litigate 借用法律語言來形容「反覆爭論誰對誰錯」，一個字就把那種行為貼上標籤，讓它顯得幼稚。用來喊停無止盡的檢討會非常有力。
swaps: Let's not re-litigate this — what's the next move?
I'd rather spend the energy forward than backward.
cards.pmNote: 事後檢討的目的是找系統問題，不是重新審判一次決策。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.quote: Every additional person in a meeting has a cost, because every additional person in a meeting makes the people in that meeting less candid than they would have been if there were fewer people in that meeting.
cards.zh: 會議每多一個人都是有代價的，因為人越多，在場的人講話就越保留。
cards.why: 把「人多不好」量化成 cost，再給一個沒人能反駁的機制（less candid）。要婉拒別人旁聽、或精簡與會名單時，這句可以直接搬去用。
swaps: Every extra seat costs us candor — let's keep this one small.
I'd rather run this with four people and share notes after.
cards.pmNote: 會議設計的第一原則：人越少越誠實；旁聽者要付出「必須有貢獻」的代價。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.quote: One thing I've learned is that I think people are really good at coming up with very rational sounding reasons to not do things that just make them uncomfortable.
cards.zh: 我學到一件事：人非常擅長替「其實只是讓自己不舒服的事」找出聽起來很有道理的理由。
cards.why: rational-sounding 這個複合形容詞是關鍵——不說對方在找藉口，只說那些理由「聽起來」合理。這樣點破而不撕破臉。
swaps: That reason sounds rational — I wonder if it's really discomfort.
We're very good at justifying the thing we didn't want to do anyway.
cards.pmNote: 團隊說某件事「不可行」時，先分辨是技術限制還是不想面對的麻煩。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.pattern: What's much more helpful than understanding what your CEO thinks is understanding how your CEO thinks.
cards.quote: And so what is much more helpful than understanding what your CEO thinks is, I think understanding how your CEO thinks.
cards.zh: 比起搞懂你的 CEO 想什麼，更有用的是搞懂他是怎麼想事情的。
cards.why: what / how 一字之差撐起整個對比，是英語裡最省力的深化句型。講完這句，後面所有「幫團隊建立老闆的心智模型」的做法就都順理成章。
swaps: Don't learn her opinions, learn her criteria.
The goal isn't to know the answer he'd give — it's to know how he gets there.
cards.pmNote: 團隊都建立起同一套「老闆會怎麼判斷」的模型後，簽核與來回確認就會自然消失。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.quote: Even if I don't agree with the feedback, what is the insight that I'm missing? How am I wrong about this? What would be true for this other person to be right?
cards.zh: 就算我不同意那個回饋，我也會問：我漏掉了什麼洞見？我哪裡想錯了？要怎麼樣，對方才會是對的？
cards.why: 第三個問句是精華：What would have to be true for X to be right? 把對立轉成一道推理題，逼自己去建構對方的世界，而不是找他的破綻。
swaps: What would have to be true for that call to make sense?
Steelman it for me — what's the strongest version of their argument?
cards.pmNote: 跟高層意見不同時，先做一次「他要在什麼前提下才是對的」推演，常常會發現你缺的是資訊不是判斷力。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.quote: And they might be right. I don't think they're right, but they might be. Let's find out.
cards.zh: 他們有可能是對的。我不覺得他們是對的，但他們有可能。我們去驗證看看。
cards.why: 同一句話正反轉三次，把「保留立場」跟「全力執行」同時交代清楚——這就是 disagree and commit 的口語版。台灣人常只做到「照做」，沒把自己的判斷留在桌上。
swaps: I still disagree, and I'm fully behind giving it a real shot.
My call would be different — but let's run it properly and see.
cards.pmNote: 反對過、輸了之後，執行要百分之百；一邊做一邊唱衰是團隊最貴的內耗。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.pattern: There are no right answers, only wrong answers — you're executing well on the least wrong one available.
cards.quote: In product, I like to joke, there's no right answers. There's only wrong answers, and you're just trying to execute well on the least wrong answer that's available to you.
cards.zh: 做產品這行我常開玩笑說：沒有對的答案，只有錯的答案；你能做的就是把眼前「最不錯」的那個做好。
cards.why: 先用 I like to joke 幫這個悲觀命題上保險，再用 least wrong 這個罕見但一聽就懂的最高級。跟人爭「哪個方案才對」時，這句能直接把戰場轉到執行。
swaps: There's no clean option here — let's pick the least bad one and commit.
Every path has holes. Which holes can we live with?
cards.pmNote: 所有方案都能被挑毛病；能被挑毛病不等於那個決定不該做。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.pattern: The magic questions aren't questions — they're statements that end with "Do you agree?" or "Is that right?"
cards.quote: I talk about what I like to call the magic questions, but the thing about magic questions is they're not actually questions, they're statements and they end with, "Do you agree?" Or "Is that right?"
cards.zh: 我把它叫做「魔法問句」，但重點是它們根本不是問句——它們是敘述句，結尾加上「你同意嗎？」或「我理解得對嗎？」
cards.why: 非母語者在英文會議裡最吃虧的就是只會問開放問題，講完還是聽不懂。改成「我把我的理解講一遍＋is that right?」既展現思考，也逼對方只需回答 yes/no。
swaps: So my understanding is X, Y, Z — is that right?
Let me play that back: we're doing A because of B. Do you agree?
cards.pmNote: 跟法務、合規、高層對齊時，丟假設請他們否認，比請他們解釋規則快得多。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.pattern: You come up thinking you're the protagonist. But in the story of your work, you are probably not the protagonist.
cards.quote: You kind of come up thinking you're the protagonist. You can be the protagonist in your life, but in the story of your work of a company, you are probably not the protagonist.
cards.zh: 你一路長大都以為自己是主角。你在自己的人生裡可以是主角，但在公司這個故事裡，你多半不是主角。
cards.why: 借小說的敘事角色來講組織位置，把一句可能很傷人的話（你沒那麼重要）包在文學隱喻裡，聽起來像洞見不像貶低。中間那句讓步（in your life you can be）是不可省的緩衝。
swaps: This isn't my story to drive — my job is to make theirs work.
I had to learn I'm a supporting character here, and that's fine.
cards.pmNote: CPO 的工作不是把自己腦中的產品做出來，是把 CEO 的願景變成最好的實體。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.pattern: You have to advocate for what you think is true in the most compelling way possible — and you have an obligation to do it.
cards.quote: But you have to be able to advocate for what you think is true in the most compelling way possible. And you have an obligation to do it.
cards.zh: 你必須用最有說服力的方式，替你認為是對的事情發聲。而且這是你的義務。
cards.why: obligation 把「敢不敢講」從個性問題轉成職責問題——這對怕衝突的人是最有效的推力。你不是愛吵，你是在履行職責。
swaps: It's part of the job to make the strongest case you can.
I owe you my honest read, even when it's inconvenient.
cards.pmNote: 先把論點打完整、輸了再 commit；沒打就投降的人不會被當成有判斷力的人。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.pattern: Give them a shout-out in the team meeting, let them demo it — make them feel like a million bucks for doing the thing.
cards.quote: When somebody is using AI to solve a problem that they wouldn't have used AI before, give them a shout-out in the team meeting, let them demo that. Again, make them feel like a million bucks for doing the thing.
cards.zh: 只要有人用 AI 解掉一個他以前不會這樣解的問題，就在團隊會議上點名讚美他，讓他 demo 一次。就是要讓他爽到不行。
cards.why: feel like a million bucks 是英語裡形容「被捧得很爽」的固定說法；讓對方 demo 比口頭稱讚更強，因為獎賞變成了舞台。
swaps: Let's get you to demo this on Thursday — the team should see it.
Huge shout-out to Mia for this one; it changed how we work.
cards.pmNote: 想推廣什麼行為，就設計它的獎賞迴路：要強、要即時、要有情緒。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.quote: I'm asking them, "What do you do for joy? Are you doing something every single day that's bringing you joy in your life?" And if they say no, I'm like, "That's a problem."
cards.zh: 我會問他們：「你都做什麼讓自己開心？你每天有沒有一件事是讓你有樂趣的？」如果回答沒有，我就會說：「那這是個問題。」
cards.why: 把私人領域的關心用工作語言處理——說 that's a problem 而不是 that's sad，等於宣告這件事跟績效一樣需要被排進待辦。這比一般的 how are you doing? 有效太多。
swaps: What's giving you energy outside work right now?
If the answer's nothing, let's treat that as an action item.
cards.pmNote: 產品領導者的續航力來自恢復；1:1 問一句「最近有什麼讓你開心」不是閒聊，是在保養人。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.pattern: But what I think that misses is, it assumes that [對方沒察覺的前提].
cards.quote: But what I think that misses is, it assumes that you go and you do this analyst job for two years, and at the end of it you have a person who knows how to make models really well.
cards.zh: 但我覺得這個說法漏掉了一件事：它預設你得先當兩年分析師，兩年之後才會長出一個很會建模型的人。
cards.why: what that misses is, it assumes... 是英語裡拆對方論點的黃金句型：不說他錯，只說他有一個沒被檢查的前提。攻擊的是假設，不是人。
swaps: The part that argument skips is the assumption that —
I'd push on one hidden premise there:
cards.pmNote: 接住反對意見時，找出對方沒說出口的前提，比正面反駁結論有效得多。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.pattern: This is my hot take. You hear people talking about [X] and it's all very wonderful — I'm totally on board, but...
cards.quote: Oh, I think this is my hot take. You hear people talking about craft and taste and product management, and it's all very wonderful. And I'm totally on board.
cards.zh: 喔，這大概是我的爭議發言了。大家都在談 craft、談品味、談產品管理，聽起來都很美好，我也完全買單——
cards.why: 先自己貼上 hot take 的標籤，等於預告「接下來的話可能得罪人」，聽者的防衛心會先降下來；再用 I'm totally on board 讓步，後面的批評才不會被當成酸。
swaps: Controversial opinion, and I say this as a fan —
Hot take incoming: I agree with all of it, and I still think we're avoiding the hard problems.
cards.pmNote: 要說爭議意見，先標記它是爭議意見；標記本身就是社交緩衝。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.quote: It is just a curiosity for in what world does this make sense for this person? What is the world of this person where the thing that they're saying makes sense?
cards.zh: 那就是一種好奇心：在什麼樣的世界裡，這個人這樣講是說得通的？他活在什麼樣的處境，才會講出這句話？
cards.why: In what world...? 平常是反諷用法（怎麼可能），這裡被翻轉成真誠的探究，非常漂亮。用它取代「他到底在想什麼」，情緒立刻從惱怒轉成好奇。
swaps: What would I have to be seeing to say what he just said?
What pressure is she under that makes this the obvious call?
cards.pmNote: 跨部門衝突多半來自資訊不對稱；先重建對方的處境，再談分歧。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

cards.pattern: Not all of these are created equal — [X] is the most important one, because [理由].
cards.quote: Not all of these variables is created equal and the manager is the most important variable in the environment, because a great manager who is empathetic, who is aware of what's going on, has the ability to move the chess pieces around.
cards.zh: 這幾個變數的份量不一樣，主管是環境裡最關鍵的那一個——因為一個有同理心、狀況清楚的好主管，是有能力幫你把棋子移一移的。
cards.why: 先承認「都很重要」再馬上排序，是避免被聽成偏頗的標準做法。not all X are created equal 是母語者講「別一視同仁」的固定說法，台灣人通常會講成 they have different importance，語氣弱很多。
swaps: They don't all carry the same weight.
These aren't equally weighted — one of them dominates.
If I had to rank them, X is far ahead.
cards.pmNote: 同樣一組指標，先講「不是每個都一樣重」再排序，比直接只講一個更容易被接受。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

cards.pattern: The goal isn't to [大家以為的目標]. Ideally, [真正該追求的].
cards.quote: You're never going to always like your manager. The goal isn't to like your manager. Ideally, you respect them and they respect you, you feel like there's things that you can learn from them.
cards.zh: 你不可能永遠喜歡你的主管。重點本來就不是喜不喜歡，而是互相尊重、而且你從他身上學得到東西。
cards.why: 「The goal isn't to X」是最省力的重新定義：不否定對方的困擾，只是把評分標準換掉。後面接 Ideally 而不是 You should，把要求講成理想值，聽起來不像在教訓人。
swaps: That was never the bar.
That's not really what we're optimizing for.
The question isn't whether you like it — it's whether it works.
cards.pmNote: 團隊卡在「喜不喜歡這個方案」時，把問題換成「這個方案能不能讓我們學到東西」通常就解開了。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

cards.pattern: Do you know someone who's really good at [具體挑戰] that I could talk to?
cards.quote: So instead of just going to someone saying, "Hey, can you be a mentor?" Coming to me and say, "Do you know someone who's actually really good at changing the way teams work or really good at communicating a new vision that I can talk to?"
cards.zh: 與其跑去問人家「你可以當我的 mentor 嗎」，不如問：「你認識誰特別擅長改變團隊運作方式、或特別會傳達新願景，可以讓我請教一下嗎？」
cards.why: 把「請你付出時間」換成「請你動用人脈」，對方的成本從幾個月變成一封介紹信，答應率天差地別。而且問題裡先描述了具體挑戰，對方腦中馬上有人選，不必反問你要什麼。
swaps: Who comes to mind as someone who's solved this before?
Is there anyone you'd point me to on this?
Who would you ask if you were me?
cards.pmNote: 找 mentor 別找「人」，要找「問題的解法」——推薦人本身會替這段關係背書。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

cards.pattern: That's a good idea, but we don't actually understand [這三件事] before we start.
cards.quote: That's a good idea, but we don't actually understand these three things before we start working on that. So maybe we should do understand work to make sure that that is actually the right idea.
cards.zh: 這個想法不錯，但在動手之前有三件事我們其實還沒搞懂。也許先做點「理解型的工作」，確認這真的是對的方向。
cards.why: 沒有說 no，只是在 yes 前面插一段前置條件——擋案子時最安全的姿勢。關鍵在 these three things：講出具體數量，讓反對聽起來像清單而不是抗拒。結尾用 maybe we should，把決定權遞回去。
swaps: I like it — I just want to close two gaps first.
Good idea. What would we need to know to be confident?
Before we commit, can we de-risk these two assumptions?
cards.pmNote: Facebook 的 understand → identify → execute，反過來的 identify → justify → execute 就是「先想做，再去撈數據來合理化」。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

cards.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
cards.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？
cards.why: 把一整份 roadmap 一刀切成「有證據」和「沒證據」兩堆，是最快讓會議停止吵架的問法。because the data tells us 這種把理由直接掛在信心後面的句法，等於逼每個人交出依據。
swaps: Which of these are we confident about, and why?
What's evidence-backed here, and what's still a hypothesis?
Where do we have data, and where are we guessing?
cards.pmNote: roadmap 排序前先分「有把握 / 待理解」兩欄，比直接排優先序有效得多。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

cards.pattern: Is it a better outcome to [快而淺], or is it a better outcome to [慢而深]?
cards.quote: Is it a better outcome to just ship more faster now, but most of the things aren't impactful? Or is it a better outcome to ship fewer things but really work on making sure that you're shipping them in the best way?
cards.zh: 到底哪個結果比較好：現在拚命多出貨，但大部分都沒什麼影響力？還是少做幾件，但每一件都確保做到最好？
cards.why: 把自己的立場包裝成一組對稱的問句，讓對方自己選——他選了就等於幫你背書。注意兩邊都用 Is it a better outcome to 開頭，句型完全對稱，但第一邊藏了 but most of the things aren't impactful 這個致命尾巴。
swaps: Which do we actually want: volume or hit rate?
Would you rather ship ten and land two, or ship four and land three?
What's the better outcome a year from now?
cards.pmNote: 衡量團隊要看 win rate（出貨命中率），不是出貨數量。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

cards.pattern: This is the irony of [X]: people think it's [Y], and it's not.
cards.quote: Well, I mean this is the irony of growth, is people think growth is overnight success and it's not. It is a lot of short wins and short-term execution for a longer-term gain.
cards.zh: 成長最諷刺的地方就在這：大家以為成長是一夜爆紅，其實不是。它是一堆短期的小勝仗，堆出長期的結果。
cards.why: the irony of X is 是一個很有效率的開場：一句話同時宣告「我要推翻常識」和「我不是在罵你」。後面用 and it's not 收得極短，比 but that's actually wrong 更乾脆、更像母語者。
swaps: The funny thing about growth is...
People imagine it's X. It's really Y.
The counterintuitive part is...
cards.pmNote: 成長是複利，不是彩券——所以 velocity 和 win rate 比單一爆款重要。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

cards.quote: When you walk into a room as a product manager, engineers, designers, researchers go to market. Nobody owes you anything. It's very similar skillset, just different domain expertise.
cards.zh: 你以 PM 身分走進一個房間，工程師、設計師、研究員、GTM——沒有人欠你什麼。技能其實一模一樣，差別只在領域知識。
cards.why: 面試被質疑背景不相關時的標準解法：承認表面差異（domain），主張底層相同（skillset）。just 這個字負責把差異縮小成「只是」，是整句的關鍵字。
swaps: Same muscles, different context.
The domain is new; the job isn't.
What transfers is the how, not the what.
cards.pmNote: 轉職敘事的核心：把過去經驗抽象到「能力層」再對接，不要停在「產業層」。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

cards.pattern: They know what to do, but they don't understand how to tie it back to [更大的脈絡].
cards.quote: It's like they know what to do, but they don't understand how to tie it back to the business context and the overall strategy needs and so where to prioritize.
cards.zh: 他們知道該做什麼，只是不知道怎麼把這件事接回商業脈絡跟整體策略，所以也就排不出優先順序。
cards.why: 給難聽回饋的安全格式：先肯定第一層能力（know what to do），再指出缺的是第二層（tie it back to）。tie it back to 這個動詞片語比 connect to 更有「拉回去」的動作感，是英文會議裡的高頻用法。
swaps: The execution's there; the framing isn't yet.
I'd like to see you connect this back to the business case.
You know the how — I want to hear the why.
cards.pmNote: 帶 manager 的重點是「綜合與評估」那一層，不是再教一次執行。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

cards.pattern: Well, that's very generous of you. I wouldn't say [誇大版]— we've done some good work so far.
cards.quote: Well, it's very generous of you. I wouldn't say... look, we've done some really good work, some good work so far at YouTube, and it's been a journey.
cards.zh: 你太抬舉我了。我不會這樣講啦——我們在 YouTube 是做了一些不錯的成績，過程也蠻曲折的。
cards.why: 被公開稱讚時，母語者不會說 no no no（否定對方判斷），而是說 that's very generous of you——把讚美說成「你人很好」，既不否認也不承接。接著自己下修一級（really good work → some good work），是英文謙虛的節奏。
swaps: That's kind of you to say.
I'd put it less strongly than that.
I'll take that, though I'd share the credit.
cards.pmNote: 被高估時主動下修，比默認接受更能建立可信度——之後你說什麼別人才會照數字信。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

cards.pattern: I can't really go into specifics, but what I would say is this.
cards.quote: I can't really go into specifics a bunch with YouTube, but what I would say is this.
cards.zh: YouTube 那邊的細節我不太方便講，但我可以講的是這個。
cards.why: 拒絕回答但不讓對話斷掉的萬用句。關鍵是 but what I would say is this——立刻補上你願意給的東西，讓「不能講」聽起來像交換而不是關門。冒號式的 this 還製造了懸念，對方通常會等你講完。
swaps: I can't get into numbers, but here's the shape of it.
That one I'll have to keep internal — what I can share is...
Not something I can detail, but directionally...
cards.pmNote: 保密與合作不衝突：講不了「什麼」的時候，可以講「怎麼想」。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

cards.pattern: The product you and I have been using for years isn't actually the product we're building for other people.
cards.quote: Often, a product that you and I use that we've been using for years isn't actually the product that we're building for other people.
cards.zh: 我們自己用了好幾年的那個產品，其實跟我們正在為別人打造的那個產品，根本不是同一個東西。
cards.why: 用 you and I 把自己也框進去，讓「你們搞錯了」變成「我們都搞錯了」，這是英文會議裡拆同事盲點最不傷人的方式。isn't actually 的 actually 負責製造反轉的重音。
swaps: We're not the user anymore.
Our version of the product doesn't exist for new users.
Power users and new users are using different products.
cards.pmNote: adjacent user theory：下一批用戶就在你現有用戶圈外一圈，要用他們的帳號、他們的手機去用產品。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

cards.pattern: Probably my time at [X] was probably not my best time.
cards.quote: Probably for me, I think my time at Instacart was probably not my best time. I think I went to Instacart with a vision of what I felt the product could be, but I was not aware or in tune with what the DNA of the company was.
cards.zh: 對我來說，Instacart 那段大概是我狀態最不好的時候。我帶著一套「產品應該長成什麼樣」的想像進去，卻沒真的看懂那家公司的 DNA 是什麼。
cards.why: 承認失敗時連用三層緩衝（probably / I think / probably），是英文裡把「我搞砸了」講得可以呼吸的方法——重點還是講出來了，但沒有跪下。not my best time 也比 I failed 保留了尊嚴。
swaps: That wasn't my strongest chapter.
I didn't do my best work there, honestly.
That one didn't go the way I wanted.
cards.pmNote: 空降失敗常常不是能力問題，是「公司此刻需要的型」跟你想給的型不合。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

cards.quote: Whenever you talk to people who are at the company, they're always try to tell you the best version of the company. It's on you to triangulate that information, but you need both sides.
cards.zh: 你去問還在公司裡的人，他們永遠給你公司最好的那個版本。要交叉比對是你自己的責任，但兩邊的說法你都得聽到。
cards.why: triangulate 是英文裡談「多方求證」的專業字，一個字取代一整句解釋，用了就顯得資深。It's on you to... 也是把責任明確歸位的固定說法，比 you should 有力。
swaps: You have to cross-check it yourself.
Neither side is the truth — the truth is between them.
Take both accounts and triangulate.
cards.pmNote: 換工作前做 understand work：在職的人給最佳版本，離職的人給最差版本，兩邊都要。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

cards.pattern: They don't reach their goals — they fall to the level of their systems.
cards.quote: People and teams don't really reach... They don't actually reach their goals. They fall to the level of their systems.
cards.zh: 人跟團隊其實不會「達成」目標。他們會掉到自己系統的水準。
cards.why: rise to goals / fall to systems 是一組刻意的動詞對比：目標往上、系統往下，一句話就把「靠意志力」打成幻覺。fall to the level of 這種結構台灣人幾乎不會主動用，但講出來份量很重。
swaps: You don't rise to your goals; you sink to your process.
The system sets the ceiling, not the ambition.
Goals are direction; systems are the actual output.
cards.pmNote: OKR 訂得再漂亮，交付水準還是由流程與節奏決定。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

cards.pattern: You just feel like you're running through mud — still doing so much work, and it's not having as much impact.
cards.quote: You just feel more like you're running through mud like, "Ah, God, we're just still doing so much work and it's not having as much of an impact."
cards.zh: 那種感覺比較像在爛泥裡跑步——「天啊，我們明明還是做了這麼多事，但影響力就是沒以前大。」
cards.why: running through mud 把「說不出哪裡卡住」的模糊感覺變成一個畫面，是描述問題但還沒診斷時最好用的開場。後面直接引一句團隊心聲，比自己下結論更容易讓大家點頭。
swaps: Everything takes more effort for less result.
It feels like we're pushing harder and moving slower.
Same input, thinner output.
cards.pmNote: 成長減速通常不是斷崖，是逐月變鈍——所以要看趨勢，不是看單月。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: I wouldn't say it's a checklist, but there's a series of questions I ask, in this order.
cards.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
cards.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。
cards.why: I wouldn't say X, but there's Y 是先擋掉聽者可能的誤解（「又是一張清單」）再上菜，這種自我修正在英文簡報裡非常常見。in this order 一講出來，就把你的框架從清單升級成邏輯鏈。
swaps: It's less a framework than a sequence.
Not a checklist — an order of operations.
These questions only work in this order.
cards.pmNote: 診斷順序本身就是價值：留存沒解決前，優化 top of funnel 是浪費。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: Just on an emotional level, you've got to go: wait a minute, that's terrible.
cards.quote: And after all of that, which clearly means they wanted it to work, they're like, "No, bye." What? Just on an emotional level, you got to go, "Wait a minute, that's terrible."
cards.zh: 經歷了這一整串——這明明代表他們很想讓它成功——結果他們說「不用了，掰」。蛤？光是情緒上你就該有反應：等一下，這超糟的。
cards.why: Just on an emotional level 是一個切換頻道的訊號：我知道等下要講數字，但先讓我們用人的感覺看一次。刻意插入的 What? 是英文口語裡的「情緒標點符號」，中文簡報幾乎不會這樣寫，講出來卻很有感染力。
swaps: Forget the math for a second — how does that feel?
Before we get to the numbers, sit with that.
Purely as a human reaction: that's bad.
cards.pmNote: churn 分析先講一個用戶的完整旅程，再進統計，說服力遠高於先丟百分比。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: There's a different metric I like to use, which keys off an idea people don't appreciate.
cards.quote: So there's a different metric that I like to use, which keys off of this idea that I think, again, people don't appreciate, which is cancellations grow faster than marketing.
cards.zh: 我比較喜歡用另一個指標，它是從一個大家常常沒放在心上的觀念推出來的：取消的成長速度比行銷快。
cards.why: keys off of 是「以⋯⋯為出發點／掛在⋯⋯上」，比 is based on 更口語也更精準。用 people don't appreciate 而不是 people don't know，暗示對方其實聽過但沒當一回事——這個字選得很狠但不失禮。
swaps: I prefer a different number, and it comes from an idea that gets overlooked.
There's a better metric here, built on something people underrate.
I'd swap that metric for one that keys off...
cards.pmNote: 取消率是百分比（指數），行銷獲客是絕對數（線性）——所以流失一定會追上獲客。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: Right — except [關鍵修正], and that's what people don't appreciate.
cards.quote: Right. Except the leaks automatically increase and that's what people don't appreciate.
cards.zh: 對——只是那個破洞會自己愈破愈大，這就是大家沒意識到的地方。
cards.why: 先給一個字的同意（Right.）再用 Except 掉頭，是英文裡修正對方比喻卻不推翻他的標準走法：你的比喻我收下了，我只補一個變數。比 Actually, no 溫和得多，力道一樣。
swaps: Yes — with one wrinkle.
That's right, except for one thing.
Almost. The part that's missing is...
cards.pmNote: leaky bucket 的比喻不完整：洞會隨桶子變大而變大。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: The wrong way is to ask "why did you X?" What you want to say is "what made you X?"
cards.quote: And when you do this, the wrong way is to ask, why did you cancel? What you want to do is say, "What made you cancel?"
cards.zh: 問的時候，錯誤版本是「你為什麼取消？」你要問的是：「是什麼讓你取消的？」
cards.why: why 把矛頭指向人（要他辯護），what made 把矛頭指向事件（要他描述）。同一件事換個提問主語，回收率會翻倍——這是英文裡最值得背下來的一個提問改寫。
swaps: What led to that decision?
What happened that made this stop working?
Walk me through what changed.
cards.pmNote: 訪談把 why 換成 what/how，可以避開受訪者的自我合理化。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: And that is never, ever the reason. How do I know? Because [證據].
cards.quote: And that is never, ever, ever the reason. How do I know? Because they already looked at your homepage, read all the stuff, saw what you promised, looked at the pricing page and decided to buy it.
cards.zh: 那絕對、絕對不會是真正的原因。我怎麼知道？因為他們早就看過你的首頁、讀完那些內容、看過你承諾了什麼、也看過定價頁，然後決定買了。
cards.why: How do I know? 是自己替聽眾問出質疑，再自己回答——等於把對方的反駁權先借走。搭配前面刻意重複的 never, ever, ever，先立強論點再馬上補證據，順序不能顛倒。
swaps: And I'm confident about that. Why? Because...
That's never it. Here's how we know.
It can't be — look at what they already did.
cards.pmNote: 「太貴」是 proximate cause，不是真因；他們既然買過，就代表當時不覺得貴。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: That's only true if you only look at [表層的東西].
cards.quote: Now see, that's incorrect. That's only true if you only look at the proximate thing, which is project ended.
cards.zh: 你看，這就不對了。那句話只有在你只看最表面那層——也就是「專案結束了」——的時候才成立。
cards.why: 只有在⋯⋯的時候才成立，是反駁時保留對方顏面的最佳結構：不說你錯，說你的成立條件太窄。That's only true if 幾乎可以套進任何會議爭論，非常值得背。
swaps: That holds only under one assumption.
That's true in the narrow case — not generally.
It's right as far as it goes.
cards.pmNote: 「專案結束」常常是你的產品沒讓專案成功的結果，不是外生原因。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: If you don't know what to do, or all else being equal, then focus on [X].
cards.quote: And then the last thing I would say about this detection is if you don't know what to do, or all else being equal, then focus on onboarding.
cards.zh: 關於怎麼提早偵測，我最後想講的是：如果你不知道該做什麼，或其他條件都差不多，那就去弄 onboarding。
cards.why: all else being equal 是英文裡給「預設值建議」的專業說法：我不是說這一定最好，我是說沒有更好理由時就選它。給建議時加上這句，責任分配立刻清楚。
swaps: When in doubt, default to onboarding.
Absent a stronger signal, I'd start there.
If nothing else is obviously bigger, do this.
cards.pmNote: 多數產品的流失集中在前 30 天，所以 onboarding 的邊際報酬最高。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: Time out. What you're going to do is [X]. You just told me [證據].
cards.quote: And I'm like, "Time out. What you're going to do is raise prices again. You just told me you 12x-ed the price and nothing observable changed."
cards.zh: 我就說：「等一下。你接下來要做的是再漲一次價。你剛剛才跟我說你把價格拉了十二倍，結果什麼都沒變。」
cards.why: Time out. 借自球場暫停，是打斷別人卻不失禮的兩個字，比 Hold on 更果斷、比 Sorry to interrupt 更有權威。後面接 You just told me...，用對方自己剛講的話當武器，對方無從反駁。
swaps: Hold on — back up.
Wait. You just said something important.
Let me stop you there, because of what you just told me.
cards.pmNote: 漲價後訊號沒變化＝你還沒碰到價格上限，先別急著把利潤花掉。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.quote: The support's not going to be good enough. They probably don't have good governance policies or other things that we need. Whether that's true or not, this is what it looks like.
cards.zh: 他們的客服大概不夠好、治理政策大概也不合我們要求。這是不是事實不重要——重點是看起來就是這樣。
cards.why: 把「事實」和「觀感」明確切開，同時避免自己被拖進「到底是不是真的」的辯論。這句在討論定價、品牌、招募觀感時特別好用：你不用同意，你只需要承認別人是這樣看的。
swaps: Fair or not, that's the perception.
Right or wrong, that's how it reads.
I'm not saying it's accurate — I'm saying it's what they see.
cards.pmNote: 定價太低會被大企業讀成「不夠成熟」，這跟產品實力無關，是訊號問題。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: [X] is not just [表面的那個東西]. It's easy to think that, but [Y] is just as important.
cards.quote: Also, price is not just the number on the webpage. It's easy to think that, but how it's structured is just as important, how the product's positioned is just as important.
cards.zh: 還有，價格不是只有網頁上那個數字。很容易這樣以為，但怎麼收費、產品怎麼定位，重要程度完全一樣。
cards.why: It's easy to think that 是先替對方的誤解找台階（誰都會這樣想），再擴大定義。重複使用 just as important 兩次，是英文口語裡用平行結構堆重量的方式，中文照抄會覺得囉唆，英文聽起來反而扎實。
swaps: Pricing is more than the number — it's the structure.
Easy assumption, but packaging matters just as much.
The number is the smallest part of pricing.
cards.pmNote: 定價＝數字 × 計價單位 × 定位敘事，只調數字通常沒用。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: What does [老闆] want to hear more — [A] or [B]? Both are good, but I know which one is [更關鍵的價值].
cards.quote: What does the CEO want to hear more? Growth or saves money? Both are good, but I know which one is healthier for the company, increases market share, is better competitively.
cards.zh: CEO 比較想聽哪一個：成長，還是省錢？兩個都好，但我知道哪一個對公司比較健康、比較能拉市佔、比較有競爭力。
cards.why: Both are good, but... 是不否定任何人的前提下做排序，讓被否掉的那方沒有失分。I know which one is 語氣自信但不指定答案，把最後一步留給聽眾自己走完，說服力更高。
swaps: Both matter. One matters more to this audience.
Which story lands better upstairs?
Same result, very different sentence.
cards.pmNote: 同一個成效，包裝成「幫你成長」比「幫你省錢」能賣到高一個量級的價格。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: I don't want to go off on too much of a tangent, but the thing you have to remember is [X].
cards.quote: It gets easier. I don't want to go off too much of a tangent, but the thing you have to remember is that pricing is not this knob that you can turn separate from the rest of your strategy.
cards.zh: 是會變簡單。我不想扯太遠，但有件事一定要記得：定價不是一個可以單獨轉的旋鈕，它跟整套策略是連在一起的。
cards.why: 先聲明自己要離題，等於買了離題的許可證——這比默默離題安全太多。not a knob you can turn separate from... 用旋鈕的意象講「牽一髮動全身」，比 it's interconnected 好懂也好記。
swaps: Slight detour, but it matters here.
One caveat before we move on.
Quick aside — I'll keep it short.
cards.pmNote: 漲價會換到不同客層，隨之而來的是新的合規、整合、服務需求，不是單一參數。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.quote: It's like, okay, it's better for us, but sorry, we have an equation where it has to be better for us and better for the customer. Sorry, it's an and.
cards.zh: 好，這對我們是比較好沒錯——但抱歉，我們的算式是：對我們好「而且」對客戶好。抱歉，這是個 and。
cards.why: 把邏輯運算子當名詞用（it's an and，不是 or），是英文裡把抽象原則變成一個可指認物件的高招。前面兩個 sorry 不是道歉，是強調「這條線我不打算談判」。
swaps: Both conditions, not either.
It's not one or the other — it's both, or no.
That's an AND, not an OR.
cards.pmNote: 內部提案常偷換成「對公司好所以對客戶好」，把它拆成兩個獨立條件就會現形。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: You could say it's obvious, but are you acting like it's true? Often we don't.
cards.quote: So this is why you could say it's obvious to say this or that, but are you acting like this is true? Often we don't.
cards.zh: 所以你當然可以說這些都是常識，但你的行為有把它當真嗎？我們常常沒有。
cards.why: 先替對方講出「這我早就知道」，再問行為，讓對方無法用「知道」擋掉。結尾把主詞從 you 換成 we，一秒把指控變成共同檢討——這個人稱切換是這句能被接受的關鍵。
swaps: We all know this. Our calendars say otherwise.
Knowing it and acting on it are different things.
If we believed that, what would we be doing differently?
cards.pmNote: 檢查一個團隊是否真的相信某個原則，看排程與預算，不看會議紀錄。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: Is that true, or is that the kind of thing [某群人] uses to make [某群人] do X even when they shouldn't?
cards.quote: We all have heard the phrase, "If you're not growing, you're dying." Is that true or is that the kind of thing that investors use to make founders grow even when they shouldn't?
cards.zh: 我們都聽過那句「不成長就是等死」。那到底是真的，還是投資人拿來逼創辦人在不該成長的時候硬成長的說法？
cards.why: 不直接說某句話是謊言，而是問它「服務誰的利益」——這是拆解權威說法最鋒利也最安全的角度。Is that true, or is that the kind of thing... 這個對照句型幾乎可以套進任何公司裡的口號。
swaps: Who benefits from us believing that?
Is that a principle, or a fundraising line?
True, or just useful to someone?
cards.pmNote: 公司內部流傳的「常識」要問一句 cui bono——它常常是某個角色的利益被說成公理。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: I don't mean to overstate this, and I don't claim there's one right answer — but surely this is the right kind of question.
cards.quote: So again, I don't mean to overstate this, and I certainly don't mean to claim that there's some answer that's right for everybody, of course, but surely this is the right kind of question.
cards.zh: 我不想把這件事講得太滿，也絕對不是說有一個答案適用所有人——但這絕對是該問的那類問題。
cards.why: 連下三道限縮（不誇大／沒有通解／當然），再用 but surely 把僅剩的那一點立場穩穩守住。這是英文裡「我讓很多、但這一點不讓」的經典節奏，主張其實一點都沒縮水。
swaps: I'll stop short of prescribing — but the question stands.
No universal answer here. The question is still the right one.
I'm hedging on the answer, not on whether to ask.
cards.pmNote: 策略討論裡，「這是不是對的問題」往往比「答案是什麼」更值得先吵清楚。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: If you tried to find a common thread through all of this, it comes back to [一件事].
cards.quote: I think if you tried to find a common thread throughout all this stuff about growth, it comes back to the customer getting value.
cards.zh: 如果你想在這一整套成長的東西裡找一條共同的線，最後都會回到同一件事：客戶有沒有真的拿到價值。
cards.why: common thread 是英文收尾時最常用的意象（一條穿過所有珠子的線），比 the main point 更有結構感。用 if you tried to... 開頭，把結論說成邀請聽眾一起找出來的，而不是你單方面宣布的。
swaps: The through-line here is...
If there's one thing under all of this, it's...
Everything we've said reduces to one question.
cards.pmNote: 收尾要給一個能覆蓋全部分支的判準，聽眾才帶得走。
cards.episode: 5 questions to ask when your product stops growing | Jason Cohen (2x unicorn founder)

cards.pattern: Communication isn't about conveying a message — it's about conveying it so the listener receives it, understands it, and remembers it.
cards.quote: Communication isn't about being able to convey a message. It's about being able to convey a message in a way that the listener receives it and understands it and remembers it. And that's really hard to do.
cards.zh: 溝通不是把訊息送出去。溝通是用一種方式送出去，讓聽的人接收到、聽懂、而且記得住。這超級難。
cards.why: X isn't about A, it's about B 是最泛用的重新定義句型；這裡厲害的是 B 用了三個動詞遞進（receives / understands / remembers），一路把標準往上加。and...and... 不用逗號分隔，是英文口語刻意堆疊的節奏。
swaps: Sending isn't the same as landing.
It's not what you said — it's what they kept.
The bar is retention, not transmission.
cards.pmNote: 簡報的成功指標不是「講完了」，是三天後對方還轉述得出來。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.pattern: My one learning there that has stuck with me — and I think it works for other people too — is [X].
cards.quote: My one learning there that has stuck with me, and I think can work for other people too, is that it's not just about doing things that actually matter, and learning. It's about being able to tell the story.
cards.zh: 那段經驗裡有一個一直留在我身上的體悟，我覺得對別人也適用：重點不只是去做真正重要的事、去學東西，還要能把這件事講成一個故事。
cards.why: my one learning 用單數，等於承諾只講一件事，聽者立刻放心。中間插一句 and I think can work for other people too，把個人經驗擴權成通則，卻用 I think 保留退路——這個組合在分享心得時非常安全。
swaps: The one thing I took from that — and I think it generalizes — is...
If I kept one lesson from it, it's this.
This might just be me, but it's held up.
cards.pmNote: 績效面談的兩個環節：做出成果，以及讓成果被理解成成果。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.pattern: We did [大成績]. It wasn't me personally. I think that's important to share.
cards.quote: So we deployed historic amounts of money in the campaign. It wasn't me, Gina, personally. I think that's important to share.
cards.zh: 我們在那場競選裡砸下的錢是歷史級的。不是我 Gina 個人在砸。我覺得這點必須講清楚。
cards.why: 主持人把功勞放大時，最俐落的處理是先接住成績（we did）再切割個人（not me personally），最後用 I think that's important to share 說明你為什麼要糾正——把謙虛升級成誠信。
swaps: That was the team, not me.
I want to be accurate about my part in that.
Credit where it's due — I owned a slice of it.
cards.pmNote: 誇大自己的貢獻範圍是信譽最快折損的方式，主動校正反而加分。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.pattern: My best bet for adding value was not to be another cook in the kitchen, but to move to [沒人在管的那一步].
cards.quote: I realized that my best bet in terms of actually adding value was not to be another cook in the kitchen trying to figure that out, but to move into the next step of the journey, which nobody was paying attention to.
cards.zh: 我意識到，我真正能加值的方式，不是再擠進廚房當第 N 個廚師，而是往旅程的下一步走——那一步根本沒人在顧。
cards.why: another cook in the kitchen 借自 too many cooks 的諺語，用來自嘲「我加進去只是添亂」，比 I wasn't needed there 有風度。which nobody was paying attention to 則是機會論證：不是我厲害，是那裡空著。
swaps: There were already enough people on that. I went where nobody was.
My leverage wasn't there — it was one step downstream.
I looked for the unowned part of the funnel.
cards.pmNote: 找影響力先找「沒有 owner 的那一步」，通常就在大家搶的那一步後面。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.pattern: None of this is going to blow anyone's minds — it's just best practices. But it's easy to overlook when [你正忙著別的].
cards.quote: None of this is going to blow anyone's minds, I think, because it's very best practices. But it's easy to overlook when you're so focused on so many different steps of a process.
cards.zh: 這些應該不會讓誰驚呆，因為都是很基本的最佳實務。但當你同時盯著流程裡一大堆步驟時，就是很容易漏掉。
cards.why: 先自貶（不會讓你驚呆）再解釋為什麼還是值得聽（因為你會漏掉），這個順序讓平凡的建議不會被當成廢話。blow anyone's minds 這種誇張說法用在否定句裡，是很典型的英文自我調降。
swaps: This is basic, and that's exactly why it gets skipped.
Nothing clever here — just the part everyone forgets.
Obvious in hindsight, invisible in the moment.
cards.pmNote: 轉換率的大幅提升常來自基本功（行動裝置優化、按鈕在首屏），不是新點子。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.pattern: That sounds cliché. I get it. But I really mean it, because [具體理由].
cards.quote: That sounds cliche. I think a lot of founders and startup people like to talk about the mission, and I get it, and I think it's real. But I really mean it.
cards.zh: 我知道這聽起來很老套。很多創辦人都愛談使命，我懂，我也覺得那是真的。但我是真心這樣講。
cards.why: 要講一個已經被講爛的主張時，先自己說它老套、再說 I get it（我懂你為什麼翻白眼），最後用 But I really mean it 重新申請信任。這一套三步在英文裡幾乎是固定程序。
swaps: I know how this sounds.
Everyone says this. I'm going to say it anyway.
Cliché, yes — and still true here.
cards.pmNote: 使命不是文宣，它是決策時的排除條件——會擋掉哪些短期賺錢的選項。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.pattern: I have survivorship bias, but I really believe in this.
cards.quote: So I got to ride in a plane that survived. So I have, oh, it's called survivor bias. I have survivor bias, but I really believe in this.
cards.zh: 我坐的是那架平安飛回來的飛機。所以我有——對，叫倖存者偏誤。我有倖存者偏誤，但我還是真的相信這件事。
cards.why: 自己先把可能被拿來攻擊你的偏誤講出來，對方就沒有那張牌可以打了。but I really believe in this 表示你知道風險仍然選擇這個立場——承認偏誤不等於撤回主張，這一點很多人搞混。
swaps: Caveat: I only saw the winners.
I'm biased by my own sample, and I still hold this.
Take this with the survivorship discount.
cards.pmNote: 引用自家成功案例時主動標記倖存者偏誤，論點反而更耐打。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.quote: I was just talking to an entrepreneur this morning, he was like, "Oh, we were able to hit a 10-cent CAC." And I'm like, "Yeah, but that grows."
cards.zh: 我今天早上才跟一個創業者聊，他說「我們把 CAC 壓到十美分欸」。我就說：「對啊，但那個數字會漲。」
cards.why: Yeah, but 是英文裡最短的反駁：先給一個字的同意權，再馬上加限定。這裡搭配 that grows 三個字就把對方的好消息重新定義成暫時現象，經濟到極點。
swaps: Sure — for now.
True today. Won't be true at 10x.
That's the early-adopter price.
cards.pmNote: 低 CAC 通常是低垂果實的價格；規模一擴大，邊際獲客成本一定往上。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.pattern: I really believe that — I don't believe. I think we all know at this point that [X].
cards.quote: And the third thing is that I really believe that... I don't believe. I think we all know at this point that the most important thing for the growth of anything tech is retention.
cards.zh: 第三件事是我真的相信——不，不是相信。我覺得到這個時間點大家都已經知道了：科技產品成長最重要的就是留存。
cards.why: 當場把 I believe 收回改成 we all know，是把一個私人意見升格成共識的即時操作。這種自我修正在英文裡不但不減分，反而顯得誠實又有份量——因為修正的方向是往上，不是往下。
swaps: This isn't a belief at this point — it's settled.
Let me put that more strongly.
Actually, that's not an opinion.
cards.pmNote: 留存不是「留住用戶」的技巧問題，是「這東西到底有沒有價值」的證據。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.pattern: An obsession for [X]. Again, sounds obvious but isn't.
cards.quote: An obsession for the product. Again, sounds obvious but isn't.
cards.zh: 對產品的偏執。一樣，聽起來理所當然，其實不是。
cards.why: sounds obvious but isn't 五個字就完成了「我知道你想跳過這段，別跳」的攔截，是英文簡報裡效率最高的一個小句。省略主詞（It sounds...）讓它更像口語重音。
swaps: Obvious on paper, rare in practice.
Sounds basic. Almost nobody does it.
Everyone agrees with this and few live it.
cards.pmNote: 抄競品的介面等於抄答案，抄不到的是背後每天看數據、提假設的過程。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.quote: So I actually ended up not letting the team run this experiment for six months so that we focus on lower hanging fruit. So that's a mistake on my end.
cards.zh: 所以我其實壓著這個實驗六個月沒讓團隊做，因為想先撿低垂的果實。這是我的錯。
cards.why: on my end 是把責任精確劃到自己那一端，比 my fault 冷靜、比 we made a mistake 誠實。先講完整決策脈絡再認錯，聽起來是判斷失誤而不是能力不足。
swaps: That call was mine, and it was wrong.
I got that one wrong.
That delay is on me.
cards.pmNote: 用 ROI 排序實驗會系統性地低估「要先建基礎設施」的那一類機會。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.pattern: If we had just [做了那件小事], we would have all known [結果].
cards.quote: We were like, "You know what? If we had just tested that, we would have all known that this was a super lame badge." And I was like, "Why are we not testing our experiments?"
cards.zh: 我們就說：「欸，我們如果當初有自己測一下，早就知道這個徽章有夠遜。」我就問：「所以我們為什麼沒有在測自己的實驗？」
cards.why: 第三條件句（If we had...we would have）是英文檢討會的預設時態，用它把「早就知道」講出來，語氣是遺憾不是指責。結尾把個案問題升級成制度問題（Why are we not...），這一跳才是重點。
swaps: One dogfood session would have caught this.
We'd have known in five minutes.
The cheapest test we didn't run.
cards.pmNote: 檢討要問「這是個案還是一類」——一類就要改流程，不是改這一次。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.pattern: It doesn't matter if you think [爭議立場]. Do you think [沒人會反對的事]? Most people would say yes.
cards.quote: It doesn't matter if you think Bloomberg or Trump should be president. Do you think everyone should have access to great education? Most people would say yes.
cards.zh: 你覺得該讓 Bloomberg 還是 Trump 當總統，都無所謂。你覺得每個人都該有機會受好的教育嗎？大多數人會說會。
cards.why: 先主動作廢一個會讓人分裂的爭議，再問一個幾乎人人會點頭的問題，等於替敘事清出一塊公共地。這是找共同立足點（common ground）的標準操作，跨部門說服時特別好用。
swaps: Set aside where you land on X. Can we agree on Y?
Whatever your view on that, this part is uncontroversial.
Different politics, same answer here.
cards.pmNote: 使命敘事要選一個「幾乎沒人反對」的層級，才會被引用、被轉述。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.pattern: We asked of every piece of copy: could this have been written by any other company?
cards.quote: We constantly looked at every copy we wrote and asked, "Could this have been written by other companies? Could this have been any other company or is it Duolingo? What makes this Duolingo?"
cards.zh: 我們每寫一段文案都會回頭問：「這段別家公司寫得出來嗎？這可以是任何一家公司，還是它就是 Duolingo？哪裡讓它是 Duolingo？」
cards.why: 把抽象的「品牌調性」變成一個可以當場判定的是非題，是這句最強的地方。三個問句層層收窄（別家能寫嗎 → 是誰 → 哪裡是），示範了怎麼把模糊標準拆成可執行的檢查。
swaps: Would this pass as anyone else's?
Swap our logo out — does it still work? Then it's not ours.
What in this sentence is only us?
cards.pmNote: 品牌一致性的可操作檢查：任何一句對外文案，換掉 logo 後還成立就代表沒差異化。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.pattern: I haven't met the person who does [X] and they're fantastic. I definitely don't want to take anything away from their work.
cards.quote: Look, I haven't met the person who does a TikTok and they're fantastic. I definitely don't want to demerit their work. It's awesome, I don't think it's easy to do.
cards.zh: 老實說我沒見過負責 TikTok 的那個人，但他們超強。我完全不想貶低他們的工作，那真的很厲害，也一點都不好做。
cards.why: 在你要說「其實不只是靠那個人」之前，先花兩句把那個人捧好——這樣後面的論點才不會被聽成搶功。Look, 開頭是英文口語裡「我要講實話了」的信號詞，語氣親近而不失禮。
swaps: Full credit to them — and there's more to it.
That's genuinely hard, and it's not the whole story.
Not taking anything away from them, but...
cards.pmNote: 拆解別家的成功時先給執行者應得的肯定，你的結構性分析才聽得進去。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.pattern: So [名字], I don't see it as a [他用的詞], because [你的版本].
cards.quote: So Lenny, I don't see it as a pivot because as we were joking in the beginning, I've been an employee, I was an operator there at early stage startups and now I'm a founder and I'm a VC.
cards.zh: Lenny，我不覺得那是轉彎——就像我們一開始開玩笑講的，我當過員工、在早期新創當過操盤手，現在是創辦人，也是投資人。
cards.why: 反對別人的用字（而不是內容）時，先喊對方名字會讓語氣從對立變成對話。I don't see it as X 是把分歧定位成視角差異，比 that's not a pivot 少了糾正的意味。
swaps: I'd frame it differently.
I wouldn't call it that, actually.
That's not how it felt from the inside.
cards.pmNote: 別人替你的職涯或專案下標籤時，當場換一個字，敘事的所有權就回到你身上。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.pattern: What are you world-class at, and how do you know? The second part is almost more important.
cards.quote: And then I would say, what are you world-class at and how do you know that you're at that? And the second part is almost more important.
cards.zh: 然後我會問：你在什麼事情上是世界級的？你怎麼知道自己是？第二個問題其實更重要。
cards.why: 問完之後自己標記哪一半才是重點（The second part is almost more important），是面試官/教練把注意力導到證據上的技巧。almost 這個副詞讓判斷留了餘地，聽起來像思考不像評分。
swaps: What's your edge, and what's the evidence?
How would you prove that to a stranger?
The 'how do you know' is the real question.
cards.pmNote: 面試看的不是自評高低，是對方有沒有用可驗證的方式評估自己。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

cards.pattern: And it stunned me into silence, because essentially that is and was [X] — and that forced me to pivot my thinking.
cards.quote: And it stunned me into silence because essentially that is and was SEO, and then that forced me to really pivot my thinking around what SEO might be.
cards.zh: 那句話讓我當場說不出話，因為 SEO 本來、現在也確實就是那樣。也就是那一刻逼我重新想：SEO 到底可以是什麼。
cards.why: 承認被外行問倒，卻把它講成自己思考升級的起點——這是把丟臉的事變成資歷的標準敘事。that is and was 用現在式加過去式並排，強調「不是他誤解，是真的一直如此」。
swaps: I didn't have an answer, and that was the point.
That question rearranged how I think about this.
He was right, and it changed my whole approach.
cards.pmNote: 客戶問「那我為什麼要付你錢」，通常是你的價值主張還停在交付項目層級。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.pattern: Actually, it's not that [他的說法] — it's that [你的說法].
cards.quote: Actually, it's not that it's harder to find, your stuff becomes less relevant. And that's the part about SEO that I'm excited about.
cards.zh: 其實不是變得比較難被找到，是你的東西變得沒那麼相關了。而這正是 SEO 讓我興奮的地方。
cards.why: It's not that A, it's that B 是最乾淨的修正句型：不否定對方觀察到的現象，只換掉他的因果解釋。後面立刻補一句自己為什麼興奮，讓糾正的落點是正面的，不會冷場。
swaps: The problem isn't visibility — it's relevance.
I'd put it slightly differently.
Close, but the mechanism is different.
cards.pmNote: AI 摘要吃掉的是 top-of-funnel 的資訊型查詢，不是有購買意圖的中段查詢。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.pattern: Transparently, I thought this was going to be [誇張的預測]. We have not seen it yet.
cards.quote: Transparently, I thought this was going to be an apocalypse. So I shared about a year ago that it's going to be an apocalypse. We have not seen it yet.
cards.zh: 老實說，我本來以為這會是世界末日。我一年前也是這樣公開講的。到目前為止並沒有發生。
cards.why: Transparently 當句首副詞是近年英文職場很流行的誠實信號（比 honestly 更正式一點）。主動翻出自己講錯的舊預測，是建立可信度最貴也最有效的方式——因為多數人不會這樣做。
swaps: To be straight with you, I called this wrong.
I predicted X publicly. It hasn't happened.
Full disclosure: my earlier take was too extreme.
cards.pmNote: 公開修正自己的舊預測，是預測型工作（策略、成長）唯一能累積信譽的方式。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.pattern: If you take all those steps back and look at it from [X] perspective, there's no way that it won't [結果].
cards.quote: So I think if you take all those steps back and you look at this from a journey perspective, there's no way that it won't be impacting search. It's just going to be hard to find.
cards.zh: 所以我覺得，只要你退開幾步、用「使用者旅程」的角度看，它不可能不影響搜尋。只是那個影響很難被指認出來。
cards.why: there's no way that it won't 是雙重否定的強調法，比 it will definitely 更有推理感——像是排除所有其他可能之後剩下的結論。後面立刻自己加上限制（很難被指認），讓強斷言不失分寸。
swaps: I don't see how it doesn't affect search.
Structurally, this has to show up somewhere.
The effect is certain; the measurement isn't.
cards.pmNote: 指標沒動不等於沒影響——同時期的其他變動可能把訊號蓋掉了。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.quote: Yeah. I actually have a better one for you.
cards.zh: 對。不過我有一個更好的例子可以給你。
cards.why: 先用 Yeah 接住對方的總結，再用 I actually have a better one 把發言權要回來——不是打斷，是加碼。for you 讓這個動作變成給予而不是搶話，是英文口語裡很小但很好用的軟化。
swaps: Can I give you a sharper example?
There's a cleaner case I'd rather use.
Actually, let me swap in a better one.
cards.pmNote: 會議裡要把討論拉回你想講的案例，用「我有一個更好的例子」比反駁對方的例子有效。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.pattern: Step one is the step that almost everyone misses, which is [X].
cards.quote: I think step one is the step that almost everyone misses on SEO, which is be the user. Try to understand who your user is.
cards.zh: 我覺得第一步就是幾乎每個人都跳過的那一步：去當那個使用者。先弄懂你的使用者是誰。
cards.why: 宣告「這是大家都漏掉的第一步」會讓一個很基本的建議聽起來像內幕。which is 後面接一個超短的祈使句（be the user），長句鋪陳、短句落地，是英文口語製造份量的標準節奏。
swaps: The part everyone skips is step one.
Before any of that: be the user.
Nobody starts here, and everybody should.
cards.pmNote: 做 SEO 前先問「使用者會搜什麼字」，答不出來就代表這個渠道不成立。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.pattern: If you can't answer the question about [X], then don't do [Y].
cards.quote: So if you can't answer the question about what is it that someone's going to do a search on, then don't do SEO, because SEO is about appealing to that user.
cards.zh: 所以如果你答不出「別人會搜什麼」這個問題，那就不要做 SEO——因為 SEO 就是在對那個使用者說話。
cards.why: 把「不要做」綁在一個可檢驗的前置條件上，讓拒絕變成規則而不是意見——對方不是被你否決，是沒通過門檻。這種條件式的 no 在跨部門擋需求時特別安全。
swaps: No answer to that question, no channel.
If we can't name the query, we shouldn't fund this.
That's the entry test. We don't pass it.
cards.pmNote: 每個獲客渠道都該有一個 go/no-go 的前置問題，答不出來就先不投資源。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.pattern: We have to really put away the myth that [X], because it's absolutely not.
cards.quote: So we have to really put away the myth that SEO is free because it's absolutely not free. There's a cost in time. There's a cost in resources.
cards.zh: 我們得先把「SEO 是免費的」這個迷思收起來，因為它絕對不免費。有時間成本，也有資源成本。
cards.why: put away the myth 把一個信念講成可以收進抽屜的東西，動作感很強，比 debunk 口語。接著用兩個對稱短句列成本，讓「不免費」不只是口號而有清單。
swaps: Let's retire the idea that this is free.
There's no such thing as a free channel.
It's not free — it's just not invoiced.
cards.pmNote: 「免費渠道」的成本藏在人力與機會成本裡，評估時要跟付費渠道用同一把尺。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.pattern: I hate to use the words "it depends," because when consultants say it depends, they're throwing their hands up.
cards.quote: So those will be custom for anything. And I hate to use the word, it depends because I think whenever consultants say it depends, they're just throwing their hands up and saying, "I don't really know."
cards.zh: 這些每家都不一樣。我很不想講「看情況」，因為顧問一講「看情況」，通常就是兩手一攤說「我其實不知道」。
cards.why: 先自我批評你即將要用的說法，再用它——這樣聽眾就不會覺得你在敷衍。throwing their hands up 是「投降式攤手」的動作意象，比 avoiding the question 生動且不點名任何人。
swaps: I know how 'it depends' sounds, so let me give you the variables.
That answer is a cop-out unless I tell you on what.
It depends — and here's exactly on what.
cards.pmNote: 回答「看情況」時一定要接著列出決定因素，否則就是沒回答。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.pattern: Total waste of time. I mean, unless there's a reason for it.
cards.quote: Yeah, total waste of time. Yeah, I mean, unless there's a reason for it. So if you're a media company and traffic means that that number keeps going up, then yes, it matters.
cards.zh: 對，純粹浪費時間。嗯，除非真的有理由啦。如果你是媒體公司、流量就是那個一路往上的數字，那當然有意義。
cards.why: 先給一句極短的重判（total waste of time），再用 unless 開一扇小門——這個先重後鬆的順序，讓立場清楚但不絕對。台灣人通常會反過來先鋪一堆條件，結果沒人記得結論。
swaps: Not worth doing — unless you're in this one case.
I'd cut it. The exception is...
Waste of effort, with one caveat.
cards.pmNote: 流量只有在它就是商業模式（媒體）時才是目標指標，其他情況都要換成轉換。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.pattern: It's not a statistically significant survey, but [結果] is fairly indicative — which surprises me.
cards.quote: It's not a statistically significant survey in general, but it will never go to 99% and one. That's fairly indicative that people are clicking the links, which surprises me.
cards.zh: 這份調查在統計上不算顯著，但它也不可能是 99 比 1。這蠻能說明大家真的有在點那些連結——這讓我有點意外。
cards.why: 承認樣本不夠好，卻指出「再不準也不會差到反轉結論」，是弱數據的正確用法。fairly indicative 這種降級的形容詞（不是 proves），加上結尾坦承結果跟自己預期相反，讓可信度反而更高。
swaps: Not rigorous, but directionally hard to ignore.
The sample's weak; the gap isn't.
I wouldn't publish this, but I'd act on it.
cards.pmNote: 小樣本可以推翻極端假設，不能拿來做精確估計——講清楚它能做什麼就不算誤用。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.pattern: It's funny that everyone says [A] and at the same time thinks [與 A 矛盾的 B].
cards.quote: It's funny that everyone complained about Google as this really, really smart, all-knowing LLM, and at the same time, they think they're dumb enough to fall for these guest posts.
cards.zh: 很好笑的是，大家一邊抱怨 Google 是那種超級聰明、什麼都知道的 LLM，一邊又覺得它笨到會被這些客座文章騙過去。
cards.why: 指出對方兩個信念互相打架，是最難反駁的一種反駁——因為攻擊的不是事實而是一致性。用 It's funny that 開頭，把嘲諷包在幽默裡，不會直接變成人身攻擊。
swaps: We can't have it both ways.
Those two beliefs can't both be true.
Pick one: they're smart, or they're fooled by this.
cards.pmNote: 碰到互相矛盾的團隊共識，先把兩句話並排唸出來，通常不需要再多論證。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.quote: Yes, there are nuances. But for the most part, you get from most... Zero to 10, you can get to step eight by just doing the best practices.
cards.zh: 對，是有很多細節。但大多數情況下，從 0 到 10，你光靠基本功就能走到第 8。
cards.why: Yes, there are nuances. But for the most part... 是應付「你講得太簡化了」這種質疑的萬用組合：一句話承認複雜度，再用比例（for the most part）把主導權拿回來。搭配 0 到 10 的量化說法特別有說服力。
swaps: Sure, edge cases exist. The 80% is straightforward.
Granted, it's more complex. It's not that much more complex.
Yes — and the basics still get you most of the way.
cards.pmNote: 把一個領域講得神秘會阻礙團隊自己動手；先給 80% 的簡化版比較實際。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.pattern: Yes, so I am biased. I think [立場].
cards.quote: Yes, so I am biased. I think they should have the right people give them advice on SEO.
cards.zh: 對，我確實有利益關係。但我還是覺得他們應該找對的人來給 SEO 建議。
cards.why: 主持人先說「你當然會偏向這個答案」，最俐落的回應是直接認下來（Yes, so I am biased），不辯解。認完之後照樣講立場，聽眾反而會自己替你的話打折而不是全盤否定。
swaps: Conflict of interest noted — here's my view anyway.
I have skin in this, so discount accordingly.
Fair, I'm not neutral on this one.
cards.pmNote: 有利益衝突時主動揭露，比等別人指出來便宜太多。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.pattern: We talked about [A], but we didn't talk about [B].
cards.quote: So I think we talked about how to decide whether to resource SEO, but we didn't talk about how to understand what the expectations are from SEO.
cards.zh: 我覺得我們談了「要不要投資源做 SEO」，但還沒談「對 SEO 的期待該怎麼設定」。
cards.why: 在會議快結束時盤點「講過什麼／沒講什麼」，是把議程主導權拿回來最自然的方式——你不是要求加時間，你只是指出缺口。這個句型也很適合會議紀錄的開頭。
swaps: One thing we haven't covered is...
We've done the whether. We haven't done the how much.
There's a gap I want to close before we wrap.
cards.pmNote: 會議收尾前主動點名沒被討論到的題目，能避免決策帶著隱形缺口離場。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.pattern: I've never seen [X] get to the truth, but it will help you make a better decision than if you just guess.
cards.quote: I've never seen a product plan get to the truth of what it could do, but it will help you make a better decision than if you just guess.
cards.zh: 我沒看過哪份產品計畫真的算準過它能做到什麼，但它還是會讓你的決定比純用猜的好。
cards.why: 先承認方法不準，再把標準從「準確」換成「比不做好」——這是替一切估算辯護的最強姿勢。better than if you just guess 給了一個誰都同意的比較基準，反對者很難再要求你精準。
swaps: It won't be right. It'll be less wrong than guessing.
The number is fiction; the reasoning isn't.
Directionally useful, precisely wrong.
cards.pmNote: 預測的價值在於逼你把假設寫下來，之後才有東西可以被推翻。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.pattern: I'm not saying [窄的說法]. I'm saying [寬的說法].
cards.quote: So I'm not saying they didn't get the exact monthly number wrong. I'm saying they got it wrong by many factors.
cards.zh: 我不是在說他們只是月份的確切數字抓錯。我是說他們錯了好幾個量級。
cards.why: I'm not saying X, I'm saying Y 是被誤解時最快的校正器：先刪掉對方的版本，再放上自己的。這裡還順手把主張放大了（不是小誤差，是量級誤差），示範了澄清也可以是加強。
swaps: To be precise: it's not off by a bit, it's off by an order of magnitude.
Let me sharpen that.
Not slightly wrong — structurally wrong.
cards.pmNote: 指出估算有誤時要講清楚是「誤差」還是「量級錯誤」，處置方式完全不同。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.pattern: They're helpful. But I don't think they're a source of actual truth.
cards.quote: So they're helpful. Tools are helpful. But I don't think they are a source of actual truth.
cards.zh: 所以它們是有幫助的。工具是有幫助的。但我不覺得它們是真相的來源。
cards.why: 重複一次 helpful（they're / tools are）是刻意把肯定講滿，這樣後面的 But 才不會被聽成全盤否定。a source of actual truth 這個名詞化的說法，把爭論從「好不好用」精準地移到「能不能當依據」。
swaps: Useful, not authoritative.
Good for direction, bad for decisions.
I'd use them to compare, not to conclude.
cards.pmNote: 第三方數據工具適合做相對比較與正規化，不適合當絕對值進財測。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

cards.pattern: You can do it, but understand there's a high cost — and the later you [做這件事的時機], the less successful it's going to be
cards.quote: if you want to change during the course of the quarter, if you want to disrupt our whole engineering product team, you can do it, but understand there's a high cost, and the later you do it in the quarter, the less successful it's going to be
cards.zh: 你想在季中改、想打亂整個工程團隊，可以啊，但你要知道代價很高——而且愈晚改，效果只會愈差。
cards.why: 不說 no，改成把 yes 的價碼標出來：you can do it 先把權力交回對方，but understand 再把後果掛在對方帳上。台灣人擋需求常只會說「這個有困難」，母語者的做法是「可以，但這是代價，你自己決定」。
swaps: We can absolutely do that — it just means X slips
That's doable. I just want you to see what it displaces first.
cards.pmNote: 擋需求最有效的不是拒絕，是把 opportunity cost 明碼標價後讓對方自己收手。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: [A], [B], whatever you want — you've got [固定額度]. But you've got to decide now.
cards.quote: HubSpot, SAP, whatever you want, you've got 10% of the budget, you've got a hundred story points, whatever metric or heuristic you use, but you've got to decide now each quarter
cards.zh: HubSpot、SAP，你要哪個都行，你有 10% 的額度、一百個 story point，隨你怎麼算——但你這一季現在就得決定。
cards.why: whatever you want 聽起來像全面讓步，其實是先把「總量」框死，再把選擇權（和排序的痛苦）丟回對方。談優先順序時，給額度比給答案有效得多。
swaps: Pick any two — you've got one sprint's worth of capacity
It's your call what goes in, but the envelope is fixed
cards.pmNote: 給 sales 固定 % 的 roadmap 額度，是把跨部門角力變成他們內部的自我排序。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: If you really need us to [激烈的要求], we'll do it. But understand — is this really what you want?
cards.quote: If you really need us to put us on the shelf and drop everything for a million dollar deal, we're a startup, we'll do it. But understand, just, is this really really what you want?
cards.zh: 如果你真的要我們把手上的東西全放下、為了這筆一百萬的案子全部重來，我們是新創，我們會做。但你想清楚——這真的是你要的嗎？
cards.why: 先答應到底（we'll do it），再用一個問句把責任整包退還。這比「不行」殺傷力更大，因為對方沒有可以吵的對象，只剩自己的判斷。
swaps: If that's the call, we'll make it. Just confirm that's the trade you want.
Say the word and we'll drop everything — but is that where you want the team?
cards.pmNote: 把不合理的需求「照單全收＋回問一次」，多數時候對方自己會撤回。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: If you need [X], if you need [Y], I want you back in six months. But today, we're not the right solution for you.
cards.quote: If you need this feature, if you need this integration, I want you back in six months when you use this big product that isn't that great. But today, we're not the right solution for you.
cards.zh: 如果你需要這個功能、需要這個串接，那你先去用那個大廠的爛產品，六個月後再回來找我。今天我們不是適合你的解法。
cards.why: 主動把自己判出局，反而建立可信度。關鍵是 I want you back in six months——拒絕的同時給了一個回來的時間點，關係沒斷。台灣人怕失去機會，往往硬撐，結果第二次連門都進不去。
swaps: Honestly, we're not the right fit for that today — come back when X
I'd rather you not buy this now and stay a fan
cards.pmNote: 頂尖 sales 敢說「現在不要買」；這叫 honest disqualification，長期 NPS 與轉介率都更高。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: I know we all [大家嘴上都這麼說], but the reality is [實況], no matter what we say
cards.quote: I know we all release 28 times a day, but the reality is, software still goes on quarterly release cycles no matter what we say
cards.zh: 我知道我們嘴上都說一天出 28 版，但現實是，不管我們怎麼講，軟體對客戶來說還是季度發版。
cards.why: 先用 I know we all… 把自己也算進那個「大家」，反對就不再是你 vs 我，而是我們 vs 現實。no matter what we say 是收尾的鎚子，堵掉「可是我們流程不是這樣」的回嘴。
swaps: I know that's what we all say, but in practice…
On paper, yes. In reality, no matter how we frame it…
cards.pmNote: 內部 release 節奏 ≠ 客戶感知節奏；客戶一年最多消化兩次大改版。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: Everyone [做了某件事]. The question I ask folks is, "Did you earn it?"
cards.quote: Everyone raised prices. The question I ask folks is, "Did you earn it?"
cards.zh: 大家都漲價了。但我會問一句：你憑什麼漲？（你賺到這個漲價了嗎？）
cards.why: 不否定行為，只加一個評分標準。earn it 把「我們可以做」偷偷換成「我們配不配」，一句話就把討論從執行層拉回價值層——而且短到沒人能迴避。
swaps: Sure, but did we earn that?
The question I'd ask is whether we've earned the right to do that yet
cards.pmNote: 漲價要先加值：漲 8% 前先問這一年是否多給了 30% 的價值。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: I'd much rather have [少而強] than [多而弱]
cards.quote: I'd much rather have two reps, each closing a million than 20 reps struggling to close 100k each.
cards.zh: 我寧可要兩個各成交一百萬的業務，也不要二十個each 苦哈哈只做十萬的。
cards.why: I'd much rather have A than B 是英文講優先順序最乾淨的骨架：不解釋、不辯論，直接把兩個具體畫面並排，讓對方自己選。台灣人常用「我覺得應該要……比較好」，力度差很多。
swaps: I'd take one great X over five okay ones any day
Given the choice, fewer and better wins
cards.pmNote: 早期把 leads 集中給最強的人，比雨露均霑更快找到可複製的打法。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing — which maybe isn't what you said — is [複述]
cards.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
cards.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……
cards.why: 三層保險：先認領困惑（我 confused，不是你講不清）、再說明動機（I want to get it right）、最後預留誤聽的退路（which maybe isn't what you said）。這是英文會議裡最安全的追問法，不會讓對方覺得被質疑。
swaps: Just so I get this right — what I'm hearing is…
Let me play that back, and tell me where I've got it wrong
cards.pmNote: 聽不懂時說「我 confused」而不是「你沒講清楚」，是跨部門對齊的基本禮貌。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: I have a lot of opinions here that are data-driven. This one, I need another year in the oven, and I'll tell you why.
cards.quote: As you can see, I have a lot of opinions on things here that are data-driven and they're live experience. This one, I need another year in the oven, and I'll tell you why.
cards.zh: 你也看得出來，我很多看法都是有數據、有實戰的。但這一題我還需要再放一年才熟，我跟你說為什麼。
cards.why: 承認不知道之前，先把自己的可信度墊高（其他題我都很有把握）——這樣「我還沒想清楚」就變成專業的訊號而不是弱點。need another year in the oven（還要再烤一年）是母語者常用、台灣人幾乎想不到的比喻。
swaps: I've got strong views on most of this — this one needs more time in the oven
Ask me again in a year; I don't have enough reps on this one yet
cards.pmNote: 資深的訊號不是每題都有答案，而是能明確標出哪一題自己還沒資格下判斷。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: It shouldn't have taken me this long to realize that [結論]
cards.quote: And the big epiphany, we already talked about it, it shouldn't have taken me this long to realize that anytime an employee fails, it's your fault.
cards.zh: 我最大的頓悟——其實前面也提過——是我不該這麼晚才明白：只要有員工陣亡，那都是你的錯。
cards.why: 把「我錯了」升級成「我太晚才懂」：承認的不是單一決策，而是自己的學習速度，聽起來更誠實也更有份量。台灣人講反省常停在「當時沒考慮到」，少了這層時間維度。
swaps: It took me way too long to see that…
I wish I'd understood this five years earlier
cards.pmNote: 招錯人是主管的責任，不是被招者的責任——這個歸因方向決定 postmortem 的品質。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: If you just want [高成本的請求], I'm sorry, honestly, I'm sorry, I don't have that. But if you want [低成本的替代]…
cards.quote: if you just want an hour of my time randomly, I'm sorry, honestly, I'm sorry, I don't have that hour of time
cards.zh: 如果你只是想隨機約我一小時，抱歉，真的很抱歉，我沒有那一小時。
cards.why: 重複的 I'm sorry, honestly, I'm sorry 不是囉唆，是把「拒絕」的情緒成本先付掉；接著馬上給替代管道，讓拒絕變成分流而不是關門。
swaps: I'm sorry — genuinely — I can't do calls. Email me the question though.
I don't have that hour, but I do read everything you send.
cards.pmNote: 拒絕請求時一定要附替代路徑，否則對方只記得被拒。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: Here's the mistake that 99% of [某群人] make. We're not really [表面在做的事], we're [真正在做的事].
cards.quote: Here's the mistake that 99% of founders and sales reps make. We're not really selling in B2B, we're solving problems.
cards.zh: 99% 的創辦人跟業務都犯同一個錯。B2B 我們其實不是在賣東西，是在解問題。
cards.why: 先丟一個「你大概也在犯」的鉤子，再用 not X, we're Y 一句話換掉整個問題框架。這個 not A, but B 的重新命名句型，是英文簡報最省力的開場武器。
swaps: Most teams get this backwards. We're not shipping features, we're removing work.
The mistake almost everyone makes is thinking this is X. It isn't — it's Y.
cards.pmNote: 問題框架（framing）一改，整場討論的評估標準跟著改。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: The best [人] never leave a meeting without a next step. The next step does not have to be [最終目標].
cards.quote: The best salespeople never leave a meeting without a next step. The next step does not have to be a check.
cards.zh: 最好的業務絕不會沒有下一步就散會。而下一步不一定要是簽約。
cards.why: 第二句是關鍵：先把「下一步」的門檻降到誰都能答應，會議才收得起來。台灣人在英文會議最常見的失敗就是收尾只說 thank you，然後在信箱裡等一個永遠不會來的回信。
swaps: Before we drop off — what's the next step?
Let's not end without something on the calendar
cards.pmNote: 每場會結束都要留下 owner + 下一個時間點，這是 DRI 制度的最小單位。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: What would it take, [名字]? How can we get going on [事情]? What would it take?
cards.quote: What would it take, Lenny? How can we get going on Riverside? What would it take?
cards.zh: 那要怎樣才成呢，Lenny？我們要怎麼把 Riverside 這件事推動起來？要什麼條件你才點頭？
cards.why: What would it take? 把「你要不要」換成「要什麼條件」——對方不用拒絕你，只需要開條件，談判就從 yes/no 變成填空題。這是英文要資源、要預算最高 CP 值的一句話。
swaps: What would need to be true for this to happen?
What would it take to get a yes from your side?
cards.pmNote: 要人要預算時，先問對方的條件式，比直接提數字更容易拿到東西。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: I know you're mad at me today, but it is your fault. A hundred percent your fault if [結果]. Don't blame them.
cards.quote: I know you're mad at me today, but it is your fault. A hundred percent your fault if any of your hires fail. Don't blame them.
cards.zh: 我知道你今天會氣我，但這是你的錯。招進來的人陣亡，百分之百是你的錯。別怪他們。
cards.why: 先替對方說出他的情緒（I know you're mad at me today），對方就沒有情緒可以再爆；接著才下重話。承認代價在先、指控在後，是英文給重話的標準順序。
swaps: You're not going to like this, but this one's on us
I know this lands badly — and it's still our call that failed
cards.pmNote: mishire 的檢討要往上歸因到招募流程，不然同一個坑會一直踩。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: And I know this is going to trigger some people, but the truth is [不受歡迎的事實]
cards.quote: And I know this is going to trigger some people, but the truth is they don't want to work.
cards.zh: 我知道這句會讓一些人不爽，但事實就是——他們不想做事。
cards.why: 先自報「這句會踩到人」，等於把反彈先繳械：聽者的力氣被用在「他知道自己在講什麼」上，而不是「他怎麼可以這樣講」。台灣人講重話常直接上，或乾脆不講。
swaps: This is going to be unpopular, but…
I'll probably catch heat for this, and I still think it's true
cards.pmNote: 在會議裡丟不受歡迎的判斷前，先標記它不受歡迎，可大幅降低防衛反應。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: [某種摩擦] is a good thing. It's a sign of [健康的組織] when there is [那個摩擦].
cards.quote: This stress between product and sales is a good thing. It's a sign of a well-run B2B company when there is stress between product and sales.
cards.zh: 產品跟業務之間的緊張是好事。B2B 公司如果產品跟業務之間有張力，那才叫營運健康。
cards.why: 把衝突重新命名為健康指標，兩邊都下得了台，接著才有空間談「怎麼管理張力」而不是「誰該讓步」。處理跨團隊卡關時，先改標籤再談方法。
swaps: The friction here isn't the problem — the lack of a process for it is
If there were no tension, I'd be more worried
cards.pmNote: 產品與業務零摩擦，通常代表產品沒進到夠多真實案子裡。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: I'm going to tell my boss that I think we should do that. I'm going to use a little social capital and say we should do this.
cards.quote: I'm going to tell my boss, on Monday, that I think we should do that. I'm going to use a little social capital and say we should do this.
cards.zh: 我禮拜一會跟我主管講，我覺得這個該做。我會動用一點我的政治額度，去替它說話。
cards.why: use a little social capital 是英文職場的高階說法：明講「我要為你花掉我的一點信用額度」，既表態支持又暗示這件事不是免費的。台灣人多半只會說「我幫你反映」，力度和誠意都輸一截。
swaps: I'll spend some capital on this one
I'll put my name on it when I raise it upstairs
cards.pmNote: IC 不該當場答應 roadmap，該做的是把訴求往上帶並標明自己願意背書多少。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: You're really only paying [小單位金額] for a couple months to see if this experiment works out. You don't have [總額] to do [X]?
cards.quote: You're really only paying 6k a month for a couple months to see if this experiment works out. You're investing 20,000, you don't have $20,000 to do sales?
