cards.zh: 你其實只是花幾個月、每月六千塊，去驗證這個實驗成不成。你等於投兩萬——你連兩萬都拿不出來做業務？
cards.why: 把嚇人的年薪拆成「幾個月 × 小數字」，再用一個反問把拒絕的成本推回對方。要預算時最有效的不是講價值，是把承諾切小到對方不好意思說不。
swaps: We're really committing to one quarter, not a year
The real ask is X per month until we know
cards.pmNote: 爭取資源時把 ask 拆成可撤回的小段（試點、單季），核准率遠高於一次要到底。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.pattern: [某種價值/原則] aren't [價值/原則] unless there's an actual trade-off
cards.quote: values aren't values unless there's an actual trade-off
cards.zh: 沒有真的要付出代價的價值觀，就不叫價值觀。
cards.why: X aren't X unless… 是英文最俐落的重新定義句型：不否定對方，只加一個門檻，讓對方原本的東西自動不合格。八個字就能終結一場關於「我們的價值觀是什麼」的空轉會議。
swaps: It's not a priority unless something else drops
A strategy isn't a strategy until it says no to something
cards.pmNote: 策略即取捨：任何沒有排除項的優先順序都是願望清單。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.pattern: It's okay to [別的做法]; it's not [適合我的], and that's okay — that's the entire point
cards.quote: it's okay to have a culture that doesn't believe that, it's not a culture for me, and that's okay, that's the entire point
cards.zh: 你們公司文化不信這一套也沒關係，那只是不適合我，這樣就好——這本來就是重點。
cards.why: 把分歧降級成「適配問題」而不是「對錯問題」：三次 okay 讓對方完全沒有被否定的感覺，但你的立場一步都沒退。這是英文表達不同意最不傷人的一招。
swaps: That works for plenty of teams — it just isn't how I'd run mine
Totally valid approach. Not mine, and that's fine.
cards.pmNote: 文化價值觀的功能是篩人，不是分對錯；能講清楚「誰不適合」的價值觀才有用。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.pattern: This is how we think about things. This is how we handle [這類狀況] here. If that's hard for you, let's find you another job.
cards.quote: This is how we think about things. This is how we handle this type of behavior here. If that's hard for you, let's find you another job.
cards.zh: 我們就是這樣想事情的。這種狀況我們在這裡就是這樣處理的。如果你覺得很難接受，那我們一起幫你找個別的工作。
cards.why: 前兩句只陳述事實、不評價人；第三句 let's find you another job 用 let's（我們一起）把開除包裝成合作。冷、清楚、但不侮辱——這是英文最難學會的重話語氣。
swaps: If that's a dealbreaker, let's help you land somewhere better
This is the deal here. If it doesn't fit, we'll help you find one that does.
cards.pmNote: 價值觀衝突要在試用期內處理完，拖越久對雙方成本越高。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.quote: We're not better than you, you're not better than us, it's just this is how we do things here.
cards.zh: 我們沒有比你好，你也沒有比我們好，就只是我們這裡是這樣做事的。
cards.why: 對稱句（不是你錯也不是我對）把價值判斷整個拿掉，只留下差異本身。處理立場衝突時，先把「誰高誰低」這個軸拔掉，剩下的就只是要不要合作。
swaps: Neither of us is wrong here — we just work differently
This isn't better or worse, it's just different
cards.pmNote: 跨團隊卡住時先確認是「標準不同」還是「利益不同」，處方完全不一樣。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.pattern: You probably didn't know, but I don't really like when [具體行為]
cards.quote: Hey, Lenny. You probably didn't know, but I don't really like when people comment on my shirt.
cards.zh: 嘿 Lenny，你可能不知道，我其實不太喜歡別人評論我的衣服。
cards.why: You probably didn't know 一句話就替對方脫罪，把「你冒犯我」變成「你少了一則資訊」。這是英文日常給微型回饋的黃金開場，台灣人不是忍著就是憋到爆炸。
swaps: You had no way of knowing this, but…
Small thing, and you couldn't have known — I'd rather we didn't…
cards.pmNote: 把最寬容的解讀（most charitable interpretation）當預設，是低內耗團隊的基本設定。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.pattern: [某個廣被接受的建議] is terrible advice. And if I'm being charitable, it's just outdated.
cards.quote: But as an overall missive, don't focus on your competitors is terrible advice. And if I'm being charitable, it's just outdated
cards.zh: 但當成通則來講，「不要管競爭對手」是很爛的建議。往好處說的話，它只是過時了。
cards.why: if I'm being charitable（往好處說的話）是英文反對時的高段緩衝：先重話、再自願讓一步，顯得你是就事論事而不是在鬥人。台灣人通常反過來——先客氣半天，重點卻沒說出口。
swaps: Being generous, it's just out of date
At best, that advice hasn't aged well
cards.pmNote: 老建議要檢查它成立時的市場條件是否還在（CAC、競品密度）。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.pattern: The biggest misconception about [X] is [誤解]. You don't have to [誤解] at all — you just have to [真正該做的].
cards.quote: the biggest misconception about customer research is I have to listen to them. You don't have to listen to them at all, you just have to understand where they are
cards.zh: 對客戶研究最大的誤解，是以為做了就得照客戶說的做。你完全不必照做，你只需要搞清楚他們現在站在哪裡。
cards.why: 接住反對時最有效的不是辯論，是指認出對方腦中那個沒說出口的假設，然後只拆掉那一塊。you don't have to X at all, you just have to Y 是這個動作的標準骨架。
swaps: You're not obligated to act on it — you just need to know it
Listening isn't obeying
cards.pmNote: 使用者研究的產出是理解，不是需求清單；判斷仍然是 PM 的工作。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.pattern: I'm giving you some heuristics, I'm giving you some benchmarks — but your mileage is going to vary.
cards.quote: So I'm giving some heuristics, I'm giving some benchmarks, but your mileage is going to vary.
cards.zh: 我給的是一些經驗法則、一些對照基準，但你們的狀況一定會不一樣。
cards.why: your mileage may vary（原本是汽車油耗廣告的免責話）已經是英語職場標配的免責句。在一長串斷言之後補這一句，等於幫自己的建議加上有效範圍，聽起來更可信不是更弱。
swaps: These are benchmarks, not laws
Treat these as starting points — your context will move the numbers
cards.pmNote: 引用 benchmark 時一定要標明樣本與情境，否則會被當成保證值。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.quote: So I don't know if I answered your question, but that's the scope of that problem I think
cards.zh: 我不確定有沒有回答到你的問題，但這大概就是這個問題的範圍。
cards.why: 講完一大段之後主動交回主控權：既承認可能離題，又順手替自己的長答案下了一個標籤（我在描述問題的範圍）。台灣人講完長答案通常就停住，讓對方尷尬地判斷要不要追問。
swaps: Not sure that's what you were asking — happy to take it from another angle
That may have been more than you wanted. Did that get at it?
cards.pmNote: 長答案結束時自評一句，是主持會議與被訪談時都通用的收尾。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.pattern: [明確立場]. And that answer offends everybody.
cards.quote: The basic idea is bootstrapping is for lifestyle businesses that want to cash flow. Funding is for companies trying to create a billion dollars in annual revenue. And that answer offends everybody.
cards.zh: 基本想法是：自力經營是給想要現金流的生活型事業，募資是給要做到年營收十億美元的公司。而這個答案會得罪所有人。
cards.why: 先把立場講死，再自己宣布「這會得罪大家」——反對的話被你先講掉，聽眾反而會想聽你怎麼撐住。這是英文丟爭議觀點的標準保護罩。
swaps: I know this annoys both camps, and here it is anyway
This take has no friends, but…
cards.pmNote: 募資與否要回推目標規模，不是回推當下現金水位。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.pattern: This was a big mistake. Yes, [好結果], but [其實可以更好的版本].
cards.quote: And I'll tell you, ProfitWell, this was a big mistake. Yes, it was a great exit, we sold for over $200 million, et cetera, but we probably, if we had taken money, we could have had a billion-dollar exit
cards.zh: 老實說 ProfitWell 這件事是個大失誤。是啦，出場很漂亮，賣了兩億多美元，但如果我們當初有拿錢，可能會是十億等級的出場。
cards.why: 承認錯誤最難的情況是「結果其實不差」。Yes, [成績], but [更高的參照點] 這個結構讓你在有成績時仍然檢討得下去——用更高的標準，而不是用失敗來自責。
swaps: It worked, and it was still the wrong call
Good outcome, wrong decision — those aren't the same thing
cards.pmNote: 檢討決策要看決策當下的資訊與可選項，不要用結果好壞倒推對錯。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.pattern: You're going to snooze it a couple of times, I get it. But just do something, even if it's super small.
cards.quote: put a calendar invite, let it renew every three months. You're going to snooze it a couple of times, I get it, I've seen this many, many times before. But just do something, even if it's super small.
cards.zh: 開一個行事曆邀請，每三個月自動重複。你一定會按掉個幾次，我懂，我看過太多次了。但就是做點什麼，再小都好。
cards.why: 先幫對方把藉口講完（你會按掉，我懂），對方就沒有藉口可以拿出來用；然後把門檻降到最低（even if it's super small）。這是英文推動別人行動最好用的兩段式。
swaps: You'll skip it a few times — that's fine. Just don't skip it forever.
I know it'll slip. Do the smallest version anyway.
cards.pmNote: 定價每季至少動一件事，比一年做一次大改版更容易累積。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.pattern: Pound for pound, it's [最關鍵的那一項]
cards.quote: The number one thing to figure out when you're thinking about the different pricing pieces, pound for pound, it's the pricing metric or the value metric.
cards.zh: 定價的各個環節裡，論投入產出比，最該先搞定的就是計價單位（價值指標）。
cards.why: pound for pound 原是拳擊術語（同量級比較），母語者拿來表示「以投入產出比來說最強的」。這是台灣人幾乎想不到、但一講出來就顯得很在地的排序用語。
swaps: Dollar for dollar, this is the highest-leverage one
If you only fix one thing, fix this
cards.pmNote: 價值指標（per seat / per 1,000 visits）決定 churn 與 expansion，比價格數字本身重要。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.pattern: I'm just going to bump you up to [新方案]. Let me know if you have any questions.
cards.quote: I'm just going to bump you up to the 100-video plan. Let me know if you have any questions.
cards.zh: 我就直接幫你升到 100 支影片的方案囉。有問題再跟我說。
cards.why: 漲價講成「已完成的服務動作」：I'm just going to… 是既成事實式語氣，Let me know if you have any questions 把異議管道留著卻不主動邀請。比「請問您願意升級嗎」成功率高得多。
swaps: I'll go ahead and move you to the next tier — shout if that's a problem
We're moving you up to X from next cycle; let me know if you'd rather not
cards.pmNote: 用量型定價的升級應該是自動發生的通知，不是一次重新銷售。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.quote: Okay, let me not overreact here. Let me seek to understand and then react or respond, versus react.
cards.zh: 好，我先別反應過度。我先搞懂發生什麼事，再回應，而不是直接反射。
cards.why: respond vs react 這組對比是英語職場處理衝突的核心詞：react 是被觸發，respond 是選擇過的。把它講出聲（let me…）等於當著對方的面按下暫停鍵，也在示範你要的團隊文化。
swaps: Let me sit with this before I answer
I want to respond to this, not react to it
cards.pmNote: 第一反應通常是資訊不足下的猜測；先問三個問題再表態。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.pattern: [某群人] who [做了 X] have [10 到 30%] higher [指標] than those who didn't
cards.quote: prospects who meet you in person have 10 to 30% higher willingness to pay than those who didn't. Churn for those folks who you meet in person is typically 20% lower than those folks who have never met you.
cards.zh: 跟你當面見過的潛在客戶，付費意願會高出 10 到 30%；見過面的客戶流失率通常比沒見過的低 20%。
cards.why: 用數據撐主張的標準句型：A 組 vs 對照組 + 區間值（10 to 30%）+ typically。給區間而不是單一數字，反而讓人更信——因為它承認了變異。
swaps: Teams that do X see roughly a 20% lift versus those that don't
Directionally, it's a 10–30% difference — not a rounding error
cards.pmNote: 引用內部數據時給區間＋樣本量，比給一個漂亮的整數更有說服力。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.quote: you can't be everything to all people, so who are you for? Who are you for and who are you not for?
cards.zh: 你不可能討好所有人，所以你到底是為誰做的？你是為誰做的、又不是為誰做的？
cards.why: 把模糊的「我們要做好」轉成一個必須排除的問題：who are you not for 這半句才是重點。定義問題時強迫對方講出排除項，是最快讓討論落地的方式。
swaps: Who is this explicitly not for?
Let's name who we're happy to lose
cards.pmNote: problem statement 要含 non-goals，否則範疇會無限擴張。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

cards.quote: One, I think that's a really fantastic, maybe not counterpoint, but thing to call out.
cards.zh: 第一，我覺得你這個提得非常好——也不算是反駁啦，但確實是該點出來的一件事。
cards.why: 被當場質疑時，先幫對方的質疑「降級命名」：不是 counterpoint（反駁），而是 thing to call out（值得點出的事）。既接住了對方，也悄悄把對立關係拆掉——你們變成同一邊在補洞。
swaps: That's a fair thing to flag — I wouldn't even call it a rebuttal
Good call-out. Let me take it head on.
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem 的精神：把反對意見當成幫你補洞的人，而不是敵人。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.pattern: When you're making decisions that could be described as [對某方有害] but a net positive for [另一方], you're probably not thinking long-term enough
cards.quote: when you're making decisions that could be described as hostile towards your customers, but a net positive for the business, you're probably not thinking long-term enough
cards.zh: 當你在做的決定可以被形容為「對客戶不友善、但對公司淨正面」時，多半代表你想得還不夠長。
cards.why: 不說對方錯，只說對方的時間軸太短——把價值爭論換成參數爭論。could be described as 又是一層緩衝（不是我說的，是這件事看起來像）。這兩層加起來，反對變得幾乎無法反彈。
swaps: That only pencils out if we're optimizing for this quarter
If it looks good for us and bad for them, the time horizon is probably too short
cards.pmNote: 「對客戶不利但對公司有利」的決策幾乎都是把未來的錢挪到現在。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.pattern: I don't know that we even talk about problems without a qualifier. Are we talking about a [商業] problem? Are we talking about a [客戶] problem?
cards.quote: I don't know that we even talk about problems without a qualifier. Are we talking about a business problem? Are we talking about a customer problem?
cards.zh: 我們大概不會不加限定詞就講「問題」這兩個字。我們現在講的是商業問題？還是客戶問題？
cards.why: 用一個「我們公司習慣」的說法（we don't talk about problems without a qualifier）把追問變成規範而不是質疑，接著用兩個並列問句逼出分類。這是把模糊抱怨變成可解問題最快的兩句話。
swaps: Before we solve it — whose problem is this?
Is that a customer problem or a metric problem?
cards.pmNote: 商業問題若不先翻譯成客戶問題，做出來的解法通常對客戶有害。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.pattern: I'll admit I'm definitely not a [領域] expert. I've been fortunate to work with [真正的專家]…
cards.quote: I'll admit I'm definitely not an SEO expert. I've been fortunate to work with some of the best marketers in the world who I think are bonafide legends at this point
cards.zh: 我坦白說我絕對不是 SEO 專家。我只是很幸運跟一些世界頂尖的行銷人共事過，那些人到今天都算是真正的傳奇。
cards.why: 承認不懂的正確順序：先劃清界線（我不是專家），再交代自己的資訊來源（我跟誰共事過）。這樣接下來講的內容仍然可信，但你不必為它背專家責任。台灣人常只做前半段，結果整段話被忽略。
swaps: I'm not the expert here — what I've picked up from the people who are is…
Caveat: this is secondhand from folks who do this for a living
cards.pmNote: 知識誠實：講出資訊來源的層級（第一手／二手），讓聽者自己調整信心權重。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.pattern: I can't give a specific number, but [仍然回答問題的定性版本]
cards.quote: I can't give a specific number, but a large percentage of our revenue flows through the product.
cards.zh: 具體數字我不能講，但我們相當高比例的營收是走產品這條路進來的。
cards.why: 拒絕透露不等於不回答。先關門（I can't give a specific number），立刻開一扇小窗（a large percentage）——對方拿到了方向感，你什麼都沒洩漏。這句在面試、對外訪談、跨公司會議都極度實用。
swaps: I can't share the exact figure — directionally it's the majority
Not something I can put a number on, but it's material
cards.pmNote: 被問敏感數字時給量級或方向，比冷冰冰的「不方便透露」保住更多關係。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.pattern: Truth be told, I think I bombed it. I actually don't think I would've hired me back then.
cards.quote: truth be told, when I interviewed with Fareed that first time, I think back to the interview and I think I bombed it. I actually don't think I would've hired me back then.
cards.zh: 老實講，我第一次跟 Fareed 面試的時候，現在回想起來我覺得我搞砸了。換成是我，當時我大概也不會錄取我自己。
cards.why: I wouldn't have hired me（我不會錄取我自己）是英文自嘲的高階用法：把自己同時放在評審與被評審的位置，顯示你有能力用客觀標準看自己。承認失手卻讓人覺得你更可靠。
swaps: Looking back, I wouldn't have hired me either
I didn't earn that offer — someone took a bet on me
cards.pmNote: 把貴人講成「押注在你身上的人（sponsor）」而不是 mentor，更準確也更有份量。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.pattern: I have a lot of rough edges that people have learned to deal with over the years, but I try to be self-aware about them
cards.quote: I have a lot of rough edges to my personality that I think people have just learned to deal with over the years, but I try to be self-aware about them
cards.zh: 我個性上有很多稜角，同事這些年大概是習慣了，但我至少努力對它們保持自覺。
cards.why: 回答缺點題的成熟版：不假謙虛、不列一個假缺點，而是承認稜角存在＋承諾自覺。rough edges 這個詞比 weakness 更中性，不會把自己講成有缺陷的產品。
swaps: I've got sharp edges; what I owe people is being aware of them
I'm not going to pretend those go away — I just try to flag them early
cards.pmNote: 面試自我覺察題的評分點是「你知不知道別人怎麼形容你」，不是缺點本身。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.pattern: If the people you most recently worked with were in a room and you weren't there, how would they talk about you?
cards.quote: if the people that you most recently worked with were in a room and you weren't there, how would they talk about you?
cards.zh: 如果你最近一起共事的那些人聚在一個房間裡、而你不在場，他們會怎麼講你？
cards.why: 把「請你自評」改成「請你模擬別人的評價」，對方無法只講漂亮話（因為他知道你可能真的會去問）。教練式提問的精髓：換一個觀察位置，答案就誠實了。
swaps: What would your last team say about you when you're not in the room?
How do you think you're described by people who've worked with you?
cards.pmNote: 這題同時是 reference check 的預告，能大幅提高回答的誠實度。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.pattern: I might even ask them to define what [關鍵詞] means to them, so we can get on the same page of what we're even talking about
cards.quote: And I might even ask them to define what product-led means to them that we can get on the same page of what we're even talking about.
cards.zh: 我甚至會請他們先定義一下「產品驅動成長」對他們來說是什麼意思，這樣我們才知道彼此在講的是不是同一件事。
cards.why: what we're even talking about 裡的 even 是關鍵語氣：暗示「我們可能連題目都不同」，但因為包在一個提議裡（I might even ask），聽起來像謹慎而不是刁難。專治大家用同一個詞、想著不同東西的會議。
swaps: Before we go further — what does X mean in your head?
Let's align on the definition, otherwise we'll argue past each other
cards.pmNote: 對齊（alignment）的第一步永遠是名詞定義，不是目標設定。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.pattern: Don't get me wrong, [承認對方那一派的正當性] — I'm not one of them.
cards.quote: And don't get me wrong, I think there's a lot of product folks out there who enjoy that modality of work, I'm not one of them.
cards.zh: 別誤會，我知道有很多產品人是真的喜歡那種工作方式的——我不是。
cards.why: Don't get me wrong 先擋掉「你在貶低別人」的解讀，把否定收斂成個人偏好（I'm not one of them）。四個字的免責聲明，換來一句可以直說的真心話。
swaps: No shade — it's just not how I like to work
Plenty of people thrive on that. I don't.
cards.pmNote: 表達偏好而非優劣，能保留跟不同工作風格的人合作的空間。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.pattern: In fact, if I'm being brutally honest, I think [大家都默認的東西] is kind of hard to achieve in [情境]
cards.quote: Our loops are less tactical. In fact, if I'm being brutally honest, I think loops are kind of hard to achieve in B2B SaaS.
cards.zh: 我們的成長迴圈比較不那麼戰術。老實說，我覺得在 B2B SaaS 裡要做出真正的迴圈其實蠻難的。
cards.why: if I'm being brutally honest 是英文的「授權自己講真話」開關，通常用在要推翻業界共識時。搭配 kind of（有點）當減壓閥，讓一句踩到整個社群的話聽起來仍然可討論。
swaps: Honestly? I don't think that model holds here.
Being blunt — I've never seen that work in this context
cards.pmNote: B2B SaaS 難有真正的成長迴圈，多半是漏斗＋口碑的宏觀飛輪。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.quote: Does this continue to serve us today? And if not, we should be really comfortable of letting it go.
cards.zh: 這件事到今天還對我們有用嗎？如果沒有，我們應該要能很坦然地把它放掉。
cards.why: serve us（為我們服務）把制度、文化、做法都降格成工具——工具過期就丟，不涉及誰對誰錯。要收回既有立場時，先把它重新定義成「當時有用的東西」。
swaps: Is this still earning its place?
That made sense then. Does it make sense now?
cards.pmNote: 定期壓力測試自家文化與流程，是規模化時的必要動作。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.quote: if I had to guess how people might talk about that, if I wasn't in the room, maybe they would cite that, but it's tough to say.
cards.zh: 如果要我猜、我不在場的時候別人會怎麼講這件事，他們可能會提到那個吧——但很難說。
cards.why: 談自己的功勞最尷尬，這句把主語換成「別人在我不在時的說法」，等於借別人的嘴講自己的成績，再用 it's tough to say 收尾保持謙遜。不吹牛也不縮小，正是升遷簡報最難拿捏的那個位置。
swaps: I'd guess that's what people would point to, though I'm not the one to say
If you asked my team, I think they'd say X — but that's their call, not mine
cards.pmNote: 談影響力時把判斷權交給第三方，可信度比自我宣告高。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.pattern: You could have all the [某種數據] in the world — it tells you what's happening, but it doesn't tell you why
cards.quote: You could have all the usage data in the world, that's going to tell you what's actually happening in your product, but it doesn't tell you why.
cards.zh: 就算你握有全世界的使用數據，它只會告訴你產品裡實際發生了什麼，不會告訴你為什麼。
cards.why: 用數據撐主張的反面技巧：主動指出自家數據的極限，反而讓你接下來要引用的質性資料變得必要。what vs why 這組對比是英文談研究方法時的固定句式。
swaps: The numbers tell us what, not why
Quant gets us to the question; qual gets us to the answer
cards.pmNote: 量化找出異常，質性解釋成因；兩者缺一，決策就會賭運氣。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.pattern: The number one mistake is hiring [某角色], giving them no resources, and expecting them to pull a rabbit out of their hat
cards.quote: the number one mistake is hiring a head of growth, giving them no resources and expecting them to pull rabbit out of their hat.
cards.zh: 最常見的錯誤，就是找了一個成長負責人來，什麼資源都不給，然後期待他變魔術。
cards.why: 要資源時最有效的說法不是「我需要 X」，而是把「沒有 X」講成一個大家都認得的失敗模式。pull a rabbit out of a hat（變兔子）讓不合理的期待聽起來荒謬，你就不必自己抱怨。
swaps: Hiring the role without the budget is how this usually fails
You can't hand someone a number and no levers
cards.pmNote: 談資源時先講失敗模式，再談需求，比直接開清單容易過關。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.pattern: Go reach out to [某人] and ask how you can make their day easier
cards.quote: go reach out to a PM and ask how you can make their day easier
cards.zh: 直接去找一個 PM，問他你可以幫他分擔什麼、讓他今天輕鬆一點。
cards.why: 把「請教／討教」翻轉成「我能替你做什麼」，對方沒有拒絕的理由，你也不欠人情。想跨進一個新領域時，這句比 can I pick your brain 好用十倍。
swaps: What could I take off your plate this week?
Is there a piece of this I could own for you?
cards.pmNote: 建立人脈的最短路徑是先提供勞力，再要資訊。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.quote: And again, these are all conjectures, which I can't prove in any way, but it's a thought experiment to talk about these things.
cards.zh: 再說一次，這些都只是我的推測，我完全沒辦法證明，但當成思想實驗來聊是有意思的。
cards.why: 先幫自己的整段論述標上「推測」標籤，再用 thought experiment 把它從「主張」降級成「一起玩的東西」。這樣講完後即使被推翻，你也沒有輸——因為你從沒宣稱它是真的。
swaps: Strictly a hypothesis — I can't back this with data
Treat this as a thought experiment, not a claim
cards.pmNote: 把假設明確標為假設，是團隊敢挑戰你的前提。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

cards.pattern: I hate the word "[某個詞]" because [理由]. So I stay away from "[那個詞]", but [你真正的回答]
cards.quote: I often tell people that I hate the word 'favorite' because it tells me to become limited in my mind. So I stay away from 'favorite', but I learn all the time from everybody.
cards.zh: 我常跟人說我討厭「最喜歡的」這個詞，因為它會逼我的腦袋變窄。所以我不用這個詞，但我隨時都在跟每個人學東西。
cards.why: 不回答問題、但也不逃避：先拒絕題目裡的那個詞（並給理由），再用自己的框架回答。這是被問到不想回答的問題時，母語者最優雅的一招——換題目，不換態度。
swaps: I'd push back on the word 'best' here — what I'd say instead is…
I try not to think in terms of favorites, but here's what I keep coming back to
cards.pmNote: 被問到框架本身有問題的問題時，先重構問題再作答。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

cards.pattern: It's a day long [主題] on its own. So some other time.
cards.quote: It's a day long podcast on its own. So some other time.
cards.zh: 那個講一整天都講不完，改天再說吧。
cards.why: 把離題的支線先讚美（值得講一整天），再乾脆地推遲（some other time）。11 個字就把會議拉回正軌，而且對方不會覺得他的話題被否定。台灣人通常是硬聽完，或直接打斷。
swaps: That's a whole meeting on its own — let's park it
Big topic. Let's take that offline.
cards.pmNote: 會議設計的基本功：離題的東西要「放進停車場」而不是砍掉。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

cards.pattern: [某個雜訊來源] is designed for [它的真實動機]. So I wouldn't read too much into it.
cards.quote: And Twitter is designed for outrage getting likes. So I wouldn't read too much into it.
cards.zh: Twitter 這個場子本來就是設計來讓憤怒獲得按讚的。所以我不會太當一回事。
cards.why: 先解釋雜訊的生成機制，再說「我不會太放在心上」——因為有了機制解釋，這句話就不是逃避批評，而是校準訊號。面對負評、酸言、非代表性回饋時最好用。
swaps: That channel selects for the loudest, not the typical — I'd weight it accordingly
I wouldn't over-index on that feedback
cards.pmNote: 回饋要先看來源的選擇偏誤，再決定要不要進 backlog。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

cards.pattern: I'm not saying that we should not [對方可能誤會的事] — that's very different.
cards.quote: I'm not saying that we should not take customer feedback, that's very different.
cards.zh: 我不是說不要聽客戶回饋——那是完全不同的兩件事。
cards.why: 講完一個激烈主張後，立刻把「可能被誤讀的版本」切掉。that's very different 是英文劃清界線最短的一句，比長篇補充有效得多。台灣人常等到被誤解之後才澄清，那時已經來不及。
swaps: To be clear, I'm not saying X — different thing entirely
Let me not be misheard: this isn't about X
cards.pmNote: 拋出強烈立場後，主動列出「這句話不包含什麼」，可省下大量後續解釋。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

cards.pattern: Somebody commenting about [你的事] who does not understand the nuance of it — you can't be reacting to everything.
cards.quote: let's say somebody commenting about your business, who does not understand the nuance of it, you can't be reacting to everything.
cards.zh: 假設有人在評論你的生意，但他根本不懂裡面的細節——你不可能每件事都去回應。
cards.why: 拒絕的理由放在「對方的資訊不足」而不是「你不重要」，語氣就不會刻薄。you can't be reacting to everything 用進行式表達一種持續消耗的狀態，比 I won't respond 更委婉也更真實。
swaps: We can't chase every piece of feedback
Not every comment deserves a response from us
cards.pmNote: 把回饋分成「懂脈絡的」與「不懂脈絡的」，只對前者投入回應成本。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

cards.quote: Sometimes I wonder if the challenges and the opportunities are exactly the same.
cards.zh: 我有時候會想，所謂的挑戰跟機會，會不會根本是同一件事。
cards.why: 被問「最大的挑戰是什麼」時，用一句話把二分法折起來，接下來的內容自動變得有洞見。Sometimes I wonder if… 又讓這個大膽命題保持在思考狀態，聽者容易跟著一起想。
swaps: I'm not sure those are two different lists
The risk and the opportunity might be the same thing here
cards.pmNote: 重新定義問題時，先檢查兩個相對的清單是不是同一份。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

cards.pattern: I have a strong view that [立場]. In fact, [更進一步的推論].
cards.quote: So I have a strong view that we will never, never have equality of wealth. In fact, chasing that is actually a bad idea.
cards.zh: 我有個很強的看法：我們永遠、永遠不會有財富平等。事實上，去追求那個本身就是個壞主意。
cards.why: I have a strong view that… 是英文宣告立場強度的標準頭銜（比 I think 重、比 I know 安全）；接著 In fact 不是舉證，而是把立場再推一級。先標強度、再加碼，是英文建立論點的常見節奏。
swaps: I hold this one strongly: …
I'd go further than that, actually
cards.pmNote: 表態時先講強度（strong view / loose hunch），聽者才知道要不要花力氣挑戰你。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

cards.pattern: No, but the nuance that is important is [你要補的那一層]
cards.quote: No, but the nuance that is important is that you can actually increase the database size infinitely.
cards.zh: 不對，但這裡有個很重要的細節：那個資料庫的大小其實是可以無限擴張的。
cards.why: 英文裡直接的 No 很傷人，但後面接 but the nuance that is important is… 就會把反對重新包裝成「補一層你漏掉的細節」。對方保留了面子，你的修正也完整送達。
swaps: Close — the nuance I'd add is…
Almost, but there's a wrinkle that changes the conclusion
cards.pmNote: 修正別人的模型時，補細節比推翻整體更容易被接受。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

cards.pattern: And therefore [抽象概念] is like [日常事物]. It's like a [屬性] service.
cards.quote: And therefore envy is like wifi. It's like a hyperlocal service.
cards.zh: 所以說，嫉妒就像 wifi，是一種超在地的服務——只在很近的範圍內有訊號。
cards.why: 用一個大家每天都在用的東西當喻體，抽象概念立刻有形狀且可傳播。母語者說服人時很少堆形容詞，而是丟一個能被複述的比喻——因為聽眾轉述得出去，你的論點才會走遠。
swaps: Think of it like wifi — the signal only reaches so far
It behaves like a local network, not a broadcast
cards.pmNote: 策略敘事的可傳播性取決於比喻，不取決於資料量。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

cards.quote: I ask myself and my key reportees every month, we go around the table and ask ourselves, "What are the hardest problems we solved last month?"
cards.zh: 我每個月都會跟直屬主管們繞著桌子問一輪：我們上個月解掉的最難的問題是什麼？
cards.why: 問題本身就是標準：不問「你做了什麼」（會得到一堆忙碌），而問「最難的是什麼」（逼出位移量）。教練式提問的核心不是引導，是換一個讓人無法用忙碌搪塞的量尺。
swaps: What's the hardest thing you unblocked this month?
What did you move that wouldn't have moved without you?
cards.pmNote: 資深者的產出應以「解掉的難題」計，不以工時或票數計。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

cards.pattern: You do a fabulous job of [具體的動作], and making it [具體的效果] for many of us
cards.quote: you do a fabulous job of taking the information asymmetry of the art of product and making it accessible to many of us across the world
cards.zh: 你把產品這門手藝裡的資訊落差拿出來，讓全世界很多人都能取得——這件事你做得非常出色。
cards.why: 稱讚時不用形容詞（you're amazing），而是描述對方做的那個「動作」與造成的「效果」。具體到能被複述的讚美才有份量，也才不會像客套。
swaps: What you do really well is taking X and making it usable for people like us
You've closed a gap that most people don't even notice exists
cards.pmNote: 公開肯定要指名具體行為與受益者，團隊才知道什麼行為值得複製。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

cards.pattern: Before you move on to the next one, I want to spend a little time on this one
cards.quote: Before you actually move on to the next one, I want to spend a little time on this one
cards.zh: 在你跳到下一點之前，我想在這一點上多待一下。
cards.why: 插話而不打斷：Before you move on 承認對方正在推進、也承認他有下一步，只請求延後。這是英文會議中最安全的切入點——比 Sorry to interrupt 更主動也更專業。
swaps: Can we stay on that one a beat longer?
Before we leave this point — one thing
cards.pmNote: 在英文會議建立存在感的關鍵是「切入的時機點」而不是講話總量。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.pattern: So I cut you off on this one. So let's keep going.
cards.quote: Okay. So, I cut you off in this one bullet point so far. So, let's keep going.
cards.zh: 好，我剛剛在這一點把你打斷了。我們繼續吧。
cards.why: 把話語權還回去的標準動作：先承認自己打斷（I cut you off），再明確交棒（let's keep going）。承認打斷這一步台灣人幾乎都省略，結果對方不確定要不要接回原本的主題。
swaps: Sorry, I derailed you — you were on point three
I jumped in there. Please carry on.
cards.pmNote: 主持會議時記得把被打斷的人送回原位，議程才不會斷線。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

cards.pattern: Let me try to summarize the things you've said and then keep going. So let me know what I'm missing here.
cards.quote: Let me try to summarize a little bit of the things you've said and then keep going. So let me know what I'm missing here.
cards.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，然後我們再往下。有漏掉的你跟我說。
cards.why: 收斂＋開放同時做到：先宣告要總結（讓對方知道你不是插話），再用 let me know what I'm missing 把校正權交回去。這句話讓總結變成共同產出，而不是你的片面詮釋。
swaps: Let me play back what I heard — correct me where I'm off
Quick recap, then tell me what I dropped
cards.pmNote: 會議結論要當場覆誦並徵求修正，才算真的有決議紀錄。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.quote: That's over my head, but I love it anyway.
cards.zh: 這超出我的理解範圍了，但我還是很喜歡。
cards.why: 承認聽不懂卻不掉價：over my head 是輕鬆的自嘲（不是 I don't understand 那種硬碰硬），加上 but I love it anyway 保住了對談的溫度。對非母語者來說，這比假裝跟得上安全太多。
swaps: That one went over my head — say more?
You lost me there, and I'm into it
cards.pmNote: 承認沒跟上，是把對方拉回共同語言的最快方式。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

cards.pattern: I probably should have clarified. I think this is mostly true in [限定情境].
cards.quote: I probably should have clarified. I think this is mostly true in PLG companies where most of the growth is coming from product
cards.zh: 我剛剛應該先講清楚的。我想這件事主要是在成長主要來自產品的 PLG 公司才成立。
cards.why: 當對方答非所問時，把責任攬到自己身上（我沒講清楚），再補上限定條件——對方不必認錯就能修正方向。這是英文會議裡化解誤會最省事的一句。
swaps: That's on me — I should have scoped the question
My fault, I left out the context: I meant in the case of X
cards.pmNote: 跨部門溝通出錯時搶著認下「我沒說清楚」，比釐清誰的錯更快解決問題。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

cards.quote: I want to zoom out a little bit before we go in a different direction.
cards.zh: 在我們轉去別的方向之前，我想先拉高一點來看。
cards.why: 轉場的雙動作句：zoom out（先升高視角收尾目前的主題）＋ before we go in a different direction（預告要換題）。聽者知道現在在哪、接下來去哪，會議節奏就不會亂。
swaps: Let me pull up a level before we switch topics
One big-picture question, then I'll move us on
cards.pmNote: 換題前先做一次拉高總結，是主持人維持議程感的基本動作。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

cards.pattern: If you were in my shoes, how would you approach [X]?
cards.quote: Because I asked them to ask a golden question, if you were in my shoes, how would you approach this? I call that the golden question. It's such a creative question.
cards.zh: 我請他們問一個「黃金問題」：如果你是我，你會怎麼處理？我把它叫做黃金問題，這問題非常有創造性。
cards.why: 把對方放進你的位置，他就不必評價你、也不必負責，只要「代入」就好——心理成本瞬間降到最低。台灣人請教常問「你覺得我這樣可以嗎？」逼對方當評審，對方反而不敢說真話。
swaps: If you were me, what would you do here?
How would you play this if you were in my position?
cards.pmNote: Phyl 把找工作當產品做：Mnookin 兩頁紙（要什麼／不要什麼）→ listening tour →收斂出 candidate market fit。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

cards.pattern: What did I do well? What do you think my strengths are? Do you think I'm accurately projecting myself?
cards.quote: This is people you used to work with before, go ask them, "Hey, what did I do well, what do you think my strengths are? What do you think I'm a fit for?
cards.zh: 去問以前的同事：「我哪裡做得好？你覺得我的強項是什麼？我是這樣想的——你覺得我對自己的認知準確嗎？」
cards.why: 最後那句 Do you think I accurately am projecting myself? 是關鍵：不是問「我好不好」，而是問「我對自己的描述準不準」。把問題從價值判斷改成事實校準，對方就敢講真話了。
swaps: Does how I describe myself match how you actually experienced working with me?
Is there a gap between how I see myself and how you see me?
cards.pmNote: Phyl 稱這叫 reverse exit interview：離職面談通常公司問你，這次換你問前同事。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

cards.pattern: I know you don't know me, but I would love your advice on [具體的事] and what you would do if you were in my shoes.
cards.quote: If they had reached out to me and said, "I know you don't know me. I have this small software company. I'm not well-connected, but I would love your advice on how to grow this business and what you would do if you were in my shoes,"
cards.zh: 如果他們寫信說：「我知道你不認識我。我有間小軟體公司，我人脈也不廣，但我很想聽聽你對怎麼把它做大的建議——如果你是我會怎麼做？」
cards.why: 冷開發信的完整結構：先主動承認關係為零（I know you don't know me），再給一句最小的背景，最後 ask 只要「建議」不要「資源」。台灣人寫冷信最常見的死法是直接跳到「可以幫我介紹某某人嗎」。
swaps: We haven't met, but I'd really value your perspective on...
This is out of the blue, but I'd love your take on...
cards.pmNote: Phyl 的判準：求「觀點」幾乎都會被接受，求「引薦」在關係建立前幾乎都會被忽略。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

cards.pattern: I have a favor to ask. Would you be willing to [具體的事]?
cards.quote: Whereas I should said, "Lenny, I have a favor to ask. Would you be willing to do this?" You just say yes or no.
cards.zh: 我應該直接說：「我有件事想拜託你，你願意幫這個忙嗎？」你回是或不是就好。
cards.why: hide the ask（把請求包裝成「這對你也有好處喔」）是英語職場很容易被識破的失禮。先自報「這是一個 favor」，等於預先給對方拒絕的權利，反而更容易被答應。
swaps: Quick favor to ask — feel free to say no.
This is purely a favor, no strings: would you be up for...?
cards.pmNote: 同理適用於 cold intro：沒先問就把兩個人湊在一起，通常是幫了 A、卻在跟 B 收人情。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

cards.pattern: Is it just me, or is [X]?
cards.quote: And he says, first question he has is, "Is this meeting, is it just me or is this meeting intense?"
cards.zh: 他說，他問的第一個問題是：「這個會議……是只有我這樣覺得，還是它真的很緊繃？」
cards.why: Is it just me, or...? 是英語職場最好用的一句社交校準：既承認了自己的困惑，又把它降級成「可能只是我」，對方不但不會看輕你，還多半會鬆一口氣說「我也是」。非母語者在陌生會議上最需要這一句。
swaps: Am I the only one finding this hard to follow?
Is this normally this fast, or am I just new?
cards.pmNote: Bradley Horowitz 就是用這句跟當時同為 director 的 Sundar Pichai 建立信任，後來一路做到 VP of Product。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

cards.pattern: You strike me as [正面評價]. Why [看似矛盾的事實]?
cards.quote: "I haven't been here very long, but you, Sundar, you strike me as a really thoughtful person and great leader. Why is your remit just working on a toolbar for Marissa?" Whoa.
cards.zh: 「我來這裡沒多久，但 Sundar，我覺得你是個非常有想法的人、很好的領導者。那為什麼你負責的範圍只是一個工具列？」
cards.why: you strike me as X 是「我的主觀印象」而非「事實斷言」，所以後面接一個尖銳問題也不會變成冒犯。前面再加 I haven't been here very long 當免責聲明，把可能的無禮預先報備掉。
swaps: You come across as someone who...
My read on you is that..., so I'm curious why...
cards.pmNote: 問前先確認關係存量：同一句話對信任你的人是好奇，對不熟的人是侮辱。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

cards.pattern: You have not earned that yet. That's not a statement about your worth. It's just [事實].
cards.quote: I'm like, "You have not earned that yet. That's not a statement about your worth. It's just you're not ready for that conversation."
cards.zh: 我會說：「這個你還沒掙到。這不是在評斷你的價值，只是你還沒到可以進行那場對話的階段。」
cards.why: 拒絕的同時明講「這不是在評價你這個人」，把 rejection 從人格層拉回事實層。That's not a statement about your worth 這句是整段的緩衝墊，沒有它，前一句就是羞辱。
swaps: That's not a judgment on you — it's just timing.
Nothing to do with your ability; the relationship just isn't there yet.
cards.pmNote: 擋需求也適用：把「不做」歸因於順位與時機，而不是提案人的能力。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

cards.pattern: I acknowledge that that's a reaction some people have. That's totally valid. [然後才反駁]
cards.quote: I acknowledge that that's a reaction that some people have. That's totally valid. This is unusual, what we're doing here.
cards.zh: 我承認有些人確實會有這種反應，這完全合理。我們在做的事本來就不太尋常。
cards.why: 先幫反對者把反對意見說出來、蓋章認證「合理」，對方的防衛就卸掉一半。最狠的是第三句主動承認自己的方案很怪——搶在對方之前講缺點，反而增加可信度。
swaps: That's a fair reaction, and honestly a common one.
I'd probably feel the same way in your position.
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem 的口語版：把最可能的反對先講完，會議剩下的時間才有機會談實質。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

cards.pattern: Every bone in your body is going to want to [直覺反應]. Just know that's what everyone feels.
cards.quote: That's why you need your job search council. This is when you really need to ask for help because every bone in your body is going to say, "I'm not going to negotiate. That's going to make it worse," and it almost never does.
cards.zh: 這就是為什麼你需要求職小組。你全身上下每根骨頭都會喊：「我不要談判，談了只會更糟。」但幾乎從來不會更糟。
cards.why: every bone in your body 這個誇張慣用語，把「我知道你會抗拒」講得有畫面又不說教。先描述對方的內心戲，再用資料打臉——比直接說「你錯了」有效太多。
swaps: Everything in you is going to want to...
Your gut is going to scream at you to...
cards.pmNote: Phyl 的數據：長期來看，開口要更高薪水有 87% 的機率會拿到（市場差時較低，但仍值得問）。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

cards.pattern: Can I share one story about [主題]?
cards.quote: Can I share one story about candidate market fit-
cards.zh: 我可以分享一個關於「候選人市場適配」的故事嗎？
cards.why: 插話的最短完整結構：請求許可＋預告內容＋限定份量（one story）。加了 one 之後對方知道你只會佔用一小段時間，答應的成本就低了。母語者在會議上搶麥克風幾乎都用這種包裝。
swaps: Can I jump in with a quick example?
Mind if I add one data point here?
cards.pmNote: 會議上的存在感不是講得多，而是每次開口都先讓人知道你要花掉多少時間、換來什麼。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

cards.quote: If we go up to the 30,000-foot level, what are we doing here? What's our mission? We're building a private safety net for all those who've been laid off or let go.
cards.zh: 如果拉到三萬英尺的高度看，我們到底在做什麼？我們的使命是什麼？我們在為所有被裁員的人建一張民間的安全網。
cards.why: go up to the 30,000-foot level 是英語職場最常用的「切換視角」訊號詞，宣告接下來要離開細節。後面接自問自答（what are we doing here? what's our mission?）製造節奏，讓聽眾準備好接一句大的。
swaps: Let's zoom out for a second.
If we pull all the way back, the question is...
cards.pmNote: 細節會議陷入僵局時，先拉到 30,000 呎重述目標，往往比繼續辯細節快。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

cards.quote: And it will still be hard. It will still be hard. I wish that weren't true, Lenny.
cards.zh: 而且還是會很辛苦。真的還是會很辛苦。我也希望不是這樣。
cards.why: I wish that weren't true 是一句成本極低、效果極高的同理：你沒有假裝能解決，但你站在對方那一邊。虛擬語氣（weren't）在這裡是必須的，用 isn't 就變成單純陳述、失去情感。
swaps: I wish I had better news.
I hate that this is the answer, but it is the answer.
cards.pmNote: 報延期／砍功能時，講一句 I wish that weren't true 比多解釋三分鐘理由更有效。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

cards.quote: And I want you to say, "This is great. I want to talk about money, but before we do, I want to think about some of the things that will set me up to see succeed in this role.
cards.zh: 我要你這樣說：「這很好。我想談薪水，但在那之前，我想先談談有哪些東西能讓我在這個角色上成功。」
cards.why: 談判的順序設計：先確認雙方都想要「你成功」，再談錢。set me up to succeed 這個片語把所有要求（預算、人力、訓練）都包裝成公司的利益，不是你的索取。這是整集最值錢的一句。
swaps: Before we land on numbers, can we talk about what I'd need to deliver on this?
I'd love to align on what success requires first, then comp.
cards.pmNote: Phyl 的四腳談判：預算、人力、訓練、決策權——全部綁回已經談定的 job mission OKRs。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

cards.pattern: Are you open to [數字]? That was really what I was hoping for. Is that something we can talk about?
cards.quote: Lenny, you can say, "Hey, are you open to 450? That was really what I was hoping for.
cards.zh: 你可以說：「你們可以接受 450 嗎？這其實是我原本期待的數字。這件事我們可以談嗎？」
cards.why: Are you open to X? 把要求改寫成一個「是非題」，對方回 no 也不傷關係。再加 Is that something we can talk about? 等於連被拒絕之後的下一步都先鋪好。這是全英語談判裡風險最低的開價句。
swaps: Is there any flexibility on the base?
Would you be open to revisiting the number?
cards.pmNote: 盡量跟 hiring manager 談而不是 recruiter——hiring manager 通常沒有明確預算上限，也更願意替你去爭取。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

cards.pattern: Don't hear this as [誤解]. We're trying to figure out [真正目的].
cards.quote: Now, again, don't hear this as antagonistic. We're not antagonistic here. We're trying to say, "What's going to help me succeed?"
cards.zh: 再說一次，不要把這聽成對立。我們不是在對抗。我們是在問：什麼能幫我把這件事做成？
cards.why: Don't hear this as X 是預先攔截誤解的專用句型——不是解釋你講了什麼，是規定對方該怎麼接收。在跨文化溝通裡特別有用，因為你無法確定對方會不會把直接當成冒犯。
swaps: I don't want this to land as pushback.
Read this as curiosity, not criticism.
cards.pmNote: 談判姿態決定結果：同樣的要求，用 collaborative 框架講，公司通常會加碼而不是縮手。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

cards.pattern: I've thought about what [X] is. I want to make sure I'm understanding it correctly. Can I share something with you?
cards.quote: I want you to pull the hiring manager aside and say, "Hey, Lenny, you're the hiring manager. I've thought about what the role is. I want to make sure I'm understanding it correctly.
cards.zh: 我要你把用人主管拉到一旁說：「我想過這個職位到底是什麼，我想確認我理解得對不對。我可以跟你分享一下嗎？」
cards.why: 把「我幫你重寫了職位描述」這種可能顯得自大的動作，包裝成「我想確認我理解對不對」。三段式：宣告我做了功課→降級成求證→請求許可。整個攻擊性歸零，但東西照樣送到對方桌上。
swaps: I put some thinking down on this — can I walk you through it and you tell me where I'm off?
I drafted my understanding of the role. Mind sanity-checking it?
cards.pmNote: Phyl 的 job mission with OKRs：面試中期私下給用人主管看你自訂的職責與成果指標，是他書裡拿到 offer 最有效的單一戰術。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

cards.pattern: Once upon a time [現狀]. And then one day [轉折]. And because of that [連鎖]. And finally [留給世界的東西].
cards.quote: And because of that and because of that... And I usually like to end it with, and finally, this was the last thing you left the world with.
cards.zh: 「很久以前……然後有一天……因為這樣、又因為這樣……最後，這就是你留給世界的東西。」
cards.why: 把童話的骨架直接搬進商業簡報。because of that 的重複是引擎，逼你把因果一節一節扣起來，不能跳步。台灣人做願景常直接跳到結論畫面，中間的因果鏈缺了，聽眾就不會相信。
swaps: Today...; then...; which means...; and ultimately...
Here's where we are. Here's what changes. Here's what that unlocks.
cards.pmNote: Ebi 的三種願景載體：Mad Libs 故事、未來的 TechCrunch 標題、App Store 截圖草稿——都比 PRD 快。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.pattern: Here's the problem statement. How might we [解決]? And here's what we think it looks like when we ship it.
cards.quote: And that's the thing they used to say, "Hey, leadership, this is the problem statement. Here's what we think how might we solve this big problem and here's what we think it looks like when we ship it." That's a mini-vision.
cards.zh: 「各位主管，這是問題陳述。我們認為可以怎麼解這個大問題，還有我們認為做出來會長什麼樣。」這就是一個小型願景。
cards.why: how might we 是設計思考留下的最好用句型：might 保留了「還沒定案」的空間，we 把提問者也綁進解法裡，所以不會變成質問。三段（問題→怎麼解→長什麼樣）是向上報告的最小完整單位。
swaps: The problem is X. How might we...? And here's the rough shape of the answer.
Problem, hypothesis, and what shipped looks like.
cards.pmNote: Lenny 稱之為 fertile question：好的問題會長出討論，壞的問題只會長出沉默。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.pattern: Do not use [藉口] as the excuse for why you don't [該做的事].
cards.quote: Do not use, I don't have a designer, to be the excuse for why you don't bring it to life.
cards.zh: 不要拿「我沒有設計師」當作你不把它具象化的藉口。
cards.why: 直接把對方預備好的藉口點名封殺。命令句＋Do not use X as the excuse 的結構很強硬，但因為它針對的是「藉口」不是「人」，在英語職場不會被當成人身攻擊。
swaps: "No resources" isn't a reason not to sketch it.
Let's not let tooling be the blocker here.
cards.pmNote: 低擬真度的手繪也有用——設計師看到醜的版本，反而更容易被激起來把它做好。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.pattern: We heard you, we parsed everything into these [N], and that's why we came to [結論].
cards.quote: It's like we heard you and then we parse them into these 10 and everybody agreed with these 10 and therefore that's why we came up with this solution.
cards.zh: 人最在意的是知道你有聽進去。「你這個願景是怎麼來的？」這種質疑就消失了——我們聽了大家的意見，收斂成這 10 條，而且大家都同意。
cards.why: 把「我聽了你的意見」變成可驗證的流程證據（你給了 10 條、被收進來、你也點頭過）。英語職場的 alignment 不是說服，是讓對方在最終結論裡找得到自己的指紋。
swaps: This came directly from what you all put in — here's the trace.
Everything on this list came from one of your teams.
cards.pmNote: 會前先收集每個利害關係人的「你該知道的 10 件事」，evangelize 階段的阻力會少一半。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.pattern: I'm not trying to get you to 100% certainty. I'm just trying to get you on the ride.
cards.quote: And then once the team has kind of gotten to a place, I'm not trying to get anyone to a hundred percent certainty, I'm trying to get you just on the ride. They will come, right?
cards.zh: 團隊到了某個程度就好——我不是要每個人百分之百確定，我只是要你先上車。剩下的他們自己會跟上。
cards.why: 主動把「成功標準」講低。一旦你宣告不需要對方 100% 同意，對方的抵抗就沒有對象了。get you on the ride 這個比喻也很關鍵：上車是可逆的，簽字不是。
swaps: I don't need you convinced, I need you curious.
You don't have to buy it — just don't get off the bus yet.
cards.pmNote: 願景文件開「留言權限」而不是「檢視權限」：讓人留得下指紋，就留得住人。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.pattern: Go as big as possible. Let people tell you to pull back.
cards.quote: Go big. Let people tell you to pull back. Let your manager use lasso and pull you back.
cards.zh: 就是要大。讓別人來叫你收，讓你的主管拿套索把你拉回來。
cards.why: Let people tell you to pull back 是很反台灣直覺的一句：預設值不是自我審查，而是先過頭、等人喊停。對習慣先自我打折的人來說，這句話等於一張授權書。
swaps: Aim past the target and let someone dial it back.
Better to be reined in than to have pre-shrunk it yourself.
cards.pmNote: Ebi 第一次做願景練習時只是 L4 PM——職級不是做願景的門檻。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.pattern: Let's say we weren't in the room — which one does the team want to get behind?
cards.quote: I'm like, "Let's say we weren't in the room as the leadership team," which is the one the team wants to get behind. Then you'll sometimes see the team hasn't even done the work between themselves talking.
cards.zh: 我會問：「假設我們這些主管不在這個房間，你們團隊自己最想投哪一個？」有時候你會發現他們彼此之間根本還沒討論過。
cards.why: 把自己的權力暫時從房間裡拿掉，讓對方能講真話。這是資深主管必備的一句——因為只要你在場，多數答案都是說給你聽的。
swaps: Forget what you think I want to hear — what's your call?
If this were entirely your decision, which way?
cards.pmNote: 團隊丟 A/B 兩案給主管選，通常代表他們還沒做完自己的功課。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.pattern: That's too easy — to come to me with A and B and have me do the work. Go figure out why you can't stand by A.
cards.quote: that's too easy to come to me and be like, "Oh, here's A and B. You do the work and tell me which you one to pick." No way.
cards.zh: 「這裡有 A 案和 B 案，你來想、你來選」——這太輕鬆了。不行。
cards.why: 退件的同時給出明確的下一步動作（go figure out why…）。英語職場的「打回去」如果只有 No way 會顯得暴躁，加上一個具體任務就變成教練。
swaps: Come back with a recommendation, not a menu.
I'll take the risk conversation, not the choice.
cards.pmNote: 有把握就給建議＋風險清單；沒把握就講清楚你卡在哪一個未知，不要把選擇題丟給主管。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.quote: I'm in too many conversations where I'm like, "Who is on the hook for this decision? Who cares if this decision is made?" It's not like six people with consensus. Who is the person?
cards.zh: 我參加過太多會議，我會問：「這個決定是誰扛？誰真的在乎它有沒有被做出來？」不是六個人共識，是哪一個人？
cards.why: on the hook for 是英語職場講「責任歸屬」最口語也最不傷人的說法（比 responsible for 更有「掛在那裡」的重量感）。連問兩個問題把「大家一起負責＝沒人負責」直接戳破。
swaps: Who's the DRI here?
Whose name goes next to this one?
cards.pmNote: informed captain：一個人做決定，但他有義務把所有 context 收齊。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.pattern: I don't believe in being [表淺的]. I believe in being [有深度的]. And that's a very different thing.
cards.quote: I do not believe in being liked. I believe in being loved, right? And that's a very, very different thing.
cards.zh: 我不追求被喜歡。我追求被愛。這是兩件非常、非常不一樣的事。
cards.why: I don't believe in X, I believe in Y 是英語裡宣告價值觀最有力的骨架：不解釋、不鋪陳，靠一組近義詞的對比製造張力。第三句 And that's a very different thing 是刻意留白，逼聽者自己去想差在哪。
swaps: I'm not optimizing for consensus, I'm optimizing for clarity.
It's not about being nice; it's about being useful.
cards.pmNote: Ebi 的定義：愛＝為了另一個人的成長而延伸自己。所以愛有時候長得像難聽的回饋。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.pattern: When the feedback comes in raw, they know it's in their best interest — because I've shown enough times that I care.
cards.quote: So when the feedback is coming like raw, they know that it's in their best interest because I've shown them enough times that I genuinely care about the person behind the role.
cards.zh: 所以當回饋很生硬地丟過來，他們知道那是為他們好——因為我已經用夠多次證明，我在乎的是角色背後那個人。
cards.why: the person behind the role（角色背後的那個人）是一個很好用的說法，把「我關心你」講得具體而不油膩。整句也點出關鍵機制：坦率的額度是靠平時累積的，不是講的時候臨時借的。
swaps: I've earned the right to be blunt with them.
The candor works because the care came first.
cards.pmNote: radical candor 的前置條件是 care personally——只有 challenge 沒有 care，就只是刻薄。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.pattern: Maybe that's another conversation for another day, but [先給一句版本].
cards.quote: Maybe that's another podcast for another day, but I fundamentally believe in when products take on some kind of persona.
cards.zh: 這可能要另開一集才講得完，但我真的相信產品應該要有某種人格。
cards.why: 把離題的東西「掛起來」而不是丟掉：先宣告這裡不展開，再給一句最短版本。這讓你既守住了會議節奏，又沒有把自己的洞見吞回去——台灣人多半直接吞回去。
swaps: That's a whole other thread — parking it for now.
Happy to go deeper offline; the short version is...
cards.pmNote: 會議上有價值的離題要放進 parking lot，不要當場辯完也不要當場消失。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.pattern: I'm [非典型背景]. I don't have [別人有的資歷], I didn't [別人走的路]. And I'm here.
cards.quote: I just want to say, I'm this Nigerian girl. I don't have an MBA, I didn't work in consulting, and I'm here, right?
cards.zh: 我只想說：我就是個奈及利亞女生。我沒有 MBA，也沒做過顧問業，但我人就在這裡。
cards.why: 非典型背景者講自己成績的教科書句型：把三個「缺的」快速列完，最後用一句 And I'm here 收——不辯解、不悲情，讓事實自己說話。對台灣讀者價值極高，因為華人習慣先道歉自己不夠格。
swaps: No CS degree, no big-tech pedigree — and I still shipped this.
I came in through the side door, and the work speaks for itself.
cards.pmNote: Ebi 認為最好的 PM 常常是從別的職能轉過來的——因為你對「另一邊」有真的同理心。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.pattern: Some of the best [職位] come from somewhere else, because you have empathy for being on the other side.
cards.quote: I genuinely think that some of the best product managers come from something else because you have empathy for being on the other side.
cards.zh: 我真心覺得最好的產品經理很多都是從別的領域轉過來的，因為你真的體會過站在另一邊是什麼感覺。
cards.why: 把「我不是本科出身」這個弱點，改寫成一個結構性優勢，而且理由具體（你當過對面那個人）。轉職者面試被問「你為什麼沒相關經驗」時，這是最漂亮的回法。
swaps: Coming from support means I've been on the receiving end of every bad decision.
My detour is the reason I catch things others don't.
cards.pmNote: 10,000 小時不必等到有職稱才開始累積：先用你自己愛用的 app 練「找出前 10 個問題」。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.quote: I read the email, I'm like, "What do you want me to do? Is this an FYI? Are you saying there's a problem? Do you want me to help?"
cards.zh: 我讀完信心想：「你到底要我做什麼？這是知會嗎？你是在說有問題嗎？還是你要我幫忙？」
cards.why: 三個選項一次攤開，讓對方只要選一個。用在你收到不知所云的訊息時很有效；反過來也是提醒：你自己寫信時，開頭就該標明是 FYI、求助、還是要決策。
swaps: Just to check — is this FYI, a decision request, or a help request?
What do you need from me on this one?
cards.pmNote: PM 的工作是製造清晰度；連自己的信都要讓人一秒知道該做什麼。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.pattern: If I could put all of this into an AI and it would spit out [你的產出], then you haven't done your job.
cards.quote: If I could put all the research into Bard or ChatGPT and it could spit out a PRD, then you haven't done your job.
cards.zh: 如果我把所有研究丟進 ChatGPT，它就能吐出一份 PRD，那代表你根本沒做到你的工作。
cards.why: 用一個條件句設下標準，而不是直接罵人。If [AI 就能做到], then [你沒做到你的工作] 這個結構現在極度好用，可以套在任何職能上，逼團隊去想自己的不可替代處在哪。
swaps: If a model can produce it from the same inputs, what did you add?
Where's the judgment that isn't in the prompt?
cards.pmNote: AI 時代 PM 的差異化在 product sense——一種靠大量接觸好產品養出來的「感覺」，不是邏輯推導。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.pattern: [被輕視的東西] is the product. Period.
cards.quote: By the way, the infrastructure piece, I know it's a nugget on the side but infrastructure is the product. Period.
cards.zh: 順帶一提，基礎建設這塊——我知道這是題外話——但基礎建設就是產品。就這樣。
cards.why: Period. 是英語裡的句點宣告，等於「這件事我不打算辯論」。再用一次改名（tech debt → product debt）把責任從工程搬到自己頭上——重新命名是 PM 最省力的一種奪權。
swaps: Reliability is a feature. Full stop.
That's not eng debt, that's roadmap debt.
cards.pmNote: 把「技術債」改叫「產品債」，這筆帳就進了你的 roadmap，而不是永遠等工程自己找時間。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

cards.pattern: I'm okay at those things. I'm potentially world-class at this other thing. Let me double down there.
cards.quote: I'm potentially world-class at this other thing. Let me see what it feels like to double down on this area."
cards.zh: 比較好的說法是：「那些事我做得還行。但這件事我可能可以做到世界級。那就往這邊押吧。」
cards.why: 解釋轉職的黃金公式：不是「我當不成工程師只好當 PM」（settle for），而是「我把賭注押在我最強的地方」（double down）。同一段人生履歷，動詞一換，聽起來就從退而求其次變成主動選擇。
swaps: I was competent there; I think I can be exceptional here.
It wasn't a step down, it was a bet on my sharpest edge.
cards.pmNote: Kevin 建議想當 PM 的人先做工程、設計或業務——你要接手誰的責任，就先去做那份工作。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.quote: I don't want to make it seem like it was me against everyone because that was definitely not the case. I think the starting engineers and designers on that team really cared about the quality of what they built too.
cards.zh: 我不想講得好像是我一個人對抗全世界，完全不是那樣。那個團隊的工程師跟設計師本來就很在乎品質。
cards.why: 講完自己的功勞後主動拆掉英雄敘事。I don't want to make it seem like… 是英語職場最實用的自我修正詞——它讓你可以先把故事講精彩，再把功勞分回去，兩邊都不虧。
swaps: To be clear, this wasn't me pushing a rock uphill alone.
I don't want to overstate my role here.
cards.pmNote: 績效面談講成績時，把團隊的貢獻主動說出來，反而讓你的判斷力顯得更可信。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.quote: Footnote, correlation versus causation. It's all put out there.
cards.zh: 附註一下：相關不等於因果。我先把話擺在這裡。
cards.why: 被誇獎時的高階回法：不否認、不謙讓，改成給一個技術性的免責聲明。Footnote 這個用法（把整句話當成註腳）很輕巧，既幽默又表現出你自己在檢查因果——反而讓人更信你。
swaps: Caveat: I can't prove those two are connected.
Survivorship bias, probably — worth saying out loud.
cards.pmNote: Kevin 的 decision log：記下判斷與理由，設好日曆提醒回頭對答案——這是練 product sense 最便宜的方式。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.pattern: I do want to apply a pretty severe caveat here though, which is [限制].
cards.quote: I do want to apply a pretty severe caveat here though, which is, a decision log is not a replacement for building products. It's a additional complimentary thing that you can be doing on your own.
cards.zh: 不過我要加一個很重的但書：決策日誌不能取代真的去做產品。它只是你自己可以額外做的補充。
cards.why: apply a caveat（加但書）是把自己剛講的東西「限定射程」的專業說法。加上 severe 這個形容詞，等於告訴聽眾這句但書比前面的建議還重要——一種先發制人的防誤用。
swaps: Big asterisk on all of that:
One important boundary on this advice:
cards.pmNote: 光坐著看市場評論不會讓你變強；決策日誌是輔助動作，不是主訓練。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.pattern: I explicitly do not mean [容易被誤解的版本].
cards.quote: I explicitly do not mean read a bunch of other PM artifacts. You're not going to become a better writer by reading PRDs or whatever it is or support articles. It needs to be writing that compels.
cards.zh: 我明確講：我不是叫你去讀一堆 PM 文件。讀 PRD 不會讓你變成更好的作者。你要讀的是那種會推著你行動的文字。
cards.why: explicitly do not mean 是精準度極高的一句：先封死最可能的誤讀，再給正解。給建議時最怕對方照字面執行到錯的地方，這句話就是那道防呆。
swaps: To be very clear, that's not what I'm suggesting.
I want to rule out one reading of this:
cards.pmNote: Kevin 的判準：好文字要 compel（推動行動），不是讓人覺得 interesting 就好。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.pattern: This is maybe going to come across a little bit flippant, but [直白的話].
cards.quote: This is maybe going to come across a little bit flippant, but they can't stop you from sending an email technically. So I'm just going to send the email.
cards.zh: 這樣講可能有點輕佻，但嚴格來說他們也不能阻止我寄信。所以我就照寄。
cards.why: come across as 是「給人的感覺是」——用它預告自己接下來的話可能不中聽，等於先幫對方消化。台灣人要嘛不敢講，要嘛講完才補「我不是那個意思」，這句是把補救提前。
swaps: This might sound harsh, but...
At the risk of sounding glib —
cards.pmNote: Kevin 的 unsell email 讓 offer 階段流失 30% 候選人，招募同事很不爽——但六個月後的留任率救回來了。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.pattern: I'm cool with six of these. This one freaks me out. Can we talk more?
cards.quote: Most of the time they will say, "Thank you. I am cool with six of these. This one freaks me out.
cards.zh: 多數人會回：「這裡面有六點我可以接受。但這一點讓我很不安，可以再聊聊嗎？」
cards.why: 回應一份混合好壞的提案時最好用的三段：先劃出可接受的範圍→只標出一個真正的痛點→提出下一步。比「我有一些疑慮」精準太多，對方馬上知道要處理什麼。
swaps: Most of this works for me; number three is the sticking point.
I'm fine with the scope. The timeline is what worries me.
cards.pmNote: unsell email：offer 階段主動把最糟的八件事寫給候選人——看完還一樣興奮的，就是 A+ 人選。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.pattern: I'll be really clear: the expectation here is going to be [不好聽的現實].
cards.quote: We are a series A startup. We are pushing really hard at product-market fit. The expectation here is going to be that you're online at 10:00, that you can occasionally hop on a meeting on a Saturday or Sunday."
cards.zh: 「我們是 A 輪新創。我們正在拚產品市場契合。這裡的預期是你晚上十點還在線上，週六日偶爾也要開會。」
cards.why: I'll be really clear 之後接一句具體到時間點的現實。壞消息要用具體數字講，不能用形容詞（"it can get busy"）——含糊的預告等於沒預告，六個月後對方一樣覺得被騙。
swaps: Let me be upfront about the parts people struggle with here.
Here's the version I'd want to know before saying yes.
cards.pmNote: 壞消息前置的成本是 offer 流失率，回報是六個月後的留任率——這筆帳要跟老闆講清楚。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.pattern: I need 20 minutes of focused time to interrogate this. We're not going to talk — you read, I respond in real time.
cards.quote: "I need 20 minutes of focused time to interrogate something that I've done. We're not going to talk. I'm literally going to force us into a room or Zoom.
cards.zh: 「我需要二十分鐘的專注時間來拷問我做的東西。我們不用講話。我就是要把大家關進一個會議室或 Zoom。」
cards.why: 開會前先宣告「這場會不講話」，把大家對會議的預期整個換掉。interrogate（拷問）用在自己的文件上很有意思：你不是在求贊同，你是在請人來拆。
swaps: This is a working session, not a presentation.
Twenty minutes, cameras off, comment as you read.
cards.pmNote: silent read（Amazon／Square 傳統）：非同步收不到回饋時，把「讀文件」本身變成一場會。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.pattern: There is a world of difference between reading a report about [X] and standing with [X].
cards.quote: The best comparison I can give is, there is a world of difference between reading a report about a lime cook and then standing with a lime cook.
cards.zh: 我能給的最好對照是：讀一份關於廚房廚師的報告，跟真的站在他旁邊，是天差地遠的兩件事。
cards.why: a world of difference between A and B 是英語裡最有力的對比句型之一。這裡的技巧是兩邊都用具體動作（reading a report / standing with），而不是抽象概念——畫面出來了，論點就成立了。
swaps: Reading the summary and sitting in the room are not the same job.
Second-hand data and first-hand exposure aren't interchangeable.
cards.pmNote: Kevin 的原則：PM 不該只透過「磨砂玻璃」看使用者——研究報告、業務轉述都已經被別人處理過。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.pattern: That is a very tempting lie to tell yourself.
cards.quote: I can use my intuition from the hundred interviews I've already done. I don't need to do one more interview."
cards.zh: 「我已經訪過一百個使用者了，靠直覺就夠。我不需要再訪一個。」
cards.why: a tempting lie to tell yourself 精準命中一種特定的自欺：不是不知道，是知道了卻選擇相信方便的版本。用 tempting 而不是 stupid，讓被說的人不必防衛，就能承認。
swaps: That's the comfortable story, not the true one.
It's an easy thing to convince yourself of.
cards.pmNote: 使用者的生活一直在變；你腦中的模型會過期，而且不會發出過期通知。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.quote: you eventually need to convince yourself that there is a difference between you not being good at something and a business or company not needing that thing at a particular moment in time
cards.zh: 你終究得說服自己：「你不擅長某件事」跟「公司此刻不需要那件事」，是兩回事。
cards.why: 被裁員、被拒絕之後最需要的一句切割。英語職場很習慣把「人」和「當下的需求」分開講，因為這樣才可能在下一場面試裡不帶怨氣地敘述同一段經歷。
swaps: That was a fit problem, not a capability problem.
The company's needs changed; my skills didn't disappear.
cards.pmNote: Kevin 被裁時太太懷孕九個月——他說最痛的不是失業，是「我以為我是 PM，這證明我不是」。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.pattern: My skills and the way that company operates were not compatible.
cards.quote: The second one though is my skills and the way that company operates are not compatible.
cards.zh: 第二種是：我的能力跟那家公司的運作方式不相容。
cards.why: 面試被問「上一份為什麼結束」的最佳骨架：用 compatible 這個中性詞（像插頭與插座），不指責公司也不貶低自己，再補一個「這很常見」的觀察把它常態化。
swaps: The operating style there and the way I work didn't line up.
It was an environment mismatch more than anything else.
cards.pmNote: 同一個人換環境就起飛，多半不是能力變了，是棲地變了。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.pattern: You are not bad. It's that the machine you're a part of isn't the kind you thrive in.
cards.quote: But the reality is, you are not bad. It is that maybe the way that your environment is working, the machine that you exist as a part of, is not the kind that you thrive in.
cards.zh: 但事實是：你不是不好。而是你所處的環境、你身在其中的那台機器，不是能讓你發揮的那種。這其實是很有力量的認知。
cards.why: 績效對話最難的一刻——對方聽到的是「我很爛」。這句把焦點從「人」移到「機器」，然後用 And that's empowering 把結論翻正：因為機器可以換，人格不能。
swaps: This isn't a verdict on you; it's a read on the fit.
The system isn't set up for how you do your best work.
cards.pmNote: 績效談話後給對方兩條路：改變自己的工作方式以適配環境，或去找適配的環境——兩條都在他控制範圍內。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.quote: writing is clarity at scale, and a key component to a PM's job is creating clarity both internally and externally
cards.zh: 寫作就是「規模化的清晰」，而 PM 工作的核心之一，就是對內對外製造清晰。
cards.why: X is Y at scale 是矽谷極常見的定義句型（clarity at scale / trust at scale / taste at scale）。一句話同時給出定義和價值主張，開會時拿來當論點的開頭非常好用。
swaps: Documentation is judgment at scale.
A good spec is alignment at scale.
cards.pmNote: Kevin 的判準：如果你沒辦法賣自己的產品、也沒辦法支援它，我不相信你能做出它。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.pattern: Follow me on a detour to [不相干的領域] for a second.
cards.quote: Yeah, so follow me on the detour to science world temporarily. If we all remember high school science classes, there was this concept of potential and kinetic energy.
cards.zh: 先跟我繞去科學世界一下。如果大家還記得高中物理，有個概念叫位能跟動能。
cards.why: 要講一個長類比之前先報備。follow me on a detour 讓聽眾知道「接下來這段看起來離題，但會繞回來」，於是他們願意等——沒有這句預告，長類比很容易被打斷。
swaps: Bear with me on a tangent for a second.
Let me take the long way round to answer that.
cards.pmNote: Kevin 的 PM 定義：把團隊的位能，用最小損耗轉成使用者拿到的動能。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.pattern: The best way to get feedback is not to ask what people think, but to put something concrete in front of them.
cards.quote: the best way to get feedback from people is not by asking what they think, but to put something concrete in front of them and then have them react to it, right?
cards.zh: 要拿到回饋，最好的方式不是問人家怎麼想，而是先擺一個具體的東西在他面前，讓他反應，對吧？
cards.why: not by X, but by Y 的對比句型把方法論壓成一句。實務價值極高：開放式問句（你覺得呢）在英語會議上通常換來沉默，一份粗糙草稿卻能換來十條意見。
swaps: Don't ask for opinions, ask for reactions to a draft.
Put a strawman up and let people knock it down.
cards.pmNote: Kevin 稱之為 tuning fork（音叉）：先發出一個音，讓別人告訴你偏了多少。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

cards.quote: And if you push a really experienced product director like that, they're going to go, "Good point, I don't. I'm going to go find out."
cards.zh: 你這樣逼一個真正資深的產品總監，他會說：「說得對，我確實不知道。我去查清楚。」
cards.why: 承認不知道的極簡三拍：認可提問（Good point）→承認（I don't）→承諾行動（I'm going to go find out）。九個字。台灣人常在第一拍就開始解釋，反而顯得心虛；資深的訊號是快、短、帶下一步。
swaps: Fair — I don't know. Let me get back to you with the answer.
You're right to push. I'll go check and come back.
cards.pmNote: Tom 的追問法：「你怎麼知道那是詐欺？」→「資料裡標的」→「你知道它怎麼被標的嗎？」→那你就不知道那是詐欺。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.pattern: How do you know that? Do you know how it gets [產生的]? Okay, so you don't actually know.
cards.quote: Turn around and be like, "How do you know that was fraud?" "Oh, it's labeled in the dataset as fraud. "Okay. Do you know how it gets labeled?"
cards.zh: 你就回問：「你怎麼知道那是詐欺？」「喔，資料集裡標成詐欺。」「好，那你知道它是怎麼被標上去的嗎？」
cards.why: 三層追問的階梯，每一層都只用一個中性問句，不帶指控。厲害在最後結論不必由你講出口——對方自己走到「我其實不知道」。這是英語會議裡最有效的挑戰假設方式。
swaps: Where does that number come from? And who defines it?
Walk me back one step — how is that measured?
cards.pmNote: 資料標籤的定義往往藏在某個 ops SOP 裡；沒人看過，但整個決策都建在上面。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.quote: One of the things I ask a lot in product review when someone says, "Hey, we want to run an experiment," is, "Okay, what do we do if it's green? What do we do if it's red?"
cards.zh: 有人說「我們想跑個實驗」，我在產品評審上最常問的就是：「如果結果是綠的我們做什麼？紅的又做什麼？」
cards.why: 兩個對稱的問句，逼對方在拿到資料之前先承諾行動。如果兩個答案一樣，這個實驗就不用跑了——這是用問題（而非否決）殺掉一個爛提案的最優雅方式。
swaps: What changes if this wins? What changes if it doesn't?
What decision does this data actually unlock?
cards.pmNote: 高成長階段不該追求 5% 的統計顯著勝利，要找會改變業務曲線、而且會複利的東西。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.quote: So I often try and start with like, am I hearing you right that this is your prior? Is there a piece of context or something that I don't have that helps inform that prior?
cards.zh: 我通常會先問：「我理解得對嗎，你的預設立場是這個？有沒有什麼我不知道的背景，讓你形成這個判斷？」
cards.why: 向上反對的最佳開場。先確認你聽懂了，再把「我不同意」改寫成「我可能缺資訊」。prior（先驗判斷）這個詞讓整段變成理性討論而非立場對抗，而且給了對方一個台階：他可以補資訊，也可以發現自己沒有。
swaps: Let me play that back — is that the assumption you're working from?
What are you seeing that I'm not?
cards.pmNote: 被主管從奇怪的角度質疑時，先停下來確認他為什麼那樣問，不要急著防守你的方案。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.quote: Sometimes it can be as simple as like, is your mind made up on this or are you open to input? If the answer is like, "No, I'm pretty set that this is the answer," shut up.
cards.zh: 有時候簡單問一句就好：「這件事你已經決定了，還是還能聽意見？」如果對方說「我滿確定就是這個答案」，那就閉嘴。
cards.why: 在花力氣說服之前先問「這場辯論存不存在」。這一句省下的會議時間比任何技巧都多，而且它把主導權交給對方，所以問了不會冒犯。母語者用得很自然，台灣人幾乎不會想到可以直接問。
swaps: Is this decided, or still open?
Do you want pushback on this, or do you want execution?
cards.pmNote: Tom 的規矩：如果雙方都沒資料，那就是兩個意見，CEO 的意見會贏——這時候就把自尊放門口。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.pattern: Definitely agree. My only build on that would be [補充／修正].
cards.quote: I think my only build on that would be to say I think those core PM skills aren't necessarily the things that we have rewarded PMs for over the last five years, versus storytelling, alignment, strategy.
cards.zh: 我唯一想補的是：那些核心 PM 能力，其實不是我們過去五年在獎勵的東西——我們獎勵的是說故事、跨部門對齊、講策略。
cards.why: build 當名詞用（my build on that）是矽谷會議室的高頻詞，意思是「我在你的基礎上加一層」。它讓一個實質上的修正聽起來像是合作蓋房子。加 only 又進一步縮小了異議的體積。
swaps: Yes, and — one build on that:
Agree with all of that; the one thing I'd layer on is...
cards.pmNote: PM 的核心能力（懂客戶、懂生意、懂技術，並把三者翻譯起來）沒變，變的是這五年獎勵了「說故事」而不是「做事」。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.pattern: No, then go — think through everything that could break, and then move anyway.
cards.quote: And I think one of the monikers we use internally is no, then go. As in just think through all the things that could go wrong, understand where scale will break, understand the things that might happen, and then move on anyway.
cards.zh: 我們內部有個口號叫「先說不，然後走」。把所有可能出錯的地方都想過一輪，知道規模在哪裡會斷，然後照樣往前。
cards.why: 把「想清楚風險」跟「因為風險而停下」拆成兩件事。and then move on anyway 是整句的關鍵——它預先回答了「你不是不知道風險，你是決定承擔」。這是被法務／財務嚇住時最好用的立場。
swaps: Pre-mortem it, then ship it anyway.
Name every failure mode, then decide to go.
cards.pmNote: 把可能出事的情況全想過一遍，你自然會順手擋掉一半——不必全部解決才動。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.quote: So assume that at least half of what I've said is wrong in the same basis that half of the things I've probably ever shipped are not correct.
cards.zh: 所以你就當我講的至少有一半是錯的——就像我這輩子出過的東西大概也有一半是錯的一樣。
cards.why: 三段收尾：宣告我確定什麼→劃清我不確定什麼→主動打折。這種主動打折在英語職場不會被讀成沒信心，反而是老手的訊號，因為只有真的做過的人才知道界線在哪。
swaps: Take what's useful, discard the rest.
This is one data point from one company, not a law.
cards.pmNote: Tom 的內部文件開宗明義：目標是打擊率五成——你期待自己錯的次數跟對的一樣多。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.pattern: There's a really common thread to it, which is [你反覆犯的那個錯].
cards.quote: So there's probably just too many specific examples of times I've screwed up in my career, but there probably is a really common thread to it. And I think it's probably an easy trap for any PM to fall into, which is averages mean nothing to the individual is probably the thing that I've really scarred by.
cards.zh: 我職涯搞砸的例子多到講不完，但它們有一條很明顯的共通線：平均值對個別使用者毫無意義——這是我被燙傷最深的一課。
cards.why: 面試被問失敗經驗的最高階答法：不是講一個故事，而是講一個「模式」。承認例子多到講不完（顯示誠實），再抽出一條可傳授的規律（顯示反省深度）。
swaps: The specific failures vary; the underlying mistake is always the same.
If I pattern-match my worst calls, they all share one thing.
cards.pmNote: 只有 3% 的人用某功能，不代表可以砍——那 3% 可能有一群人，那是他們 100% 的用途。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.pattern: I tried to be my most ordinary self, as opposed to my interview self.
cards.quote: And I tried through that to be my most ordinary self as opposed to interview self, if that makes sense. Because you got to ask yourself, do I really want to spend my whole time having this discussion and this debate?
cards.zh: 整個過程我盡量拿出最平常的自己，而不是「面試版的自己」。因為你得問自己：我真的想每天都花時間在這種討論上嗎？
cards.why: my ordinary self / my interview self 這組對比是英語裡很好用的自我描述法，一句就把「表演」跟「真實」拆開。用在面試回顧、談公司文化契合度時，比 authentic 這種空詞具體太多。
swaps: I deliberately didn't perform in that conversation.
I showed up as I'd actually be on a Tuesday, not as a candidate.
cards.pmNote: 面試資深職位是雙向的：你在測「我想不想每天跟這個人辯論這些事」。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.quote: And then there is an art to learning how to push somebody without competing with them. And I think a lot of the times I've seen the CPO CEO relationship go badly. It ends up with the CPO is competing with the CEO for vision and they end up at loggerheads.
cards.zh: 怎麼推對方一把、又不變成跟他競爭，這是一門功夫。我看過很多 CPO 跟 CEO 關係搞砸，都是因為 CPO 在跟 CEO 搶願景。
cards.why: push somebody vs compete with somebody 這組區別是向上管理的核心。there is an art to X 這個開場也很好用：它宣告接下來講的是難以言傳的手感，聽的人就會放下防衛、進入學習模式。
swaps: You can challenge the thinking without contesting the ownership.
Push on the logic, not on whose vision it is.
cards.pmNote: 在創辦人主導的公司，你的工作是把他的直覺翻譯成現實，不是替換掉他的直覺。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.quote: I think maybe on the flip side of less positive is what it definitely learned is most of the time you hear it's really complex, it isn't. Leadership's just weak.
cards.zh: 我確實學到的是：多數時候你聽到「這件事很複雜」，其實它不複雜。只是領導層軟弱而已。
cards.why: Most of the time you hear X, it isn't 是一個很強的懷疑句型，把「複雜」當成一種需要被檢驗的說法而不是事實。中間插一句 nobody died 的黑色幽默，讓這種挑戰不至於太硬。
swaps: "It's complicated" is often code for "no one wants to decide."
Nine times out of ten, complexity is a stand-in for reluctance.
cards.pmNote: Twitter 花了三年多才把 140 字上限拿掉——所有人都知道該做，只是沒人願意拍板。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.pattern: I don't think this is right. I'm going to clear the rest of my day. Let's sit and figure it out.
cards.quote: he'll sit in a review and be like, "I don't think this is right." And then he'll pause and say, "I'm going to clear the rest of my day. Let's sit and figure it out."
cards.zh: 他會在評審會上說：「我覺得這不對。」然後停一下說：「我把今天剩下的行程清掉，我們一起坐下來把它弄清楚。」
cards.why: 否決之後立刻用自己的時間補上，把「我不同意」變成「我陪你解」。I'm going to clear the rest of my day 是英語職場最有份量的一句承諾——它花的是說話者的成本，不是聽者的。
swaps: I'm not convinced — let's block the afternoon and work it through.
Rather than send you away, let's solve it here.
cards.pmNote: 評審會不該是「求綠燈」；把它變成一起找答案，PM 就不必為了信用而護航爛方案。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.pattern: Whatever is required to most effectively [目標] is the short answer.
cards.quote: Whatever is required to most effectively ship is the short answer. Have I personally shipped some production code at Whatnot? Yes.
cards.zh: 簡短的答案是：出貨需要什麼我就做什麼。我自己在 Whatnot 有沒有推過正式環境的程式碼？有。
cards.why: 先給一句可以直接引用的短答（…is the short answer），再用自問自答補細節。這種「短答＋自問自答」是英語訪談與會議裡收放自如的節奏控制，聽者隨時可以喊停。
swaps: The short answer is whatever unblocks the ship date.
Short version: I do the work the outcome needs.
cards.pmNote: PM 寫程式的價值多半在「理解程式碼」而不是「提交程式碼」——後者你會踩光工程師 L4 就學會避開的坑。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.quote: I actually think it's easier. Spicy take.
cards.zh: 我其實覺得更容易。這個看法比較嗆。
cards.why: Spicy take 是先幫自己的話貼標籤（＝我知道這不主流），聽眾就會用「聽個新鮮觀點」的心態接收，而不是「這人不懂行情」。兩個字，換掉整段的接收框架。
swaps: Hot take, but hear me out:
Contrarian view — and I might be wrong:
cards.pmNote: Tom 的算法：與其養一整層 PM 金字塔，不如用同樣的錢請三個能自己交付的資深 IC。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.pattern: [做法] would be my push.
cards.quote: Start doing IC work in the role you're in would be my push. Get back to the basics of make sure that you're taking on practical work.
cards.zh: 我會建議的是：在你現在這個職位上就開始做 IC 的工作。回到基本功，確保你手上有實作的事情。
cards.why: 把建議放在句尾用 would be my push 收，比開頭就下命令柔軟得多。push 這個名詞用法（我會推你往這邊）保留了「你可以不接受」的空間，是資深主管給建議的常見語氣。
swaps: My push would be to start before you switch jobs.
If I were advising you, I'd start there.
cards.pmNote: 在現職就把 IC 肌肉練回來——這件事對你現在的位置也有幫助，不只是為了下一份工作。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.pattern: I can tell you what's definitely trending down: [具體行為].
cards.quote: I can tell you what's definitely trending down. It's folks who spend a lot of the time in their interviews talking about those alignment meetings and driving alignment and stakeholder management and those pieces.
cards.zh: 我可以告訴你什麼明顯在退燒：那些在面試裡花大量時間講「跨部門對齊」「利害關係人管理」的人。
cards.why: 被問一個難答的雙面問題（什麼在漲、什麼在跌）時，先答你有把握的那半。I can tell you what's definitely X 是一個誠實又不失控的切入，等於公開告訴對方「另一半我沒把握」。
swaps: What I'm confident about is the downside of the question.
I can speak to what's fading; the rest I'd be guessing.
cards.pmNote: Tom 的反指標：面試裡的失敗故事如果是「我沒讓 CEO 同步到最新進度」，那多半是政治型 PM。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.pattern: I'll figure it out. Most things are not as hard as people think.
cards.quote: I'll figure it out, is probably the closest. It turns out most things are not as hard as people think. We'll work it out.
cards.zh: 最接近的大概是「我會想辦法搞定」。事實證明多數事情沒有大家想的那麼難。我們會弄出來的。
cards.why: I'll figure it out 是英語裡承擔模糊任務的標準句：不承諾方法，只承諾結果。台灣人面對沒把握的任務常說 I'll try my best，聽起來像預先鋪好失敗的台階；這句剛好相反。
swaps: I don't know how yet, but I'll work it out.
Leave it with me — I'll find the path.
cards.pmNote: Tom 的補充：如果你不願意投入那些成本，那它八成本來就不是個大問題。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

cards.pattern: I'm obviously limited on what exactly I can share, but it is true that [可以講的那一半]
cards.quote: I'm obviously limited on what exactly I can share, but it is true that our retention numbers are really exciting and that is actually the thing we look at.
cards.zh: 我能講的東西確實有限，不過可以說的是，我們的留存數字真的很好看，而且那正是我們在看的指標。
cards.why: 台灣人碰到「不能講」通常只會說 I can't say，對話就死了。母語者的做法是先承認限制（limited on what I can share），立刻用 but it is true that 交出一塊真的有資訊量的東西。你守住了保密，也沒讓對方空手而回。
swaps: There's only so much I can get into, but what I can say is...
I can't give you the exact number, but directionally...
cards.pmNote: 被問到不能揭露的指標時，給「方向」不給「數值」是業界慣例——講 trend 不講 absolute。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.quote: I'll let you know when we figure it out. We're hiring. I think there's so many interesting product problems here.
