cards.zh: 等我們想通了再告訴你。我們還在徵人，這裡真的有一堆很有意思的產品問題。
cards.why: 把「我不知道」講成一個未來的承諾而不是現在的缺口——I'll let you know when 預設了「終究會知道」。後面立刻補一句有能量的話（we're hiring），整段從示弱翻轉成自信。這句短到可以背起來當萬用擋箭牌。
swaps: Ask me again in six months.
We're still working through that one—I'll circle back when we have a view.
cards.pmNote: 產品願景被追問細節時，坦承「還沒答案」比硬編一個 roadmap 安全得多——編出來的都會變成別人拿來考核你的承諾。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.pattern: my advice is super lame, which is [建議], which is not as actionable as [對方] would ideally like
cards.quote: And for that reason, my advice is super lame, which is make really high quality content, which is not as actionable as I think people making content would ideally like.
cards.zh: 所以我的建議很沒創意，就是做出真正高品質的內容——我知道這對做內容的人來說不夠具體可執行。
cards.why: 他自己先替對方把吐槽講完（super lame、not as actionable as you'd like），對方就無話可說了。這叫「自嘲式先制」：先認領建議的弱點，聽起來反而像誠實而不是敷衍。台灣人常反過來——把弱建議包裝得很厲害，結果被戳破更難看。
swaps: I know this is a boring answer, but...
This is going to sound unsatisfying, and I'm aware of that:
cards.pmNote: 給不出戰術層建議時，明講「這只是原則不是 playbook」，可以避免對方照著做卻沒效果而回頭怪你。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.pattern: Definitely don't bring me on here as a [領域] expert, I think you have got better people for that.
cards.quote: Definitely don't bring me on here as a pricing expert, I think you have got better people for that.
cards.zh: 千萬別把我當定價專家找來，這題你應該去找更懂的人。
cards.why: 剛講完一個很成功的定價故事，馬上主動卸下「專家」這個頭銜。母語者在職場上很會做這件事——你可以分享經驗，但不接受一個你撐不住的標籤。台灣人常見的失誤是默默接下標籤，之後被問到深處就崩。
swaps: Don't take this as expert advice—it's just what happened to work for us.
I'm a sample size of one on this.
cards.pmNote: 分享做法時要區分「我們的做法」與「最佳實務」，否則會被當成 benchmark 反過來要求你負責。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.pattern: I'm baffled by [A]. Even more baffled by [更誇張的 B].
cards.quote: I'm baffled by how much it took off as a concept. Even more baffled by how many people have copied the paradigm rather than trying out a different way of interacting with AI.
cards.zh: 這個概念會紅成這樣，我到現在都想不通。更想不通的是，怎麼那麼多人直接照抄，而不是去試別的跟 AI 互動的方式。
cards.why: baffled 是「困惑到說不出話」，比 surprised 強、比 confused 有格調。重點在第二句只用 Even more baffled by 開頭、省略主詞動詞——這種省略是口語裡加強語氣的節奏技巧，寫下來反而不對。
swaps: It still puzzles me how... And what puzzles me more is...
I genuinely don't understand why... Even less why...
cards.pmNote: 自家產品爆紅卻說不出所以然，是誠實訊號；假裝一切都在計畫中的 PM，通常學不到下一次成功的原因。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.pattern: We get a lot of crap for [某個爛設計], and I own it.
cards.quote: We get a lot of crap for the model chooser, and I own it. I've tried to say that to everyone who will listen.
cards.zh: 模型選單被罵翻，這我認。我逢人就講這件事是我的責任。
cards.why: I own it 是英語職場最短、最有份量的認錯句，三個字結案，不解釋不辯護。前面用 get a lot of crap for 把外界批評如實引述（不美化成 feedback），可信度立刻上來。台灣人習慣先解釋再認錯，順序顛倒就沒了力道。
swaps: That one's on me.
We've taken a lot of heat for that, and rightly so.
cards.pmNote: 公開認領一個已知爛設計，可以讓團隊不必再花力氣替它辯護，直接進到「怎麼修」。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.pattern: What happened is that we pushed out an update that made [產品] more likely to [壞行為]
cards.quote: But basically what happened is that we pushed out an update that made the model more likely to tell you things that sound good in the moment.
cards.zh: 簡單講就是，我們推了一個更新，結果讓模型更容易講出那種當下聽起來很順耳的話。
cards.why: 事故說明的黃金結構：主詞是 we（不是 the system / a bug），動詞是主動的 pushed out，然後平鋪直敘描述後果。全句沒有一個形容詞在替自己緩頰。what happened is that 這個開場也很好用——宣告接下來是事實敘述，不是立場。
swaps: What went wrong was that we shipped a change that...
The short version is: we rolled out an update that...
cards.pmNote: postmortem 的第一段一定要用主動語態指出「誰做了什麼」，被動語態（a change was made）是逃避責任的訊號。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.pattern: It's [負面形容], but that's strictly less bad than [替代方案的代價].
cards.quote: You know what? We should ship. It's embarrassing, but that's strictly less bad than not getting the feedback you wanted.
cards.zh: 我覺得就出吧。是很難看沒錯，但這比拿不到你要的回饋還是好一點。
cards.why: strictly less bad 是精算式的英文——不宣稱「這是好事」，只宣稱「在兩個壞選項裡它比較不壞」。這種「比爛」框架特別適合報壞消息：你沒有粉飾，也沒有讓對方覺得沒得選。embarrassing 先自認難看，也堵住了對方要講的第一句話。
swaps: It's not pretty, but it beats the alternative.
This is the least bad option on the table.
cards.pmNote: 決策不是在好與壞之間選，多數時候是在兩個壞之間選——把選項的代價攤開講，比推銷「這是好方案」更有說服力。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.pattern: The thing you can't really express in [常見的衡量方式] is [真正重要的東西]
cards.quote: But again, the thing you can't really express in use cases or data is the vibe of the model.
cards.zh: 但話說回來，用案例或數據講不出來的那個東西，才是這個模型的「感覺」。
cards.why: 用「現有工具測不到」來定義一個問題，是資深者的招式：先承認既有衡量方式（use cases、data）的邊界，再把注意力導到那個沒被測到的東西。這比直接說「vibe 很重要」有力太多，因為你已經解釋了為什麼大家沒注意到它。
swaps: What doesn't show up in the numbers is...
The part our metrics can't capture is...
cards.pmNote: 指標抓不到的東西不代表不存在——把「未被衡量」明講出來，才有機會爭取資源去建新的衡量方式。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.pattern: [現況] feels a little bit like [舊時代的東西]. We haven't built [新時代的東西] yet, and it'll be obvious once we do.
cards.quote: I still feel like ChatGPT feels a little bit like MS-DOS, like we haven't built Windows yet. And it'll be obvious once we do.
cards.zh: 我還是覺得 ChatGPT 有點像 MS-DOS——我們的 Windows 還沒做出來。而且一旦做出來，大家馬上就會知道那就是了。
cards.why: 用歷史上「大家都知道結局」的類比講願景，聽者不必相信你的預測，只要相信歷史會重演。最狠的是最後那句 it'll be obvious once we do——把「我說不清楚那是什麼」轉成一種自信，而不是心虛。
swaps: We're still at the command-line stage of this.
Today's version is the flip phone; the smartphone hasn't shown up yet.
cards.pmNote: 願景講不清細節時，用「我們在哪個歷史階段」代替「產品長什麼樣」，可以對齊方向而不鎖死解法。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.pattern: You absolutely should [做 X], but you won't know [關鍵資訊] until after you [動作].
cards.quote: You absolutely should polish things like the model output, but you won't know what to polish until after you ship.
cards.zh: 該打磨的東西當然要打磨，像是模型輸出；但你要磨哪裡，得等出貨之後才會知道。
cards.why: 先把對方的價值觀完整接住（You absolutely should polish），再指出一個「順序問題」而非「對錯問題」。這是說服品質派最有效的角度：我不是叫你別做，我是說你現在做的時間點不對。absolutely 這個副詞在這裡是真心的，不是諷刺。
swaps: It's not that quality doesn't matter—it's that you're guessing until you ship.
Craft matters, but you need real usage to know where to spend it.
cards.pmNote: 在需求不明的階段投入打磨，本質是在賭你猜對了使用場景——多數時候賭輸。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.pattern: I also think it would be easy to use all what I just said as an excuse not to [對方擔心的事].
cards.quote: I also think it would be easy to use all what I just said as an excuse not to eventually build a great product.
cards.zh: 我也覺得，我剛剛講的那些很容易被拿來當藉口，變成「反正最後也不用做出好產品」。
cards.why: 講完一套可能被濫用的主張後，自己先把濫用方式點名。這招在英語職場叫「封住後門」——你堵住了最惡意的解讀，聽者反而更願意接受你原本的主張。台灣人常等到被人濫用了才回頭澄清，那時已經來不及。
swaps: I can see how this gets misused as a licence to ship junk.
To be clear, this isn't permission to stop caring about quality.
cards.pmNote: 推「快速出貨」文化時務必配一句「這不等於降低標準」，否則三個月後你會收到一堆用你的話當擋箭牌的爛東西。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.pattern: So, yes on [X], but no on [Y], is where I would describe my point of view.
cards.quote: So, yes on natural language, but no on chat is where I would describe my point of view.
cards.zh: 所以自然語言我贊成，但聊天介面我不贊成——這大概是我的立場。
cards.why: 把一個被綁在一起的概念拆成兩半，一半贊成一半反對，再用 is where I would describe my point of view 把它降級成「我的看法」而非定論。整句只有十幾個字，卻同時完成了拆解、表態、留餘地三件事。這是會議收斂的高效句。
swaps: I'm with you on the first half, not the second.
Agree on the principle, disagree on the format.
cards.pmNote: 很多爭論其實是兩個議題被綁在一起——拆開之後常會發現雙方在一半的事上早就同意了。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.pattern: It's not that you actually [做 X], but it gives you [心理效果]
cards.quote: It's not that you actually are going to watch it the whole time, but it gives you a mental model and makes you feel in control.
cards.zh: 並不是說你真的會全程盯著看，而是它讓你有一個心智模型，讓你覺得自己掌握著方向盤。
cards.why: 解釋一個「看起來沒用」的設計時，先誠實承認它字面上的用途不成立（It's not that you actually...），再把真正的價值放到心理層。這個先自拆再重建的順序，讓對方沒機會先提出質疑。
swaps: Nobody actually reads it—but knowing it's there changes how you feel.
The point isn't the information, it's the sense of control.
cards.pmNote: 自動化產品的信任感常來自「可觀察性」而不是「可控性」——讓用戶看得到過程，比讓他真的介入更重要。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.pattern: You've got to do [A], you've got to do [B], if you want to be a serious player. And those are just non-negotiable.
cards.quote: You've got to do HIPAA, you got to do SOC 2, you've got to do all those things if you want to be a serious player. And those are just non-negotiable.
cards.zh: HIPAA 要做、SOC 2 要做，這些全都得做，你才算是玩真的。這些就是沒得談。
cards.why: non-negotiable 是英語職場結束討論最乾淨的一個詞——不是「我不想談」，是「這件事本來就不在談判桌上」。前面先用 if you want to be a serious player 把標準外部化成行業門檻，讓你的堅持不像個人偏好。
swaps: That one's table stakes—it's not on the table.
There's no version of this where we skip that.
cards.pmNote: 把 compliance 類需求標成 non-negotiable 並放進基準線，可以省下每季重新爭辯一次的成本。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.pattern: This is not something I'd ever say about myself. It's nice that someone else would say it, but [降溫]
cards.quote: Yeah, this is not something I'd ever say about myself. It's nice that someone else would say it, but it's a mysterious thing.
cards.zh: 這種話我自己絕對講不出口。有別人這樣說當然開心，不過這東西其實挺玄的。
cards.why: 接住讚美的三步：拒絕自封（I'd never say that about myself）、感謝來源（it's nice that someone else would）、然後把話題轉回內容本身。整段沒有一句 no no no 的假謙虛，卻完全沒有自誇的姿態。這是英語職場處理稱讚最安全的公式。
swaps: That's generous of them—I wouldn't claim that myself.
I'll take the compliment, but I'm not sure I'd describe it that way.
cards.pmNote: 被公開稱讚時把功勞轉回具體做法而非個人特質，既謙虛又順便傳播了做法本身。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.pattern: I love [高強度的事], but in order to do that with confidence, I need [你要的資源]
cards.quote: I love setting a fast pace at the company, but in order to do that with confidence, I need at least one day every week that I'm entirely unplugged.
cards.zh: 我很喜歡替公司設一個快節奏，但要有信心這樣衝，我每週至少需要一天完全斷線。
cards.why: 要資源（這裡是時間）的最佳姿勢：先證明你認同組織的目標（I love setting a fast pace），再把需求包裝成「達成那個目標的必要條件」而不是個人福利。in order to do that with confidence 這半句是關鍵鉸鏈，缺了它就變成在討休假。
swaps: I'm all in on the timeline—to hit it I need one more engineer.
I can commit to that, provided I get X.
cards.pmNote: 爭取資源時把需求綁在對方在乎的目標上（而非你的負擔上），拒絕的成本就轉嫁到對方身上了。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

cards.pattern: I can't speak to [你沒經歷的部分]. But what I can tell you about [你經歷過的] is [具體感受]
cards.quote: I can't speak to that whole period. But what I can tell you about what I'm feeling now is just an incredible sense of focus and urgency to deliver great products quickly.
cards.zh: 那一整段期間我沒辦法評論。但我可以告訴你現在的感受——一種非常強烈的專注感和急迫感，就是要快點把好產品交出去。
cards.why: I can't speak to X / what I can tell you is Y 是英語職場最實用的一組配對句。前半劃出你沒有第一手資訊的範圍（不是拒答，是誠實），後半立刻交出你確實握有的東西。整個過程沒有任何防禦姿態，聽者反而更信你後半那段。
swaps: I wasn't there for that, so I can't comment—what I can speak to is...
That predates me. What I do know firsthand is...
cards.pmNote: 被問到自己接手前的歷史時，明說「我沒經歷過」比轉述二手版本安全——二手版本出錯時責任會算在你頭上。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.pattern: I don't think there's any one thing. A lot of times people ascribe momentum to a one-time change or a single person.
cards.quote: I don't think there's any one thing that has happened. I think that a lot of times people ascribe a lot of momentum to a one time change or a single person.
cards.zh: 我不覺得有哪一件事是關鍵。很多時候大家會把一整段動能歸給某一次改動、或某一個人。
cards.why: 拒絕回答「關鍵是什麼」這種問題時，不要只說「沒有單一原因」，要順手指出提問背後的認知偏誤（ascribe momentum to a single person）。這樣你的拒答就升級成一個洞見，對方會覺得學到東西而不是被打槍。
swaps: There's rarely a single cause—we tend to over-attribute.
I'd push back on the premise that it was one decision.
cards.pmNote: 成長歸因給單一功能是常見錯誤，會讓團隊重複投資在其實只佔一小部分貢獻的東西上。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.quote: People come to search for a ridiculously wide set of things. They want a phone number, a price, directions. I think the vastness of that is underappreciated by many people.
cards.zh: 大家來搜尋的東西範圍寬到誇張——找電話、查價格、要路線。我覺得這個「廣度」被太多人低估了。
cards.why: underappreciated 是英語職場講「大家沒看到重點」時最有禮貌的字，不像 people don't understand 那樣把對方講成笨蛋。先給三個具體例子再下這個判斷，順序很重要：證據在前，斷言在後，聽者會自己得出同樣結論。
swaps: I don't think people fully appreciate how broad that is.
This gets consistently underrated.
cards.pmNote: 為既有產品辯護時，用「使用情境的廣度」而非「功能的深度」來反駁「它要被取代了」的論述。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.pattern: You get to these points of diminishing marginal return where you could put 50 people on it and it's just not going to move the needle.
cards.quote: You get to these points of just diminishing marginal return in every system where it feels like you could put 50 people on this project, it's just not going to dramatically move the needle.
cards.zh: 每個系統都會走到邊際效益遞減的那個點——你感覺得出來，就算再丟 50 個人下去，也不會讓數字有什麼大變化。
cards.why: 講「這裡不值得再投資」時，用經濟學的 diminishing marginal return 而不是「這個沒救了」，指標從主觀判斷變成結構性事實。後半刻意給一個誇張的數字（50 people），讓對方自己去感受投入與產出的落差，比講一堆數據有效。
swaps: We've squeezed most of the juice out of this one.
More headcount here doesn't buy us much anymore.
cards.pmNote: 判斷該不該從成熟功能撤資，看的是「再投入一單位資源能換回多少」，不是這個功能現在的絕對規模。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.quote: That was one of the big motivations, actually identifying that user problem, being very disgruntled on behalf of the user. We're just failing the user every day.
cards.zh: 那就是最大的動力之一：真的把使用者的問題認出來，然後代替使用者生氣。我們每天都在辜負他們。
cards.why: on behalf of the user 這個介系詞片語是整句的樞紐——它把「我不爽」正當化成「我替使用者不爽」，情緒立刻變成專業立場。後面短句 We're just failing the user every day 用現在進行式加 every day，製造持續中的急迫感。
swaps: I'm annoyed on the user's behalf here.
We're letting people down on this, every single day.
cards.pmNote: 在會議上替使用者發火，比替自己的 roadmap 發火有效——前者沒有人能反對，後者馬上變成部門角力。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.quote: Yeah, I don't think of them as an or. I think they have to be intersected because basically the way I think about it is you actually start with a problem.
cards.zh: 我不覺得這是二選一。我覺得這兩件事必須交集在一起，因為在我看來，你本來就是從一個問題開始。
cards.why: 拒絕一個假二分法的標準句。an or 把 or 當名詞用是很地道的口語（等於「一個二選一的題目」）。intersected 又給了正面替代方案——你不只否定了問題，還提供了新的框架。反對而不空手，是這句的精髓。
swaps: I don't see that as either/or.
That's a false choice—it's both, and they feed each other.
cards.pmNote: 「做好產品 vs. 衝指標」幾乎永遠是假對立——真正的問題是你有沒有把指標選對。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.quote: You have to really understand why someone uses your product, because not every great thing is going to be invented by you.
cards.zh: 你得真的搞懂別人為什麼用你的產品，因為不是每一個好東西都會由你發明出來。
cards.why: 面對「你們抄襲」這種指控，這句用一個近乎常識的普遍原則，把爭議降級成「這是產業常態」。句子沒有辯解、沒有情緒，只是陳述一個沒人能否認的事實——這正是它有效的原因。
swaps: Good ideas don't only come from inside your building.
You don't have a monopoly on good ideas, and that's fine.
cards.pmNote: 採用競品驗證過的形式（format）不等於抄產品——要看你有沒有針對自家用戶重做一次判斷。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.quote: These things become core primitives and formats, and then at the end of the day, you're just robbing your user base of the opportunity to have a better product.
cards.zh: 這些東西很快就變成核心的基本元件跟格式了，說到底，你不做只是在剝奪你的用戶擁有更好產品的機會。
cards.why: 把「抄襲」這個指控整個翻面：不做才是加害者，被害者是用戶。robbing 這個動詞刻意用了道德重量很高的字，把道德高地從指控方手上搶過來。這是英語辯論裡典型的 reframe，適合在被質疑動機時使用。
swaps: Refusing to build it just punishes our users.
The purist position here costs the user, not us.
cards.pmNote: 產品倫理的爭論最後都會回到「誰的利益」——把用戶利益放到論述中心，通常是最站得住腳的位置。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.quote: And so you have to add product carefully, but it needs to feel coherent but different.
cards.zh: 所以加東西要很小心，它必須感覺上是一體的，但同時又是不一樣的。
cards.why: 用兩個相反的形容詞夾出一個設計準則（coherent but different），短到可以貼在牆上。英語職場很愛這種「張力式標準」——它不給答案，但給了一把尺，讓團隊自己判斷每個決定落在哪。
swaps: Familiar enough to trust, distinct enough to notice.
It should belong here, but not blend in.
cards.pmNote: 新功能放進成熟產品時，視覺與互動要繼承（coherent），但心智模型要明確分離（different），否則用戶會用舊規則去解讀新東西。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.pattern: One of the things I see people fail on the most is they assume [在別處有效的東西] will work in your world.
cards.quote: It's actually one of the things I see people fail on the most is they assume something working for one system will work in your world.
cards.zh: 我看到最多人栽的地方就是：他們假設在別的系統上行得通的東西，在你這邊也會行得通。
cards.why: 用「我看過最多人失敗的地方」開場，把批評包裝成經驗分享，聽者不會覺得被針對。I see people fail on the most 是很典型的資深者句式——不指名、不說教，但殺傷力十足。
swaps: The most common mistake I see is assuming it transfers.
What works there won't automatically work here.
cards.pmNote: 抄成功案例前先問「他們的用戶在那個時刻的期待是什麼」——形式可以借，情境不能借。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.quote: I think I made the product better, but is anyone using it? Does anyone care? Or are we just congratulating ourselves?
cards.zh: 我覺得我把產品做得更好了——可是有人在用嗎？有人在乎嗎？還是我們只是在自我感覺良好？
cards.why: 三個連續反問，一個比一個尖，最後一句 congratulating ourselves 直接點名團隊的自我陶醉。用 we 而不是 you，讓這記重拳打在全體身上包含自己，因此在會議上說出來不會結仇。
swaps: Did that move anything, or did it just feel good?
Are we celebrating output instead of outcome?
cards.pmNote: review 會議固定問一句「這有人在用嗎」，可以擋掉大量只有內部覺得酷的功能。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.pattern: It wasn't very good, but it had these moments of brilliance.
cards.quote: We were really plugging away on it, and then we saw this little version of it emerge that wasn't very good, but it had this moments of brilliance.
cards.zh: 我們一直死磕著做，後來看到一個很小的雛形跑出來，其實不怎麼樣，但偶爾會閃出一些很厲害的時刻。
cards.why: 報告一個還很爛的原型時的標準句：先誠實下判斷（wasn't very good），再指出訊號（moments of brilliance）。順序不能反——先講亮點會像在推銷，先講缺點才會讓亮點顯得可信。這是爭取繼續投資的最佳角度。
swaps: Mostly rough, but there were flashes of something.
It was bad on average and great in patches—that's the interesting part.
cards.pmNote: 早期原型不該用平均品質評估，要看「最好的那幾次」有多好——那才是天花板的訊號。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.pattern: You've got to have people test it to tell you the truth, and tell you when it sucks, because it probably does.
cards.quote: We tried to treat it a little more like a startup, because we feel like you got to have people test it to tell you the truth, and tell you when it sucks, because it probably does.
cards.zh: 我們刻意把它當成一個新創在做，因為你需要有人真的告訴你實話、告訴你它哪裡爛——而它八成真的很爛。
cards.why: because it probably does 這五個字是全句靈魂：預先承認自家東西大概就是不好。用 sucks 這種直白的字（而不是 has room for improvement）也是刻意的——你用什麼語氣談自家產品，別人就用什麼語氣給你回饋。
swaps: We need testers who'll tell us it's bad—because it is.
Assume version one is broken and go find out how.
cards.pmNote: 找 trusted tester 時要明講「請告訴我們哪裡爛」，否則你會收到一堆客氣的正面回饋，等於沒測。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.quote: Don't think of users as using your product. Think of users as hiring you to do something for them.
cards.zh: 別把使用者想成「在用你的產品」。要想成他們是「雇用你」去替他們完成某件事。
cards.why: Don't think of X as A. Think of X as B. 是最乾淨的觀念置換句型，兩句對稱、只換一個動詞。hiring 這個動詞立刻帶進「可以被開除」「有職務說明」「有績效」三層意涵，一個字換掉整個心智模型。
swaps: They're not using the product, they're hiring it for a job.
Stop asking what they do in the app; ask what they hired it to fix.
cards.pmNote: Jobs to be Done 的核心不是框架本身，而是逼你去找「他上次決定開始用的那一刻發生了什麼」。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.quote: And then the third one's around really designing for clarity instead of cleverness.
cards.zh: 第三點是：為了「清楚」而設計，不是為了「聰明」而設計。
cards.why: clarity instead of cleverness 用頭韻（都是 cl-）讓一條原則好記到不行。英語職場很多能傳開的原則都靠這種聲音上的設計。X instead of Y 這個結構本身也值得學——不是「要 X」，而是「用 X 取代那個你本來會選的 Y」。
swaps: Obvious beats clever.
Optimise for being understood, not for being interesting.
cards.pmNote: 命名與圖示要用產業通用符號，自創符號的認知成本永遠由用戶付。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.quote: So we shipped it, we thought it would be great. This is the be humble part, wasn't great, had a bunch of, it was just super confusing.
cards.zh: 我們就上線了，本來以為會很棒。這就是「要謙虛」的那段——並不棒，做得超級混亂。
cards.why: This is the be humble part 是把自己剛講過的原則當場拿來自嘲，一句話就把失敗故事講得輕鬆又誠實。後面 wasn't great 省略主詞，是口語裡收得很快的節奏——講失敗不要拖長，拖長就變自憐。
swaps: We were sure it would land. It didn't.
Spoiler: it flopped.
cards.pmNote: 把失敗案例當成方法論的示範材料，比單獨檢討更有教學效果，也讓團隊敢承認失敗。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.pattern: There's this cult of [流行做法]. At some level it's true, but [你的保留]
cards.quote: I think there's this cult of lean, scrappy, fast, throw away your product quickly, keep moving. And I think at some level it's true, but a lot of times I see teams give up too early.
cards.zh: 現在有一種「精實、克難、快、東西不行就丟、繼續往前」的教派。某種程度上它是對的，但我常看到團隊太早就放棄了。
cards.why: cult of 是給流行做法降溫最有效的一個詞——不是說它錯，是說信奉它的人已經不思考了。接著 at some level it's true 先讓步再轉折，讓你的反對聽起來是補充而不是叫板。這是反對主流意見最安全的走法。
swaps: There's a bit of dogma around this. It's directionally right, but...
This has become an article of faith, and I'd add a caveat:
cards.pmNote: 小團隊不是目的而是手段——要問的是「這個野心需要多少人才做得出來」，而不是「怎麼維持人數最少」。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.quote: Yeah, it's the other thing. No advice is right universally, right?
cards.zh: 對，這就是另一種情況了。沒有哪個建議是放諸四海皆準的嘛。
cards.why: 被指出「這跟你剛剛講的原則矛盾」時的最省力回應。不辯解、不修正原則，只承認原則有適用範圍。句尾的 right? 把裁決權交給對方，整句既坦然又不失立場。台灣人遇到這種當面矛盾常會慌，其實一句話就能過。
swaps: Every rule has exceptions, and that's one.
Fair—that one breaks the pattern.
cards.pmNote: 被抓到原則與案例不一致時，承認原則有邊界比修改原則更好——原則一改再改就沒人記得住了。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

cards.pattern: You're pushing for a future you believe is true, but all the while you're getting new information. You need to kill the beliefs that you had.
cards.quote: It's this weird tightrope where you're pushing for a future that you believe is true, but all the while you're getting new information. You need to kill the beliefs that you had.
cards.zh: 這是一條很怪的鋼索：你一邊在推動一個你相信會成真的未來，一邊又不斷收到新資訊。你得親手殺掉自己原本的信念。
cards.why: kill the beliefs that you had 這個動詞選得很重——不是 update 也不是 revise，是「殺掉」。英語職場在講改變立場時，用越強烈的動詞越顯得果斷而非動搖。tightrope（鋼索）也把矛盾狀態變成一個可以想像的畫面。
swaps: Hold the conviction, but be ruthless about updating it.
You have to be willing to shoot your own assumptions.
cards.pmNote: strong opinions, loosely held 的實作就是：每個假設都要事先寫下「什麼證據會讓我放棄它」。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

cards.pattern: Fast-forward to [時間], [新事實]. So now our hypotheses are just wrong.
cards.quote: Fast-forward to the middle of 2023, everything looks like it's going to be a transformer. So now our hypotheses are just wrong.
cards.zh: 快轉到 2023 年中，看起來全部都會走向 transformer。所以我們原本的假設就是錯的。
cards.why: 承認錯誤時最漂亮的走法：先講外部事實變了（fast-forward to），再讓「我們錯了」變成事實的自然結論。just wrong 三個字乾脆到不留餘地，反而讓人覺得你有掌握狀況——拖泥帶水的認錯才顯得心虛。
swaps: By mid-2023 the picture had changed, and our thesis no longer held.
The world moved, and that assumption stopped being true.
cards.pmNote: 策略假設要標註「基於什麼外部條件」，條件變了才能乾淨地換策略，而不是變成有人判斷失誤。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

cards.pattern: If I told you [荒謬版本], you should rightfully say [反駁]. And you'd be right.
cards.quote: If I told you, I'm going to build an autonomous vehicle, and I said our team is 10 people, you should rightfully say, Varun, you're not serious. And you'd be right.
cards.zh: 如果我跟你說我要做自駕車，然後說團隊只有 10 個人，你完全應該回我：Varun，你不是認真的吧。而且你會是對的。
cards.why: 自己扮演對方、自己講出對方的質疑、再自己認證那個質疑是對的。三步做完，你的主張就不必再證明了。you should rightfully say 裡的 rightfully 是關鍵——它預先授權對方懷疑你，反而讓你顯得極度有把握。
swaps: If I said that with a straight face, you'd rightly call it out.
You'd be entitled to laugh at me, and you should.
cards.pmNote: 論證資源需求時，用一個明顯過小的假設版本做對照，比直接喊數字更有說服力。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

cards.pattern: It's not because people are bad people—most people are well-intentioned. But what happens is [結構性後果]
cards.quote: And it's not because people are bad people. I think most people are really well-intentioned. But what happens when you have people that join and you didn't really need them?
cards.zh: 這不是因為誰是壞人，我覺得大多數人動機都很好。但問題是：當你招了一批其實不需要的人，會發生什麼事？
cards.why: 在批評一個現象前，先把「人品」這條路封死（not because people are bad people），剩下的就只能往結構去解釋。這是英語職場給難聽回饋時的必備前置——你不做這個切割，聽者一定會把批評接收成人身攻擊。
swaps: This isn't about anyone's intentions—it's about incentives.
Good people, bad structure.
cards.pmNote: 組織問題九成是結構問題——先檢查誘因與編制，再檢討個人表現。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

cards.quote: You don't win by doing 10 things well. You win by doing one thing really well and maybe you fail nine things.
cards.zh: 你不是靠十件事都做得不錯來贏。你是靠一件事做到非常好而贏，另外九件搞砸也沒關係。
cards.why: You don't win by X. You win by Y. 這組對仗句是英語裡宣告優先順序最有力的格式。關鍵在 maybe you fail nine things——他沒有假裝取捨沒有代價，而是明白把代價講出來。承認代價才讓主張可信。
swaps: Winning is one thing done exceptionally, not ten done adequately.
Breadth doesn't win. Depth on the right thing does.
cards.pmNote: 季度規劃時強迫排出「唯一的第一名」，其餘全部標成可犧牲——沒有可犧牲清單的優先順序等於沒排。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

cards.quote: This is very different than school. In school you optimize for your total GPA. But for companies, I just need to get an A+ on the one class that matters.
cards.zh: 這跟學校完全不一樣。在學校你是在拚總平均，但在公司，我只需要在那門真正重要的課拿 A+。
cards.why: 用「學校 vs. 公司」這個所有人都經歷過的對照，一秒解釋清楚為什麼平均分很危險。台灣的教育經驗讓這句特別扎——很多人職場上的痛苦，就是還在用 GPA 的方式工作。這種取自共同經驗的類比，是說服力最高的一種。
swaps: Careers aren't graded on a curve across all subjects.
Nobody's averaging your scores—one result carries the whole term.
cards.pmNote: 績效敘事要挑一個代表作講深，不要把十件小事平均展示——評審記得住的只有一件。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

cards.quote: If a software project could get built in two to three weeks, what does that really mean about the true complexity of what you built? Unless you believe you are way smarter than everyone else, but I think that's hubris.
cards.zh: 如果一個軟體專案兩三週就能做出來，那它到底有多複雜、多難被取代？除非你相信自己比全世界聰明太多——但我覺得那叫自大。
cards.why: 先給出一個唯一能讓對方站得住的前提（unless you believe...），再自己把那個前提命名為 hubris。這是英語辯論裡把對手逼進死角最優雅的方式：你沒有直接反駁，只是讓那條唯一的退路聽起來很難堪。
swaps: The only way that's true is if we're smarter than everyone—which I doubt.
That argument requires believing we're exceptional. I wouldn't bet on it.
cards.pmNote: 估時過度樂觀時，反問「為什麼別人要六個月我們只要三週」，通常能逼出被忽略的隱藏工作量。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

cards.quote: I think this is an interesting thing that technical founders sometimes don't really like. They think sales is a very negative part of the process. I think it's not that black and white.
cards.zh: 技術背景的創辦人常常不太喜歡這件事，他們覺得業務是整個過程裡很負面的一塊。我覺得沒那麼非黑即白。
cards.why: not that black and white 是英語職場最常用、也最安全的溫和反對句，它反對的是「立場的絕對性」而不是立場本身。前面先中性地描述對方的看法（不加貶義），再輕輕加上這一句，幾乎不會引起防衛。這句該背起來。
swaps: I'd say it's more nuanced than that.
It's less binary than people make it out to be.
cards.pmNote: PLG 與 enterprise sales 不是二選一——多數 B2B 成長曲線是兩者疊在一起的。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

cards.pattern: Granted, [自認的缺點], but [仍然成立的重點]
cards.quote: Granted this looks hideous, but in some ways if I wanted to, I could go out and do that, right?
cards.zh: 當然啦，這看起來很醜，但重點是我如果想，我確實可以直接這樣改，對吧。
cards.why: Granted 是一個專門用來「認領缺點」的連接詞，比 I know 更利落、比 admittedly 更口語。Demo 出包時這句可以救場：先承認眼前的難看，再把注意力導回你真正要示範的能力。台灣人 demo 時常裝作沒看到，反而更尷尬。
swaps: Yes, it looks terrible—that's not the point here.
Ugly, I know. The point is that it worked at all.
cards.pmNote: Demo 前先講明「這一段只是為了示範 X，視覺不代表成品」，可以避免整場討論被無關的細節綁架。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

cards.pattern: I don't want to be very negative, but it's very hard [做某事]
cards.quote: And maybe this is a... I don't want to be very negative, but it's very hard inside a company like ours to task our best engineers to build a best in class sales product.
cards.zh: 我不想講得太負面，但在我們這種公司裡，要把最好的工程師派去做一個頂尖的業務工具，是非常困難的。
cards.why: I don't want to be negative, but... 是一個坦率的預告：接下來的話會不好聽，我知道，我還是要說。這比裝作中立更誠實，也讓聽者有心理準備。注意他講的是自家的限制（inside a company like ours），把批評落在自己身上而非對方，殺傷力就降到最低。
swaps: I don't mean to sound pessimistic, but...
This is the uncomfortable part:
cards.pmNote: 談自建 vs. 採購時，最誠實的判準是「我們願不願意派最強的人去做它」——答案是否，就該買。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

cards.quote: If something is just purely code planning, there's not a great reason why we would be the best at that. I can't come up with a coherent argument for that.
cards.zh: 如果只是純粹的程式規劃，我想不出我們憑什麼會是最強的。這個我實在提不出一個站得住腳的論證。
cards.why: 承認「我論證不出來」而不是「這不重要」——這是知識誠實的最高標準。coherent argument 這個詞組把標準拉得很高：不是沒有理由，是沒有一個前後一致的理由。對自家產品講這句話，可信度會爆表。
swaps: I don't have a good story for why we'd win there.
I can't defend that one on the merits.
cards.pmNote: 評估差異化時要能講出一條「為什麼是我們」的因果鏈——講不出來就代表那不是護城河。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

cards.pattern: Maybe just to set the record straight, [X] doesn't mean [被推導出的錯誤結論]
cards.quote: First of all, maybe just to set the record straight, if AI is writing over 90% of the code, that doesn't mean engineers are 10X as productive.
cards.zh: 首先，我先把話講清楚：就算 AI 寫了九成以上的程式碼，也不代表工程師的產出就變成十倍。
cards.why: set the record straight 是在對方還沒說錯之前先澄清一個廣為流傳的誤推。這個片語帶有「我要修正公共認知」的份量，適合在你是該領域最有資格說話的人時使用。X doesn't mean Y 的結構則精準指出錯在推論那一步，不是事實那一步。
swaps: Let me correct a common misreading of that stat:
That number gets misused—it doesn't imply what people think.
cards.pmNote: 引用生產力數據時要一併說明「分母是什麼」，否則局部加速會被誤讀成整體加速。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

cards.pattern: We should be cannibalizing our own product every [週期]. It should make our existing product look silly.
cards.quote: We should be cannibalizing the existing state of our product every six to 12 months. Every six to 12 months, it should make our existing product look silly.
cards.zh: 我們應該每六到十二個月就把自己現有的產品吃掉一次。每六到十二個月，新的東西就該讓舊的看起來很蠢。
cards.why: 願景不用形容詞、用一個可檢驗的標準：舊版本看起來蠢不蠢。make our existing product look silly 這種具體到近乎粗魯的說法，比 continuous innovation 這種抽象詞管用一百倍——它讓團隊每半年可以自己驗收一次。
swaps: If last year's version still looks good, we didn't move enough.
We should be obsoleting ourselves on a schedule.
cards.pmNote: 把「自我淘汰」設成節奏（每 6-12 個月）而非口號，才有辦法在漸進式優化的壓力下保留破壞式投資。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

cards.quote: Incremental feels very safe. But that is not the reason why we're going to win. That's almost table stakes.
cards.zh: 有個很微妙的張力：漸進式改動感覺很安全，多加一顆按鈕嘛。但那不是我們會贏的原因，那幾乎只是入場資格。
cards.why: table stakes（賭桌上的最低下注額）是英語商務裡把某件事降級成「基本盤」的關鍵詞——不是不做，是做了也不加分。先承認漸進式的心理吸引力（feels very safe），再把它降級，比直接罵它保守有效得多。
swaps: Those are table stakes, not differentiation.
Necessary, but it's not where the win comes from.
cards.pmNote: roadmap 要分「維持入場資格」與「創造差異化」兩欄，兩者搶同一批人時要明確標出誰讓步。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

cards.pattern: Maybe [某個詞] is the wrong term, but this idea of just being okay with being wrong faster.
cards.quote: Maybe humility is the wrong term, but this idea of just being okay with being wrong faster. I always think about this when we make decisions.
cards.zh: 也許「謙虛」不是最準的詞，但就是那種「更快接受自己錯了」的心態。我們在做決策時我常想到這件事。
cards.why: Maybe X is the wrong term, but... 讓你可以用一個不夠精準的詞卻不被抓語病——你自己先承認了。這是英語口語裡處理「我知道我要講的東西還沒找到名字」的標準做法，比在腦中卡住找完美用詞流暢太多。
swaps: That's not quite the right word, but you know what I mean—
For lack of a better term,
cards.pmNote: 決策速度的真正瓶頸常常不是「多快做決定」，而是「多快承認決定錯了」。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

cards.pattern: I guess it's kind of an embarrassing thing to say, because everyone thinks [同樣的事], but [你的版本]
cards.quote: And I guess it's kind of an embarrassing thing to say because everyone who's a startup founder thinks, my startup moves super fast and the talent bar is super high.
cards.zh: 說這話其實有點難為情，因為每個新創創辦人都覺得「我們超快、人才標準超高」。
cards.why: 要講一句聽起來很老套的話之前，先承認它老套。it's kind of an embarrassing thing to say 把聽者心裡的白眼先講出來，之後你講什麼都會被當成真心話。這招在英語職場叫 disarming——先解除對方的武裝。
swaps: I know how this sounds—everyone says this—but...
This is a cliché and I'm about to say it anyway:
cards.pmNote: 講「我們很快」這種所有公司都會講的話時，一定要接一個可驗證的具體事例，否則等於沒講。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.pattern: Even if [極端讓步], which is absolutely not the case, we'd still [你的主張]
cards.quote: Even if we had no more progress today with models, which is absolutely not the case, but even if we had no more progress, we are way behind on product.
cards.zh: 就算模型從今天起完全不再進步——當然實際上完全不是這樣——就算真的不再進步，我們在產品上還是落後一大截。
cards.why: 先給對方一個最極端的讓步，讓你的結論在最不利的假設下也成立。which is absolutely not the case 這個插入語很關鍵：讓步只是修辭，不是真的認同。這是英語論證裡最強的一種結構，能一次擋掉所有「可是如果……」。
swaps: Even in the worst case—which I don't believe—the conclusion holds.
Assume none of that improves. We'd still have this problem.
cards.pmNote: 提案要能通過「最保守假設」的檢驗——只有在樂觀假設下才成立的提案，通常會在第一個季度死掉。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.pattern: Maybe this is a harsh thing to say, but [直白的判斷]
cards.quote: Maybe this is a harsh thing to say, but I think very few companies have the talent caliber to be able to do that. So it might need to be adjusted if you were going to implement this.
cards.zh: 這樣講可能有點刺耳，但我覺得能做到這件事的公司真的很少。所以你要照搬的話，大概得先調整過。
cards.why: harsh 這個字讓你在說出難聽話之前先自我標註，聽者就會把它接收成「誠實」而非「不客氣」。更精細的是後面補了一句實用的調整建議——講完狠話留一條路，是英語職場給難聽回饋的完整動作。
swaps: This might come across as blunt, but...
I'll say the unpopular thing:
cards.pmNote: 介紹別家公司的做法時要標明前提條件（人才密度、規模、資金），否則會被當成通用最佳實務照抄。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.pattern: We can have good conversations about a year out and about weeks out. But there's this awkward middle ground.
cards.quote: We can have really good conversations about something that's a year plus from now. And we can have really good conversations about what's happening in weeks. But there's this awkward middle ground.
cards.zh: 我們可以很好地討論一年以後的事，也可以很好地討論接下來幾週的事。但中間那一段就很尷尬。
cards.why: 把一個大家都隱約感覺到卻沒名字的困難命名為 awkward middle ground。給問題命名是資深者最有價值的動作之一——一旦有了名字，團隊就可以討論它、承認它、繞過它，而不是每次都重新卡住。
swaps: The hard horizon is the one in between.
Long-range and short-range are both tractable; the middle isn't.
cards.pmNote: 規劃週期要對應可預測性：一年看方向、幾週看執行，中間那段（一季到半年）刻意留彈性，別假裝能規劃。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.pattern: It's a bit like [具體角色] that refuses to [行為] and doesn't [行為] unless you ask it to.
cards.quote: It's a bit like this really smart intern that refuses to read Slack and doesn't check Datadog or Sentry unless you ask it to.
cards.zh: 它有點像一個超聰明、但死不看 Slack、你不叫他他就不會去看 Datadog 或 Sentry 的實習生。
cards.why: 解釋一個抽象技術限制時，用「一個有性格缺陷的人」來比喻。refuses to（拒絕）把工具擬人化成有脾氣的同事，比 lacks context 這種正確但無感的說法好記十倍。要能用的關鍵是：比喻裡的缺點必須精準對應真實限制。
swaps: Think of it as a brilliant new hire with no access to any of your tools.
It's like a contractor who's never read your docs.
cards.pmNote: 向非技術利害關係人解釋 AI 能力邊界時，用「同事的能力與盲點」比講模型參數有效得多。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.pattern: I'm not going to try to define [術語] exactly, but at least [你能給的操作型描述]
cards.quote: And I'm not going to try to define agent exactly, but at least the stack that we think of it as having is you have this model, really smart reasoning model.
cards.zh: 我不打算給 agent 一個精準的定義，但至少我們認為它的堆疊長這樣：底下有一個很會推理的模型。
cards.why: 拒絕定義，但給出操作型描述。這一招讓你完全避開「定義之爭」這種最浪費時間的討論，同時仍然把事情講清楚。at least 這個轉折詞是關鍵——它承認你給的不是完整答案，但也是有用的答案。
swaps: I won't attempt a definition, but here's how we use the word:
Rather than define it, let me describe what it does.
cards.pmNote: 討論新概念時先講「我們在這個 context 下怎麼用這個詞」，可以省下整場會議的名詞戰爭。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.quote: So I'll give you a contention and a plausible way we get there, but as for how it happens, who knows?
cards.zh: 我可以給你一個主張，還有一條看起來說得通的路徑，但實際上會怎麼發生，誰知道。
cards.why: 把答案明確拆成三層：主張（我相信什麼）、路徑（一種可能的走法）、機制（我不知道）。這種分層讓你能大膽預測而不必為細節負責。who knows 這種近乎隨性的收尾，在英語裡是自信的表現，不是敷衍。
swaps: Here's the claim and one path to it—the actual route, no idea.
I'll give you the destination and a plausible route, not a schedule.
cards.pmNote: 談長期願景時要明確區分「我們相信的終局」與「我們規劃的路徑」，後者一定會改，前者不該常改。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.pattern: I'm coming up with this on the spot, so it's not a good name, but [新概念]
cards.quote: So almost that it's like, I'm coming up with this on the spot, so it's not a good name, but chatter-driven development.
cards.zh: 有點像是——這名字是我現場亂想的，取得不好——「閒聊驅動開發」。
cards.why: 即興提出新概念時，先替名字道歉，重點就會落在概念本身而不是命名。on the spot（當場）這個片語明確標記了「未經打磨」，讓你可以放心丟出半成品想法。腦力激盪時這句幾乎萬用。
swaps: Terrible name, I just made it up, but the idea is—
Working title, don't judge it:
cards.pmNote: 腦力激盪階段要刻意把想法標成粗胚，否則團隊會開始批評包裝而不是討論核心。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.quote: Yeah. To be clear, we're not building that, but it's a fun idea.
cards.zh: 喔對，先說清楚，我們沒有要做這個，只是覺得這想法很好玩。
cards.why: 剛剛講了一個生動的假設情境，馬上澄清那不是產品計畫。To be clear 是英語裡專門用來防止誤引的訊號詞——尤其在公開場合、錄音、對媒體時是必備動作。台灣人常忘記做這一步，結果一個玩笑被寫成新聞標題。
swaps: That's not a roadmap item, just a thought experiment.
Hypothetical only—don't put that in the notes.
cards.pmNote: 對外談假設情境前後都要標記「這不是承諾」，任何被聽成 roadmap 的東西之後都會有人來要交期。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.pattern: I'm curious what you think. I still don't think [流行看法] as much as a lot of people think.
cards.quote: I'm curious what you think. I still don't think ideas are worth as much as maybe a lot of people think. I still think execution is really hard.
cards.zh: 我反而想聽你怎麼看。我還是不覺得點子有大家講的那麼值錢，我還是覺得執行才難。
cards.why: 先把發言權遞出去（I'm curious what you think），再講自己的反對意見——這個順序讓反對變成對話而不是宣告。still 這個副詞也很妙：暗示「我知道風向變了，但我沒被說服」，堅持得很有禮貌。
swaps: Curious how you see it—I'm not convinced that's true.
I might be in the minority here, but I still think...
cards.pmNote: 反駁流行論述時先問對方看法，可以在你不知道對方立場時避免正面衝撞。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.pattern: If I could only choose one thing to [做/懂], it would be [X].
cards.quote: But now I think we're getting to this point where actually if I could only choose one thing to understand, it would be really meaningful understanding of the problems that a certain customer has.
cards.zh: 但我覺得我們現在走到一個階段：如果只能挑一件事搞懂，那就是真正深刻地了解某一群客戶的問題。
cards.why: If I could only choose one thing 是強迫自己排序的句型，也逼聽者接受這是取捨而非清單。比起列出五個重點，這種「只准選一個」的假設能讓你的主張穿透力大得多，適合用在建議、面試、給後輩指路。
swaps: If you only invest in one thing, make it—
Forced to pick a single competency, I'd take...
cards.pmNote: 建構能力時要先問「哪一項最難被 AI 或工具取代」——多半是對特定客戶問題的深度理解。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.pattern: We can accidentally spend a lot of time on [某類事], and so we can end up oversolving for that.
cards.quote: So we can accidentally spend a lot of our time thinking about features that are very deep in the user adoption journey. And so we can kind of end up oversolving for that.
cards.zh: 我們很容易不小心把時間都花在使用者旅程很後段的功能上，結果就在那一段過度投入了。
cards.why: accidentally 和 end up 這兩個詞把一個團隊層級的錯誤講成「沒人故意的漂移」，沒有人被指責，問題卻被講清楚了。oversolving 是很好用的自創複合詞——不是做錯，是做太多，這種區分在資源討論時特別重要。
swaps: We drift towards the problems we personally feel.
There's a gravitational pull towards power-user features.
cards.pmNote: 團隊都是重度使用者時，會系統性高估進階功能、低估新手體驗——固定回頭看 D7 retention 是最簡單的解藥。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.pattern: I worked on [X] for a bit. I don't work on it now. But [你能講的角度]
cards.quote: So I worked on Atlas for a bit. I don't work on it now. But a bit of the narrative here for me just to tell my story a bit was...
cards.zh: 我做過 Atlas 一陣子，現在沒在做了。不過就我自己的角度、講一下我的版本的話……
cards.why: 被問到你只沾過邊的專案時，兩句話劃清界線再開口。for a bit（一陣子）與 I don't work on it now 把你的發言權限講得很精準，後面 my story 又進一步限縮成個人視角。這樣講出來的內容，就算之後被證明不完整也傷不到你。
swaps: I was on that team early on, not anymore—so from my angle...
I've got partial context on that. Here's my slice of it.
cards.pmNote: 跨團隊回答問題時先聲明你的資訊新鮮度，避免過期資訊被當成現況傳出去。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.quote: I will say if you're like, the hardest problem I have is that I need to build a new unicorn business, obviously that's not going to work. Not yet.
cards.zh: 當然啦，如果你說「我最難的問題是要生出一家獨角獸」，那顯然行不通。目前還不行。
cards.why: 剛給完一個很大方的建議（把最難的問題丟給它），立刻自己畫出上限，防止對方測試到荒謬的邊界然後說你唬爛。Not yet 這個獨立短句是精髓——同時承認現在的限制與未來的可能，兩個字做完兩件事。
swaps: There's obviously a ceiling—we're not there yet.
Within reason, of course.
cards.pmNote: 宣傳產品能力時主動標出「還做不到什麼」，可以擋掉大量因期待落差而流失的新用戶。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.pattern: Unfortunately, I don't think that's going to be binary. It's going to be very dependent on [變數].
cards.quote: So if we can rebuild systems to let the agent be default useful, we'll start unlocking hockey sticks. Unfortunately, I don't think that's going to be binary.
cards.zh: 所以如果我們能把系統重建成讓 agent 預設就有用，成長曲線就會開始往上翹。可惜我不覺得這會是一刀切的事。
cards.why: Unfortunately 放在句首不是在道歉，而是在標記「接下來要講的事不符合大家的期待」。binary 這個字精準表達了「不會有一個明確的時間點」，比 gradual 有力——因為它直接否定了提問者心中的模型。
swaps: It won't be a switch that flips.
There's no single moment—it'll be uneven across companies.
cards.pmNote: 談技術轉型時間點時，用「不同族群何時跨過門檻」取代「哪一年會發生」，判斷才有實用價值。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.pattern: So my long answer to your question—maybe boring answer—is that [結論]
cards.quote: So basically my long answer to your question, maybe boring answer is that I think starting next year, we're going to see early adopters starting to hockey stick their productivity.
cards.zh: 所以我這個落落長、可能還有點無聊的答案就是：我覺得從明年開始，早期採用者的生產力會開始往上翹。
cards.why: 講了很長一段之後，用 So my long answer is that 把整段壓縮成一句。這是英語會議裡非常受歡迎的動作——聽者已經累了，你替他做總結。中間插入 maybe boring answer 又順手降低期待，讓結論即使平淡也不失望。
swaps: The short version of all that is—
To land the plane: my answer is...
cards.pmNote: 長篇回答一定要自己收尾成一句，否則聽者記走的會是他自己挑的那句，而不是你的結論。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.pattern: We would realize that we were in fact not [X] six months ago, and we needed to be even more [X].
cards.quote: We would remind ourselves of this motto and then we would become more candid. And then six months later, we would realize that we were in fact not candid six months ago.
cards.zh: 我們會提醒自己這句座右銘，然後變得更坦白一點。結果半年後又發現，半年前的我們其實一點也不坦白。
cards.why: 承認一個「反覆犯的錯」而不是一次性的錯，難度高很多。in fact 這個插入語在這裡帶著自嘲的重量——事實跟我們當時的自我認知不符。這種螺旋式的自我修正敘事，在績效檢討和團隊回顧時特別有說服力。
swaps: Every six months we discover we were still sugar-coating things.
In hindsight, what felt direct at the time really wasn't.
cards.pmNote: 回顧會議要問「半年前我們以為自己做到了什麼，其實沒做到」——這比列新問題更能抓到系統性盲點。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.quote: So then the question is, how should we be candid? Okay, well, let's think of being candid as an act of kindness.
cards.zh: 所以問題變成：我們該怎麼坦白？後來想通了——把「坦白」當成一種善意的行為。
cards.why: 把兩個看似對立的價值（kind 與 candid）用 as an act of 綁在一起，直言就不再需要在善良與誠實之間選邊。這個句型 think of X as an act of Y 很好移植——把任何令人不安的行為重新歸類成一種美德。
swaps: Directness is the kind thing to do here.
Withholding the truth isn't kindness, it's avoidance.
cards.pmNote: 延遲難談的對話幾乎總是讓成本變高——把坦白重新定義成善意，是團隊敢給真回饋的文化前提。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.pattern: We don't have to agree on [大方向], but [你真正在乎的條件]
cards.quote: We're very interested in folks who have already been thinking about what the future should look like with agents. And we don't have to agree on where we're going, but we want people who are very passionate.
cards.zh: 我們很想找那種已經在思考「agent 的未來該長什麼樣」的人。方向上我們不一定要有共識，但我們要真的在乎這件事的人。
cards.why: 明講「不必同意我」是很高階的招募與協作訊號——你把門檻從「立場一致」換成「投入程度」。don't have to agree on X, but 這個結構在跨團隊合作時也很好用：先解除對方的立場壓力，再講你真正的要求。
swaps: You don't have to share my view—you do have to have one.
Disagreement is fine. Indifference isn't.
cards.pmNote: 招人時測「有沒有觀點」比測「觀點對不對」有用——觀點會改，思考習慣不會。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

cards.pattern: I don't know if I have [對方問的東西], but maybe I can tell you about [你真的有的東西]
cards.quote: I don't know if I have a life motto, but maybe I can tell you about the number one company value from my startup.
cards.zh: 我不確定我有什麼人生座右銘，不過也許我可以講一下我以前創業時的第一條公司價值觀。
cards.why: 被問到答不上來的問題時，不要硬掰，也不要只說「沒有」。這句用 but maybe I can tell you about 把話題平移到一個你真正有料的鄰近主題，對方完全不會覺得被打槍。面試遇到不擅長的問題時特別好用。
swaps: Not sure I have one of those—can I give you something adjacent?
I'll answer a slightly different question, if that's okay.
cards.pmNote: 面試被問到沒有素材的題目時，明說「我換一個角度回答」比硬編案例安全，面試官通常也接受。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos
